project.description: A local, AI-first project orchestrator that provides a web interface for managing multi-project workflows with Claude Code as the execution engine. It covers the full project lifecycle: ideation, specification, kanban-based planning, automated code generation via Claude Code CLI, real-time agent monitoring, and release management.
project.spec:
# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

## 1. Project overview

Arij is an MIT-licensed, local-first project orchestrator for planning, building, reviewing, and releasing software with AI coding agents. It combines a multi-project dashboard, specification editor, Kanban board, chat workspace, agent monitoring, Git automation, QA reports, project memory, and release management in one Next.js application.

Claude Code is the default execution engine. Named agents can instead use OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Kimi, Zai, Pi, or Oh My Pi. An OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint provides a direct, low-latency chat path; it is not a build, review, QA, or merge provider.

Arij has no hosted service, Arij account, cloud synchronization, or telemetry. Its database, documents, logs, clones, worktrees, and runtime artifacts remain on the local machine. Configured AI CLIs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Git remotes, and GitHub APIs may still communicate with their respective external services.

The package manifest reports version `0.1.0`. The only recorded product release and Git tag are `0.0.1` and `v0.0.1`; the main branch contains substantial completed work beyond that release.

### 1.1 Current implementation state

The GitHub import lifecycle is complete. Arij can:

- Attach a project to an existing local directory.
- Import a GitHub repository from a supported URL or `owner/repo` shorthand.
- Clone into an app-managed workspace and safely reuse a healthy matching clone.
- Analyze a repository or short-circuit from an existing `arji.json`.
- Populate GitHub ownership, clean remote URL, and detected default branch.
- Delete a clone only when database provenance, path containment, and an on-disk ownership marker all prove that Arij created it.

The current main branch also includes:

- Guarded epic and story transitions with explicit activity records for both accepted and refused moves.
- Manual and chat-driven epic creation, bug tickets, stories, dependencies, comments, screenshots, and review findings.
- A redesigned ticket detail surface with a hierarchical sticky header, mobile-safe layout, and compact, scannable activity feed.
- Isolated epic branches and Git worktrees for code-producing agents.
- Single-ticket pipelines, dependency-aware batch builds, night runs, Team Mode, and Full Auto Mode.
- Simplified named-agent creation based on a name and CLI, with optional model overrides and advanced role/runtime configuration.
- Agent reliability badges and opt-in reliability-based Full Auto dispatch.
- Manual and release-triggered specification rewrites.
- Per-session memory distillation and cross-session Dreaming.
- GitHub pull requests, issues, releases, push/pull status, and synchronization logs.
- Persisted session chunks, outcome classification, usage reporting, full failure notifications, and stalled-session detection.
- Project-scoped Server-Sent Events with polling fallback.

### 1.2 Development boundary

The following work is under review on feature branches and is not part of stable main-branch behavior:

- Mandatory red-to-green regression checks for bug tickets. The review branch contains bug-specific prompts, a mechanical regression checker, pipeline gating, reports, UI integration, and tests, but it has not been merged.
- Persisting `submit_findings`’ overall verdict and making it authoritative over prose-based review classification. Main currently persists findings and their originating session but not the structured overall verdict.

Principal backlog items include:

- A deterministic Arij-owned `test`/`lint`/`build` verification stage and persisted verification reports.
- Sorting the Sessions view by last activity instead of creation time.
- Structured acceptance-criteria grading.
- Scheduled routines and CI monitoring with opt-in autofix.
- Per-agent-type model policies, effort escalation, and optional second opinions before merge.
- Visual session artifacts and review evidence.
- Agent friction reports that can be converted into tickets.
- Recurring-failure digests.
- Extending the build/review agent MCP toolset so agents can create attributed, rate-limited bug tickets. Chat board tools can already create tickets.

These items must not be described as current product behavior until they are merged.

## 2. Objectives

1. **Unify the software lifecycle.** Let a user move from an idea or imported repository to a specification, actionable tickets, agent execution, review, merge, and release without switching project-management systems.

2. **Keep the application local-first.** Store project state, credentials, logs, documents, clones, worktrees, and runtime artifacts locally without requiring an Arij account or hosted backend.

3. **Support multiple execution providers.** Use Claude Code as the built-in default while allowing named agents backed by other supported CLIs and a separate OpenAI-compatible direct-chat mode.

4. **Protect repositories during autonomous work.** Isolate code changes in worktrees, serialize conflicting work, honor the repository’s real base branch, and refuse destructive filesystem actions without explicit ownership evidence.

5. **Make automation observable and interruptible.** Persist session state and output, classify terminal outcomes, surface failures and questions, expose live activity, support cancellation, and retain an audit trail for automated decisions.

6. **Automate without bypassing workflow rules.** Route manual actions, MCP requests, imports, pipelines, approval, release, and Full Auto through the same transition service. Completion must come from approval or a guarded merge, never an ordinary status write.

7. **Preserve project context.** Inject the project specification, learned memory, relevant tickets, user-authored comments, screenshots, and explicitly mentioned documents into the prompts that need them.

8. **Improve dispatch quality from evidence.** Show per-agent reliability and duration statistics and optionally select the strongest sufficiently sampled agent when the user has not made an explicit choice.

9. **Replace prose-only confidence with mechanical evidence.** Add deterministic verification, regression gates, structured review verdicts, acceptance grading, and review artifacts without treating agent assertions as proof.

## 3. Product principles and constraints

### 3.1 Local execution and access

- Arij is a single local Next.js application backed by SQLite.
- API access is restricted to localhost host/origin values by default. Additional origins require explicit `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` configuration.
- There is no multi-user authentication, cloud synchronization, external queue, worker service, or event broker.
- Long-running agents are local child processes. Authentication and provider-specific configuration belong to their respective CLIs.
- Scheduler queues, launch closures, active pipeline registries, live night-run state, Full Auto runtime locks, MCP tokens, and SSE subscriptions live in the server process.
- Agent session rows, chunks, settings, documents, tickets, releases, and batch tags are durable.
- On restart:
  - queued sessions whose launch closures were lost are cancelled as orphaned;
  - running sessions are failed and any unverifiable mid-run review promotion is pulled back when possible;
  - active pipelines and waves are not resumed;
  - night-run summaries can be partially reconstructed from tagged session rows;
  - Full Auto restarts from its persisted settings.
- GitHub clone and repository analysis requests are synchronous and do not have a background cancellation service.

### 3.2 Database and migrations

- SQLite runs with WAL mode and foreign keys enabled.
- Drizzle migrations are applied at server startup.
- Migrations are hand-written under `lib/db/migrations/`.
- `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run. Snapshot files stop at `0013`, while the migration journal reaches index `31` and migration `0032_review_comment_session`.
- A new relational change requires:
  - a numbered SQL migration;
  - a new monotonically increasing entry in `lib/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json`;
  - a `when` value greater than every previously applied migration.
- Settings keys, document kinds, and session agent types are free-form text and need no migration unless the relational schema changes.
- Legacy databases without migration bookkeeping are baseline-stamped and then advanced through the runtime migration path.

### 3.3 Git and repository safety

- `simple-git` remains the Git integration library. GitHub API operations use `@octokit/rest`; the `gh` CLI is not part of the architecture.
- GitHub imports are full clones. `--depth` and `--single-branch` are forbidden because worktrees, merge-base computation, branch integration, and releases require complete history.
- Code-producing work runs in an epic-specific branch and worktree, not directly in the project’s base checkout.
- Stories within one epic share the epic branch. Work on multiple stories of the same epic is serialized.
- Worktrees are created in the repository’s sibling `.arij-worktrees` directory. Worktrees outside the expected managed directory are treated as user-owned.
- The stored or repository-derived default branch is authoritative. `main` and `master` are fallbacks, not assumptions.
- Existing directories are never silently overwritten.
- A matching healthy clone may be fetched and reused. A mismatching or unowned destination is a conflict.
- Local repositories supplied by the user are never deleted by Arij.
- Clone deletion requires all of the following:
  - `projects.clone_source = "github"`;
  - the resolved directory remains inside the current projects root;
  - the repository contains a valid `.git/arij-clone.json` marker.
- Registered worktrees are removed during managed-clone cleanup only when they are inside the expected `.arij-worktrees` and projects roots.

### 3.4 Credentials and external communication

- The GitHub PAT is stored in the local `settings` table under `github_pat`.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not read by the application.
- Clone and reuse-fetch operations first try anonymously. Authentication is retried only for credential-related failures.
- Authenticated Git uses a one-command `http.extraHeader`; the PAT is not embedded in the remote URL or persisted in `.git/config`.
- Clone errors are redacted for authorization headers, URL user information, bearer tokens, GitHub token patterns, and the exact supplied secret.
- GitHub API operations use the stored PAT through Octokit.
- Ordinary push, pull, and tag-push operations still rely on the machine’s Git credential configuration. A private repository imported with a PAT may need a credential helper for later Git transport.
- OpenAI-compatible credentials are stored locally but are sent to the configured endpoint when that chat mode is used.
- AI CLI providers may transmit prompts, code, and project context according to their own configuration and service terms.

### 3.5 Workflow integrity

- Existing epic and story status writes go through `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts` and the workflow engine.
- Successful moves are logged. Guard refusals create explicit same-state activity entries.
- A build moves its target—and, for story work, the parent epic—to `in_progress` before its queued session row is created.
- A queued or running code-producing session owns its target’s `in_progress` state.
- Other users, agents, and system actions cannot move that target out of `in_progress` while the code session owns it.
- The sole owning code session may move its own target only from `in_progress` to `review`. It cannot demote the ticket, approve it, move it to Done, or move a story’s parent epic directly.
- If an owning session promotes work and then fails, asks a question, or otherwise does not deliver, terminal handling attempts to return the target to `in_progress`.
- Successful epic builds move the epic and the stories that were part of the build to `review`.
- Successful story builds move the story to `review`; the parent epic advances only after every sibling is in `review` or `done`.
- Failed, silent, refused, or question-ending builds remain or return to an appropriate held state with an explicit reason.
- A negative review returns the affected scope to `in_progress`.
- `review → done` requires an approval or merge source, a completed review where required, and no open blocking findings.
- Explicit human story approval acts as the review decision for that story but does not resolve epic-scoped findings.
- `released` is terminal and may only be entered by the system during release creation.
- Agent sessions cannot approve their own work through ordinary status updates.
- `arji.json` imports reconcile content transactionally and route existing status changes through the same guards. Refused statuses are reported and skipped.

### 3.6 Testing and delivery

- Unit, integration, and component tests live primarily in `__tests__/` and run with Vitest.
- Browser tests live in `e2e/` and run with Playwright.
- Vitest excludes dependencies, build output, app-managed clones, `.claude` worktrees, and runtime data artifacts.
- CI uses Node.js 22 and runs the complete Vitest suite on pushes and pull requests.
- Type checking, linting, production builds, and relevant Playwright tests remain expected verification steps but are not all enforced by the current CI workflow.
- Bug fixes are expected to include a regression test with a demonstrated failing state and passing fix. Product-level enforcement of that rule is still under review and is not active on main.
- Generated artifacts such as `arji.json`, databases, logs, uploads, managed clones, worktrees, and Playwright output must not be confused with source changes.

## 4. Technical stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node.js 20.9 or newer; CI uses Node.js 22 |
| Application | Next.js 16.1, App Router, TypeScript 5.9 |
| UI | React 19.2, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/Radix components |
| Kanban drag and drop | dnd-kit |
| Database | SQLite through `better-sqlite3`, WAL mode, foreign keys enabled |
| ORM and validation | Drizzle ORM and Zod |
| Git | Git CLI through `simple-git` |
| GitHub | `@octokit/rest` |
| Agent execution | Local CLI child processes behind a common provider interface |
| Agent tool protocol | Model Context Protocol through `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` |
| Direct chat API | OpenAI-compatible chat-completions HTTP/SSE |
| Real-time UI | Server-Sent Events with reconnect and polling fallback |
| Markdown | `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` |
| Documents | `mammoth` for DOCX and `pdf-parse` for PDF |
| IDs | nanoid |
| Tests | Vitest, Testing Library, jsdom, and Playwright |
| Packaging | npm package with the `arij` CLI wrapper |

## 5. Implemented product surface

### 5.1 Projects and repository import

A project can be created against an existing local directory or imported from an existing codebase.

The import flow supports:

- A local filesystem path validated as an existing directory.
- GitHub HTTPS, SSH-shaped, `git://`, scheme-less, browser, and `owner/repo` inputs.
- Strict owner/repository segment validation and clone-root containment.
- Separate “Cloning” and “Analyzing” progress states.
- An editable preview before creating the project and its tickets.
- An existing `arji.json` short-circuit that avoids agent analysis.
- Automatic creation of epics and stories followed by an `arji.json` export.
- A deterministic clone destination under the configured projects root.
- Reuse of a healthy matching clone.
- Replacement only of broken clone debris carrying Arij’s marker for the same repository.
- Staging-directory cloning followed by an atomic rename.
- Project deletion with optional, provenance-guarded clone cleanup.

GitHub imports normalize the remote to a clean HTTPS URL and populate `githubOwnerRepo`, `gitRemoteUrl`, and `defaultBranch`.

### 5.2 Planning and Kanban

Each project provides:

- Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review, Done, and Released columns.
- Feature epics and red-highlighted bug tickets with readable IDs.
- User stories, descriptions, acceptance criteria, priorities, dependencies, comments, findings, screenshots, and activity history.
- Manual drag-and-drop and API/MCP moves through the shared workflow engine.
- Direct manual epic creation with inline stories.
- Chat-driven epic refinement and creation.
- Bug creation with clipboard paste, drag-and-drop, or file-picker screenshots.
- Batch selection with parallel, sequential, dependency-aware, and Team Mode execution.
- Project-scoped SSE updates, move animations, live agent indicators, and polling fallback.
- A ticket detail panel with prioritized information and actions, a sticky header, responsive layout, and a compact chronological activity feed.
- Unread-agent and failure indicators derived from persisted session state.

### 5.3 Chat, specifications, documents, and memory

The unified chat workspace provides tabbed conversations, persisted history, provider or named-agent selection, attachments for supported CLI modes, and streamed responses.

Regular chat conversations can use board tools to:

- List and inspect tickets.
- Create and edit tickets.
- Request guarded status changes.
- Post comments.
- Inspect agent status.
- Start builds.

The board-tool channel is available to the OpenAI-compatible path and to supported CLI chat providers when MCP tools are enabled. Structured brainstorm and epic-creation conversations keep their output contracts isolated from board tools.

The OpenAI-compatible mode stores a base URL, optional API key, model, and reasoning effort. It supports connection testing and token-by-token SSE streaming. It can run normal, brainstorm, and epic-creation conversations, but structured conversations receive no board tools. Image attachments are rejected in this mode.

Project context can include:

- Project name and description.
- The stored specification.
- Learned project memory.
- Ticket and story details.
- User-authored comments and review findings.
- Bug screenshots.
- Explicitly mentioned project documents.

The specification can be:

- Edited manually.
- Initially generated by an agent.
- Rewritten by a selected plan-mode agent with an optional instruction.
- Automatically rewritten after release creation when the opt-in setting is enabled.

Agent-driven specification output replaces the saved specification only after an answered run with usable content. Failed, silent, cancelled, or question-ending sessions leave it unchanged. Successful writes re-export `arji.json`.

Documents support:

- Manual upload of PDF, DOCX, Markdown, plain text, and images.
- Markdown conversion for supported text formats.
- Local storage and display of image documents.
- `@filename` and `@{filename with spaces}` references.
- Repository scanning for PDF, Markdown, text, DOC, and DOCX candidates.
- User selection before import.
- Idempotent, case-insensitive duplicate handling.
- Per-file import failures without aborting the entire batch.

Legacy `.doc` files can be discovered but must be converted to `.docx`. Repository scanning skips symlinks, dependencies, VCS internals, worktrees, caches, and build output.

### 5.4 Learned memory and Dreaming

Each project has one capped Markdown memory document that is injected into relevant prompts.

Per-session memory distillation can run:

- Manually from an eligible completed session.
- Automatically after successful build-type sessions when enabled.

Auto-distillation is off by default and skips failures, unresolved questions, memory-writer sessions, and concurrent memory rewrites.

Dreaming is the cross-session memory pass. It:

- Collects recent completed build and review evidence across multiple tickets.
- Includes successful, failed, silent, question-ending, and transition-refused outcomes where applicable.
- Incorporates final-response tails, major findings, review conclusions, errors, and forensic diagnostics.
- Reads at most 30 eligible terminal sessions from a rolling window of up to 14 days, bounded by the last successful collection cutoff.
- Can be started manually or after a night run when enabled.
- Rewrites memory into four required sections:
  - Codebase pitfalls
  - Recurring agent mistakes
  - Strategies that work
  - Build instructions
- Serializes Dreaming and per-session distillation through one memory-writer lock.
- Refuses to overwrite a manual memory edit made while the agent was running.
- Preserves one pre-Dreaming snapshot for recovery.
- Emits an activity trace and notification after a successful rewrite.

### 5.5 Agent configuration and execution

A named agent contains:

- A user-facing name.
- One supported CLI.
- An optional model override; an empty value uses the CLI’s default.

The default creation path requires only a name and CLI. Availability indicators show whether each CLI is detected. Advanced configuration exposes:

- Per-role assignments.
- Global and project-scoped prompts.
- Custom review agents.
- Reviewer/provider segregation.
- Runtime concurrency and watchdog settings.
- Reliability and duration statistics.

Provider authentication and low-level configuration remain each CLI’s responsibility.

Agent resolution follows this precedence:

1. Explicit named-agent choice.
2. Project-scoped role assignment.
3. Global role assignment.
4. Built-in Claude Code fallback.

For reviews, optional provider segregation may choose an installed provider different from the last successful builder, but never overrides an explicit choice.

Agent sessions persist:

- Lifecycle status.
- Provider, model, named-agent identity, and task type.
- Project, epic, and story scope.
- Prompt, CLI command display, branch, worktree, and logs path.
- Ordered output chunks.
- Terminal outcome and full error information.
- Start, completion, and activity timestamps.
- Token and reported-cost usage.
- Batch or night-run attribution.
- Provider session identifiers where available.

Sessions can be queued, monitored, cancelled, inspected, and resumed for providers whose CLI exposes usable continuity.

A per-project in-process scheduler applies an optional concurrency cap. The built-in default is unlimited; a stored value of `0` also means unlimited. Positive values create a FIFO queue.

### 5.6 Automation modes

Arij provides three automation scopes.

#### Single-ticket autonomous pipeline

The pipeline runs:

```text
build → review → optional fix → re-review
```

It includes:

- Per-stage retry ladders.
- Optional provider escalation on later attempts.
- A configurable fix-cycle limit.
- A hard limit of 12 sessions per run.
- Cancellation, question, target-conflict, and workflow guards.
- A forensic diagnostic after exhausted stage failures.

A clean result leaves the ticket in Review awaiting approval or merge. The pipeline does not approve its own work.

#### Night run

A night run processes selected epics through dependency-ordered waves. Each launched epic runs the complete autonomous pipeline.

Night runs support:

- To Do tickets and optionally selected Backlog work.
- Dependency blocking.
- Continue-or-stop failure policies.
- A configurable consecutive-failure circuit breaker.
- A reported-cost cap.
- Explicit user stopping.
- Notifications and detailed morning summaries.
- Reconstruction of interrupted history from session batch tags.
- Optional Dreaming after the run terminates.

#### Full Auto Mode

Full Auto is a standing per-project supervisor. It repeatedly:

1. Reconciles its in-flight state.
2. Merges eligible cleanly reviewed epics.
3. Dispatches reviews within the review budget.
4. Dispatches builds within the build budget.

It considers buildable Backlog, To Do, and unoccupied In Progress work, while skipping tickets that are busy, awaiting a user reply, blocked by dependencies, owned by another pipeline or night run, or parked after repeated failures.

Full Auto provides:

- Separate build and review concurrency budgets.
- Explicit build and review agent choices.
- Opt-in smart dispatch.
- Activity entries for automatic choices and skips.
- A fresh-review requirement before merge.
- Blocking-finding checks.
- Soft parking after three consecutive failures.
- Hard parking after unresolved merge conflicts.

Smart dispatch is off by default. When enabled and no role agent was explicitly selected, it chooses the highest-success named agent over the previous 30 days among agents with at least five terminal runs for that role. Ties are deterministic, and the choice is recorded in the ticket activity log.

A clean merge uses the normal Git and workflow guards. On a genuine content conflict, Full Auto may dispatch one merge-resolution agent and retry once. An unresolved conflict parks the epic and notifies the user.

### 5.7 Reviews, QA, and releases

Built-in reviews cover:

- Security.
- Code quality.
- Compliance.
- Feature completeness.

Custom review agents can add their own instructions.

Review findings are stored with file and line anchors and may be linked to the session that filed them. Open findings block guarded completion.

On main, review decisions use fresh structured finding rows when available and retain a prose-verdict fallback. `submit_findings`’ overall verdict is not yet persisted as the authoritative transition signal; that work remains under review.

QA supports:

- Technology checks.
- E2E test sessions.
- Custom prompts.
- Named-agent selection.
- Persisted reports and report history.
- Creating feature or bug epics from report findings.

QA checks are agent-driven. Project documents are not injected automatically merely because a QA job was started. Arij does not yet independently execute configured test, lint, or build commands.

Release creation:

- Accepts completed, unreleased work.
- Generates a structured changelog or falls back to ticket titles.
- Creates or reuses a `release/v<version>` branch.
- Writes and commits `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Creates a `v<version>` Git tag targeting the release commit.
- Optionally pushes the tag and creates a draft GitHub release.
- Moves included epics from Done to Released.
- Emits project events and an optional webhook.
- May trigger the opt-in automatic specification rewrite.

### 5.8 GitHub integration

Once `githubOwnerRepo` and a PAT are configured, Arij supports:

- Detecting and connecting repository remotes.
- Branch ahead/behind status.
- Guarded push and pull operations with conflict reporting.
- Creating and synchronizing pull requests.
- Synchronizing open GitHub issues.
- Filtering and triaging issues.
- Mapping issue labels to feature or bug ticket types.
- Importing selected issues as Arij tickets.
- Creating draft GitHub releases and publishing them.
- Recording Git operations in `git_sync_log`.

## 6. Architecture

### 6.1 Runtime overview

```text
Browser
  |
  | HTTP + Server-Sent Events
  v
Next.js App Router
  |
  +-- API routes and workflow services
  +-- SQLite / Drizzle
  +-- local files under data/
  +-- in-process scheduler, watchdog, event bus, pipelines and supervisors
  |
  +-- AI CLI child processes
  +-- OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint
  +-- Git CLI through simple-git
  +-- GitHub API through Octokit
```

Arij is intentionally a single-process local application. The database is the durable state source; process-local registries coordinate active work but are not a durable job queue.

### 6.2 Filesystem layout

```text
<arij>/
  data/
    arij.db
    sessions/<session-id>/
    documents/<project-id>/
    uploads/<project-id>/
    migrations/
  projects/
    <owner>-<repo>/
      .git/arij-clone.json
    .arij-worktrees/
  lib/db/migrations/

<linked-repository>/
  arji.json
  ../.arij-worktrees/
```

The managed projects root defaults to `<cwd>/projects` and can be overridden with the absolute `projects_root` setting. Generated and runtime artifacts are excluded from source control.

### 6.3 GitHub import flow

```text
GitHub input
    |
    v
POST /api/projects/clone
    |
    +-- parse and validate owner/repo
    +-- resolve destination inside projects_root
    +-- serialize access to that destination
    +-- reuse and fetch a healthy matching clone
    +-- or clone into a private staging directory
    +-- stamp the ownership marker
    +-- atomically rename into place
    |
    v
POST /api/projects/import
    |
    +-- validate the local directory
    +-- read existing arji.json
    +-- or run repository analysis
    |
    v
Editable preview
    |
    v
Project and ticket creation
    |
    v
Export arji.json
```

Clone and analysis remain separate synchronous requests. This preserves the established analysis pipeline and exposes honest progress without introducing another job system.

### 6.4 Build lifecycle

```text
Build request
    |
    +-- validate project, target, workflow and concurrency
    +-- resolve the named agent and provider
    +-- create or attach the epic worktree and branch
    +-- move target and parent to In Progress
    +-- create the queued session
    |
    v
Per-project scheduler
    |
    v
Provider child process
    |
    +-- persist chunks and activity
    +-- accept scoped Arij MCP actions where supported
    +-- classify answered / asked_question / silent / error
    |
    v
Terminal workflow handler
    |
    +-- delivered success -> Review
    +-- failure/question/refusal -> hold or return to In Progress
    +-- emit events, comments, notifications and automation hooks
```

Build start and completion share the same workflow helpers across manual dispatch, pipelines, batches, night runs, and Full Auto.

### 6.5 Workflow and automation layering

```text
UI / API / MCP / arji.json / release / automation
                         |
                         v
              Transition service
                         |
             +-----------+-----------+
             |                       |
             v                       v
       Workflow guards          Activity log
             |
             v
         SQLite write
             |
             v
     Project-scoped SSE event
```

Automation engines select work and dispatch stages; they do not receive an alternate status-writing path.

### 6.6 Provider layer and MCP channel

`lib/providers/` defines a shared interface for spawning, streaming, cancelling, resuming, and checking CLI availability.

Shared child-process behavior includes:

- Bounded output handling.
- CLI session ID extraction where available.
- Ordered chunk persistence.
- Usage extraction.
- Command display with prompt and secret redaction.
- SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL cancellation for process-backed providers.

Claude Code and Codex support per-spawn MCP configuration. Their agent toolset currently exposes:

- `get_ticket`
- `update_ticket_status`
- `post_comment`
- `ask_question`
- `submit_findings`

Regular chat uses a broader board toolset that includes listing, creating, and editing tickets and starting builds.

Each MCP token is short-lived and scoped to a session, project, epic, story, and agent type. Tokens are revoked when the process ends.

Claude Code receives its MCP configuration through a permission-restricted temporary file that is deleted after the session. Codex receives process-level configuration overrides; the real command line therefore has residual token exposure to local process inspection, although the persisted display command is redacted.

Providers without per-spawn MCP injection still receive prompt context but cannot use Arij’s structured agent tools.

### 6.7 Durable state, events, and observability

SQLite stores:

- Projects, epics, bugs, stories, dependencies, and activity.
- Conversations, messages, attachments, documents, and project memory.
- Agent sessions, ordered chunks, prompts, named agents, and role assignments.
- Review comments, QA reports, releases, pull requests, and GitHub issues.
- Git synchronization logs, notifications, read cursors, and provider usage snapshots.
- Free-form global and project-scoped settings.

The server emits project-scoped SSE events for ticket, session, and release changes. Clients reconnect with exponential backoff and use polling when disconnected. This is an in-process event bus, not a durable event stream.

The watchdog periodically checks running sessions against their last persisted output activity. It creates one stalled notification and activity entry per stall but never kills the agent automatically.

Terminal failures retain the full readable error in the session and notification, with a deep link to the affected session.

### 6.8 Specification and memory writers

Specification and memory rewrites are project-level plan-mode sessions.

- A project can have only one pending specification-generation session.
- Per-session memory distillation and Dreaming share one memory-writer exclusion rule.
- Agent output replaces durable content only after a successful, answered run.
- Dreaming and distillation compare the current memory with the version used to build the prompt before committing a replacement.
- Successful specification writes re-export `arji.json`.
- Successful Dreaming writes archive the immediately previous memory and advance the collection cutoff atomically.

### 6.9 `arji.json` synchronization

`arji.json` is the repository-facing projection of project metadata, specification, epics, stories, and comments.

Board writes trigger best-effort export. Users can also request explicit export or guarded import.

Import behavior:

- Reconciles project and ticket content.
- Creates or updates tickets by stable ID.
- Removes rows absent from the file through the synchronization path.
- Sends existing epic and story status changes through the workflow service.
- Reports and skips refused status changes.
- Emits move events only after the database transaction commits.

## 7. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Local Next.js application with SQLite | Keeps installation simple and puts durable project data under the user’s control. |
| CLI agents instead of a single vendor API | Reuses existing CLI authentication and supports multiple agent ecosystems. |
| OpenAI-compatible HTTP as chat-only | Provides low-latency conversation without pretending a stateless chat endpoint is a build or review runner. |
| Named agents separate identity from task role | Users configure understandable agents once and assign them globally, per project, per role, or per dispatch. |
| Provider configuration belongs to each CLI | Arij stores provider and model choice without duplicating every CLI’s authentication and runtime settings. |
| Explicit agent choices beat automation | A user’s selection always wins over reviewer segregation and reliability-based smart dispatch. |
| Worktree and branch per epic | Supports parallel work across epics while keeping one integration unit for stories, review, and merge. |
| Central transition service | Manual actions, API calls, MCP actions, imports, approval, release, pipelines, and Full Auto share the same guards and audit trail. |
| Owning-session promotion is narrowly scoped | A build can deliver its own target to Review without unlocking unrelated moves or self-approval. |
| SSE with polling fallback | Provides responsive local updates without a WebSocket server or external broker. |
| In-process scheduling | Fits the single-process deployment while providing optional concurrency limits and FIFO admission. |
| Separate pipeline, night-run, and Full Auto modes | Each automation scope has a clear lifecycle, budget, and termination model. |
| Smart dispatch is opt-in and deterministic | Reliability data can improve unattended work without silently changing established agent choices. |
| Structured MCP channels are capability-gated | Claude Code and Codex receive scoped tools without writing shared provider configuration into repositories. |
| Full clone in a deterministic root | Worktrees, merges, tags, retry, and safe cleanup need complete history and predictable paths. |
| Clone into staging, then rename atomically | Failed or interrupted downloads cannot leave a half-valid destination. |
| Ownership marker plus database provenance | Location, remote URL, or a request flag alone is insufficient authority to delete source code. |
| PAT supplied through one-command Git configuration | Private clone and reuse-fetch operations work without persisting credentials in repository configuration. |
| Clone and analysis remain separate endpoints | Reuses the established import pipeline and exposes accurate progress without new infrastructure. |
| Agent-written durable documents commit only after answered runs | Failed, silent, cancelled, question-ending, or concurrent rewrites cannot corrupt saved context. |
| Per-session distillation and cross-session Dreaming remain distinct | One captures a fresh local lesson; the other extracts recurring patterns across many outcomes. |
| Deterministic verification remains a separate planned stage | Agent prose and AI review are not substitutes for mechanically executed tests, lint, and builds. |
| Full Auto conflict resolution is explicit and opt-in | It enables unattended progress while acknowledging the risk of merging an agent-resolved conflict without a second review. |

## 8. Current limitations and exclusions

- GitHub is the only supported clone host. GitLab, Bitbucket, and self-hosted Git services are not implemented.
- SSH-shaped GitHub inputs are normalized to HTTPS; SSH-key-based private cloning is not a supported credential path.
- Monorepo subdirectory imports are not supported.
- Clone and analysis requests are synchronous and have no background cancellation or progress service beyond the two UI phases.
- Scheduler queues, active pipelines, wave registries, runtime locks, MCP tokens, and live event subscriptions do not survive a server restart.
- Full Auto configuration survives restart, but its in-flight and parking state does not.
- Arij is a single-user local application, not a collaborative hosted service.
- Team Mode is limited to Claude Code.
- OpenAI-compatible mode is chat-only and does not support image attachments.
- Providers other than Claude Code and Codex do not receive per-session Arij MCP tools.
- The build/review agent MCP toolset cannot yet create bug tickets; that capability is distinct from chat ticket creation and remains backlog.
- Repository document scanning performs no OCR and does not import image files.
- Legacy `.doc` documents require conversion to `.docx`.
- Git push, pull, and tag transport may require an external credential helper for private repositories.
- Pipeline verification is agent-instructed rather than independently executed by Arij.
- The red-to-green bug regression gate exists only on an unmerged review branch.
- Review transition decisions still retain a prose fallback, and `submit_findings`’ overall structured verdict is not yet authoritative on main.
- The Sessions page sorts by creation time; last-activity sorting remains backlog.
- Full Auto conflict resolution allows an agent to modify the epic worktree and merge a successful resolution without a second review. Projects that do not accept that risk should leave Full Auto disabled.

epics.title: Ordre d'exécution unifié : position seule source de vérité du full-auto
epics.description:
## Contexte
Le board et le full-auto divergent : le board trie par `position` seule (hooks/useKanban.ts:76) alors que le supervisor full-auto trie par `priority DESC, position ASC` (lib/auto-mode/select.ts:554-558, compareEpics). De plus, le full-auto pioche dans le backlog (BUILDABLE_EPIC_STATUSES, select.ts:55) et ignore complètement la table `ticket_dependencies` (le respect des dépendances n'existe que dans les builds par vagues, lib/dependencies/wave-runner.ts).

## Objectif
Le rang visuel intra-colonne devient l'unique source de vérité de l'ordre d'exécution (WYSIWYG) :
- Le full-auto sélectionne strictement par `position ASC` dans **To do** ; la priorité 0–3 reste un badge + filtre, plus un critère de sélection.
- `backlog` sort des statuts buildables du full-auto : seuls `todo` et `in_progress` sont éligibles au build.
- Le full-auto respecte `ticket_dependencies` : un ticket dont un prérequis n'est pas done/released est sauté (réutiliser lib/dependencies/validation.ts — filterBuildableTickets / getTransitiveDependencies — comme wave-runner.ts).
- Bouton « Trier par priorité » sur Backlog/To do qui réécrit les positions en bloc (priority DESC, ordre courant stable pour les égalités), via la route reorder existante.

## Fichiers clés
lib/auto-mode/select.ts (compareEpics, BUILDABLE_EPIC_STATUSES, isEpicSelectable), lib/dependencies/validation.ts, hooks/useKanban.ts, app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/reorder/route.ts.

## Hors périmètre
Fractional indexing des positions (ticket séparé si besoin).

user_stories.title: Le full-auto sélectionne strictement par position ASC dans To do
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: compareEpics ne lit plus priority ; à priorités différentes, c'est le ticket le plus haut de la colonne qui part en premier ; tests unitaires de select.ts mis à jour.

user_stories.title: Le backlog n'est plus buildable par le full-auto
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: BUILDABLE_EPIC_STATUSES = { todo, in_progress } ; un ticket en backlog n'est jamais sélectionné par le sweep, même sans candidat en To do.

user_stories.title: Le full-auto respecte les dépendances
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Un ticket dont une dépendance (directe ou transitive) n'est pas done/released est sauté par selectBuildCandidates ; la logique est partagée avec lib/dependencies (pas de duplication) ; test couvrant le cas prérequis en in_progress.

user_stories.title: Bouton « Trier par priorité » sur les colonnes Backlog et To do
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Réécrit les positions en bloc (priority DESC, stable pour les égalités) via la route reorder ; l'ordre affiché après clic correspond à l'ordre que le full-auto exécutera.

epics.title: Lisibilité du board : file d'exécution, tickets bloqués, readiness
epics.description:
## Contexte
Prérequis : « Ordre d'exécution unifié » (position = file d'exécution). Le board doit rendre visible ce que l'orchestrateur va faire, sans ouvrir chaque ticket.

## Contenu
1. **File d'exécution** : les cartes To do affichent leur rang (#1, #2, …), la première porte un marqueur « prochain ».
2. **État bloqué** : carte grisée + mention « attend : <ticket> » quand une dépendance n'est pas done/released — cohérent avec le skip du full-auto.
3. **Survol** : hover sur une carte → surbrillance de ses prédécesseurs/successeurs sur le board.
4. **Readiness backlog** : indicateur sur les cartes Backlog (questions agent répondues via lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts, description non vide, critères d'acceptation présents). Le drag backlog→todo reste toujours permis ; warning discret si des questions sont ouvertes — jamais bloquant, c'est l'utilisateur qui décide.
5. **Drag sous filtre** : réautoriser le déplacement inter-colonne quand un filtre est actif (Board.tsx:336 désactive tout aujourd'hui) ; le réordonnancement fin intra-colonne peut rester désactivé sous filtre.

## Fichiers clés
components/kanban/Board.tsx, EpicCard.tsx, Column.tsx, hooks/useKanban.ts, lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts, view-models des cartes côté API board.

user_stories.title: Rang de file (#1, #2, …) et marqueur « prochain » sur les cartes To do
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Le rang reflète position ASC ; il se met à jour immédiatement après un drag ; les tickets bloqués ou awaiting-reply sont exclus de la numérotation effective ou marqués comme sautés.

user_stories.title: État visuel « bloqué » quand une dépendance n'est pas livrée
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Carte grisée + libellé « attend : <readableId> » ; disparaît dès que toutes les dépendances sont done/released.

user_stories.title: Surbrillance des dépendances au survol d'une carte
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Hover ≥150 ms → prédécesseurs et successeurs surlignés (styles distincts), le reste atténué ; aucune gêne au drag.

user_stories.title: Indicateur de readiness sur les cartes Backlog
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Trois critères : pas de question agent en attente, description non vide, critères d'acceptation présents ; affiché « Prêt n/3 » ; warning non bloquant au drag backlog→todo si questions ouvertes.

user_stories.title: Drag inter-colonne autorisé quand un filtre est actif
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Sous filtre, déplacer une carte vers une autre colonne fonctionne (drop en fin de colonne) ; le réordonnancement intra-colonne sous filtre peut rester désactivé.

epics.title: Colonne Review divisée : section « Prêt à merger »
epics.description:
## Contexte
« Prêt à merger » est déjà un état dérivé côté auto-mode : hasFreshCleanReview (review terminée postérieure au dernier changement de code, lib/auto-mode/select.ts:589) + zéro review_comments ouvert (selectMergeCandidates, select.ts:692). L'UI n'expose pas ce signal : la colonne Review est une salle d'attente opaque.

## Contenu
1. Exposer le signal merge-ready par ticket dans l'API qui alimente le board — extraire un prédicat partagé avec selectMergeCandidates, pas de duplication.
2. Diviser visuellement la colonne Review : section haute « Prêt à merger », section basse « En review ». L'appartenance est dérivée, pas draggable entre sections.
3. Bouton Merge directement sur les cartes prêtes (réutilise la route approve existante et ses garde-fous : merge git d'abord, résolution des findings, transition review→done).
4. Sur les cartes non prêtes, afficher la raison bloquante : « 2 findings ouverts », « review périmée par un nouveau commit », « merge en conflit ».

## Non-objectif
Pas de nouveau statut to_merge dans la state machine — état dérivé uniquement (éviter de toucher lib/workflow/engine.ts, lib/types/kanban.ts, le schéma MCP, etc.).

user_stories.title: Prédicat merge-ready partagé exposé dans l'API du board
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Même logique que selectMergeCandidates (review fraîche + zéro finding ouvert) factorisée en un prédicat unique consommé par l'auto-mode et par l'API board.

user_stories.title: Colonne Review divisée en deux sections dérivées
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Section haute « Prêt à merger » (accent visuel), section basse « En review » ; un ticket change de section automatiquement quand son signal change ; pas de drag entre sections.

user_stories.title: Bouton Merge sur les cartes prêtes
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Appelle la route approve existante ; états loading/erreur gérés ; en cas d'échec de merge la carte affiche le conflit et propose Resolve merge.

user_stories.title: Raison bloquante affichée sur les cartes Review non prêtes
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Cause précise et actionnable : nombre de findings ouverts, review périmée, conflit ; mise à jour au polling du board.

epics.title: Agent Refinement : repasse automatique sur Backlog et To do
epics.description:
## Contexte
Bouton « Agent Refinement » sur le board : un agent fait une repasse sur tous les tickets Backlog + To do et remet le board en état — questions, priorités, ordre, dépendances, promotion.

## Contenu
1. **Nouveaux outils MCP** (app/api/mcp/*) : set_priority, reorder_tickets, add_dependency / remove_dependency, promote_ticket (backlog→todo et rétrogradation inverse). Chaque écriture passe par ticket_activity_log avec une justification (actor « agent ») : le ticket garde la trace de pourquoi l'agent l'a déplacé.
2. **Agent refinement** : nouvel agentType avec prompt dédié. Il reçoit le snapshot des tickets backlog/todo (dépendances + état awaiting-reply inclus) et : signale en commentaire les questions principales restées sans réponse, complète/ajuste les dépendances, réordonne To do, promeut en To do les tickets prêts, rétrograde en Backlog ceux qui ne le sont pas (en posant la question manquante).
3. **Bouton UI** dans le header du board, avec état « en cours » (infra agentSessions existante).
4. **Rapport de synthèse** en fin de session : notification + commentaire récapitulatif (« 4 promus, 2 renvoyés en backlog, 3 arêtes ajoutées, To do réordonné »).
5. Optionnel : déclinable en routine périodique (lib/routines).

## Garde-fous
Le refinement a le droit de promouvoir backlog→todo (décision produit validée). Il ne touche jamais aux colonnes in_progress / review / done. Ses réordonnancements utilisent la même route reorder que le drag (transactionnelle).

user_stories.title: Outils MCP de refinement (priorité, ordre, dépendances, promotion)
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: set_priority, reorder_tickets, add_dependency, remove_dependency, promote_ticket disponibles pour les tokens de session non-chat ; chaque appel exige une justification, journalisée dans ticket_activity_log ; validation DAG (cycles refusés) réutilisée.

user_stories.title: Agent refinement : prompt et pipeline de repasse
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: L'agent traite tous les tickets backlog/todo ; questions sans réponse signalées en commentaire ; tickets prêts promus, tickets non prêts rétrogradés avec question posée ; aucune écriture hors backlog/todo.

user_stories.title: Bouton « Agent Refinement » dans le header du board
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Dispatch une session agent visible dans le suivi existant ; bouton désactivé pendant l'exécution avec indicateur ; erreurs de session remontées en notification.

user_stories.title: Rapport de synthèse en fin de refinement
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Notification + commentaire récapitulatif listant promotions, rétrogradations, changements de priorité/ordre et arêtes de dépendance modifiées, avec liens vers les tickets.

epics.title: Sessions oh-my-pi sans token MCP : tous les appels arij tombent en 401
epics.description:
## Symptôme
Tout agent `oh-my-pi` qui appelle un outil MCP arij (`submit_findings`, `ask_question`, `create_bug`, `submit_grading`, …) reçoit UNAUTHORIZED « Invalid or expired MCP token ». Constaté sur l'epic « Providers Documentation » (WwtYAgC2ezhu, projet Arij Front) : 3 sessions de review consécutives incapables de déposer leurs findings — `review_comments` vide, `review_verdict` null sur toutes les sessions, zéro grading. Le reviewer a posté son rapport en commentaire à la place.

## Cause racine
- `providerSupportsMcp` ne retourne true que pour `claude-code` et `codex` (lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:123-125) : pour une session omp, process-manager.ts:117 ne mint AUCUN token et n'injecte aucune config.
- Mais omp charge le serveur arij depuis sa config globale `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`, qui attend le token par interpolation d'env : `"ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN": "${ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN}"`. Arij ne pose jamais cette variable au spawn d'omp → le shim démarre avec un token vide.
- Les outils se montent quand même (chez omp le toolset se monte sur présence de la clé de config, pas sur validité du token) → l'agent voit les outils, les appelle, 401 systématique.

## Fix proposé
1. Inclure `oh-my-pi` dans `providerSupportsMcp`.
2. Au spawn omp (lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts / pi.ts), passer `ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN` et `ARIJ_BASE_URL` dans l'env du process enfant — la config globale omp les interpole déjà, rien à changer côté omp. Ne pas oublier le cas readonly (overlay xdev-off, voir l'en-tête de oh-my-pi.ts : avec xdev off les outils MCP se montent en first-class, c'est le chemin déjà validé).
3. Vérifier que la révocation de token en fin de session (process-manager) couvre bien ce nouveau chemin.

## Critères d'acceptation
- Une session de review omp dépose ses findings : lignes `review_comments` créées, `agent_sessions.review_verdict` renseigné.
- `ask_question` d'un agent omp produit outcome `asked_question` et le badge « Awaiting your reply ».
- Un smoke test sur un epic jetable (build omp + review omp) passe de bout en bout.
- Re-sonder le comportement après tout upgrade d'omp (le montage des toolsets a déjà changé entre versions).

epics.title: Une review sans findings déposables compte comme « clean » et débloque le merge
epics.description:
## Symptôme
Sur l'epic « Providers Documentation » (Arij Front), 3 reviews consécutives n'ont pas pu déposer leurs findings (cf. bug token MCP omp). Les rounds 1-2 n'ont bloqué que parce que le fallback prose a trouvé « changes requested » dans le texte ; le round 3 n'avait pas ces sous-chaînes → le gate review→done (« review terminée + zéro review_comments ouvert ») était vacuously satisfait et l'epic est devenu mergeable, findings perdus dans un commentaire.

## Problème
Le gate confond « zéro finding déposé » et « zéro problème trouvé ». Une review dont le canal de dépôt est cassé compte quand même comme terminée (outcome `answered`) et donc comme clean.

## Durcissement proposé
1. **Côté serveur** : quand `/api/mcp/submit-findings` rejette en 401 un appel dont le body référence une session de review connue/récente, tracer l'échec (activity log + notification) et marquer la review non fiable — elle ne doit pas compter pour `hasFreshCleanReview` ni pour le guard review→done.
2. **Pour les providers MCP-capables** (claude-code, codex, omp une fois le canal réparé) : une review ne compte comme « clean » que si elle a soumis un verdict structuré via `submit_findings` (`approved` / `approved_with_minor_issues`). Le fallback prose de lib/pipeline/findings.ts reste réservé aux providers sans MCP (gemini-cli…), sa raison d'être documentée.
3. Exposer l'état « review non vérifiable » dans l'UI de la colonne Review (raison bloquante), en cohérence avec l'epic E-arij-126 (section « Prêt à merger »).

## Fichiers clés
lib/pipeline/findings.ts (assessReviewOutcome / resolveReviewVerdict), lib/workflow/engine.ts (guards →done), lib/auto-mode/select.ts (hasFreshCleanReview), app/api/mcp/submit-findings/route.ts.

## Critères d'acceptation
- Une review claude-code/codex/omp terminée SANS verdict structuré ne rend pas l'epic mergeable.
- Un 401 sur submit_findings pendant une review produit une notification visible et une entrée d'activity log sur le ticket.
- Les providers sans MCP conservent le comportement prose actuel (non-régression, tests findings.ts).

epics.title: Merge (auto et manuel) passe l'epic en done sans cascader les user stories
epics.description:
## Symptôme
Epic « Providers Documentation » (Arij Front) : statut `done` après merge, mais ses 3 user stories sont restées en `review` pour toujours (0 US done sur un ticket done, cercles vides dans le détail).

## Cause
La cascade stories review→done n'existe que sur la route **approve** (app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/approve/route.ts:288-296). Les chemins **merge** ne la font pas :
- auto-merge : `finalizeMergedEpic` (lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:149-190) transitionne l'epic seul ;
- route merge manuelle : idem, aucune écriture user_stories.

## Fix proposé
1. Factoriser la cascade stories (review→done, via le transition service, une entrée de log par story) dans un helper partagé, appelé par approve, par la route merge et par `finalizeMergedEpic` (y compris le chemin retryMergeAfterFix).
2. Ceinture-bretelles : le workflow engine refuse (ou corrige) une transition epic→done laissant des stories en review — à trancher à l'implémentation : refus strict casserait le rollback du merge auto, la cascade systématique est probablement le bon choix.
3. Réparation des données : script/migration ponctuelle pour les epics déjà done avec stories en review (au moins WwtYAgC2ezhu).
4. Au passage : quand le merge est déclenché par un humain via l'UI, l'activity log ne doit pas attribuer la transition à « Auto mode » (libellé AUTO_MODE_REASONS.merged utilisé quel que soit le déclencheur).

## Critères d'acceptation
- Après un merge (bouton UI ou auto-merge), toutes les stories en review passent done, avec entrées d'activity log par story.
- Les stories non-review (todo/in_progress) sont laissées telles quelles et signalées, comme le fait déjà approve.
- Les epics done existants avec stories en review sont réparés.
- L'attribution user vs auto du merge est correcte dans l'activity log.

epics.title: Merge en conflit : 500 au lieu de 409, et le reload HMR fait disparaître « Resolve with Agent »
epics.description:
## Symptôme
POST /epics/:id/merge sur un ticket dont la branche conflicte → réponse 500, la page se recharge toute seule, et le bouton « Resolve with Agent » n'apparaît jamais : impossible de dispatcher l'agent de résolution depuis l'UI. Reproduit sur E-arij-120 (10 fichiers en conflit avec main). Séquence observée dans les logs dev : POST merge 500 → « ✓ Compiled in 194ms » → re-GET de toute la page.

## Trois causes distinctes
1. **Sémantique HTTP** : le fallback de la route merge (app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/merge/route.ts:315-318) renvoie 500 pour N'IMPORTE QUEL échec, y compris un simple conflit — qui n'est pas une erreur serveur. La route approve, elle, répond 409 avec commentaire + notification + entrée d'activity log (« Approval blocked: … CONFLICTS: … »). La route merge n'écrit AUCUNE trace : après coup, rien en base ne dit qu'un merge a échoué.
2. **État éphémère** : `mergeError` (hooks/useEpicMutations.ts:23) est le SEUL chemin vers le bouton « Resolve with Agent » (components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicGitSection.tsx:252-270). C'est un state React : tout reload le perd, et l'option de résolution avec lui. L'état « conflit de merge en attente » doit être dérivé de données persistées (l'échec loggé au point 1), pour survivre au reload — et alimenter la « raison bloquante » des cartes Review (cohérence avec E-arij-126).
3. **Self-hosting** : `mergeWorktree` (lib/git/manager.ts:344) checkout main et merge DANS l'arbre vivant du repo. Quand le projet mergé est Arij lui-même, cet arbre est celui que le dev server sert : le merge conflictuel écrit puis restaure des dizaines de fichiers sources → tempête HMR → full reload Fast Refresh → perte de l'état du point 2. C'est le déclencheur du symptôme, et il se reproduira à chaque merge du projet Arij par Arij.

## Fix proposé
1. Conflit → 409 avec payload structuré (`{ error, reason: "conflict", conflictFiles }`) ; le client distingue conflit / vraie erreur. Persister l'échec : activity log + (comme approve) commentaire ou notification.
2. Dériver l'affichage « merge en conflit — Resolve with Agent » de l'échec persisté (dernier échec de merge postérieur au dernier commit de la branche), plus du state éphémère seul.
3. Détecter les conflits SANS toucher l'arbre vivant : `git merge-tree` (plumbing, zéro écriture) en pré-vol ; ne faire le vrai merge dans l'arbre que s'il est propre. Alternative : merger dans un worktree dédié de la branche par défaut. Bénéfice annexe : plus de fenêtre où le serveur sert des fichiers avec marqueurs de conflit.

## Critères d'acceptation
- Un merge en conflit répond 409 avec la liste des fichiers, et laisse une trace persistée (activity log au minimum).
- Après un reload de la page, un ticket dont le dernier merge a échoué affiche toujours l'erreur et le bouton « Resolve with Agent ».
- Tenter de merger un ticket du projet Arij (self-hosted) en conflit ne déclenche plus de rechargement de la page : aucun fichier de l'arbre vivant n'est modifié tant que le merge n'est pas propre.
- Non-régression : merge propre, branche manquante, marqueurs de conflit committés (reason "conflict-markers") gardent leur comportement.

epics.title: Chat CLI persistant : un process chaud par conversation (tac au tac sans API)
epics.description:
## Problème
Deux modes de chat aujourd'hui : l'API directe (rapide mais payante / GPU local) et le chat agent CLI (abonnement, mais chaque tour respawne un process `claude --print -p <msg>` avec --resume — lib/claude/spawn.ts:148 — donc plusieurs secondes de boot + config MCP + reprise de session avant le premier token).

## Solution
Un processus CLI **longue durée par conversation**, gardé chaud entre les tours : la latence retombe à l'inférence seule, et c'est l'abonnement qui paie. Le chat existant reste l'interface — pas de terminal, pas de TUI.

## Compatibilité providers (mesurée le 2026-08-25 sur les binaires installés)
- **claude-code** : natif — `claude --print --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages` ; messages utilisateur en JSON sur stdin, events streamés sur stdout. Cible V1.
- **oh-my-pi v17.2.1** : natif — `omp --mode rpc` émet immédiatement un handshake `{"type":"ready","protocolVersion":1,"supportedProtocolVersions":[1,2],"maxFrameBytes":1048576,...}` puis des events (available_commands_update, extension_ui_request…) : vrai mode d'embedding stdio, framé et versionné. Story dédiée (spike protocole d'envoi des messages user, puis adaptateur).
- **codex** : pas de mode persistant simple (`codex exec` = one-shot). Chemin : `codex app-server` (EXPÉRIMENTAL — daemon JSON-RPC, `proxy` stdio, `generate-ts` pour les bindings). Spike séparé, API instable.

## Architecture
- `lib/chat/persistent-runner.ts` : registre de processus par conversationId sur **globalThis** (pattern token-store — indispensable pour survivre au hot-reload dev), spawn lazy au premier message.
- Chaque tour : write d'un message JSON sur stdin, events streamés vers l'infra chunks/SSE existante.
- **Canal MCP par conversation** : le token chat (lib/chat/cli-tool-channel.ts) est minté à l'ouverture du process et révoqué à sa mort — plus un mint par tour.
- **Reaper** : kill après ~15 min d'inactivité + cap de N conversations chaudes simultanées (budget ~200-400 MB RAM par process). Auto-guérison : le tour suivant respawne avec `--resume <cliSessionId>` — couvre aussi le restart du dev server (seul le premier tour d'après coupure est lent).
- UI : badge « session chaude/froide », action « Restart session », le mode apparaît comme option de provider du chat.

## Hors périmètre
Le terminal interactif complet (tmux/node-pty/xterm.js) — feature séparée si le besoin persiste. Les permission prompts interactifs en boutons de chat — stretch ultérieur.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Pi + Oh My Pi ajoutés aux providers CLI

Commit `46eab87`. Suite complète verte (257 fichiers / 2544 tests), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Ce que sont réellement ces deux CLI

- **Pi** = `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, binaire `pi` — harness terminal minimal, headless via `--mode json`.
- **Oh My Pi** = paquet npm `oh-my-pi`, **extension de Pi**, pas un agent autonome : son binaire `oh-my-pi` ne fait que `doctor`/`init`/`version`. L'agent, c'est `pi` avec l'extension chargée (prompt système remplacé par un orchestrateur multi-agents).

Il est donc modélisé comme `pi … -e oh-my-pi`. `-e` résout les sources npm à la demande, donc ça marche que l'utilisateur ait fait `pi install oh-my-pi` ou non (réseau requis au premier run). La disponibilité se réduit à « `pi` est dans le PATH », comme pour Pi.

### Comportement des providers

| | Pi / Oh My Pi |
|---|---|
| Commande | `pi --mode json [--tools …] [--session <ID>] [--model <M>] [-e oh-my-pi] -p <prompt>` |
| plan / analyze | `--tools read,grep,find,ls` (pi n'a pas de système de permissions — la capacité passe par l'allowlist d'outils) |
| code | jeu d'outils par défaut (ajoute write, edit, bash) |
| Résultat | dernier `message_end` assistant — exactement ce que le mode texte de pi imprime — avec repli sur les tours précédents puis sur la sortie brute |
| Resume | `--session <ID>`, id pris dans l'en-tête `{"type":"session","id":…}` du flux |

**Point non évident :** en `--mode json`, pi sort avec le code 0 **même quand le run s'est terminé sur une erreur modèle** (seul son mode texte mappe ça sur exit 1). `handleExit()` déclasse donc le succès en se basant sur le `stopReason` du dernier tour, pas sur le code de sortie. Sans ça, un run raté serait enregistré comme réussi.

### Câblage

`ProviderType`, registre, `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` / `PROVIDER_LABELS` / `PROVIDER_TIERS` (Tier 2), `/api/providers/available`, `useProvidersAvailable`, classification resume. Les deux sont ajoutés **en fin** de `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` pour que la ségrégation reviewer/builder continue de choisir les mêmes alternatives qu'avant.

### Deux nettoyages au passage

- `normalizeProvider()` dans `agent-resolution.ts` était une chaîne de 9 `if` à maintenir en phase avec `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` → remplacée par `isAgentProvider()` (idiome déjà utilisé dans `named-agents.ts`).
- `AgentMonitor` étiquetait « CC » **tout** provider autre que Gemini/Codex — donc opencode, qwen, kimi… et maintenant Pi. Il retombe désormais sur `PROVIDER_LABELS` ; « CC » et « Gemini » restent inchangés.

### Vérification

35 tests unitaires dans `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts` (args, parsing du flux, extraction du session id, détection d'échec, cycle de spawn complet avec `child_process` mocké).

En plus des tests, j'ai fait tourner les arguments que le provider émet à travers le **vrai parseur de pi** (`dist/cli/args.js` du paquet publié) : aucun flag inconnu, aucun diagnostic, le prompt arrive bien dans `messages`.

**Limite documentée dans le code :** pi ne traite l'argument après `-p` comme prompt que s'il ne commence pas par `-`, et n'offre pas de séparateur `--`. Un prompt commençant par un tiret simple serait avalé comme option inconnue (run avec prompt vide). Inatteignable aujourd'hui — tous les prompts Arij sont composés par template et commencent par un titre — mais c'est noté dans `lib/providers/pi.ts`.

### Hors périmètre

Le chat streaming (`/chat/stream`, `/sessions/resumable`) restreint déjà les providers à claude-code / gemini-cli / codex par une allowlist en dur, antérieure à ce ticket. Je ne l'ai pas élargie : c'est une décision produit séparée. MCP reste limité à claude-code / codex — pi n'a pas de support MCP natif (uniquement via un adaptateur tiers).

comments.content:
Done — commit `46eab87`, ticket moved to review.

## What I found first

The ticket had no user stories, so I researched what these CLIs actually are before writing code. The important discovery:

**Oh My Pi is not an agent CLI.** It's an npm *extension* for Pi — its own `oh-my-pi` binary only does `doctor`/`init`/`version`. The agent is `pi` with the extension loaded, which swaps Pi's system prompt for a multi-agent orchestrator. So it's modelled as `pi … -e oh-my-pi`, not as a separate binary.

**Pi** is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (binary `pi`), headless via `--mode json`.

## Implementation

`lib/providers/pi.ts` + `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts` (the latter extends the former, adding `-e oh-my-pi`):

- **Mode mapping** — Pi has no permission system, so capability rides on the tool allowlist: plan/analyze get `--tools read,grep,find,ls`; code keeps the default set.
- **Result** — last assistant `message_end`, which is exactly what Pi's own text mode prints.
- **Resume** — `--session <ID>` from the stream's session header.

One non-obvious thing worth flagging: **in `--mode json`, Pi exits 0 even when the run ended on a model error** — only its text mode maps that to exit 1. `handleExit()` therefore downgrades success based on the final turn's `stopReason`. Without that, failed runs would be recorded as successful.

Wiring covers `ProviderType`, the registry, `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`/`LABELS`/`TIERS`, the availability route, the client hook, and resume classification. Both are appended at the end of `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` so reviewer/builder segregation keeps picking the same alternatives as before.

## Verification

35 new tests in `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts`; full suite 2544 tests passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Beyond the tests, I ran the args my provider emits through **Pi's real parser** from the published package — no unknown flags, no diagnostics, prompt lands in `messages`.

That exercise turned up a caveat I documented in the code: Pi only treats the argument after `-p` as the prompt if it doesn't start with `-`, and offers no `--` separator. Unreachable today (all Arij prompts are template-composed and start with a heading), but a leading-dash prompt would be silently dropped.

## Tests

`it.each(["pi","oh-my-pi"])` asserting the conversation runs on its own provider, `spawnClaudeStream` is never called, and no id is minted; plus codex single-spawn and the gemini fallback. Confirmed the Pi cases fail against the old allowlist.

## Across the four rounds

The epic surfaced that session-continuity capability was scattered across diverging inline lists in roughly fifteen files. It now lives in `lib/agent-sessions/resume-capability.ts` as three distinct questions, with every dispatch site giving the same answer. The codex inconsistencies weren't introduced here — they'd been latent since February; adding Pi made them reachable.

epics.title: Direct Chat via OpenAI-Compatible API (Fast Mode)
epics.description:
Add a new 'OpenAI-compatible' provider to the chat provider dropdown (per-conversation selection, alongside the existing CLI providers). When selected, chat messages bypass the CLI agents entirely and go straight to the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint ({base_url}/chat/completions) with stream: true, giving real token-by-token SSE streaming — the responsiveness win over today's non-streaming CLI path where non-Claude providers reply as a single end-of-call block. Epic-creation and brainstorm conversations stay agent-only.

Implementation plan:
1. Settings (no migration — the generic settings KV table is reused): keys openai_base_url, openai_api_key, openai_model, openai_reasoning_effort (off|low|medium|high, default off). New lib/openai/ module: constants.ts (key names, client-safe, no db import — same convention as lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts) and client.ts (getOpenAiConfigFromSettings(), testConnection(), streamChatCompletion() with SSE parsing).
2. app/api/settings/route.ts: mask openai_api_key in GET following the existing github_pat pattern ({ hasToken: boolean }) — the key is never returned in plaintext.
3. New POST /api/settings/openai/test route (mirrors the /api/settings/github/validate pattern): reads the saved config server-side, performs a minimal non-streaming chat completion, returns success (model name) or a readable error (invalid URL, 401, timeout, connection refused). The API key never round-trips to the client.
4. lib/agent-config/constants.ts: register 'openai-compatible' in PROVIDER_LABELS / isAgentProvider so conversation create/update routes and the chat dropdown accept it; mark it as non-eligible for epic-creation and brainstorm conversation types.
5. app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts: dedicated HTTP branch ahead of the CLI branches when the resolved provider is openai-compatible — build a proper messages array (system prompt from resolveAgentPrompt('chat', projectId) + last 20 messages + current user message) instead of the single inlined prompt string, POST with stream: true, parse SSE chunks (data: lines, [DONE]) and emit real delta events, include reasoning_effort in the body only when not off, send Authorization: Bearer only when a key is configured, reuse the existing assistant-message persistence and conversation-status transitions. Backstops: 400 when the conversation type is epic creation/brainstorm, 400 when attachmentIds are present (images unsupported in this mode). No resume-session logic for this provider — history travels in the messages array.
6. UI: components/chat/ provider dropdown lists 'OpenAI-compatible' (hidden for epic/brainstorm conversations; a named-agent selection still takes precedence when set, existing behavior); the image-attachment button is disabled in this mode. app/settings/page.tsx gains an 'OpenAI-compatible API' section: Base URL (required), API key (password input, optional for local servers), Model (required), Reasoning select, Save + Test connection buttons with inline success/error feedback.
7. Constraints: no new npm dependencies (native fetch + hand-rolled SSE parsing), zero modifications to the existing CLI providers, the API key lives only in SQLite (never on disk, in .git/config, or in logs), Claude-based title generation unchanged.
