comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Review finding F1 resolved — `44c761c`

The reviewer was right: returning `branch` inside a 501 body is not "forwarded to the clone service", and the test asserting `json.data.branch` proved nothing — it only re-read a value the route had just written.

**What changed**

`lib/git/clone.ts` (new) defines the contract between this epic's parsing layer and the clone service:

- `CloneGitHubRepoOptions` takes an already-validated `ParsedGitHubRepoInput` plus the optional branch, so the git layer is structurally incapable of receiving an owner/repo pair that skipped `parseGitHubRepoInput()`.
- `CloneGitHubRepoResult` matches the `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` shape from spec §4.2.
- `cloneGitHubRepo()` throws `CloneServiceUnavailableError` until epic `drG2ZnRFKHeC` fills in the body.

`POST /api/projects/clone` now calls the service and returns its result (200), mapping `CloneServiceUnavailableError` to 501. This also shrinks the merge surface I flagged earlier: the clone epic replaces **one function body**, not the route.

**One thing I added beyond the finding:** an unexpected git error now returns a generic 500 instead of `e.message`. A raw git failure can echo back the `http.extraHeader` `Authorization: Basic …` value, and the redaction helper from spec §4.4 lands with the clone epic — so until then nothing from the git layer reaches the client. There's a test asserting the 500 body contains neither `Basic` nor `Authorization`.

**Tests** (16 → 18): exact forwarded arguments and a 200 with the service result; `branch` forwarded as `"develop"` and as `null` when omitted; schema rejections, non-GitHub hosts and traversal attempts never reach the service; the 501 and the non-leaking 500.

I checked these aren't vacuous by mutation — hardcoding `branch: null` in the route fails the forwarding test, and restoring it passes. The old assertion would have survived that mutation, which is exactly the gap the review caught.

**Verification:** 2501 tests / 253 files green, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on all epic files. (The 45 pre-existing eslint errors elsewhere in the repo are untouched by this branch.)

**Minor note, not fixed by design:** the `owner/repo` shorthand rule means a two-segment paste like `gitlab.com/repo` parses as owner `gitlab.com`, and fails later at clone time with a 404 rather than up front as "not a GitHub URL". Three-segment `gitlab.com/owner/repo` is correctly rejected. Adding a host-like heuristic risks rejecting legitimate owners, so I left the explicit "`owner/repo` shorthand parses" criterion to win. Say the word if you'd rather trade that off.

epics.title: Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor
epics.description:
## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## Réutilisation (ne rien réécrire)

| Besoin | Existant | Chemin |
|---|---|---|
| Dispatch build/review programmatique | `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage({stage})` — « réplique les closures des routes au byte près pour que le board ne puisse pas distinguer une étape de pipeline d'un dispatch humain ». Supporte `scope: 'epic' \| 'story'`. | `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:140` |
| Primitive de merge | `mergeWorktree(gitRepoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` → `{merged, commitHash, error}` | `lib/git/manager.ts` |
| Porte « la review est OK » | Les gardes `→ done` du moteur de workflow | `lib/workflow/engine.ts:49-97` |
| Transition validée + event + log | `applyTransition({... source:'merge'})` | `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:47` |
| « Un agent est-il déjà sur ce ticket ? » | `getRunningSessionForTarget(target)` — compte `queued` + `running` | `lib/agents/concurrency.ts:94` |
| « Ce ticket attend-il un humain ? » | `isAwaitingReply(signal)` — pur, client-safe | `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:30` |
| Budget de slots + file FIFO | `agentScheduler.submit(projectId, sessionId, launch)` | `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:124` |
| Patron de boucle permanente | Watchdog : singleton globalThis, `start()` idempotent, interval `unref()`, `sweep(now)` pur pour les tests | `lib/agents/watchdog.ts` |
| Patron de registre mémoire | `NightRunRegistry` — map active + ring récent, pas de table | `lib/night/registry.ts` |
| Convention constantes client-safe | clé + fn clé par projet + défaut + `parseX` renvoyant `null` pour tomber au niveau suivant | `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` |
| Wiring au boot | `register()` dans `instrumentation.ts` (démarre déjà le watchdog) | `instrumentation.ts` |
| UI sélecteur agent + concurrence | `NightRunDialog` compose déjà `NamedAgentSelect` + `Input` de concurrence + `OptionRow` | `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx` |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

## Plan d'implémentation

Aucune migration. Toute la config vit dans la table clé/valeur `settings` existante et chaque session dispatchée est une ligne `agent_sessions` ordinaire.

1. `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` (client-safe, sans import `db`) — clés par projet avec repli global : `auto_mode_enabled:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency:<projectId>`. Plus `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2`, `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`, `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, parsers renvoyant `null`, `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` pour l'UI, chaînes de raison d'activity-log préfixées `"Auto mode "`, et `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` pour tamponner `batchRunId`.
2. `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` — résolveur serveur par projet → global → défaut, copie de `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject`.
3. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` — les trois sélecteurs (build, review, merge) avec toutes les exclusions.
4. `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` — état mémoire globalThis + map de parking.
5. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` — `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`.
6. `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` — le sweep avec mutex par projet.
7. Extension du driver : ajouter `reviewNamedAgentId` optionnel à `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
8. `instrumentation.ts` — `startAutoMode()` + chaînage du hook terminal.
9. `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts` — GET/PUT.
10. `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx` + toggle dans la toolbar du board.

## Hors périmètre

Reviews par story (les stories sont des unités de travail, les epics des unités d'intégration), switch global multi-projets, table persistée pour l'état du mode, planification horaire (le mode est ON/OFF, pas « de 22h à 6h »).

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want auto-mode configuration stored in the settings table with a client-safe constants module, so that I can enable the mode per project and tune agents and concurrency without a schema migration
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` following the exact convention established by `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` and `lib/pipeline/constants.ts`: a header comment explaining why the file is split, the global setting key, a `<key>:<projectId>` per-project override function, defaults with an inclusive clamp range, and a `parseX` returning `null` for "not configured" so callers fall through the chain. The five keys are `auto_mode_enabled`, `auto_mode_build_agent`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency`, `auto_mode_review_agent`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency`. Also export `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"`, an `AUTO_MODE_REASONS` object mirroring `PIPELINE_REASONS`, and a client-side `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` for the dialog. comments.content:
**Full Auto Mode implemented — all 7 user stories, 7 commits, tests green.**

`lib/auto-mode/` (new): `constants.ts` (client-safe, 5 settings keys + parsers + clamps + reasons), `config.ts` (project → global → default resolver, re-read per sweep), `select.ts` (3 selectors, one 9-query board snapshot, no N+1), `registry.ts` (globalThis state: in-flight map, per-project mutex, parking, recent ring), `merge.ts` (`tryAutoMerge`), `engine.ts` (the sweep + timer + kicks), `status.ts` (type-only API contract).

Plus: `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts`, `components/auto-mode/{AutoModeDialog,AutoModeToggle}.tsx`, board toolbar wiring, composed terminal hook in `instrumentation.ts`, and an additive `reviewNamedAgentId` on `PipelineStageDriverInit`.

**No migration** — `lib/db/migrations/` untouched, all config in the `settings` table.

The four hazards, as implemented:
1. *Infinite re-review* — temporal guard (no terminal review newer than the last terminal code session), not verdict-based.
2. *Bulldozing a question* — `isAwaitingReply` excludes the ticket until the user comments.
3. *Merging something unapproved* — no new boolean; `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` is the gate, guards validated **before** git runs so a merge can't land on main while the ticket refuses to move. `POST .../approve` is never called.
4. *Double-counted budgets* — own admission control; the dialog warns when N+M > `agent_max_concurrent` and never raises it.

Two deviations worth flagging, both deliberate:
- The merge pre-flights the workflow guards with `validateOnly` before `mergeWorktree` (the story described merge-then-transition, which is the human route's order — unattended that risks main and the board disagreeing).
- Parking counts failed *sessions*, not only failed dispatches; otherwise a permanently broken build would loop forever since a failed build leaves the epic in `in_progress`.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run` → 268 files / 2712 tests passing (139 new). Typecheck clean; new modules lint clean.

`npm run build` fails at the static-prerender step (`/_global-error`, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')`) — **this reproduces identically on the unmodified tree at HEAD**, so it is pre-existing and not caused by this work. Compilation itself succeeds ("Compiled successfully").

Note: this worktree had no `node_modules`; I hardlinked a copy from the main checkout so tests could run (gitignored).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

Note: I could not file structured Arij MCP findings because the MCP call was rejected by the current approval policy (`never`). Review was performed from the working tree, with delegated read-only subreviews.

## Findings

### 1. Critical
**Location:** `instrumentation.ts:58`  
**Description:** The terminal hook kicks auto-mode synchronously from `markSessionTerminal`, before pipeline/merge closures finish their ticket updates. A successful build can be picked up again before it moves to `review`; a negative review can be merged before `finalizeReviewSession` moves it back to `in_progress`.  
**Recommendation:** Trigger auto-mode only after the full session finalization path completes, or defer the kick from an explicit post-finalize hook.

### 2. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:266`  
**Description:** Merge-conflict recovery dispatches an agent into `worktreePath`, but `mergeWorktree` removes that worktree before attempting the merge (`lib/git/manager.ts:95`). The merge-fix agent can start in a missing cwd.  
**Recommendation:** Keep/recreate the worktree before dispatching the merge-fix agent, or use a helper that leaves the conflicted worktree intact.

### 3. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:370`  
**Description:** Merge-fix sessions are dispatched before checking build-budget capacity, then “charged” afterward. With `buildConcurrency = 0`, or multiple merge conflicts, auto-mode can exceed its own build cap.  
**Recommendation:** Gate conflict-agent dispatch on available build capacity before launching it.

### 4. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:505`  
**Description:** `needsReview` treats failed/cancelled review sessions as fresh terminal reviews. A failed review leaves the epic in `review`, but then it is neither reviewed again nor mergeable, so parking never triggers.  
**Recommendation:** Let failed/cancelled review sessions remain review candidates until they complete successfully or hit the parking threshold.

### 5. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:518`  
**Description:** Merge freshness accepts any completed review session, including `asked_question` or `silent`. After the user answers a review question, the epic can become mergeable without a clean review verdict.  
**Recommendation:** Require an acceptable structured outcome, or introduce a real clean-review signal before auto-merge.

### 6. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:276`  
**Description:** Epic review facts aggregate story-scoped review sessions because they group only by `epicId`. A completed story review can satisfy the epic-level merge gate, despite the design requiring review/merge to be epic-scoped.  
**Recommendation:** Exclude `userStoryId IS NOT NULL` from epic review facts; keep story sessions only for code-change freshness where appropriate.

### 7. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:310`  
**Description:** Epic awaiting-reply facts also rank story-scoped sessions, but compare only epic-level user comments. A story question can keep the parent epic blocked even after the user replies on the story.  
**Recommendation:** Build epic awaiting facts from epic-scoped sessions only, or match story questions to story replies.

### 8. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:461`  
**Description:** A merge-fix session that succeeds but whose retry fails parks the epic, but the completed session remains in auto-mode’s in-flight map. The next reconcile can clear the failure streak and unpark it.  
**Recommendation:** Remove merge-fix sessions from in-flight before parking, or preserve unresolved merge-conflict parks during reconcile.

### 9. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/config.ts:81`  
**Description:** `resolveAutoModeConfigForProject` can return `enabled: true` from the global key, while `listAutoModeEnabledProjectIds` only sweeps per-project enabled keys. UI/API can say enabled while the supervisor never runs.  
**Recommendation:** Make enabled strictly per-project or make sweep discovery honor the same fallback semantics.

### 10. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts:283`  
**Description:** `AUTO_MODE_REASONS.merged` is `"Auto mode: ..."`, which does not match `AUTO_MODE_REASON_PREFIX = "Auto mode "`. `isAutoModeActivityReason` misses successful auto-merge activity.  
**Recommendation:** Align the reason prefix or update the predicate/tests to cover this expected string.

### 11. Minor
**Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts:187`  
**Description:** PUT returns status before `kickAutoMode`, so runtime fields like `running`, `inFlight`, and `lastSweepAt` can be stale immediately after enable/disable.  
**Recommendation:** Mirror registry enablement before building the response, or return status after a synchronous state update.

### 12. Minor
**Location:** `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx:131`  
**Description:** The dialog load path does not check `res.ok`; a 404/500 JSON error can leave default/stale state with Save enabled.  
**Recommendation:** Treat non-2xx or missing `data` as a load error and disable save until valid status is loaded.

## Checklist Coverage

- **Readability:** No issues found.
- **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
- **Error Handling:** Findings 1, 2, 8, 12.
- **Performance:** No issues found.
- **Naming Conventions:** Finding 10.
- **Type Safety:** No issues found.
- **Testing:** Missing coverage for Findings 1-8, especially real merge-conflict worktree behavior and failed review retries.
- **API Design:** Findings 9, 11, 12.

## Summary

Critical: 1  
Major: 7  
Minor: 4  
Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Review findings fixed — all 12, one commit (`65f5830`). 2737 tests passing.**

I verified each finding against the code before changing anything; all 12 were real.

**[critical] Terminal-hook race.** Confirmed and worse than described. `markSessionTerminal` fires the hook synchronously, and `sweepProject` runs its board load + merge selection synchronously too — so the sweep ran entirely *before* `finalizeReviewSession`. An epic whose review had just come back negative still looked clean (in `review`, completed reviewer newer than the build, zero open findings) and got **merged into main**. Kicks are now debounced 250 ms onto a later macrotask. `__tests__/auto-mode-e2e.test.ts` reproduces the exact `markSessionTerminal` → revert ordering; I confirmed it fails when I temporarily restore the synchronous kick.

**[major] Merge-fix worktree.** Confirmed — `mergeWorktree` removes the worktree at `manager.ts:95` before merging, and the conflict path aborts without restoring it, so the agent got a deleted cwd. The branch survives (deletion only happens after a successful merge), so the conflict path now re-attaches with `createWorktree`.

**[major] Conflict-agent budget.** Now gated: the engine passes `dispatchConflictAgent` from free build capacity; `buildConcurrency: 0` dispatches none.

**[major] Failed reviews.** Confirmed a hard deadlock — a failed review was neither re-reviewable nor mergeable, and couldn't even reach the parking threshold. Only *completed* reviews count as an attempt now.

**[major] `asked_question` / `silent` satisfying the merge gate.** Split into two signals: `lastReviewAttemptAt` (blocks re-review) and `lastCleanReviewAt` (satisfies merge). `silent` blocks re-review but never approves — re-dispatching a reviewer that says nothing would just burn tokens.

**[major] Story sessions at epic level** (findings 6 + 7). Review and awaiting-reply facts are epic-scoped now. Story *builds* still count as code changes (same branch). A story question is answered by a comment on either thread, since the notification deep-links to the epic.

**[major] Un-parking a merge conflict.** Confirmed: the merge-fix agent completes *successfully* before its retry fails, so reconcile credited it and cleared the park → infinite loop. Merge-conflict parks are now **hard** — immune to `clearFailures`, reversed only by `unpark` or toggling the mode.

**Minors 9–12** all fixed: discovery honours the resolver's fallback chain; `isAutoModeActivityReason` matches the colon form (`Auto mode: review clean, merged` was being dropped from the feed); PUT mirrors the flag into the registry before responding; the dialog checks `res.ok` and disables Save on a failed load.

Also hardened beyond the findings: `finalizeMergedEpic` re-reads the epic status after the merge instead of validating against a snapshot taken seconds earlier — `mergeWorktree` is slow enough for a human to act during it.

**Verification:** 268 files / 2737 tests passing (25 new). Typecheck and lint clean on all touched modules. Docs updated with the new review-outcome table, the kick-deferral rationale, and the hard-park semantics.

comments.content:
All 12 findings are fixed in commit `65f5830`. I verified each against the code first — all were real.

## The critical one was worse than reported

`markSessionTerminal` fires the hook synchronously, and `sweepProject` also runs its board load and merge selection synchronously — so the whole sweep completed *before* `finalizeReviewSession`. An epic whose review had just come back negative still looked clean (in `review`, completed reviewer newer than the build, zero open findings) and **got merged into main**.

Kicks are now debounced 250 ms onto a later macrotask. I wrote a regression test reproducing the exact `markSessionTerminal` → revert ordering, then temporarily restored the synchronous kick to confirm the test fails without the fix — it does.

## The other majors

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Merge-fix worktree | Confirmed — `mergeWorktree` deletes the worktree *before* merging. The branch survives, so the conflict path re-attaches with `createWorktree`. |
| Conflict-agent budget | Engine passes `dispatchConflictAgent` from free build capacity; `buildConcurrency: 0` dispatches none. |
| Failed reviews | Confirmed a hard deadlock — never re-reviewed, never mergeable, couldn't even reach the parking threshold. Only completed reviews count as an attempt. |
| `asked_question`/`silent` merging | Split into `lastReviewAttemptAt` (blocks re-review) and `lastCleanReviewAt` (satisfies merge). `silent` blocks re-review but never approves. |
| Story sessions at epic level (6+7) | Review and awaiting facts are epic-scoped. Story *builds* still count as code changes; a story question is answered from either thread. |
| Un-parking a merge conflict | Confirmed — the merge-fix agent completes *successfully* before its retry fails, so reconcile credited it and looped forever. Merge-conflict parks are now **hard**. |

All four minors fixed too. Beyond the findings, I hardened `finalizeMergedEpic` to re-read the epic status after the merge rather than validating against a snapshot taken seconds earlier — `mergeWorktree` is slow enough for a human to act during it.

**Verification:** 268 files / 2737 tests passing (25 new). Typecheck and lint clean. Docs updated with the review-outcome table, the kick-deferral rationale, and the hard-park semantics.

**Second review round fixed — all 14, one commit (`ec4b6b4`). 2764 tests passing (269 files).**

Verified each finding against the code first; all 14 were real.

**[critical] Merge mutates main before revalidation.** This was the residual window I flagged last round, and the reviewer is right that logging it isn't enough. `tryAutoMerge` now captures a rollback checkpoint (main + branch tips) *before* git runs; when the post-merge guard refuses, `rollbackMerge` resets main and restores the branch. Unattended, "we changed main and then found out we shouldn't have" has to be recoverable — nobody is watching.

**[major] PUT partial writes.** `{enabled: true, buildConcurrency: "lots"}` armed the supervisor *and* returned 400. Whole payload parsed first, written in one transaction.

**[major] Build target not revalidated.** Confirmed — only reviews had a last-moment status check. Build dispatch now validates the target status, and story scope additionally checks the parent epic (`checkGuards` reports the *story's* status for those, so the epic needs its own read).

**[major] Merge-fix terminal-before-retry.** Confirmed and nasty: the session goes terminal (firing the kick) while `retryMergeAfterFix` is still awaiting git. An epic now holds a **merge lock** from the first git command until the retry settles; the selectors exclude locked epics entirely.

**[major] `enabled` read once per sweep.** Re-read before every merge and every dispatch — "off" now means off *now*.

**[major] Merge attempted without repair capacity.** Confirmed: it tore the worktree down every 15s forever. The worktree is restored and the epic's merge deferred 5 minutes.

**[major] `mergeWorktree` over-broad try.** Split at the point of no return: once `git merge` succeeds, main *has* changed, so a failed `git log` or branch delete no longer reports `merged: false` (which would have sent callers off to "fix" a merge that already landed). This also fixes the same latent bug in the human merge route.

**[major] Every failure treated as a conflict.** Failures now carry `reason: 'conflict' | 'branch-missing' | 'error'`; only a real conflict earns an agent.

**[major] Branch name re-derived from the title.** New `attachWorktree(repo, branchName)` binds to the exact stored branch.

**[major] Findings 10 + 11 together.** They pulled in opposite directions — excluding `silent` from clean-reviews while counting it as an attempt was the deadlock, and requiring `answered` would have made NULL rows deadlock the same way. So the two signals collapse into **one**: a review is a completed, epic-scoped session with `outcome = 'answered'`. Everything else re-reviews, bounded by the parking ladder — and silent reviews are charged as failures, so three park the epic. `needsReview` is now literally `!hasFreshCleanReview`, which makes "reviewed exactly once, then merged" true by construction.

**Minors 12–14:** guard refusals log `"Auto mode skipped …"` instead of vanishing; `NamedAgentSelect` accepts `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` and the dialog passes both; dialog errors carry `role="alert"`.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

Note: Arij MCP `submit_findings` was attempted, but rejected by the current approval policy (`never`), so findings were not filed structurally. This was a source review; I did not rerun the full test suite.

## Findings

### 1. Critical
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:718`  
**Description:** The merge-conflict retry path calls `mergeWorktree` without the preflight/checkpoint/rollback protection used by the clean merge path. If the retry lands on `main` and `finalizeMergedEpic` then refuses, `main` stays changed while the ticket is parked outside `done`.  
**Recommendation:** Preflight again before retry, capture a retry checkpoint, and roll back/restoring the branch on post-retry guard refusal.

### 2. Critical
**Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:173`  
**Description:** `rollbackMerge` resets the integration branch to the captured `mainHead` unconditionally. If `main` advanced after the checkpoint, rollback can discard unrelated commits.  
**Recommendation:** Serialize repo-level merge/rollback work, or verify current `HEAD` is exactly the auto-merge commit being undone before resetting.

### 3. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:351`  
**Description:** Auto mode proceeds even when `captureMergeCheckpoint` returns `null`. If the post-merge guard refuses, there is no undo path.  
**Recommendation:** Treat missing checkpoint capture as a pre-merge skip/failure for unattended auto-merge.

### 4. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:356`  
**Description:** `tryAutoMerge` does not do a last-moment active-session/status recheck before `mergeWorktree` removes the worktree and checks out `main`. A stale merge candidate can race with manual work.  
**Recommendation:** Re-read target status and `getRunningSessionForTarget` immediately before mutating git.

### 5. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:569`  
**Description:** The merge lock is released only after `retryMergeAfterFix`. If the scheduled launch closure throws before that point, the scheduler marks the session failed while the auto-mode merge lock remains forever.  
**Recommendation:** Wrap the entire scheduled launch closure in `try/finally` and always call `endMergeWork`.

### 6. Major
**Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:237`  
**Description:** Every `git merge` rejection is classified as `reason: "conflict"`. Non-conflict errors can incorrectly dispatch a merge-fix agent.  
**Recommendation:** Inspect `git status().conflicted`; return `reason: "error"` when no real conflict exists.

### 7. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts:147`  
**Description:** `setEnabled(projectId, false)` deletes all project state, including sweep and merge locks. Disable/re-enable during in-flight work can erase the mutex and allow overlapping sweeps/merges.  
**Recommendation:** Preserve active locks with a disabled/generation marker, then clear runtime state after active work releases.

### 8. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:168`  
**Description:** Auto-mode review dispatch allows `targetStatus === "done"`. A stale review candidate can still dispatch after a human approves it, and review finalization may move the completed ticket back to `in_progress`.  
**Recommendation:** Require `targetStatus === "review"` for auto-mode review dispatch.

### 9. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:673`  
**Description:** After `await deps.dispatch(...)`, the engine records the session in-flight without checking whether auto mode was disabled during the await.  
**Recommendation:** Re-check enabled state or a registry generation before mutating registry state.

### 10. Major
**Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts:158`  
**Description:** `buildAgent` / `reviewAgent` accept arbitrary or deleted string IDs, so status can report an agent that dispatch later does not honor.  
**Recommendation:** Validate string IDs against `named_agents`; reject invalid non-null IDs.

### 11. Major
**Location:** `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx:156`  
**Description:** Invalid or empty concurrency input is coerced to defaults before save, so clearing the field can overwrite stored budgets with `2` / `1`.  
**Recommendation:** Treat `null` parse results as invalid UI state and disable Save.

### 12. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:462`  
**Description:** `storyRows.find(...)` runs once per latest story session, making board loading O(stories × storySessions).  
**Recommendation:** Build a `Map<storyId, story>` while processing `storyRows`.

## Checklist Coverage

- **Readability:** No issues found.
- **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
- **Error Handling:** Findings 1-7, 9.
- **Performance:** Finding 12.
- **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
- **Type Safety:** No issues found.
- **Testing:** Missing coverage for findings 1-9 and the invalid UI/API inputs in findings 10-11.
- **API Design:** Finding 10.

## Summary

Critical: 2  
Major: 9  
Minor: 1  
Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

## Epic to Implement

### Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor

## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## Réutilisation (ne rien réécrire)

| Besoin | Existant | Chemin |
|---|---|---|
| Dispatch build/review programmatique | `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage({stage})` — « réplique les closures des routes au byte près pour que le board ne puisse pas distinguer une étape de pipeline d'un dispatch humain ». Supporte `scope: 'epic' \| 'story'`. | `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:140` |
| Primitive de merge | `mergeWorktree(gitRepoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` → `{merged, commitHash, error}` | `lib/git/manager.ts` |
| Porte « la review est OK » | Les gardes `→ done` du moteur de workflow | `lib/workflow/engine.ts:49-97` |
| Transition validée + event + log | `applyTransition({... source:'merge'})` | `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:47` |
| « Un agent est-il déjà sur ce ticket ? » | `getRunningSessionForTarget(target)` — compte `queued` + `running` | `lib/agents/concurrency.ts:94` |
| « Ce ticket attend-il un humain ? » | `isAwaitingReply(signal)` — pur, client-safe | `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:30` |
| Budget de slots + file FIFO | `agentScheduler.submit(projectId, sessionId, launch)` | `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:124` |
| Patron de boucle permanente | Watchdog : singleton globalThis, `start()` idempotent, interval `unref()`, `sweep(now)` pur pour les tests | `lib/agents/watchdog.ts` |
| Patron de registre mémoire | `NightRunRegistry` — map active + ring récent, pas de table | `lib/night/registry.ts` |
| Convention constantes client-safe | clé + fn clé par projet + défaut + `parseX` renvoyant `null` pour tomber au niveau suivant | `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` |
| Wiring au boot | `register()` dans `instrumentation.ts` (démarre déjà le watchdog) | `instrumentation.ts` |
| UI sélecteur agent + concurrence | `NightRunDialog` compose déjà `NamedAgentSelect` + `Input` de concurrence + `OptionRow` | `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx` |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

## Plan d'implémentation

Aucune migration. Toute la config vit dans la table clé/valeur `settings` existante et chaque session dispatchée est une ligne `agent_sessions` ordinaire.

1. `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` (client-safe, sans import `db`) — clés par projet avec repli global : `auto_mode_enabled:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency:<projectId>`. Plus `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2`, `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`, `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, parsers renvoyant `null`, `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` pour l'UI, chaînes de raison d'activity-log préfixées `"Auto mode "`, et `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` pour tamponner `batchRunId`.
2. `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` — résolveur serveur par projet → global → défaut, copie de `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject`.
3. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` — les trois sélecteurs (build, review, merge) avec toutes les exclusions.
4. `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` — état mémoire globalThis + map de parking.
5. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` — `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`.
6. `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` — le sweep avec mutex par projet.
7. Extension du driver : ajouter `reviewNamedAgentId` optionnel à `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
8. `instrumentation.ts` — `startAutoMode()` + chaînage du hook terminal.
9. `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts` — GET/PUT.
10. `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx` + toggle dans la toolbar du board.

## Hors périmètre

Reviews par story (les stories sont des unités de travail, les epics des unités d'intégration), switch global multi-projets, table persistée pour l'état du mode, planification horaire (le mode est ON/OFF, pas « de 22h à 6h »).

129:export async function PUT(
130:  request: NextRequest,
131:  { params }: { params: Promise<{ projectId: string }> }
132:) {
133:  const { projectId } = await params;
134:
135:  const found = getProjectOr404(projectId);
136:  if (isErrorResponse(found)) return found;
137:
138:  const body = await request.json().catch(() => null);
139:  if (!body || typeof body !== "object") {
140:    return NextResponse.json(
141:      { error: "Invalid payload. Send a JSON object of auto mode settings." },
142:      { status: 400 }
143:    );
144:  }
145:
146:  const payload = body as Record<string, unknown>;
147:
148:  // Every field is optional so the dialog can toggle the switch without
149:  // resending the whole form. Values go through the same parsers the resolver
150:  // uses, so a clamp applies at write time as well as read time.
151:  //
152:  // The whole payload is validated into `writes` BEFORE anything is
153:  // persisted. Validating as we went would let `{enabled: true,
154:  // buildConcurrency: "lots"}` arm the mode and then return 400 — the caller
155:  // would believe nothing happened while a supervisor started dispatching.
156:  const writes: Array<[string, unknown]> = [];
157:
158:  if ("enabled" in payload) {
159:    const enabled = parseAutoModeEnabled(payload.enabled);
160:    if (enabled === null) {
161:      return NextResponse.json(
162:        { error: "`enabled` must be a boolean." },
163:        { status: 400 }
164:      );
165:    }
166:    writes.push([autoModeEnabledSettingKey(projectId), enabled]);
167:  }
168:
169:  // A named-agent id is only useful if it still resolves to a row. Writing an
170:  // unknown or since-deleted id would have the status endpoint report an agent
171:  // that dispatch quietly ignores — the mode would run for hours with a
172:  // provider the user never chose. `null` stays valid: it means "use the
173:  // normal resolution chain".
174:  for (const field of ["buildAgent", "reviewAgent"] as const) {
175:    if (!(field in payload)) continue;
176:    const agentId = parseAutoModeAgent(payload[field]);
177:    if (agentId !== null && !namedAgentExists(agentId)) {
178:      return NextResponse.json(
179:        { error: `\`${field}\` is not a known named agent.` },
180:        { status: 400 }
181:      );
182:    }
183:    writes.push([
184:      field === "buildAgent"
185:        ? autoModeBuildAgentSettingKey(projectId)
186:        : autoModeReviewAgentSettingKey(projectId),
187:      agentId,
188:    ]);
189:  }
190:
191:  if ("buildConcurrency" in payload) {
192:    const value = parseAutoModeConcurrency(payload.buildConcurrency);
193:    if (value === null) {
194:      return NextResponse.json(
195:        { error: "`buildConcurrency` must be an integer between 0 and 10." },
196:        { status: 400 }
197:      );
198:    }
199:    writes.push([autoModeBuildConcurrencySettingKey(projectId), value]);
200:  }
201:
202:  if ("reviewConcurrency" in payload) {
203:    const value = parseAutoModeConcurrency(payload.reviewConcurrency);
204:    if (value === null) {
205:      return NextResponse.json(
206:        { error: "`reviewConcurrency` must be an integer between 0 and 10." },
207:        { status: 400 }
208:      );
209:    }
210:    writes.push([autoModeReviewConcurrencySettingKey(projectId), value]);
211:  }
212:
213:  try {
214:    // All-or-nothing: a half-applied configuration is how an unattended mode
215:    // ends up running with settings nobody chose.
216:    db.transaction(() => {
217:      for (const [key, value] of writes) putSetting(key, value);
218:    });
219:
220:    // Mirror the persisted flag into the registry BEFORE building the
221:    // response, so the runtime fields the dialog reads back (`running`, and
222:    // the in-flight counts a disable clears) describe the state the caller
223:    // just asked for rather than the one the sweep has not caught up with.
224:    const config = resolveAutoModeConfigForProject(projectId);
225:    autoModeRegistry.setEnabled(projectId, config.enabled);
226:
227:    const status = buildStatus(projectId);
228:
229:    // Enabling (or retuning) takes effect now, not on the next 15s tick.
230:    // Disabling also sweeps: that pass is what settles the registry state.
231:    kickAutoMode(projectId);
232:
233:    return NextResponse.json({ data: status });
234:  } catch (error) {
235:    return errorResponse(error, "Failed to update auto mode settings");
236:  }
237:}

### Summary of Delivered Work: Full Auto Mode

We have implemented **Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor** in full accordance with the epic specification and all user stories.

---

### Implementation Details by User Story

#### 1. Configuration & Constants (`lib/auto-mode/constants.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/config.ts`)
- Client-safe `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` importing nothing from `lib/db`, defining global settings keys and per-project key helpers (`autoModeEnabledSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildConcurrencySettingKey`, `autoModeReviewAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeReviewConcurrencySettingKey`).
- Coercion parsers (`parseAutoModeEnabled`, `parseAutoModeConcurrency`, `parseAutoModeAgent`) tolerating raw, string, and JSON-encoded forms, clamping concurrency to $0..10$, and returning `null` for unconfigured values to allow fall-through.
- `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` resolving per-project key $\rightarrow$ global key $\rightarrow$ built-in default, discovering enabled projects via `listAutoModeEnabledProjectIds()`.
- **No schema migration added.**

#### 2. Review Agent Support in Pipeline Stage Driver (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`)
- Added optional `reviewNamedAgentId?: string | null` to `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
- When set, review stage dispatch resolves the named agent (`init.reviewNamedAgentId`); when `null` or omitted, defaults to previous resolution behavior with reviewer provider segregation.

#### 3. Candidate Selectors (`lib/auto-mode/select.ts`)
- `selectBuildCandidates`: story-scoped candidates when epic has stories, epic-scoped otherwise; ordered by epic `priority DESC, position ASC` then story `position ASC`.
- `selectReviewCandidates`: epics in `review` with freshness temporal guard (newest terminal review newer than newest terminal code session excluded from re-review).
- `selectMergeCandidates`: epics in `review` with non-null `branchName`, fresh clean review, and 0 open review comments.
- Batched query architecture (`loadAutoModeBoard`) without N+1 queries.
- Exclusions for tickets with `queued`/`running` sessions (`getRunningSessionForTarget`), active pipeline runs, DAG batches, night runs, `isAwaitingReply`, and parked tickets.

#### 4. Auto-Merge on Clean Review (`lib/auto-mode/merge.ts`)
- Pure git merge via `mergeWorktree(repoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` without consuming scheduler slots or agent sessions for clean merges.
- Transitions through `applyTransition({ fromStatus, toStatus: 'done', actor: 'agent', source: 'merge' })`, clears `epics.branchName`, and calls `tryExportArjiJson`.
- On merge conflict: dispatches a `merge` fix agent charged to the build budget, with worktree re-attached to the exact surviving branch, and retries the merge once. A second failure parks the ticket with a hard flag and triggers `createAutoModeMergeParkedNotification`.
- Guard refusal or human intervention rolls back `main` and restores the branch via `rollbackMerge`.
- `POST .../approve` is strictly avoided to preserve blocking review comments.

#### 5. Standing Sweep Engine & Lifecycle (`lib/auto-mode/registry.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`)
- GlobalThis-backed `autoModeRegistry` tracking enabled state, in-flight build/review sessions, sweep mutex, failure tallies, and recent dispatches.
- Mutual exclusion per project ensuring two sweeps never overlap.
- Reconciles terminal sessions, merges candidates first to drain the `review` column, then dispatches reviews ($< M$) and builds ($< N$) via `createPipelineStageDriver`.
- Timer loop at `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`unref()`'d).
- `instrumentation.ts` starts auto mode on server boot and chains the session terminal hook (`kickAutoModeForSession` composed with `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal`).

#### 6. Auto Mode API & Board UI (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts`, `components/auto-mode/`)
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: returns status, in-flight counts, candidate counts, parked tickets, and recent activity.
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: validates and persists settings, updates registry, and triggers an immediate sweep.
- `AutoModeDialog.tsx`: enable switch, build and review named agent selects, concurrency inputs ($0..10$), candidate indicators, and scheduler budget overload warning.
- `AutoModeToggle.tsx`: board toolbar toggle with active running badge (`N building · M reviewing`).

#### 7. Safety Verification & Documentation
- Verified safety guards: infinite re-review prevention, agent question guard (`isAwaitingReply`), coexistence with manual/night/DAG runs, and story serialization.
- Documented in `README.md` and `docs/architecture/full-auto-mode.md`.

# Epic Implementation: Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat

## Root Cause Analysis
1. **Dual Conflicting Dropdowns:** `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx` was rendering two distinct dropdowns side-by-side: `ChatProviderSelect` and `NamedAgentSelect`. When a named agent was associated with the active conversation (standard default in Arij), `ChatProviderSelect` was disabled (`disabled={... || Boolean(activeConversation?.namedAgentId)}`).
2. **Missing Direct API in Active Selector:** The active dropdown `NamedAgentSelect` only listed Named Agents from the database (CLI providers) and had no option for the direct API ("OpenAI-compatible").
3. **Artificial Conversation Type Block:** `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` blocked `brainstorm` and `epic_creation` conversation types from using OpenAI-compatible mode, making it impossible to use the direct API across the app.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Unified Single Dropdown Selector
- **`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx`:** Refactored into a single unified selector component that offers:
  - **Direct API:** `OpenAI-compatible`
  - **Named Agents:** All user-configured Named Agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.)
- **`components/chat/ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx`:** Removed the secondary redundant dropdown. The header now renders exactly one interactive selector.
- **`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx`:** Added `handleSelectAgentOrProvider` to update both `namedAgentId` and `provider` when switching between Named Agents and Direct API.

### 2. Conversation & Chat Stream Updates
- **`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts` & `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts`:** Lifted the artificial conversation type restriction so OpenAI-compatible fast mode can be selected and used across chat conversations.
- **`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts`:** Updated the conversation update PATCH route to cleanly set `provider = "openai-compatible"` and clear `namedAgentId` when direct API is selected.

### 3. Verification & Testing
- **`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx`:** Added dedicated unit tests verifying:
  - Exactly one dropdown is rendered in the chat header (no secondary disabled dropdown).
  - Direct API ("OpenAI-compatible") and all configured Named Agents are available options.
  - Proper payload dispatching when switching between Direct API and Named Agents.
  - Gating behavior on active vs busy/has-messages conversations.
- **`__tests__/chat-provider-select.test.tsx`**, **`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx`**, and **`__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts`:** Updated mocks and assertions to match the unified selector and direct API support.
- **Full Test Suite:** All 267 test files and 2,660 tests pass.
