comments.content:
**Code Review**

I can't call `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — the session is in plan mode, which blocks it, and no `ExitPlanMode` tool is available to leave. The full report is below and is also saved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-federated-fern.md`. Exit plan mode (shift+tab) and say "file the findings" and I'll submit them as anchored review comments.

---

# Code Review — Bug fix: « Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat »

**Scope:** commit `307144a` only (10 files). Earlier branch commits that introduced the OpenAI-compatible provider were reviewed in prior passes.

**Verification performed:** read every touched file plus the surrounding call graph (`hooks/useConversations.ts`, `hooks/useEpicCreate.ts`, `lib/db/init.ts`, `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/generate-spec/route.ts`); ran `npx eslint` on the changed files; ran `npx vitest run` on the five touched test files — 42 tests, all green.

The reported bug is genuinely fixed: one selector renders, it is no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, and "OpenAI-compatible" is present. Two blocking problems remain.

---

## 1. Critical — one selection fires three concurrent PATCHes, and the last one unlinks the named agent

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:109`** (wired at `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:66-68`, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:363-365`)

`handleValueChange` invokes **all three** callbacks for a single choice:

```ts
onSelect?.({ namedAgentId: nextValue, provider }); // -> handleSelectAgentOrProvider
onAgentChange?.(nextValue);                        // -> handleAgentChange
onProviderChange?.(provider);                      // -> handleProviderChange
```

The header passes all three, and `UnifiedChatPanel` maps each to its own `updateConversation()` — three independent `PATCH /conversations/:id` requests in the same tick, no ordering guarantee.

The third is the damaging one. Its body is `{ provider: "codex" }` with **no** `namedAgentId` key; `updateConversationSchema` uses zod `.nullish()`, which drops absent keys, so `hasOwnProperty(body, "namedAgentId")` is false and it lands in the legacy branch at `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:152-161`, which does `updates.namedAgentId = null`.

**Failure scenario:** user picks "Codex (GPT-5)". PATCH#1 sets `namedAgentId = agent-2`; PATCH#3 clears it. Last write wins. When #3 wins, the conversation runs on the *default* chat agent with only the provider overridden (`chat/stream/route.ts:124-127`), silently losing the selected agent's model — and local state is overwritten by whichever response resolves last, so the dropdown can snap back to a different agent. The direct-API path duplicates too (2 PATCHes), idempotent but wasteful.

**Recommendation:** emit exactly one event. Keep `onSelect` as the sole callback and drop `onAgentChange`/`onProviderChange` from this component and the header's wiring — `ChatWorkspaceHeader.handleSelect` already implements the correct mutually-exclusive fallback one level up.

## 2. Major — Direct API on an epic-creation conversation silently degrades to plain chat

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts:274`**

Removing the gate (lines 130-149) makes fast mode *selectable* for `epic_creation`, but the fast-mode branch returns at line 274 — before the block at 410-441 that builds `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` / `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt`. In fast mode the `finalize` flag parsed at line 102 is never read, and the model gets the generic chat system prompt.

**Failure scenario:** epic-creation conversation → switch to OpenAI-compatible → discuss → "Create Epic & Generate Stories". `useEpicCreate` (`hooks/useEpicCreate.ts:58-82`) sends two finalization prompts, gets prose back (nothing instructs a fenced JSON block), `parseEpicFromConversation` finds nothing, user sees *"I couldn't extract a full epic yet."* with no hint the provider is the cause.

`brainstorm` is genuinely fine — the CLI path also uses `buildChatPrompt` for it, and "Generate Spec & Plan" posts to `/generate-spec`, which ignores the body's `provider` and resolves the `spec_generation` agent independently. Only `epic_creation` regresses.

**Recommendation:** move the `isEpicCreationConversationAgentType` prompt block above line 274 and feed it in as the fast-mode system message, or keep `epic_creation` ineligible and lift the gate only for `brainstorm`/`chat`.

**Test gap:** `__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts:282` asserts only `status === 200` + "fetch was called" — it passes identically whether the epic prompt is wired or not.

## 3. Major — CLI providers without a named agent are no longer selectable

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:142`**

The old select rendered `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (11 CLI providers). The unified one lists only Direct API + `named_agents` rows. A fresh DB seeds exactly one named agent — "Claude Code" (`lib/db/init.ts:15-17`) — so out of the box a conversation can run on Claude Code or the direct API and nothing else. Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi… become unreachable from chat until the user creates a named agent for each, while the API layer still accepts them. `normalizeProvider()` at `chat/stream/route.ts:39-50` carries a doc comment explicitly warning against exactly this narrowing.

**Recommendation:** add a third `SelectGroup` ("Providers") listing `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`. If the narrowing is intentional, say so and remove the now-unreachable provider-only PATCH branches.

## 4. Minor — dead function

**`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts:45`** — `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` unconditionally returns `false`, ignores `_type`, and has zero callers (grepped across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `__tests__/`). Delete it.

## 5. Minor — unused import flagged by lint

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:16`** — `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` was dropped but `type ChatModeProvider` was left unused:

```
16:8  warning  'ChatModeProvider' is defined but never used  @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars
```

(The one eslint *error*, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:252`, is pre-existing from `4bfd1e6` — unrelated.)

## 6. Minor — over-broad, partly dead props contract

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:25-37`** — eight optional props with overlapping meaning. `value`/`onChange` are legacy shims no caller passes; `conversationType` is declared but not destructured, so it's silently ignored; `ChatAgentSelection.provider` is `string` where `ChatModeProvider` (`constants.ts:103`) is precise. Narrowing to `{ activeConversation, activeProvider, onSelect, disabled, className }` also fixes #1 structurally rather than by convention.

## 7. Minor — hardcoded provider fallback

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:104`** — `?? "claude-code"` where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` exists (`lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:38`). Also unreachable by construction, so it hides the impossible case rather than handling it.

## 8. Minor — the select can display an agent the conversation isn't using

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:85-89`** — with no `namedAgentId` and no provider match, the fallback is `agents[0]?.id`. A conversation on `provider: "pi"` with no Pi agent renders "Claude Code" as selected; with several agents sharing a provider, `find()` picks an arbitrary one. Since the select disables once messages exist, the user can't correct it. Prefer an empty value (placeholder shows) or a synthetic "Default (<label>)" entry.

## 9. Minor (DRY) — redundant PATCH branch

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:104`** — this leading branch and the nested one at 136-143, both added in this commit, produce identical `updates` for the payload the UI actually sends (`{ provider: "openai-compatible", namedAgentId: null }`): `namedAgentIdInput` is `""`, so the nested `else if` runs, and `isChatProvider("openai-compatible")` is `true`. The only input it changes behaviour for is `{ namedAgentId: "<id>", provider: "openai-compatible" }`, which no caller sends.

## 10. Suggestion — the regression test cannot catch #1

**`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:257`** — `toHaveBeenCalledWith` passes when *any* call matches, so the three-PATCH storm is invisible; the test is green today despite the bug. `expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` turns it into a real guard. Related: `chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx` exercises the component in isolation with one `onSelect` spy — the failing paths only appear once header, panel and route are wired together, which no test covers.

---

## Checklist verdicts

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Issues — #4, #5, #6, #7 |
| DRY | Issues — #1 (three code paths for one action), #9 |
| Error handling | No issues found |
| Performance | Issue — #1 (3× write amplification per selection) |
| Naming conventions | No issues found |
| Type safety | Issues — #6; no `any` introduced |
| Testing | Issues — #2 (test asserts nothing meaningful), #10 |
| API design | Issue — #9; status codes and `{data}`/`{error}` shape consistent |

## Summary

**Critical:** 1 · **Major:** 2 · **Minor:** 6 · **Suggestion:** 1

The two-dropdown and disabled-selector problems are genuinely fixed and the direct API is now reachable. But the unified component fans a single selection out to three conflicting write paths that can undo the user's choice, and lifting the epic-creation gate exposes a mode that silently cannot finalize an epic.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review Findings Resolved

All [critical], [major], and [minor] review findings have been resolved and verified across the codebase:

---

### Summary of Fixes

1. **Critical — Eliminated write amplification / triple concurrent PATCH calls (`ChatProviderSelect.tsx`, `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx`, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx`):**
   - Removed redundant `onAgentChange` and `onProviderChange` callbacks from `ChatProviderSelect`.
   - Unified selection handling through a single `onSelect` callback.
   - `UnifiedChatPanel` now dispatches exactly **one** `updateConversation()` (PATCH request) on user selection.

2. **Major — Supported Epic Refinement and Finalization in Fast Mode (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts`):**
   - For `epic_creation` conversations in OpenAI-compatible fast mode, the system now builds `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt` (when `finalize: true`) or `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` (when `finalize: false`).
   - The generated prompt is enriched with document mentions and passed as the system prompt to the OpenAI endpoint, enabling successful epic JSON creation from fast mode.

3. **Major — Restored CLI Providers alongside Direct API & Named Agents (`ChatProviderSelect.tsx`):**
   - `ChatProviderSelect` now displays three clearly grouped options:
     - **Direct API:** `OpenAI-compatible`
     - **Named Agents:** All user-configured named agents from the DB
     - **CLI Providers:** All available CLI providers from `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (`Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Gemini CLI`, `Pi`, `Oh My Pi`, etc.)

4. **Minor — Cleaned up Dead Code & Unused Types (`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts`, `components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx`):**
   - Removed the dead `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` function.
   - Cleaned unused imports and narrowed `ChatProviderSelect` props contract to `{ activeConversation, activeProvider, onSelect, disabled, className }`.
   - Typed `ChatAgentSelection.provider` strictly as `ChatModeProvider`.

5. **Minor — Centralized Provider Fallback & Streamlined PATCH Route (`lib/agent-config/constants.ts`, `lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts`):**

**Scope:** commits `307144a` + `a681bae` + `38131f4` (12 files). Earlier branch commits were covered by prior passes.

**Verification performed**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **4 errors** (all in `__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx`)
- `npx eslint` on the 7 changed source files → 1 error, pre-existing (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:253`, on `main` since `4bfd1e6`)
- `npx vitest run` on the 6 touched test files → 55 tests, all green (vitest does not type-check)
- Read the call graph: `useConversations`, `useEpicCreate`, `useSpecGeneration`, `generate-spec/route.ts`, `agent-resolution.ts`, `prompts.ts`, `prompt-builder.ts`, `lib/db/init.ts`, `lib/providers/codex.ts`

## The reported bug is fixed

`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:45-50` renders exactly one selector, no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, with "OpenAI-compatible" as a first-class option. End-to-end verified: select → **one** PATCH → `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:128-135` → `chat/stream/route.ts:123-130` → fast-mode branch. All prior findings (triple PATCH, epic prompts, dead helper, duplicate history) are genuinely closed.

## 1. Major — `npx tsc --noEmit` fails; the project no longer type-checks

`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx:127, 142, 217, 228`

`38131f4` made `onSelectAgentOrProvider` required on `ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps` and updated only **one** of the five `<ChatWorkspaceHeader>` renders in this file (line 86).

```
error TS2741: Property 'onSelectAgentOrProvider' is missing in type
'{ activeConversation: Conversation; activeProvider: string; hasMessages: false; isBusy: false; }'
but required in type 'ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps'.
```

Vitest strips types, so the suite stays green and hides it. `tsconfig.json` includes `**/*.tsx` with no `__tests__` exclusion and `next.config.ts` does not set `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`, so the same diagnostics gate `next build`. **Fix:** add `onSelectAgentOrProvider={noop}` to the four remaining renders.

## 2. Major — Direct API chat runs with no project context (fresh install: no system prompt at all)

`chat/stream/route.ts:308-310`, `:344-358`, `:457-459`

For non-epic conversations the fast-mode system prompt is `resolveAgentPrompt("chat", projectId)` — a raw configured string. `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS.chat` is `""` and nothing is seeded, so by default `fastModeSystemPrompt.trim()` is falsy and **no system message is sent**: the request is the last 20 raw turns and nothing else. The CLI branch one `if` below calls `buildChatPrompt()`, which adds `projectContextSections()` (spec, memory, documents) plus the "answer considering the full project context above" instructions. `38131f4` moved that call *below* the fast-mode return, making the asymmetry structural.

**Failure scenario:** user switches a chat to "OpenAI-compatible" and asks "what's left on the auth epic?". Claude Code / Codex in the same dropdown answer from the project spec; the direct API answers as a generic assistant with no idea what the project is. `307144a` widens this: lifting the gate routes `brainstorm` — the type whose whole purpose is discussing *this* project — down the same context-free path. Epic creation is unaffected (its builder embeds everything).

**Recommendation:** `buildChatPrompt(project, [], [], chatSystemPrompt)` with empty history (history already travels in `openAiMessages`), or export `projectContextSections()` and prepend it.

## 3. Major — picking a CLI provider spawns that CLI with another provider's model

`chat/stream/route.ts:123-127` + `ChatProviderSelect.tsx:150-163`

The "CLI Providers" group (added in `a681bae`) PATCHes `{provider, namedAgentId: null}`. The route then keeps the *default chat agent's* model and overrides only the provider:

```ts
resolvedAgent = conversationProvider && !conversation?.namedAgentId
  ? { ...resolvedByNamedAgent, provider: conversationProvider }   // model untouched
  : resolvedByNamedAgent;
```

`resolveAgentByNamedId("chat", projectId, null)` → the seeded default agent, `claude-code` / `claude-opus-4-6` (`lib/db/init.ts:16-17`). The model passes through unnormalized (`lib/providers/types.ts:69`) and codex renders it verbatim: `args.push("-m", model)` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:133`, `:168`).

**Failure scenario:** fresh install → pick "Codex (CLI)" → send → `codex exec … -m claude-opus-4-6` → CLI rejects the model, user sees `Error: <codex stderr>`. Newly reachable: `main` exposed only `NamedAgentSelect`, and the branch's earlier select was disabled whenever a `namedAgentId` existed — i.e. the bug being fixed. **Recommendation:** drop the model when the provider differs from the resolved agent's, or resolve a per-provider default.

## 4. Minor — epic fast mode still sends the latest user message twice
`chat/stream/route.ts:336-343` — `fullHistory` includes the just-saved message and the epic builders embed it via `chatHistorySection()`; it is pushed again as the `user` turn. Much smaller than before (one message), and a user turn is needed by most endpoints — but the system prompt could carry history minus the current message.

## 5. Minor (DRY) — the two branches differ by one loop
`chat/stream/route.ts:335-358` — the system push and trailing user push are written twice; only the `messageHistory` loop is conditional.

## 6. Minor — dead fallback branch and a now-redundant prop
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:79-83` — that arm only runs when `activeConversation` is null, and the sole caller disables the select in exactly that case (`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:49`). `activeProvider` is derived from `activeConversation?.provider` (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:146`), so it carries no new information.

## 7. Minor — a deleted named agent renders an empty selector
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:72-73` — `selectedValue` takes `namedAgentId` without checking it exists in `safeAgents`; if deleted, Radix shows the placeholder while the conversation runs on the resolved default.

## 8. Minor (API design) — named-agent PATCH carries a `provider` the server ignores
`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:312` sends `{namedAgentId, provider}`; `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:122-123` re-derives it from the agent row. `chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:264` asserts the exact body, locking the redundant field into the contract.

## 9. Suggestion — test gaps and one leftover
- No test drives header → panel → PATCH for **Direct API** or a **CLI provider**; only the named-agent case is covered end-to-end. Findings #3 and #8 live in that gap.
- `chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts` mocks the prompt builders to constants, so #2 is invisible by construction — the non-epic assertions never inspect the system message.
- `lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:39-40` — double blank line left where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` moved out; the constant now has a single consumer, back in the file it came from.

| Readability | Issues — #5, #6 |
| DRY | Issues — #5, #8 |
| Error handling | No issues found — fast-mode abort/mid-stream/cancel paths complete; `useChat` surfaces `payload.error` for the 400s |
| Performance | Issue — #4; `buildChatPrompt` no longer computed-and-discarded |

**Summary:** Major 3 · Minor 5 · Suggestion 1

The dual-dropdown and disabled-selector defects are properly fixed and the direct API is reachable from every conversation type — the ticket's actual complaint is resolved. What blocks approval is collateral: the branch no longer type-checks, and the two options the fix newly exposes (Direct API for chat/brainstorm, raw CLI providers) each reach the model in a degraded state.

epics.title: Échec de build silencieux : « Agent error » sans message d'erreur ni notification
epics.description:
## Problème

Sur un deuxième projet, la tentative de build d'un ticket échoue avec uniquement un message **« Agent error »** en tout petit en bas de l'interface. Aucune indication sur la nature de l'erreur n'est affichée, ni dans l'UI ni via une notification.

## Comportement attendu

Quand un build (ou toute session d'agent) échoue :

1. **Notification** : une notification du système de notifications global doit être émise, avec le **message d'erreur complet** (stderr / sortie de l'agent / raison de l'échec), pas seulement un libellé générique.
2. **Visibilité dans l'UI** : l'erreur doit être visible et lisible sur la carte / le ticket — pas un texte minuscule tronqué. Un clic doit permettre de voir le détail complet (par exemple via la modale de notifications ou la vue session).
3. **Traçabilité** : l'erreur complète doit rester consultable après coup (log de session), pas seulement au moment de l'échec.

## Contexte

- Le système de notifications global existe déjà (E-arij-009, done) — il faut le brancher sur les échecs de session/build.
- Un bug proche a déjà été traité : B-arij-108 (« Le badge "Session failed" réapparaît après un retry réussi ») et E-arij-010 (« trop de cas de "(no textual output)" ») — vérifier que la cause n'est pas liée (sortie vide de l'agent → message générique au lieu de l'erreur réelle).
- Piste probable : quand la sortie de l'agent est vide ou que le process meurt sans stderr, l'UI retombe sur le libellé « Agent error » sans surface pour afficher la raison.

## Critères d'acceptation

- Un build qui échoue déclenche une notification contenant le message d'erreur complet (ou, si l'agent n'a produit aucune sortie, un message explicite le disant + où trouver les logs).
- Le message « Agent error » seul, en tout petit, n'est plus le seul signal : le détail est accessible en un clic.
- L'erreur reste consultable après coup dans l'historique de la session.
- Cas vide/no-output couvert explicitement (cf. leçon E-arij-010).

**Forensic diagnostic**

**Probable root cause** — The run never started. Arij's pi adapter passes the configured model verbatim as `--model qwen3.8-27b` and never emits a `--provider` flag (`lib/providers/pi.ts:203-207`, `buildArgs`). Two authenticated pi providers (`ninfer` and `vllm`) both serve that model name, so the pi CLI refused to disambiguate and exited during argument/model resolution — before emitting its `session` header or any `message_end` event. Because the failure is a startup error on stderr rather than a stream event, nothing reached the output stream and no assistant text was produced, so the pipeline surfaced only the generic "Agent error" with no message. This is a configuration defect (an under-qualified model identifier), not a defect in the ticket's code or prompt; retrying was futile, which is why both `build` attempts failed identically.

**Evidence**

- The recorded error is a pi CLI resolution failure, not a task failure: `Error: Model "qwen3.8-27b" is ambiguous across providers: ninfer/qwen3.8-27b, vllm/qwen3.8-27b. More than one matching provider is authenticated. Use --provider or provider/model.`
- The run produced nothing: *Output stream (tail): (none)* and *Last text produced: (none)* — consistent with an exit before pi's `--mode json` stream opened, which is what leaves the UI with an empty "Agent error".
- The raw stream tail contains that single error line and nothing else — no `{"type":"session"…}` header, no tool calls — confirming the process died at startup rather than mid-task.

**Recommended next action**

- Requalify the model in the agent/pipeline config for this ticket from the bare `qwen3.8-27b` to a provider-qualified `vllm/qwen3.8-27b` (or `ninfer/qwen3.8-27b`, whichever endpoint is intended) — pi's own message accepts the `provider/model` form, and Arij forwards the string unchanged to `--model`, so this needs no code change — then re-run the `build` stage. If both providers should stay authenticated long-term, follow up separately by teaching `PiProvider.buildArgs` to emit `--provider`, since bare model names will keep colliding.

epics.title: Bugs : test de régression obligatoire (règle RoboBun rouge→vert)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement RoboBun (Bun, Code with Claude 2026) : une PR de bug n'est soumise QUE si elle contient un test qui échoue avant le correctif et passe après. C'est la garantie mécanique que le bug est réellement reproduit puis corrigé — ce qui a fait de RoboBun un contributeur majeur du repo Bun. Prérequis : l'étage `verify` du pipeline (ticket lié en dépendance) doit exister.

## À construire
1. **Prompts** : pour un ticket `type = 'bug'`, les prompts de build (`buildBuildPrompt`, `buildTicketBuildPrompt`, `buildTeamBuildPrompt` dans `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts`) exigent explicitement : écrire d'abord un test qui reproduit le bug et échoue, puis corriger, et committer le(s) fichier(s) de test avec le fix.
2. **Vérification mécanique** `lib/verify/regression-check.ts` :
   - identifier les fichiers de test ajoutés/modifiés sur la branche : `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD` filtré par les motifs de test du projet (setting `test_file_patterns`, défaut `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**`) ;
   - **vert** : la commande de test ciblée (setting `bug_regression_command`, template avec placeholder `{files}`, ex. `npx vitest run {files}`) passe dans le worktree de l'epic ;
   - **rouge** : créer un worktree temporaire détaché sur le merge-base (`git worktree add --detach`), y copier UNIQUEMENT les fichiers de test nouveaux/modifiés, relancer la même commande — elle DOIT échouer. Nettoyage du worktree temporaire dans un finally.
   - Cas dégradés explicites dans le rapport : aucun fichier de test dans le diff → fail raison `no_test_in_diff` ; le test passe déjà sur le merge-base → fail `test_passes_on_base` ; le test échoue sur la branche → fail `test_fails_on_branch`.
3. **Câblage** : dans l'étage verify du pipeline, après les `verify_commands`, si `type = 'bug'` ET setting `bug_regression_check` activé (tri-state, défaut OFF). Échec → fix cycle avec la raison précise injectée dans le prompt. Résultat intégré au rapport verify (champ `regression: {status, reason, testFiles}`).
4. **UI** : la section verify du ticket affiche le bloc régression (fichiers de test détectés, rouge/vert, raison d'échec).

## Contraintes
- Le worktree temporaire vit dans `.arij-worktrees/` comme les autres (voir `lib/git/manager.ts`) avec un préfixe distinct (ex. `regression-check-`), et est détruit même en cas de crash (finally ; le détecteur d'orphelins de `lib/git/worktrees.ts` doit le reconnaître).
- Ne jamais toucher à la branche de l'epic ni à main.
- Tests vitest : détection des fichiers de test, cas no_test_in_diff, cas test_passes_on_base, nettoyage du worktree temporaire (y compris sur exception).

## Hors scope
Extension aux features (une feature sans test ne bloque pas) ; analyse de couverture.

- `lib/verify/regression-check.ts` + client-safe `regression-constants.ts`. Repairs over the mangled prior draft: restored missing `resolveBaseBranch` import (shared `lib/git/base-branch.ts`), fixed a doc-comment containing a literal `` `**/` `` that terminated the block early, and added a `failedToRun` outcome mapped to the `command_error` reason (spawn failure vs. genuine red).
- Red proof: throwaway detached worktree at `<repo>/../.arij-worktrees/regression-check-*` cut at the true merge-base, only test files copied in, same command re-run; destroyed in `finally` including on exception. The generic orphan detector in `lib/git/worktrees.ts` recognizes any leftover record.

### Story 3 — Câblage pipeline + rapport + UI (commit `d1244a4`)

- **Runner**: optional `runVerifyGate` in `runPipeline`; red verdict with fix-cycle budget left → fix dispatch carrying `verifyFailure`; budget exhausted → terminal `Pipeline failed: mandatory regression test still failing…`.
- **Prompt injection**: `stages.ts` appends `buildRegressionFixSection` (exact reason + detected files + command tail) to fix prompts.
- **Report/UI**: verdict persisted as an agent ticket comment (marker `<!-- arij:regression-report -->` + fenced JSON); rendered as a dedicated red/green block in both the epic activity feed and story comment thread via `components/verify/RegressionReportBlock.tsx`. New tri-state toggle in Settings → Autonomous Pipeline.

I built the minimal mechanical verify stage at the pipeline's natural insertion point so the dependency-ticket's future command runner can extend it; the regression check runs "after verify_commands" vacuously.

**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on all touched files, full vitest suite green — **354 files / 4067 tests**, including 24 new tests across the three suites.

comments.author: agent
agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic: Bugs : test de régression obligatoire (règle RoboBun rouge→vert)

**Branch:** `feature/epic-BYH37ko3jUxA-bugs-test-de-r-gression-obligatoire-r-gl` (4 commits vs `main`, 18 files, +1965/−6)
**Scope:** all three stories, including the fix pass in `9e7935b`.

> Tooling note: this session is in plan mode, so `mcp__arij__submit_findings` / `post_comment` (writes) were not called. Findings are file+line anchored and can be filed as-is.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong. Module headers state *why* (`regression-check.ts:16-31`, `verify.ts:31-45`), the failure-reason vocabulary is one union shared by prompt → gate → report → UI, and the client-safe constants split mirrors `lib/pipeline/constants.ts`. The comment on `defaultRunCommand`'s no-numeric-code branch (`regression-check.ts:175-177`) explains a genuinely subtle discrimination.

**[Minor] `components/verify/RegressionReportBlock.tsx:17` — the name no longer matches the responsibility.** After the swaps at `EpicActivityFeed.tsx:286` and `CommentThread.tsx:104`, this renders *every* ticket comment and special-cases regression reports. A reader at either call site sees `<RegressionReportBlock content={comment.content} />` on an ordinary user comment. Rename to `TicketCommentContent`, or branch at the call site.

**[Minor] `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:650` — stray blank line** left inside `TeamEpic` when the redundant `type` redeclaration was removed.

---

## 2. DRY Principle

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-constants.ts:153-168` — `resolveBugRegressionCheckEnabled` is still dead code.** Grepped repo-wide: exported, documented, referenced by nothing — not the settings page (which uses `parseBugRegressionSetting`), not a test. Its per-project → global → default precedence is re-implemented independently by `readRegressionConfig` (`lib/pipeline/verify.ts:84-129`). Delete it, or have `readRegressionConfig` build a map and call it.

Otherwise good: `worktreesRootFor` (`lib/projects/workspace.ts:105`) is now reused, `resolveBaseBranch` is shared with `createWorktree`, and the `{files}` quoting lives in one place.

---

## 3. Error Handling

The `finally` cleanup (`regression-check.ts:353-355`, `removeRedWorktree:372-387`) is correct and genuinely tested against a live exception (`regression-check.test.ts:277-301`). Checked against git 2.53: `remove refuses to remove an unclean worktree unless --force is used` — a single `--force` is sufficient here (double force is only for *locked* worktrees), so the untracked copied test files do not defeat the removal, and the admin record goes with it. `persistReportComment` correctly refuses to fail the stage on a DB error. `maxBuffer` and the timeout/signal discrimination from the fix pass are right.

**[Major] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:280-286` — the environmental discriminator was only added to the red run; the green run still reports environmental failures as `test_fails_on_branch`.**

`looksLikeStartupFailure` is consulted at line 343 for the red run only. The green run executes in the epic worktree, which `createWorktree` produces with a bare `git worktree add` (`lib/git/manager.ts:59-104`) — **no `node_modules`**, and nothing in the application ever installs or links them (`grep -rn node_modules lib/ app/` returns only `regression-check.ts:311` and the document-scan ignore list).

*Failure scenario:* default `bug_regression_command` = `npx vitest run {files}`, bug ticket, gate ON, fresh epic worktree. The green run cannot resolve vitest or the project's own imports and exits non-zero. The gate reports `test_fails_on_branch` → the fix prompt tells the agent *"the regression test fails on the branch — the fix does not work yet"* (`regression-report.ts:33-34`) → the agent chases a test failure that does not exist → after `maxFixCycles` the run terminates with *"mandatory regression test still failing"*, on a branch whose test is fine. The byte-identical output on the red side is correctly reported as `command_error`.

*Recommendation:* run `looksLikeStartupFailure(green.output)` before classifying `test_fails_on_branch` and return `command_error` with the environmental detail; and/or surface "the epic worktree has no `node_modules`" explicitly in the report so the operator sees the real cause. The unit suite cannot catch this — the probe (`regression-check.test.ts:34-44`) is dependency-free by construction.

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:343-351` — the startup signature can swallow a genuine red.** `REGRESSION_STARTUP_FAILURE_PATTERNS` matches anywhere in the output, including assertion text. Two realistic false positives: a regression test *for* a module-resolution bug, and a test whose new helper/fixture is not itself a test file (so it is never copied into the red worktree — only `testFiles` are, line 320-324) and whose absence prints `Cannot find module './fixtures/x'`. Both report `command_error` on a correct branch. Narrow the verdict (e.g. only when the `node_modules` link could not be established, or when the signature precedes any test-result output) and say in the report which case was hit.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:507-513` — "regression gate crashed" is still the only `finish(...)` in the state machine with no `onTrace`.** Every sibling traces first (lines 313, 327, 339, 429, 477, 526, 535, 588). The ticket's activity log shows the run dying with no pipeline-tagged reason for `isPipelineActivityReason` to pick up.

---

## 4. Correctness / Functional gaps

**[Major] `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:524-532` — a bug rejected by the mandatory gate is left sitting in `review`.**

`finalizeCodeSession` → `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome` moves a successful build to `review`, and it runs *inside* `runStageSession` before `settleLaunch` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:715-745`). So by the time the gate runs, the ticket is already in Review. On the budget-exhausted branch the runner returns `finish("failed", …)` and moves nothing.

Every other terminal failure parks the ticket in `in_progress`: the findings path goes through `transitionReviewRejected` (`stages.ts:897,915`) before the runner reaches `failedFindings`. The regression path is the only one that ends in the approval-ready column.

*Failure scenario A:* `pipeline_max_fix_cycles = 0` (legal — `PIPELINE_MAX_FIX_CYCLES_RANGE.min` is 0, `constants.ts:140`), bug ticket, gate red on the first build. Run fails; the ticket sits in Review with a red regression block and **no review session was ever dispatched** — board-wise indistinguishable from a bug that passed the gate and is awaiting sign-off.
*Failure scenario B:* build → gate green → review with findings → fix → gate red → budget exhausted. Now a completed review session exists, so the `hasCompletedReview` guard on `review → done` (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:67-74`) no longer blocks approval of a branch the mandatory gate rejected.

*Recommendation:* call `transitionReviewRejected` (or the equivalent guarded `review → in_progress`) before `finish` on the regression-exhausted path, mirroring what the review rejection already does. `review → in_progress` is permitted by the engine (`engine.ts:22`).

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:323` — the red run tests the working-tree file, not the committed one.** `copyFileSync(path.join(input.repoPath, relPath), …)` reads the epic worktree's current file while the file list came from `mergeBase..head` (committed state). Uncommitted agent edits make the red proof describe a file that is not on the branch; a committed-then-deleted file makes it throw ENOENT. Use `git show ${head}:${relPath}`.

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:253-254` — `git diff --name-only` is subject to `core.quotePath`.** With the default `true`, a test file with any non-ASCII character comes back C-quoted (`"src/caf\303\251.test.ts"`, quotes included), which either misses `fileMatchesAnyPattern` or makes `copyFileSync` throw. Use `-c core.quotePath=false`, or `-z` and split on NUL.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/verify.ts:137-147` — the report comment sets both `epicId` and `userStoryId` on story scope, and omits `agentSessionId`.** The convention is visible three functions away: `finalizeCodeSession` (`stages.ts:794-798`) and `finalizeReviewSession` (`stages.ts:829-833`) both write `...(scope === "story" && userStoryId ? { userStoryId } : { epicId })` **and** set `agentSessionId`. Because `epics/[epicId]/comments/route.ts` filters on `epicId` alone, a story-scoped regression report also renders in the parent epic's feed and is injected into every subsequent epic-scope build prompt (`stages.ts:475-487`). The gate already has `lastCodeSessionId` in hand for the missing link.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/verify.ts:223-231` — a report comment is written on every gate invocation, passes included**, and those comments are re-injected into every later prompt in the same run (each carrying a fenced JSON blob plus up to 2000 chars of command output). Consider persisting only failures, or trimming the payload from the prompt-visible portion.

Verified correct and worth noting: the team-build `type` fix (`build/route.ts:288`) is real — it is the only `TeamEpic` construction site in production code, so `buildTeamBuildPrompt`'s bug section now actually fires. The `worktreeRoot` fix removes the nested `.arij-worktrees/.arij-worktrees` topology. The gate is reachable from all three pipeline entry points, since night runs and both build routes go through `startPipelineRun` (`lib/pipeline/index.ts:223-229`), and `worktreePath` is persisted on the session row (`stages.ts:623`) so the gate can find it.

---

## 5. Performance

No issues found. `readRegressionConfig` batches all six keys into one `inArray` query; `parseRegressionReportComment` short-circuits on a cheap `includes`; `globToRegExp` compiles per call but over diff-sized inputs.

---

## 6. Naming Conventions

No issues found beyond §1. Setting keys match the free-form-settings convention, `lib/` files are kebab-case, the component is PascalCase under `components/verify/`.

---

## 7. Type Safety

No `any`. `RegressionFailureReason` is the single source of the vocabulary and `REPORT_REASON_LABELS` is a total `Record` over it, so a new reason is a compile error until its label exists.

**[Suggestion] `lib/verify/regression-report.ts:89-97`** — the `as RegressionReportPayload` cast is broader than the guard: `reason` and `checkedAt` are unvalidated. Impact is low (`REPORT_REASON_LABELS[unknown]` → `undefined` → empty string), but narrow the cast or widen the check.

---

## 8. Testing

30 tests across four suites, and the structure is right: pure logic (`globToRegExp`, `buildRegressionCommand`, `looksLikeStartupFailure`, the wire format) tested directly; the runner tested through an injected fake gate covering all five branches including the crash; the check tested against **real throwaway git repositories** with a forced true merge-base (`commitOnBase`) and no `main`/`master` assumption. `assertNoRedWorktreeLeft` checks both the disk *and* the porcelain record — that is the right assertion. All four AC-named reasons plus cleanup-on-exception are covered.

**[Minor] Still no test for `createVerifyGate` / `readRegressionConfig` (`lib/pipeline/verify.ts`).** That module holds the branching rules — bug-only gating, per-project key beating global, `firstParsed` skipping an unparseable per-project value, default-OFF, report persistence — and the runner tests fake the whole gate away. A regression in the precedence chain (e.g. a per-project `"false"` failing to override a global `true`) would ship green.

---

## 9. API Design

No issues found. No new HTTP routes; the toggle reuses `PATCH /api/settings` through `savePipelineSettings` with the same optimistic-update + revert + visible failure message as its siblings.

**[Suggestion] The configuration surface is still incomplete for the feature to be usable.** Only the tri-state toggle has UI. `test_file_patterns` and `bug_regression_command` are settable solely via `PATCH /api/settings` or the DB, and the `npx vitest run {files}` default is wrong for any non-vitest project — with §4's Major-1, turning the toggle on produces a wrong verdict with no in-app way to correct it.

The runner branches on `gate.ran && !gate.passed` only; the *reason* is never inspected. `command_error` means "the command could not be executed / did not really run" — a missing runner, an unresolvable config, an absent `node_modules`, a malformed command template. Each such verdict costs a full agent session, and the fix prompt (`regression-report.ts:115-129`) instructs the agent to make its test go red→green — impossible when the command never ran. After `maxFixCycles` the run terminates with *"mandatory regression test still failing"* and the ticket is parked in `in_progress`, describing a test problem that does not exist.

```
sh: 1: npx vitest run 'a.test.ts': not found     → exit 127
```

No `any`. `RegressionFailureReason` is the single source of the vocabulary and `REPORT_REASON_LABELS` is a total `Record` over it, so a new reason is a compile error until its label exists. `firstParsed`'s `parsed !== null` check correctly distinguishes a parsed `false` from "not configured" — the naive truthiness version would have broken the per-project OFF override.

## Note on the epic's stated prerequisite

The epic requires *"l'étage `verify` du pipeline (ticket lié en dépendance) doit exister"*. Confirmed by grep: no `verify_commands` machinery exists on this branch or on `main`. The branch builds the minimal verify stage itself at the natural insertion point, so "après les `verify_commands`" is satisfied vacuously. That deviation was declared by the implementing session and is not counted as a finding here.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| **Major** | **2** — configured `bug_regression_command` is unusable (JSON envelope not decoded) and misreported as `test_fails_on_branch`; `command_error` burns the agent fix budget |

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-constants.ts:153-173` — `resolveBugRegressionCheckEnabled` is still unused in production; it is now test-only.**
Grepped repo-wide: the only non-definition references are in `__tests__/verify-gate.test.ts`. The fix report describes it as "fully covered with tests", which addresses coverage but not the finding: its per-project → global → default precedence remains a second, independent implementation of `readRegressionConfig`'s rule (`verify.ts:106-125`), and the tests now pin that duplicate in place. Delete it, or have `readRegressionConfig` build a decoded map and call it.

---

## 3. Error Handling

The `finally` cleanup (`regression-check.ts:389-391`, `removeRedWorktree:408-423`) is correct and tested against a live exception. `git worktree remove --force` is sufficient for the unclean temp worktree, and neither git's removal nor `fs.rmSync` follows the `node_modules` symlink, so the epic worktree's real dependencies cannot be destroyed by cleanup. `persistReportComment` refuses to fail the stage on a DB error. `maxBuffer: 16 MiB` and the timeout/signal discrimination are right and covered by a real-timeout test.

**[Major] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:379-387` + `lib/verify/regression-constants.ts:60-69` — the environmental signature rejects genuine reds, and `aab5d75` made that verdict fatal while simultaneously widening the signature.**

`looksLikeStartupFailure` matches its eight regexes anywhere in the red run's output. The most ordinary shape of a bug fix — *add a module, import it from the new test* — produces exactly that text on the merge-base, because the module does not exist there yet: jest prints `Cannot find module './x' from '…'`, node/tsx print `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. That is the required red, and it is classified `command_error`.

This is not a hypothetical: **the test suite codifies it.** `__tests__/regression-check.test.ts:45-55` defines the `envfail` probe as a test that *fails without the fix and passes with it* — a correct red→green test — whose failure output merely mentions a module, and `:314-329` asserts the result must be `command_error`.

Before `aab5d75` that cost one fix cycle. Now `runner.ts:541-570` routes `command_error` to an immediate terminal failure with no fix dispatch and a board park. The same commit also added `/command not found/i` and `/:\s*not found/i` — the latter is broad enough to swallow any red whose output contains `Error: not found`, a plausible assertion for a "404 / missing entity" bug.

*Failure scenario:* jest project, bug fix adds `lib/normalize.ts` + `__tests__/normalize.test.ts`. Green passes. Red fails on the base with `Cannot find module '../lib/normalize'` — a textbook reproduction. Gate returns `command_error` → run terminates with `Pipeline failed: regression command error` → ticket parked back to `in_progress` → no review was ever dispatched. A correct bug branch cannot pass the gate.

*Recommendation:* the green run already proved the runner, config and dependencies work with the identical command; after that, output text alone is not evidence of an environment fault. Gate the red-side environmental verdict on the deterministic fact instead — whether the `node_modules` link could actually be established (`regression-check.ts:339-346` already knows) — and/or check that the module named in the error is not a path added by the branch diff. Separately, anchor `/:\s*not found/i` to a line start so it only catches shell "not found" lines. The `envfail` test then needs to flip to asserting `passed`.

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:243` — an infrastructure fault is reported as `no_test_in_diff`.**
A worktree with no branch checked out returns `failed("no_test_in_diff", [], "no branch checked out")`. `no_test_in_diff` is one of the three *actionable* reasons, so the runner dispatches a fix telling the agent "no test file in the branch diff — write a test that reproduces the bug" (`regression-report.ts:31-32`) when the real problem is a detached HEAD. Use `command_error`.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/index.ts:240-241` — the park reason is a false statement on two of its three call sites.**
`"Mandatory regression test rejected the branch (red → green)"` is written to the activity log for the exhaustion path (true), the `command_error` path (`runner.ts:555` — the command never ran, nothing was rejected) and the crash path (`runner.ts:525` — the gate itself broke). Pass the reason through from the caller.

---

## 4. Correctness / Functional gaps

**[Major] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:281-283, 297-314` — the deterministic environmental signal is still computed and discarded, in the one environment where it is always negative.**

`depsHint` is derived from `fs.existsSync(<epic worktree>/node_modules)` and used only to decorate a message string; the verdict rests entirely on `looksLikeStartupFailure`. Meanwhile `createWorktree` (`lib/git/manager.ts:59-104`) does a bare `git worktree add` and never installs dependencies, and `grep -rn node_modules lib/ app/` returns only `regression-check.ts` and `lib/documents/scan-constants.ts:30` — **nothing in Arij ever populates `node_modules` in an epic worktree.**

So on every production bug ticket with the toggle ON, the green run executes the default `npx vitest run {files}` in a tree with no dependencies. Whether the operator gets an honest `command_error` or the agent gets blamed with `test_fails_on_branch` depends on whether that particular runner's output happens to match one of eight regexes — and the likeliest vitest text for this case, `Failed to resolve import "…". Does the file exist?`, is not among them.

*Failure scenario:* toggle ON, bug ticket, fresh epic worktree. Green fails for want of dependencies with a message outside the pattern list → `test_fails_on_branch` → the fix prompt tells the agent *"the regression test fails on the branch — the fix does not work yet"* → the agent chases a failure that does not exist → after `maxFixCycles` the run terminates and the ticket is parked. The unit suite cannot catch this: the probe (`regression-check.test.ts:37-42`) is dependency-free by construction.

*Recommendation:* make the absent-`node_modules` fact part of the verdict rather than the wording — if the epic worktree has no `node_modules` and the green run failed, that is `command_error`, deterministically. Better still, link the main repo's `node_modules` into the epic worktree the way `regression-check.ts:339-346` already links it into the red one; that is the difference between a feature that reports honestly and a feature that works.

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-check.ts:287` vs `:353-357` — green tests the working tree, red tests the committed blob.**
`d90a6fa` correctly moved the red copy to `git show <head>:<file>`, but the green run still executes against `input.repoPath`'s working tree. The two halves of the proof therefore describe different states of the branch.

*Failure scenario:* the agent commits the test file but leaves the fix unstaged (partial `git add`). Green passes — the working tree has the fix. Red fails — the base plus the committed test. The gate reports **passed** for a branch whose committed state is red, and the pipeline proceeds to review and, under Full Auto, to merge. *Recommendation:* run `git status --porcelain` in the worktree and either refuse or surface a dirty-tree warning in the report; the gate's whole value is that it is mechanical.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:516-534` — the gate-crash handler parks the board without knowing whether the gate even applies.**
`createVerifyGate` already wraps `runRegressionCheck` (`verify.ts:198-219`) and `persistReportComment` in their own try/catch, so the *only* throws that reach the runner come from the three unguarded DB reads that decide applicability — the `epics` lookup (`verify.ts:163`), `readRegressionConfig` (`:168`) and the session lookup (`:173-185`). A transient error there during a **feature** epic's pipeline now fails the run *and* pulls that feature out of `review` with a reason claiming a regression test rejected it. *Recommendation:* make the gate total — wrap the closure body and return `notRun()` when applicability cannot be established — so the crash branch becomes unreachable.

**[Minor] `components/verify/RegressionReportBlock.tsx:18-21` — a comment that merely *contains* a report is replaced by the block, and its own prose is dropped.**
The component renders the parsed payload and never renders `content`. Any comment carrying the marker plus a `json` fence is swallowed whole. That path is reachable by construction: report comments are persisted as ordinary ticket comments and injected verbatim into every subsequent build/fix prompt (`stages.ts:475-490`), so an agent quoting one back into its own result comment loses that comment's entire body in the UI. Render the block *plus* the surrounding markdown, or strip only the report region.

**[Minor] `lib/pipeline/verify.ts:221-233` — a report comment is written on every gate invocation, passes included,** and `formatRegressionReportComment` (`regression-report.ts:66-71`) emits `detail` twice — once in a fenced block, once inside the JSON payload. Those comments then feed back into every later prompt in the same run. Persist only failures, or keep the JSON payload out of the prompt-visible portion.

**[Minor] `lib/verify/regression-report.ts:150` — the fix prompt hard-codes the default patterns.**
The instruction lists `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**` regardless of the project's configured `test_file_patterns`, which the gate has in hand (`verify.ts:121`) and does not pass. On a project with narrower patterns the agent is told the wrong rule for the check it must satisfy. `BUG_RED_GREEN_SECTION` (`prompt-builder.ts:81-93`) has the same gap.

Verified correct and worth noting: the settings JSON round-trip is genuinely fixed and pinned by a test that seeds rows exactly as `PATCH /api/settings` does (`verify-gate.test.ts:31-40, 177-192`) — `parseBugRegressionCommand` and `parseTestFilePatterns` now decode the envelope; the story-scope comment now sets `userStoryId` alone plus `agentSessionId`, matching `finalizeCodeSession` (`stages.ts:794-798`), and no longer leaks into the epic feed or epic-scope prompts; `type: epic.type` at `build/route.ts:288` is the only `TeamEpic` construction site in production code; the committed-blob copy, `core.quotePath=false` and the `worktreeRoot` topology fix are all correct and covered by discriminating tests; the temp worktree is recognized by the generic orphan detector (`lib/git/worktrees.ts:82-88`, prunable-or-missing), satisfying the epic's constraint; the exhaustion park is guarded on the ticket actually sitting in `review`/`done`, `review → in_progress` is a legal edge (`engine.ts:22`), and same-status transitions are always valid (`engine.ts:141,153`) so the epic no-op inside `transitionReviewRejected` cannot refuse.

---

## 5. Performance

No issues found in the data paths: `readRegressionConfig` batches all six keys into one `inArray` query, `parseRegressionReportComment` short-circuits on a cheap `includes`, `globToRegExp` compiles per call but over diff-sized inputs.

**[Suggestion]** The gate runs the test command **twice** per successful code stage, each with a hard-coded 10-minute ceiling — `verify.ts:199-211` never passes `commandTimeoutMs`, so `DEFAULT_BUG_REGRESSION_TIMEOUT_MS` always applies. The input field exists but no setting key feeds it.

---

## 6. Naming Conventions

No issues found beyond §1. Setting keys match the free-form-settings convention, `lib/` files are kebab-case, the component is PascalCase under `components/verify/`.

---

## 7. Type Safety

No `any`. `RegressionFailureReason` is the single source of the vocabulary and `REPORT_REASON_LABELS` is a total `Record` over it, so a new reason is a compile error until its label exists. `firstParsed`'s `parsed !== null` check correctly distinguishes a parsed `false` from "not configured". The round-3 suggestion is resolved: `parseRegressionReportComment` (`regression-report.ts:93-123`) now validates `status`, `reason`, `testFiles`, `detail` and `checkedAt` and builds the result field by field, with no cast.

---

## 8. Testing

52 tests across six suites, all passing, and the structure is right: pure logic tested directly; the runner tested through an injected fake gate covering all six branches including the crash, the `command_error` short-circuit and the park callback's exact-once semantics; the check tested against **real throwaway git repositories** with a forced merge-base and no `main`/`master` assumption; `assertNoRedWorktreeLeft` checks disk *and* the porcelain record. The round-3 gap is closed: `__tests__/verify-gate.test.ts` now covers settings precedence, bug-only gating and report scope/session linkage against real DB rows written the way the API writes them. Full suite: 356 files / 4094 tests green.

**[Major — see §3] `__tests__/regression-check.test.ts:45-55, 314-329` — one test asserts the wrong behavior.** The `envfail` probe is, by its own construction, a test that reproduces the bug (red on base, green on branch); the assertion requires the gate to reject it as `command_error`. Whatever fix lands for §3's Major must flip this expectation, not preserve it.

**[Minor] No coverage for the `no_test_in_diff`-vs-infrastructure confusion or for a dirty worktree** (§4's first two minors) — both are silent-wrong-answer paths, which is exactly the class this gate exists to eliminate.

---

## 9. API Design

No new HTTP routes; the toggle reuses `PATCH /api/settings` through `savePipelineSettings` (`app/settings/page.tsx:285-294`) with the same optimistic-update + revert + visible failure message as its siblings.

**[Suggestion] The configuration surface is still incomplete.** Only the tri-state toggle has UI; `test_file_patterns` and `bug_regression_command` are settable solely through `PATCH /api/settings` or the DB. The encoding trap is fixed, but the default `npx vitest run {files}` remains wrong for any non-vitest project, with no in-app way to correct it. The toggle also writes the global key only, so a per-project override set via the API silently disagrees with what the checkbox displays.

**[Suggestion] `regression-check.ts:143-145` — `quotePath` is POSIX-only.** The `'` → `'\''` escaping correctly neutralises agent-controlled filenames and is tested, but under `cmd.exe` single quotes are not quoting characters.

---

## Note on the epic's stated prerequisite

The epic requires *"l'étage `verify` du pipeline (ticket lié en dépendance) doit exister"*. Confirmed by grep: no `verify_commands` machinery exists on this branch or on `main`. The branch builds the minimal verify stage itself at the natural insertion point, so "après les `verify_commands`" is satisfied vacuously. That deviation was declared by the implementing session and is not counted as a finding.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| **Major** | **2** — the environmental signature rejects genuine reds and that verdict is now fatal; the deterministic `node_modules` signal is discarded in the one environment where it is always negative |
| Minor | 9 |
| Suggestion | 4 |

Three fix passes have done real work, and this round confirms most of it: the settings JSON round-trip is fixed *and* pinned by a test that writes rows the way the API does, `command_error` no longer burns the agent's fix budget, the story-scoped report no longer leaks into the epic feed and now carries its session link, the parser cast is gone, and the board is parked on rejection. Verification is clean across the board.

What blocks acceptance is that both halves of the red→green proof still decide "environment fault" versus "real verdict" by pattern-matching command output, while the one fact that settles it — whether dependencies are present — is computed on line 281 and thrown away. On the red side that misfires on the most ordinary bug fix there is (add a module, import it from the new test): the merge-base cannot resolve the module, which *is* the reproduction, and `aab5d75` turned that misfire from one wasted fix cycle into an immediate run kill plus a board park. The `envfail` fixture makes this explicit — it describes a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, and the suite requires the gate to reject it. On the green side the same heuristic guards a command running in a worktree that Arij guarantees has no `node_modules`, so the honest `command_error` and the wrong `test_fails_on_branch` are separated by a coin flip on the runner's phrasing.

Both resolve at the same place and are small: use the `node_modules` fact as the verdict rather than as prose, and drop the red-side text heuristic now that a successful green has already proven the runner works. `no_test_in_diff`-for-a-detached-HEAD, the park reason string, the crash-path applicability guard, and the working-tree/committed-blob asymmetry are worth folding into the same pass.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Dreaming : distillation transversale des sessions (mémoire projet)
epics.description:
## Contexte
`lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts` distille session par session. « Dreaming » (annonce majeure de Code with Claude 2026) est la passe transversale : analyser en batch les N dernières sessions de PLUSIEURS tickets — succès ET échecs — pour découvrir ce qu'aucune session isolée ne montre : erreurs récurrentes, pièges du codebase, stratégies gagnantes. Rakuten annonce −90 % d'erreurs de premier passage avec ce motif.

## À construire
1. **Collecteur** `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts` : sélectionner les sessions terminées récentes du projet (fenêtre : depuis le dernier dream, plafonnée à ~30 sessions / 14 jours ; types build/ticket_build/team_build/review/fix) et construire un digest compact PAR session : métadonnées (ticket, agentType, provider, outcome, durée, coût), verdicts de review, findings `[critical]`/`[major]`, entrées `transition_refused`, rapports forensic, fin de la réponse finale. NE PAS embarquer les chunks bruts complets — budget de taille dur sur le digest (~60 Ko) avec troncature équitable par session.
2. **Session de dream** : builder `buildDreamingPrompt` dans `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts` — session en mode plan qui reçoit la mémoire actuelle + le digest et réécrit la mémoire projet (document `kind='memory'`, `lib/documents/memory.ts`). Structure imposée en sections : pièges du codebase / erreurs récurrentes des agents / stratégies qui marchent / consignes de build. Même garde que `spec-auto-rewrite.ts` : la mémoire n'est remplacée QUE si la session livre réellement.
3. **Plafond mémoire** : étendre `MEMORY_MAX_LENGTH` (`lib/documents/memory-constants.ts`) de 4000 à 8000 caractères — la mémoire dreamée est plus riche. Vérifier l'impact sur les prompts (injection quasi partout via `memorySection()`).
4. **Déclencheurs** : (a) bouton manuel — `POST /api/projects/:projectId/memory/dream` ; (b) fin de night run si setting `dreaming_after_night_run` (tri-state, défaut OFF), en héritant du `batchRunId` du run pour rester sous le cost cap (même piège documenté que memory-distill).
5. **Garde-fous** : jamais deux dreams concurrents sur un projet ; no-op silencieux journalisé si aucune session nouvelle depuis le dernier dream ; snapshot de l'ancienne mémoire conservé (document archive ou équivalent — trancher et documenter) ; notification deep-link « mémoire mise à jour par Dreaming » avec résumé du changement.

## Contraintes
- Session en mode plan (lecture seule), agentType dédié `dreaming` — l'intégrer PARTOUT où `memory_distill` est listé (watchdog thresholds, classification d'outcome, constantes) : chercher les usages existants pour la liste exhaustive.
- Ne bloque aucun ticket : pas d'epicId sur la ligne de session (même astuce que `lib/pipeline/forensic.ts`).
- Tests vitest : collecteur (fenêtre, plafonds, troncature équitable), garde anti-concurrence, no-op sans sessions nouvelles, non-remplacement si la session ne livre pas.

comments.content:
## Review findings corrigées — 5 major + 3 minor, 4129 tests verts

4 commits (8086a0f, 390819d, a0590e2, 20dff75). Détail par finding :

### Major 1 + 2 — fenêtre de collecte (390819d)
Les deux findings avaient la même racine : **la borne et le filtre ne répondaient pas à la même question**. La borne disait « quand le dernier dream s'est *terminé* », le filtre disait « quand une session a *démarré* ».

- **Terminal time** : une session appartient à une fenêtre par le moment où elle est **devenue une preuve** (`sessionTerminalMs` = `endedAt`/`completedAt`), pas par son démarrage. Un build commencé avant un dream et fini après tombait dans le trou entre deux fenêtres et était perdu définitivement. C'est aussi la nouvelle clé de tri, donc le plafond de 30 garde les sessions les plus fraîchement terminées.
- **Cutoff persisté** : nouveau `dreaming_last_cutoff:<projectId>` contenant l'**instant de collecte**, écrit à un seul endroit — *après* que le document mémoire a réellement été remplacé. `findLastDreamAt()` (dérivé de la ligne de session) est supprimé : une ligne `completed`/`answered` ne prouve rien sur la mémoire. Un save qui échoue laisse le cutoff intact → le dream suivant relit les mêmes sessions. Relire coûte quelques tokens, sauter perd la leçon pour toujours : l'égalité va à la relecture.

**Tests** : la session « à cheval » est épinglée des deux côtés (incluse si elle finit après le cutoff, exclue si elle avait déjà fini), et l'échec de persistance est **réel, non mocké** — je squatte le nom de fichier unique du document mémoire (`Project memory`) pour faire lever `saveProjectMemory` comme le ferait une erreur disque, puis je vérifie que le cutoff n'a pas bougé, qu'aucune notification n'a menti, et que le retry retrouve bien la session.

### Major 3 — verrou partagé entre les deux writers (8086a0f)
`lib/workflow/memory-writer-lock.ts` : un seul prédicat `hasPendingMemoryWriter()` consulté par **les deux** chemins de dispatch. Module dédié parce que faire importer l'un par l'autre créerait un cycle. `hasPendingMemoryDistill` garde son nom (c'est la garde du flux distill) mais délègue.

Les deux dispatches **re-vérifient en synchrone juste avant l'insert** : la première vérification tourne avant `await resolveAgentPrompt`, donc seule elle ne rend le verrou que « généralement » vrai. Le distill lève `MEMORY_WRITER_BUSY_MESSAGE` à cet endroit, que sa route mappe en **409** — perdre cette course est un conflit, pas une faute.

**Tests** : dream refusé pendant un distill queued, distill refusé pendant un dream running, et une course `Promise.allSettled` dream+distill où exactement une ligne de session est créée.

### Major 4 — cost cap du night run (a0590e2)
Le cap et l'`abortReason` sont maintenant **passés explicitement** au trigger, mesurés à l'instant du finish, et ré-appliqués par `evaluateNightRunDreamGuards()` avant tout dispatch :
- cap déjà atteint → refus journalisé ;
- run stoppé par l'utilisateur → refus (« stopper ce run » veut dire « arrêter d'y dépenser ») ;
- **circuit breaker → autorisé** : un run qui a échoué jusqu'au breaker est précisément celui dont les leçons valent le plus.

Le seul chiffre où le dream ne peut toujours pas apparaître est la **notification** de résumé matinal, envoyée avant qu'il démarre. C'est l'arbitrage assumé, désormais écrit dans les deux docblocks : le résumé ne doit pas attendre des minutes, et son deep-link ouvre la vue détail qui re-dérive le total depuis la base — laquelle, elle, inclut le dream.

### Major 5 — bouton Dream et édits non sauvegardés (20dff75)
Désactivé pendant `dirty`/`saving`, avec un `title` et une ligne inline expliquant pourquoi (l'agent réécrit la mémoire **sauvegardée**, et la navigation vers la session jetterait les édits en cours).

### Minor 1 — forensic attribué par story (8086a0f)
`ticket_comments.userStoryId` est chargé et l'appariement est une **égalité stricte de scope** : une session story-scopée ne réclame que le post-mortem de sa story, une session epic-scopée que les rapports epic-scopés (null des deux côtés). Le pipeline dépose le commentaire avec le `userStoryId` de la session morte, donc l'égalité est le test honnête. Deux tests : deux stories du même epic aux fenêtres chevauchantes reçoivent chacune *son* diagnostic (avec le rapport de B déposé **avant** celui de A, pour que la version epic-only échoue), et un rapport epic-scopé n'est jamais collé sur une session story-scopée.

### Minor 2 — nettoyage des settings (390819d)
`dreaming_after_night_run:<id>` **et** `dreaming_last_cutoff:<id>` rejoignent `perProjectSettingKeys()` ; le test d'exhaustivité est mis à jour.

### Minor 3 — documents mémoire protégés (20dff75)
Filtrés à la frontière partagée via `isInternalMemoryDocKind` (mémoire vive + archive) : la route GET ne les sert plus, la page applique la même règle, et la route DELETE **les refuse** — de sorte qu'une requête faite à la main ne peut pas non plus atteindre le chemin de suppression générique.

### Vérification
`tsc --noEmit` propre, eslint propre sur les fichiers touchés (le warning `useEffect`/`loadDocs` de `documents/page.tsx` préexiste, ligne non modifiée), suite complète **353 fichiers / 4129 tests** (+19 depuis la review).

Un point d'hygiène : les changements de `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts` (verrou, terminal time, forensic, cutoff) sont répartis entre 8086a0f et 390819d parce que le fichier est unique — les messages restent lisibles finding par finding mais un `git show` par commit ne les isole pas parfaitement.

comments.content:
All 8 review findings are fixed, committed in 4 commits, with the full suite green.

**The two window findings had one root cause** — the lower bound and the filter were answering different questions. The bound said "when the last dream *finished*"; the filter said "when a session *started*". Fixing either alone would have left the gap, so both moved: a session now belongs to a window by when it reached a **terminal state**, and the bound is a persisted `dreaming_last_cutoff` row holding the **collection instant**, written only after the memory document actually changed. A dream that answered but failed to save no longer advances the window past evidence nothing learned from.

For that one I wrote a **real, un-mocked failure**: squatting the memory document's unique filename makes `saveProjectMemory` throw exactly as a disk or constraint error would, and the test then proves the cutoff stayed put, no notification lied, and the retry still finds the session.

**The shared writer lock** (`lib/workflow/memory-writer-lock.ts`) is one predicate both dispatch paths consult, plus a synchronous re-check immediately before each insert — the first check runs before an `await`, so alone it only makes the lock usually hold. The distill throws there and its route maps that to 409, since losing the race is a conflict rather than a fault.

**On the night-run cap** I made one judgement call worth flagging: a **circuit-breaker abort still dreams**. A cost cap and a user stop both mean "stop spending", so those refuse — but a run that failed its way to a breaker trip is exactly the one whose lessons are worth having. And one limit remains by design: the dream cannot appear in the morning-summary *notification*, which is sent before it starts. The summary must not wait minutes for a dream; its deep link opens the detail view, which re-derives the total from the database and does include it. That trade is now stated in both docblocks rather than left implicit.

Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on touched files (the one remaining `useEffect`/`loadDocs` warning is pre-existing on a line I didn't touch), **353 files / 4129 tests passing** — 19 more than before the review.

One hygiene note: because `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts` is a single file, its changes are split across commits 8086a0f and 390819d, so `git show` per commit doesn't isolate them perfectly even though the messages read finding by finding.

The ticket is still `in_progress` and I've posted the fix report to it. I have not attempted the transition to `review` — the same session-running refusal from last time would apply, and that promotion is the orchestrator's to make once this session ends.

## Round 2 corrigée — 2 major + 5 minor, 4139 tests verts

3 commits : fdb12de, 366dd3e, 4b583fb.

### Major 1 — snapshot et remplacement atomiques (fdb12de)
`archiveProjectMemory` + `saveProjectMemory` étaient deux instructions. Un save qui lève laissait l'archive **déjà écrasée** par un texte qui est toujours la mémoire vive : on brûlait la seule copie de secours de l'utilisateur en échange d'une réécriture qui n'a pas eu lieu — un mode d'échec strictement pire que ne rien faire.

`replaceProjectMemoryWithSnapshot()` enveloppe les deux écritures dans **une transaction** : soit la mémoire a bougé et l'archive contient ce qu'elle remplaçait, soit rien n'a bougé.

**Test au niveau du stockage, où l'échec se force honnêtement.** Un premier essai côté dispatch ne marchait pas : avec une mémoire vive présente, le save passe par UPDATE, qui ne peut pas violer la contrainte d'unicité — et si je supprime la ligne vive pour forcer l'INSERT, `previous` devient null et l'archive ne s'écrit plus du tout. Le scénario du finding n'était donc reproductible qu'en injectant l'échec **sur l'UPDATE** (ce qu'est précisément une erreur disque/IO en production), via un proxy de db. Deux cas : une première archive ne doit pas apparaître, et une archive **existante** doit toujours contenir l'ancienne mémoire plutôt que le texte vif qu'une version en deux temps y aurait estampé.

### Major 2 — forensic attribué à la session terminale la plus proche (366dd3e)
Le post-mortem était réclamé par la **première** session (ordre chronologique) dont la fenêtre le couvrait. Avec un stage échoué → rejoué → ré-échoué, les deux tentatives couvrent le diagnostic du retry : la première le prenait, et le dream raisonnait alors sur un échec appartenant à une autre révision du code.

`assignForensicComments()` résout le lot **en une passe globale** — une passe par session ne peut pas comparer les candidates entre elles. Pour chaque diagnostic : la session de même scope la plus proche, en préférant celle qui était **déjà terminée** (c'est pour les morts que le pipeline dépose des post-mortems). Toujours au plus un dans chaque sens.

**Régressions** : une paire rerun où les deux fenêtres se chevauchent et où seul « le plus proche » les départage, et un diagnostic isolé qui doit atterrir sur le run qui venait de finir.

### Minor 1 — `listProjectDocuments()` (4b583fb)
Il renvoyait encore les documents mémoire, et c'est lui qui alimente la résolution des `@mentions` — donc `@Project memory` pouvait résoudre vers un document et injecter une **seconde** copie d'un texte que `memorySection()` met déjà dans chaque prompt. Filtré à cette frontière unique.

### Minor 2 — contrat 409 de la route dream (4b583fb)
La course perdue au dernier moment renvoyait 200 + `dispatched:false`, en contradiction avec le contrat de la route elle-même. Mappée en **409 `DREAMING_PENDING`** : « un writer tient la mémoire » a désormais une seule réponse, pas deux.

### Minor 3 — classification dans le monitor (4b583fb)
`dreaming` et `memory_distill` sont des lignes en mode plan, donc l'heuristique de mode les classait en review et le monitor affichait « Reviewing » pendant qu'un agent réécrivait la mémoire projet. Nouveau type d'activité **`memory`** (union serveur + client), icône dédiée, et libellés honnêtes : « Dreaming: rewriting project memory » / « Distilling project memory ». Aucun des deux ne porte d'epicId, donc il n'y a pas de ticket à nommer — le type d'agent *est* toute l'information.

### Minor 4 — chargement de la carte mémoire (4b583fb)
`res.ok` n'était pas vérifié : un 404/500 s'affichait en éditeur vide, ce qui se lit « ce projet n'a pas de mémoire » — et sauvegarder depuis là aurait effacé une mémoire qui n'avait fait qu'échouer à charger. L'erreur serveur est maintenant remontée.

### Minor 5 — isolation du test (4b583fb)
Le setting **global** survit à un test et tous les projets le lisent. Nettoyé dans `beforeEach`, et le test « per-project true / global off » pose son global explicitement, puisque c'est justement l'override battant un global OFF qui est l'assertion.

### Vérification
`tsc --noEmit` propre, suite complète **353 fichiers / 4139 tests** (+10). Eslint propre sur les fichiers touchés, à une exception **préexistante** : `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts` déclenche `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` — vérifié en lintant la version de `HEAD` du fichier, l'erreur y est déjà (même ligne, décalée par les 8 lignes d'union que j'ai ajoutées). Je ne l'ai pas corrigée : c'est hors du périmètre de cet epic et de ces findings.
