comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic: Routines (cron interne + surveillance CI des PRs, autofix opt-in)

**Scope reviewed:** `c2ac46d`, `0f4f9e9`, `a099af1`, `4bfd596` against merge-base `269e399` — 38 files, +4630/−14.

**Verification run:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; the 12 touched test files (342 tests) pass.

---

## Overall architecture

The delegation discipline the epic asked for is genuinely respected. Every kind hands off to a canonical service — the batch route in `dag`+`pipeline` mode (`lib/routines/actions.ts:51`), `syncProjectGitHubIssues` behind `isGitHubIssueSyncDue`, and the ordinary epic build route for autofix (`lib/routines/ci-autofix.ts:30`). Nothing is reimplemented.

Three things are notably well done:

- **Idempotency key namespacing.** `ci-autofix:<epic>:pr-N:<sha>` on `agent_sessions.batch_run_id` cannot be confused with night runs — every consumer filters on `night_%` or `isNightRunId` (`lib/night/summary.ts:296`, `app/api/dashboard/summary/route.ts:61`). Verified across all call sites.
- **Double-checked claim in the build route.** The `findExistingCiAutofixAttempt` re-run immediately before the no-await transition/insert block (`build/route.ts:298`) closes the real window that the first lookup leaves open across worktree preparation.
- **Fail-closed opt-in.** `isCiAutofixEnabled` returns `false` on a settings read exception, and `classifyPullRequestCi` returns `pending` (not `passing`) when no CI signal exists — both are the safe direction.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comments explain *why* (the claim-before-dispatch ordering, the tilde fence guard, the retained-observation rationale) rather than restating code.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `lib/notifications/create.ts:99`: duplicated `ROUTINE_KIND_LABELS`.** A second label map alongside `lib/routines/constants.ts:23`, differing only by including `dreaming`. Two maps for one concept will drift. Widen the constants map to all `ROUTINE_KIND` values and import it.

**Minor — `lib/routines/settings.ts:55`: hand-rolled settings upsert.** Select-then-insert/update where the codebase already has the one-statement idiom (`lib/github/label-mapping.ts:61`, `.onConflictDoUpdate({ target: settings.key, … })`). `parseBooleanSetting` also re-derives the tri-state shape of `parsePipelineEnabledSetting` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:80`).

**Minor — `components/routines/RoutinesSettings.tsx:325`: shadcn primitives bypassed.** Raw `<select>`, raw `<input type="checkbox">` and a hand-rolled `role="tablist"` (with no `tabpanel` and a single always-selected tab) while `components/ui/select.tsx`, `checkbox.tsx` and `tabs.tsx` exist. CLAUDE.md states components use the `components/ui/` primitives.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:246`: one bad PR aborts the whole sweep.** `fetchPullRequestCi` and `launchAutofix` throw straight out of the `for` loop, so every epic after the failing one is silently skipped for that cycle. This becomes permanent for a plausible state: an epic in `done` with a stale `pr_status = "open"` fails `isBuildableStatus` in the build route → 400 → `launchCiAutofixSession` throws → CI watch is dead for every other PR in the project, every cycle. Wrap the per-epic body in `try/catch`, count failures, continue, and report them in the result message.

**Major — `lib/routines/ci-autofix.ts:30` / `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1024`: the autofix loop never closes.** Only the PR-creation route and the manual push route call `pushGitBranch` — nothing pushes after a build session. The autofix commits locally, so the PR head SHA never changes: CI stays red, `ci_watch` will not re-notify (same SHA, `failureNotified`) and will not re-attempt (`autofixAttempted`). The fix sits on a local branch indefinitely with nothing telling the user. Auto-pushing would contradict the project's git-safety rule, so the fix is a signal: emit a notification/activity entry on a successful autofix stating the branch carries an unpushed fix for PR #N.

Beyond those: `notifySafely`, the `markFinished` failure path, and the log-fetch fallback to `logTail: null` are all correctly defensive.

## 4. Performance

**Major — `lib/routines/scheduler.ts:183`: routine notifications flood the notification table.** Every trigger notifies, including no-op `ci_watch` polls. At the default 15-minute interval that is ~96 rows/day/project against a global `MAX_NOTIFICATIONS = 200` (`lib/notifications/create.ts:21`), which prunes oldest-first. Within about two days routine chatter evicts every real alert — including the CI-failure notifications this epic exists to deliver. The epic did ask for "chaque déclenchement notifié", but that requirement was written for daily kinds; a 15-minute poll makes it pathological. Notify on `failed`, and on `completed` only when something actually happened.

**Major — `lib/routines/ci-autofix-shared.ts:53`: unbounded CI evidence → E2BIG.** The payload validator accepts 100 failures × 20 000 chars, and `fetchPullRequestCiFailureEvidence` tails 8 000 chars per check with no global cap. `lib/providers/codex.ts:152` passes the prompt as a *single argv element*, and Linux caps one argument at `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (128 KB). A CI matrix with 17+ failing jobs produces a prompt that kills the session before it starts — the failure mode already on record for this repo. Add a combined budget (e.g. 12 checks / ~60 KB) in the fetcher and enforce the same ceiling in `parseCiAutofixPayload`.

**Minor — `lib/github/pull-requests.ts:276`: no pagination.** `checks.listForRef` and `getCombinedStatusForRef` use `per_page: 100` without `octokit.paginate`. Past 100 check runs the response truncates silently, and a failing check on page 2 classifies the PR as *passing* — a false green. Use `octokit.paginate`.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. Files, exports and settings keys follow the established patterns (`<key>:<projectId>`, correctly registered in `perProjectSettingKeys`).

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; the single `as unknown as` (`pull-requests.ts:362`) is a justified narrowing of an Octokit response body. `parseStoredState` and `parseCiAutofixPayload` validate untrusted JSON field-by-field rather than casting. The `as RoutineDto` casts in `crud.ts:227` are a mild smell (they encode "we just inserted an available kind") but are correct.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is strong: dueness across all four axes, restart replay, concurrent-sweep guard, per-SHA notification identity, green-interlude retention, autofix rearm on new SHA, and a real integration test through the scheduler queue asserting prompt content, `batch_run_id`, monitor visibility, and the activity reason.

**Minor — `__tests__/ci-watch.test.ts:252` locks in a questionable behaviour.** "does not retry a busy target until GitHub reports a new head SHA" asserts that a `target_busy` skip consumes the one-shot `(PR, SHA)` claim permanently. The common trigger is precisely a transient one: CI fails right after the build session that pushed, while that session (or its review) is still running on the epic. The autofix is then never attempted for that failure. `getRunningSessionForTarget` should cause a *deferral*, not consumption of the claim — leave `autofixAttempted` false on `reason === "target_busy"` and invert the test.

Gaps: no test for a mid-sweep GitHub error, and none for the first-fire-after-creation case below.

## 8. API Design

`{ data }` / `{ error }` shapes, 201 on create, 400/404 mapped from typed errors, Zod `.strict()` — all consistent. Two notes:

**Major — `lib/routines/scheduler.ts:61`: a daily routine fires immediately when its time has already passed.** A routine created (or re-enabled, or re-timed earlier) after its `timeOfDay` with `last_run_at` null is due on the next 60 s sweep. Creating a "22:00 night run" at 23:15 launches an unattended, cost-bearing night run within a minute — the user asked for tonight, not now. Seed `last_run_at` at creation when today's slot has already passed.

**Minor — `lib/db/migrations/0033_routines.sql:24`: no uniqueness on `(project_id, kind)`.** Nothing in the DB, the CRUD layer or the UI prevents two `ci_watch` routines on one project. Each keeps its own `ciWatchState`, so the same failing PR head produces two notifications (the build-route dedupe does correctly block a second session). Migration and schema bookkeeping are otherwise correct: hand-written, monotonic `when` (1786713000000 > 1786712900000), and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` needs no `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` entry.

**Minor — `lib/github/pull-requests.ts:99`: non-failures classified as failures.** `action_required` (a check awaiting manual approval), `cancelled` and `stale` sit in `FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS`, so they raise a red alert and, with autofix on, dispatch a code-writing agent against a condition with nothing to fix.

**Minor — `lib/routines/constants.ts:51`: misleading default config.** `github_issue_sync` is scheduled daily by `timeOfDay`, so its `intervalMinutes` is only the TTL guard and is always satisfied once a day — yet the UI hint presents it as the schedule.

**Minor — `components/routines/RoutinesSettings.tsx:159`: toggling Enabled discards unsaved edits.** `toggleEnabled` PATCHes only `enabled`; the refreshed `routine` prop re-runs the reset effect and silently wipes typed kind/time/config. Key the effect on `routine.id` and merge `enabled` from the response.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 5 |
| Minor | 9 |
| Suggestion | 0 |

The design is right and the durability reasoning is careful — the claim ordering, the SHA guard, the `batch_run_id` namespacing and the fail-closed opt-in all hold up under inspection. What blocks it is operational: the notification flood makes the inbox unusable within days of enabling `ci_watch`, one unreachable PR silently kills polling for the whole project, an oversized evidence prompt kills the session on argv-based providers, the autofix commit never reaches GitHub with nothing saying so, and a routine can fire a paid night run within a minute of being created.

A remediation plan with concrete fixes and required tests is at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-cosmic-widget.md`.

Note: plan mode is active in this session, which blocks writes — so these findings are **not** filed via `submit_findings`. Say the word once plan mode is off and I'll file all 14 with their file/line anchors.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review — Epic: Routines (cron interne + surveillance CI des PRs, autofix opt-in)

**Scope:** `c2ac46d`, `0f4f9e9`, `a099af1`, `4bfd596`, `73eaf5d`, `68543b2`, `5f29b93`, `a12d048`, `2206b6f` against merge-base `269e399` — 40 files, +5626/−26. Worktree clean.

One finding is new and is a **regression introduced by the last hardening commit**; one is a narrowed but still-open version of the notification-flood finding.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — four duplications inside the new module.** `DAILY_KINDS` (`lib/routines/scheduler.ts:13`) duplicates `isDailyRoutineKind` (`lib/routines/constants.ts:45`); `TIME_OF_DAY_PATTERN` and `isSameLocalDay` exist in both `scheduler.ts:17,20` and `crud.ts:11,223`; `parseConfig` is byte-identical in `lib/routines/actions.ts:113` and `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:135`. All four belong in `constants.ts`.

**Minor — `lib/routines/settings.ts:11`.** `parseBooleanSetting` still re-implements the exported `parsePipelineEnabledSetting` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:80`) — same tri-state contract, same accepted encodings. Third time raised.

## 3. Error Handling

The per-PR `try/catch` (`ci-watch.ts:249`), `notifySafely`, the `markFinished` failure path, the `logTail: null` fallback and the boot reconciliation are all correctly defensive. One ordering nit:

**Minor — `lib/notifications/create.ts:407`.** The revised comment says a message-bearing row means "a specialized completion signal such as a local CI autofix awaiting a push", implying it suppresses the generic row. It cannot: `markSessionTerminal` → `emitSessionCompleted` → `createNotificationFromSession` runs first and inserts "Build completed" with a NULL message, and only then does `build/route.ts:442` create the push signal. The user gets both, and the comment describes an ordering the route does not produce.

## 4. Performance

**Major — `lib/routines/scheduler.ts:270` / `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:375`: a persistent error still notifies on every poll.** `a12d048` silenced quiet polls, but not repeated errors. `runCiWatchRoutine` sets `shouldNotify: true` whenever `failedPullRequestNumbers.length > 0`, and a throwing `fetchPullRequestCi` is *not* self-limiting — an expired PAT, a deleted or transferred PR, a renamed repo, or a 403 reproduces every cycle. A thrown action (`"Project is not connected to a GitHub repository"`, `ci-watch.ts:242`) reaches `run()`'s catch, which calls `notifySafely` unconditionally. At the default `intervalMinutes: 15` that is ~96 identical rows/day/project against a global `MAX_NOTIFICATIONS = 200` pruned oldest-first (`lib/notifications/create.ts:22`, `:981`). Within about two days the chatter evicts every real alert — including the `createCiWatchFailureNotification` rows this epic exists to deliver. Suppress repeats of an unchanged error signature; keep `lastStatus`, the console line and the UI badge unconditional.

**Minor — `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:306`.** `fetchFailureEvidence` still runs before `launchAutofix`, so while a target stays busy every 15-minute poll re-downloads up to 12 Actions job logs and discards them. Second time raised.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`; untrusted JSON is validated field-by-field in `parseStoredState` and `parseCiAutofixPayload`. But see finding 8.1 — `tsc` is clean *because* the octokit types assert a normalisation that does not happen at runtime, so `failedChecks: string[]` receives `undefined`.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is strong at the unit level: dueness across all four axes, restart replay, concurrent-sweep guard, per-SHA notification identity, green-interlude retention, autofix rearm on new SHA, mid-sweep GitHub error, quiet-poll suppression, interrupted-run recovery, and the `target_busy` deferral.

**Major (contributing) — `__tests__/github-pr-ci.test.ts:37`.** The suite mocks `octokit.paginate` with a hand-written normaliser (`data.check_runs ?? data.statuses ?? []`) that unwraps the combined-status object — which is precisely what real octokit does *not* do. That mock is what let finding 8.1 through a green run. Mock at the `octokit.request` / `hook.wrap` layer, or import the real `normalizePaginatedListResponse`.

Gaps: no test asserts `state === "passing"` end-to-end through `fetchPullRequestCiStatus`, and none feeds a realistic combined-status payload.

## 8. API Design

**Major — `lib/github/pull-requests.ts:308`: `octokit.paginate` does not unwrap the combined commit status.** `@octokit/plugin-paginate-rest@14.0.0` normalises a wrapped list response only when `("total_count" in data) && !("url" in data)` (`normalize-paginated-list-response.js:11`), and the `combined-commit-status` schema *has* a `url` field (`@octokit/openapi-types/types.d.ts:24510`). So `paginate` concatenates the raw object. Proven against the installed packages:

```
paginate(combined) -> [{"state":"failure"}]     // contexts ci/circleci + codecov lost
paginate(checks)   -> ["unit"]                  // checks.listForRef is fine
```

Three consequences:

- `commitStatuses` is always `[{ context: undefined, state: <combined state> }]`. A commit with no statuses returns combined `"pending"`, so `hasPendingSignal` (`:197`) is now always true and `classifyPullRequestCi` can **never** return `passing`.
- A failing third-party status (CircleCI, Jenkins, Codecov, Buildkite) adds `undefined` to `failedChecks`; the notification degrades to `"Failing checks: unknown check"` or `"unit, "`.
- With `ci_autofix_enabled` ON it **crashes the autofix path**: `boundCiAutofixEvidence` (`lib/routines/ci-autofix-limits.ts:66`) calls `failure.name.trim()` on `undefined`. Both the primary call and the `catch` fallback at `ci-watch.ts:316` throw, so the PR is recorded as "could not be processed" — and `autofixAttempted` was already claimed at `:300`, so that PR head never gets a fix session.

**Minor — `lib/routines/settings.ts:11`.** `parseBooleanSetting` still re-implements the exported `parsePipelineEnabledSetting` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:80`) — same tri-state contract, same accepted encodings. *(Fifth time raised.)*

## 3. Error Handling

**Minor — `lib/routines/scheduler.ts:270`: the error-signature dedup does not cover thrown errors.** `450bae3` added signature dedup *inside* `runCiWatchRoutine`. Anything thrown out of it — `parseConfig` on a corrupted `config` (`ci-watch.ts:143`), a `persistState` transaction failure (`:425`), a `listOpenPullRequestEpics` DB error — reaches `run()`'s catch, which calls `notifySafely` unconditionally. At the default `intervalMinutes: 15` that is ~96 identical rows/day against a global `MAX_NOTIFICATIONS = 200` pruned oldest-first. Narrower than the original flood (the CRUD layer keeps `config` well-formed), but the same shape. Hash the signature in the scheduler's catch too.

Otherwise correct and defensive: per-PR `try/catch` with failure counting (`ci-watch.ts:405`), `notifySafely`, the `markFinished` failure path, the `logTail: null` fallback, boot reconciliation of stale `running` rows (`scheduler.ts:140`), and the fail-closed `isCiAutofixEnabled` catch.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:104`: stale `pr_status` polls forever.** Nothing reconciles the column automatically; a PR merged or closed on GitHub keeps `pr_status = 'open'` and is polled every interval indefinitely (3 API calls each, in a serial loop that delays the live PRs). `fetchPullRequestCiStatus` already calls `pulls.get` — returning the state would let the sweep write the column back and drop the epic. *(Second time raised.)*

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. Settings keys follow `<key>:<projectId>` and are registered in `perProjectSettingKeys`; the free-form notification `agentType` values (`routine`, `ci_watch`, `ci_autofix`) match the existing precedent (`approve_merge_failed`) and degrade to the raw string in `buildTitle`.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is strong: dueness across all four axes, restart replay, concurrent-sweep guard, per-SHA notification identity, green-interlude retention, autofix rearm on new SHA, mid-sweep GitHub error, unchanged-error suppression, quiet-poll suppression, interrupted-run recovery, `target_busy` deferral, config-edit-during-sweep preservation, realistic pagination through `octokit.paginate`, and an end-to-end dispatch through the scheduler queue asserting prompt content, `batch_run_id`, branch and notification.

**Major (contributing) — `__tests__/github-pr-ci.test.ts:332`.** "prioritizes actionable failures over cancelled matrix siblings" mocks `downloadJobLogs` with the 15-byte string `"failure details"`, so the 60 KB budget never binds, and asserts only that the *download call* was made. It cannot observe whether the actionable failure's log survives the budget — which is exactly finding 8.1.

## 8. API Design

**Major — `lib/routines/ci-autofix-limits.ts:75` / `lib/github/pull-requests.ts:432`: the evidence budget is spent alphabetically, so the real failure's log is the one dropped.** `2206b6f` made the *download selection* priority-aware (`compareFailedCheckRuns`, `pull-requests.ts:420`), but `evidence` is then built by mapping over `snapshot.failedChecks`, which `classifyPullRequestCi` sorted with `localeCompare` (`:206`). `boundCiAutofixEvidence` walks that array and assigns `remainingBytes` greedily, first-come-first-served.

12 logged checks × 8 000 chars ≈ 96 KB against `CI_AUTOFIX_MAX_EVIDENCE_BYTES = 60 000`, so the budget is exhausted after roughly seven entries — always the alphabetically-first seven.

Failure scenario: `fail-fast: true` matrix with jobs `a-cancelled-0…11` (conclusion `cancelled`, ~8 KB of runner/setup log each — cancelled jobs are not empty) and `z-real-failure` (conclusion `failure`). This is the precise outcome the pass-4 fix was written to prevent.

Fix: bound in priority order and re-sort for display, or pass an explicit ordering into `boundCiAutofixEvidence`; a per-check fair share (`remaining / remainingLoggedChecks`) also stops one verbose job starving the rest.

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:244`: the worktree is never checked against the PR head SHA.** `attachWorktree` puts the session on the right *branch*, but nothing compares its tip to `ciAutofix.headSha`. The agent then receives CI logs for commit A while working on tree B, and the "push `<branch>` for PR #N" notification (`:464`) describes a branch that also carries unrelated work. Read HEAD after attach and either say so in the prompt or skip.

**Minor — `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:104`: draft PRs are never watched.** The filter is `eq(epics.prStatus, "open")`, but the PR route persists `"draft"` for draft PRs (`pr/route.ts:173`, `:201`) and draft PRs still run CI. A user who opens a draft PR silently gets no CI watching.

On a 20-job fail-fast matrix the notification lists twenty names for one real failure and the prompt's check list is padded to match. Log *ranking* is right; the reported set is not. *(Third time raised.)*

**Minor — `lib/routines/crud.ts:264`.** `seededLastRunAt` writes a `last_run_at` for a run that never happened, so the UI renders "Last run: \<today\> · Status: Not run" (`RoutinesSettings.tsx:413`), or re-stamps a stale `completed`/`failed` onto today on a re-time. The first-fire fix is right; the display is misleading. *(Fifth time raised.)*

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 (+1 contributing test gap) |
| Minor | 10 |

The architecture and durability reasoning have held across five passes and remain sound: claim-before-dispatch ordering, the per-SHA guard, `batch_run_id` namespacing that no night-run consumer can confuse, the fail-closed opt-in, per-PR error isolation, error-signature dedup, real pagination with newest-per-context dedup, honest check classification, and now the PR-branch attachment. What blocks it is one half-applied fix. Pass 4 asked for the log budget to stop being spent on cancelled matrix siblings; the download order was corrected but the byte allocation still runs alphabetically, so on the fail-fast matrix that motivated the finding the agent still gets twelve sibling logs and nothing for the job that failed. The suite's own mock is 15 bytes, which is why it reads green.

A remediation plan with concrete fixes and required tests is at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-jaunty-wind.md`.

One blocking issue remains. It is not in `lib/routines/` — it is in the epic-build route, where the autofix branch inherits a prompt-assembly step written for ordinary builds.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. Comments consistently explain *why* (claim-before-dispatch ordering, the tilde fence guard, the retained-observation rationale, why `paginate` is safe on `listCommitStatusesForRef` but not on the combined status).

## 2. DRY Principle

No issues found. `TIME_OF_DAY_PATTERN`, `isSameLocalDay`, `parseRoutineConfig` and `isDailyRoutineKind` now live once in `lib/routines/constants.ts`; `lib/routines/settings.ts:4` imports `parsePipelineEnabledSetting` instead of re-deriving the tri-state. The one remaining hand-rolled config read (`scheduler.ts:32`) is deliberate and commented — `isRoutineDue` must not throw where `parseRoutineConfig` does.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. Per-PR `try/catch` with failure counting, `notifySafely`, the `markFinished` failure path, the `logTail: null` fetch fallback, boot reconciliation of stale `running` rows, and the fail-closed `isCiAutofixEnabled` catch are all correctly defensive.

## 4. Performance

The notification-flood thread — five passes long — is closed. Quiet polls are silent (`ci-watch.ts:476`), persistent per-PR and project-scope errors are deduped by durable signature (`:302`, `:439`), thrown errors are deduped in memory by the scheduler, and evidence is no longer downloaded for a dispatch that cannot happen.

**Minor — `lib/routines/ci-autofix-limits.ts:79`: the byte budget has no per-check floor.** The greedy walk lets the first priority-ranked check spend the entire 60 KB. With a genuine multi-job failure (one type error breaking eight matrix jobs, ~8 KB each) the later jobs fall to `logTail: null`. See finding 8.2 for what the prompt then says about them.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `ciAutofixEnabledSettingKey` follows `<key>:<projectId>` and is registered in `perProjectSettingKeys` (`lib/projects/project-settings-keys.ts:43`), so the row is swept on project deletion.

**Minor — `lib/github/pull-requests.ts:89`: `prState` is optional.** A `CiWatchDeps.fetchPullRequestCi` implementation that omits it type-checks cleanly and silently disables the closed/merged reconciliation `4c05593` added. Make it required.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is strong and the pass-5 contributing gap is closed — the budget test now uses 8 KB logs so the ceiling binds, rather than the 15-byte mock that made the alphabetical spend look green. Dueness across all four axes, restart replay, concurrent-sweep guard, per-SHA notification identity, green-interlude retention, autofix rearm on new SHA, mid-sweep GitHub error, unchanged-error suppression, quiet-poll suppression, interrupted-run recovery, both `target_busy` deferral shapes, draft-PR watching, merged-PR reconciliation, and an end-to-end dispatch through the scheduler queue asserting prompt content, `batch_run_id`, branch and the divergence note.

**Minor — two gaps map to the findings below.** Nothing asserts what does or does not reach the CI-autofix prompt beyond the CI evidence itself (finding 8.1 is entirely uncovered). ## 8. API Design

**Major — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:285`: open review comments override the CI-fix prompt's own instructions.**

`buildCiFixPrompt` closes with an explicit narrowing (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1141`):

> `Fix only the code or tests responsible for the CI failures above.`
> `Make the smallest correct change and run the relevant checks again.`

`build/route.ts:285` then appends, unconditionally and as the **last** block of the prompt:

> `The following review comments were left on your previous changes. Address each one:`

The two blocks contradict each other and the wider one wins by recency. The triggering state is the common one, not an edge case: CI goes red on a PR whose epic sits in Review with open findings — which is exactly when `ci_watch` fires.

Three consequences:

- a session the user opted into as "fix the failing check" makes broad unrequested changes on the PR branch;
- the one-shot `(PR, head SHA)` claim is consumed by that wider work, so the CI failure gets no second attempt without a new push;
- `createCiAutofixReadyNotification` and the activity reason still describe it as *"CI autofix … carries an unpushed fix"*, so the scope of what actually landed is never disclosed.

The route already special-cases `ciAutofix` to disable resume (`:310`), disable the pipeline (`:534`), attach rather than derive the worktree (`:251`) and skip the branch-name rewrite (`:388`) — the review-context append is the one that was missed. Skip both the load (`:215`) and the append when `ciAutofix` is set, and add a test asserting the autofix prompt carries no `## Code Review Feedback` section while an ordinary build still does.

**Minor — `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1135`: a budget-dropped log is reported as a missing log.** When `boundCiAutofixEvidence` drops a tail for budget, the prompt prints *"GitHub did not expose a downloadable log for this check"* — false for a log that was downloaded and discarded, and it steers the agent away from a check it could have diagnosed. **Minor — `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1084`: `CI_FIX_MAX_SPEC_CHARS` bounds characters, not bytes.** The commit message claims the `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` risk is eliminated; it is reduced. A multi-byte spec is up to 4× the cap in bytes, and two other contributors to the same prompt stay uncapped — the resolved build system prompt and (until 8.1 lands) `reviewContext`. Codex passes the whole prompt as one argv element (`lib/providers/codex.ts:152`) against 128 KB. Use `Buffer.byteLength` and add one assembly-level byte budget on the autofix branch.

**Minor — `lib/routines/ci-watch.ts:276`, `:337`: CI-watch state housekeeping.** The `openPullRequests.length === 0` early return skips the closing `persistState`, so once every PR closes, `ciWatchState` is never pruned. Reconciliation is also one-way — an epic written back to `closed` leaves the watch list permanently, and a reopened PR needs a manual `/pr/sync` to return. And `setEpicPullRequestState` writes `epics.pr_status` with no project event, so an open board shows the stale status until the next refetch.

**Minor — reformatting noise.** `lib/git/manager.ts` and `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts` carry ~35 hunks of pure formatting churn with no logic change. Prettier is not a project dependency, so nothing enforces it either way; the churn inflates the review surface and will conflict with concurrent work in two heavily-shared files.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 8 |

The routines module itself is in good shape. Six passes of durability reasoning have held: claim-before-dispatch ordering, the per-SHA guard, `batch_run_id` namespacing no night-run consumer can confuse, the fail-closed opt-in, per-PR error isolation, error-signature dedup, real pagination with newest-per-context dedup, honest check classification, PR-branch attachment, and now a genuinely priority-ordered evidence budget with a test that can observe it. Migration bookkeeping is correct — hand-written `0036`/`0037`, monotonic `when` values, journal entries appended, no `drizzle-kit generate`. Delegation to canonical services is real throughout.

What blocks it is one line inherited from the ordinary-build path. **Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=C5mp_eSMFVc1 -->

**Probable root cause** — `spawn E2BIG` is the kernel refusing the `exec` itself, not a Claude/model failure: the child never started, which is why the raw stream, output stream and last-text fields are all empty. Arij passes the entire agent prompt as a single argv element (`args.push("--print", "-p", prompt)` in `lib/claude/spawn.ts:148`), and Linux caps one argv string at `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 128 KiB. The review stage builds the largest prompt in the pipeline: `buildEpicReviewPrompt` concatenates spec + project memory + documents + epic description + all user stories **plus the full, unbounded comment history** (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1624-1632`), fed by an uncapped `select … from ticketComments` in `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:558-573`. This ticket ("routines : cron interne + surveillance CI des PRs") accumulated a long agent/user comment thread, so the review prompt crossed 128 KiB. The failure is deterministic — the retry rebuilt the same (in fact slightly longer) prompt and died identically, hence 2/2 attempts with zero output. Note this is the same failure class already recorded for the Codex provider; it is provider-independent because the argv path is shared.

**Evidence**
- `spawn E2BIG` with `Raw stream (tail): (none)`, `Output stream (tail): (none)`, `Last text produced: (none)` — the exec failed before any child I/O, ruling out a model/agent-side error.
- `lib/claude/spawn.ts:148`: `args.push("--print", "-p", prompt);` — the whole prompt is one argv entry, subject to the 128 KiB per-argument limit.
- `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:558-573` selects every `ticketComments` row for the epic with no `limit`, and `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1624-1632` inlines them all into the review prompt — prompt size grows without bound as the thread grows.

**Recommended next action**
- Cap the prompt before spawn rather than retrying as-is: truncate the comment-history section in `buildEpicReviewPrompt` (keep the newest N comments / a char budget, as `SPEC_UPDATE_MAX_*` already does elsewhere) or write the prompt to a temp file and feed it on stdin instead of `-p`; as an immediate unblock for this ticket, a human can prune/collapse the comment thread on the epic and re-run the `review` stage.

epics.title: Stats → dispatch : badge de fiabilité + sélection intelligente en Full Auto
epics.description:
## Contexte
`lib/agent-config/stats.ts` calcule taux de réussite et durée médiane par agent × provider, affichés dans l'onglet Stats — mais rien ne les consomme. Le badge de fiabilité dans les sélecteurs d'agents est un écart assumé documenté (`docs/plans/2026-08-15-feature-ideas.md`). Enseignement GitHub (Code with Claude 2026) : mesurer les résultats et les faire piloter les choix.

## À construire
1. **Badge dans les sélecteurs** : partout où on choisit un agent de dispatch (lancement de build, review, réglages auto-mode), afficher à côté de chaque named agent son taux de réussite et sa durée médiane sur les 30 derniers jours POUR le type de tâche concerné (réutiliser stats.ts ; endpoint léger si besoin). Échantillon < 5 sessions → afficher « — » plutôt qu'un pourcentage trompeur.
2. **Sélection informée en Full Auto** : setting `auto_mode_smart_dispatch` (tri-state, défaut OFF). Quand l'agent de build/review du Full Auto n'est PAS explicitement configuré, choisir parmi les named agents éligibles celui au meilleur taux de réussite sur 30 jours pour cet agentType (minimum 5 sessions, sinon défaut actuel). Choix tracé : namedAgentId sur la session + `reason` dans ticket_activity_log.
3. **Ne pas sur-construire** : un simple argmax avec seuil d'échantillon — pas de bandit multi-bras, pas d'exploration/exploitation. Documenter cette limite dans l'en-tête du module.

## Contraintes
- Aucun changement quand le setting est OFF ou quand un agent est explicitement configuré.
- Pas de requête N+1 dans les sélecteurs : agrégat en une passe.
- Tests vitest : agent configuré prime, échantillon insuffisant → défaut actuel, sélection argmax correcte, traçabilité du choix.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**

**Probable root cause** — The `build` stage never reached the model at all: the `oh-my-pi` CLI aborted at startup because the model id it was handed, `ninfer/qwen3.8-27b`, is not declared in the local omp model registry. `/home/orosius/.omp/agent/models.yml` defines exactly one model under the `ninfer` provider — `qwen3.6-27b` — so the configured id is a version-digit mismatch (`3.8` vs `3.6`). Because omp cannot resolve the id to a provider entry, it falls through to its "no model / no credentials" branch and exits before emitting a single token, which is why both the output stream and the last text produced are empty. This is a deterministic configuration fault, not a flaky or ticket-specific one — hence identical output on both attempts.

**Evidence**

- The recorded error is a registry lookup failure, not a build or code error: `Model "ninfer/qwen3.8-27b" not found`, followed by `Or create /home/orosius/.omp/agent/models.yml` — omp pointing at the very file that should declare the id.
- The local registry declares a different version: `providers: ninfer: ... models: - id: qwen3.6-27b`. No `qwen3.8-27b` entry exists.
- The failure is pre-execution: `Output stream (tail): (none)` and `Last text produced: (none)` — the agent produced nothing, so nothing about the ticket scope ("Stats → dispatch : badge de fiabilité…") contributed to the failure.
- The bad id is board-wide, not a one-off: `grep -o "ninfer/[a-z0-9.\-]*" arji.json` returns 4 occurrences of `ninfer/qwen3.8-27b` and zero of the valid id.

**Recommended next action**

- Human config fix, then plain retry: correct the model id used by the `oh-my-pi` provider from `ninfer/qwen3.8-27b` to `ninfer/qwen3.6-27b` (or add a `qwen3.8-27b` entry to `/home/orosius/.omp/agent/models.yml` if that model is actually served at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`) — the id appears 4× in `arji.json`, so fix it at the source that exports the board rather than in the file. Re-dispatch the ticket unchanged; no prompt or scope change is warranted since the agent never ran.

## Épic livré — 2 commits

**`2e9c4bc`** — Badge de fiabilité dans les sélecteurs d'agents
**`00c36eb`** — `auto_mode_smart_dispatch` (sélection informée en Full Auto)

### Story 1 — Badge

- `getNamedAgentDispatchReliability()` (`lib/agent-config/stats.ts`) : **une seule requête**, groupée par (named agent × rôle de dispatch), fenêtre glissante 30 jours, runs terminaux uniquement — l'échantillon est donc exactement le dénominateur du taux.
- **Choix de conception** : la clé de groupe est un *rôle* (build / review / merge / qa / chat / spec / release / maintenance), pas l'`agentType` brut. Le dossier d'un reviewer est la même question sur `review_code` et `review_security`, et surtout une médiane ne se recombine pas après coup à partir de médianes par type — le regroupement doit avoir lieu dans la passe SQL. La partition des `AGENT_TYPES` est totale et vérifiée à l'import.
- `GET /api/agent-config/dispatch-stats` renvoie tous les rôles en une réponse ; `useDispatchReliability` déduplique au niveau module → **N sélecteurs = 1 requête**, jamais une par agent.
- Sous 5 sessions (y compris « aucune ligne ») : « — », et le tooltip dit la taille de l'échantillon sans laisser fuiter le pourcentage.
- Câblé partout : build (barre d'actions, toolbar batch, night run), review, merge (résolution de conflit + git-sync), QA, release notes, et les deux sélecteurs du dialogue Full Auto.

### Story 2 — `auto_mode_smart_dispatch`

- Tri-state projet → global → OFF, OFF par défaut.
- Ne s'applique qu'à un rôle **sans** agent explicite ; sinon le sélecteur n'est même pas consulté.
- Argmax simple avec seuil de 5, limite documentée en en-tête de `lib/agent-config/smart-dispatch.ts` (pas de bandit, pas d'exploration). Départages déterministes (échantillon → médiane → nom) pour que le mode reste reproductible depuis son log.
- Rien ne franchit le seuil → chaîne de résolution actuelle inchangée.
- Traçabilité : `namedAgentId` sur la session (via le driver) + entrée `ticket_activity_log` nommant l'agent, son taux et son échantillon.
- Résolu une fois par rôle et par sweep, derrière une garde « aucun candidat » : un sweep à vide (toutes les 15 s) ne coûte aucune requête stats.

### Vérification

- **353 fichiers / 4080 tests vitest verts** (30 nouveaux tests : agrégat, fenêtre, seuil, formatage, argmax, priorité du choix explicite, traçabilité, une seule requête).
- `tsc --noEmit` propre ; lint sans nouvel écart (91 problèmes préexistants, aucun dans les fichiers touchés).
- ⚠️ `npm run build` échoue au prerender de `/inbox` (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')`) — **préexistant** : erreur et digest identiques sur l'arbre propre (vérifié par `git stash`). Sans rapport avec cet épic.

Docs mises à jour : `docs/architecture/full-auto-mode.md` (clé + section « Informed selection ») et l'écart assumé de `docs/plans/2026-08-15-feature-ideas.md`, désormais marqué livré.

## Epic complete — 4/4 stories, all acceptance criteria met

The UI parcours was already implemented in `19eb33b`. This session verified it against every acceptance criterion and fixed one genuine gap found in the process.

### Verification
- **2478 tests pass** (256 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, no new lint findings in touched files.
- Story-level coverage is direct: `github-url-selector.test.tsx` (11), `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` (18), `import-progress-step.test.tsx` (4), `new-project-page-errors.test.tsx` (4), `projects-create-clone-metadata.test.ts` (9).
- The "`GitHubConnectBanner` does not appear" criterion is covered by the pre-existing `github-connect-banner.test.tsx:73` — the banner returns `null` because `shouldAttemptDetect` requires `!githubOwnerRepo`.

### Gap found and fixed — `249d9eb`
The last criterion of story 3 ("sending an epic to dev on a freshly cloned project creates a worktree and branch successfully") **did not hold**. `createWorktree` guessed `main` and otherwise fell back to `master`, so a clone whose default branch is neither failed outright:

```
fatal: invalid reference: master
```

Reproduced against a real clone in the `projects/<owner>-<repo>` layout this flow now creates. `resolveBaseBranch` keeps `main` then `master` as the first answers — every existing repo is unaffected and **no call site changed** — then asks the clone itself via `origin/HEAD`, which is what spec §4.5 means by using `default_branch` instead of the main/master guess. Verified end to end against two real clones (default `main`, default `develop`); both produce a worktree in `projects/.arij-worktrees/` on the expected branch.

I deliberately did **not** thread `projects.default_branch` from the DB through the 8 `createWorktree` call sites — that is route-layer work owned by the git/clone epics, and resolving from the clone achieves the same result with no conflict risk at integration.

### Left to the sibling epics (out of this epic's scope)
- `POST /api/projects/clone` does not exist on this branch. The UI is written against its documented `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` contract and every branch of it is covered by mocked-fetch tests, so integration should be drop-in.
- Spec §4.1 asks for `/projects` in `.gitignore`; it is still absent. That belongs to the workspace-layout epic (alongside `lib/projects/workspace.ts`), so I left it rather than risk a conflicting one-line edit — worth confirming it lands there.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report — "Parcours d'import depuis une URL GitHub (UI)"

Scope reviewed: `app/projects/import/page.tsx`, `app/projects/new/page.tsx`, `components/import/{FolderSelector,GitHubUrlSelector,ImportProgress,ImportPreview}.tsx`, `lib/git/github-url.ts`, `lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/validation/schemas.ts`, `app/api/projects/route.ts`, `app/api/projects/import/route.ts`, `lib/db/migrations/0027_project_clone_source.sql` + `meta/_journal.json`, `lib/db/init.ts`, and the six new/updated test files. Commits `19eb33b`, `249d9eb` on base `c9d404e`.

Overall the implementation is strong: the state machine is clean, the client-safe parser split is well justified, the migration/journal/legacy-baseline handling is correct (0027 at `idx: 26`, `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` entry, `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated), and test coverage is direct for every story. The findings below are mostly about the failure paths this epic exists to harden — two of them are re-openings of findings from the previous review round that were not fully addressed.

## 1. Readability

No issues found.

Names are descriptive (`sendJson`, `applyProjectUpdate`, `createEpicsAndStories`, `exportArjiJson`, `resolveBaseBranch`), the non-obvious decisions carry good comments (why `cloneInfo`-gated metadata, why the preview is locked once a project row exists, why `main`/`master` keep priority), and the step helpers read top-to-bottom.

## 2. DRY Principle

### Finding 1
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:13-21` vs `lib/git/remote.ts:40-45`
- **Description:** The four remote-URL regexes are duplicated between the new client-safe module and the existing `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`. The module doc says `remote.ts` should re-export at integration, but nothing enforces it and `remote.ts` on this branch has no `parseGitHubRepoInput` at all — so today there is *no* shared source of truth, and the two grammars can drift (they already differ on segment safety: `remote.ts` performs no `.`/`..`/leading-`-` checks).
- **Recommendation:** At integration, make `github-url.ts` the single grammar owner and have `remote.ts` re-export/compose from it; add a parity test asserting both modules reject the same inputs.

### Finding 2
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:36` and `components/import/ImportPreview.tsx:11`
- **Description:** `ImportData` is declared twice with subtly different fields (the page's copy adds `status`, `spec`, `priority`, `position`; the preview's doesn't). Structural typing papers over the divergence, but a new arji.json field now has to be added in two places.
- **Recommendation:** Hoist one `ImportData` type to a shared module (e.g. `lib/sync/arji-json.ts` or a `components/import/types.ts`) and import it in both.

## 3. Error Handling

### Finding 3
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:122` (unchecked cast) and `app/projects/import/page.tsx:246` (unguarded dereference)
- **Description:** `sendJson()` still treats a 2xx response with a malformed or envelope-less body as success: `response.json().catch(() => null)` yields `null`/`{}`/a scalar, and the function returns `{ ok: true, data: payload?.data as T }` — i.e. `data === undefined` — without any check. `runAnalysis()` then does `setImportData(result.data.preview)`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. There is no try/catch around `runAnalysis` in either `handleAnalyze` or `handleGitHubImport`, so the rejection is unhandled and the state is never left `"analyzing"`. Result: a permanent "Analyzing project…" spinner with no error and no recovery except reload. This is exactly the previous review's Finding 2, still open, on the epic's primary flow — and it defeats US4's "never left on a dead screen" goal.
- **Recommendation:** Treat `payload === null` / non-object payload / missing expected envelope as a failed request (`ok: false`, error like "unexpected response from /api/projects/import"), and/or validate endpoint-specific shapes. Add a test: 2xx with non-JSON body and 2xx with `{}` for `/api/projects/import` must land back on `select` with the message rendered.

### Finding 4
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:311` (only write of `createdProjectId`, never reset), `:460` (`busy={validating || createdProjectId !== null}`), `:462-464` (Cancel handler)
- **Description:** The partial-creation dead end from the previous review's Finding 1 was only half-fixed. Sequence: GitHub import → project created → one epic fails → issues + "Open the partially created project" link shown, Validate disabled. User clicks **Cancel** → `resetFeedback()` clears the issues and link, state → `select`, but `createdProjectId` survives. The user starts another import (natural action), spends minutes on clone + analysis, and lands on a preview where "Validate & Import" is **permanently disabled with no message and no link** — a dead screen reachable through the epic's own happy-path failure. Additionally, Cancel remains clickable while `validating` is true: the in-flight chain keeps running after the user left the preview, so a late `router.push` or a late `setIssues`/`setError` can land on top of a *second, concurrent* import flow (stale `cloneInfo`/`folderPath` interleaving included).
- **Recommendation:** (a) Disable (or no-op) Cancel while `validating`; (b) reset `createdProjectId` when the user deliberately starts a new import (`handleAnalyze`/`handleGitHubImport`), which also un-locks the preview. Add the regression test the previous review asked for: partial failure → Cancel → new import → Validate must be enabled.

### Finding 5
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:18-27` (`DebugInfo`) and the debug `<details>` block; producer side `app/api/projects/import/route.ts` (`debug: { stack }`, `{ duration, rawPreview }`, `{ duration, keys }`)
- **Description:** The debug contract is partially lost in transit: `stack` is declared on `DebugInfo` but never rendered, and the import route's `rawPreview` / `keys` fields are not in the type at all. For the `{ stack }` debug shape (unexpected server error) the "Debug info" disclosure renders an empty body; for invalid-arji.json failures the most useful field (`rawPreview`) is silently dropped. This undercuts the "every step reports its own failure" goal for the two most diagnostic cases.
- **Recommendation:** Render `stack`, and add `rawPreview`/`keys` to `DebugInfo` (or a generic `Record<string, unknown>` escape hatch) plus one test each.

Positive: everything else in the chain is handled — clone failure returns to `select` with a context-prefixed message, a clone response missing `path` is caught, create-failure keeps the preview editable with the API message + zod `details` expansion, each epic/story/sync/patch step reports distinctly, a failed epic skips its stories without orphans and continues, and `new/page.tsx` now surfaces `data.error` with a status-code fallback and network-failure path.

## 4. Performance

No issues found.

Sequential epic/story creation matches the existing pipeline and the data volumes involved (dozens of tickets). `parseGitHubRepoInput` per keystroke is a handful of regexes. `structuredClone` on edit per keystroke in `ImportPreview` is pre-existing and negligible at preview size. No re-render hazards: `ImportProgress`/selectors are trivial, the page is conditionally rendered per state.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

`camelCase` throughout, components in PascalCase, `ImportSource`/`ImportState`/`CloneInfo`/`GitHubImportRequest` all read well; `app/projects/import/page.tsx` copy uses consistent "…" ellipsis vs "..." only in the progress headings (`"Cloning Orolol/arij..."`) — cosmetic at most, not worth a change.

## 6. Type Safety

### Finding 6
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:46`
- **Description:** `isSafeRepoSegment` rejects any segment *containing* `..` (`segment.includes("..")`), but the spec (and the previous review's Finding 5) only rejects segments exactly equal to `.` or `..`. GitHub repo names may contain consecutive dots, so `owner/repo..v2` (a valid, creatable repo) is rejected by the button, by the parse, and — via the same grammar — by any server re-parse. The over-rejection is safe (no traversal risk inside an already-isolated segment) but silently makes valid repos un-importable.
- **Recommendation:** Use exact `segment === "." || segment === ".."` and add a `owner/repo..v2` acceptance regression case.

No `any` types anywhere in the touched code. The one unchecked cast is `payload?.data as T` at `page.tsx:122` — already covered by Finding 3.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is the epic's strongest asset: `github-url-client-parser.test.ts` (accept/reject matrix, suffix stripping, no-simple-git-leak check), `github-url-selector.test.tsx` (11), `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` (18, including gated-response sequencing for the clone→analyze→preview transitions), `import-progress-step.test.tsx` (4), `new-project-page-errors.test.tsx` (4), `projects-create-clone-metadata.test.ts` (9), three new `createWorktree` cases for the `origin/HEAD` path, and the `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated for 0027.

### Finding 7
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `__tests__/import-page-github-flow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/worktree-manager.test.ts`, `__tests__/github-url-client-parser.test.ts`
- **Description:** The suite is comprehensive on the happy path and on per-step failures, but each of the findings above sits exactly in an untested seam: no 2xx envelope-less response case (Finding 3), no "partial import → Cancel → new import" case (Finding 4), no `mergeWorktree` with a non-main/master default (Finding 8), no embedded-`..` parse case (Finding 6).
- **Recommendation:** Add those four regression tests; the fetch-mock harness in `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` already supports all of them.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 8
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:124` (`const mainBranch = branches.all.includes("main") ? "main" : "master";`), consumed by `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/merge/route.ts:75,210` and `resolve-merge/route.ts:98,245`
- **Description:** The `249d9eb` fix threaded real-default-branch resolution through `createWorktree` (via `resolveBaseBranch` → `origin/HEAD`) and `release.ts`'s `pickBaseBranch` already falls back to `branches[0]` — but `mergeWorktree` still hard-guesses `main`/`master` and then `git.checkout(mainBranch)`. On a freshly cloned repo whose default is `develop`/`trunk` (the exact class this epic exists to support), the epic can now be built (thanks to the fix) but **cannot be merged back**: checkout of non-existent `master` fails, so the review→merge loop — Arij's core lifecycle — breaks with a confusing error. Before this epic such repos couldn't even reach that point (worktree creation failed first), so the fix newly exposes the gap; spec §4.5 states `default_branch` is used "instead of the main/master guess", and the migration header itself says the code should "stop guessing between main and master".
- **Recommendation:** Extract the resolution (local `main` → local `master` → `origin/HEAD` → current branch) into a shared helper and use it in `mergeWorktree` as the merge target, or thread `projects.default_branch` from the row through the merge routes. Add a `develop`-default repo test for the merge path.

### Finding 9
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:109-142`
- **Description:** `POST /api/projects` accepts the client-asserted `cloneSource: "github"` ownership flag (plus `gitRemoteUrl`/`defaultBranch`) with no consistency check: nothing verifies `githubOwnerRepo` matches `gitRemoteUrl`, that the remote parses as GitHub, that `gitRepoPath` lies under the managed clone root, or that the directory's actual `origin` matches. A crafted request can mark any existing directory as Arij-owned. No deletion consumer exists on this branch yet (the `DELETE` route only removes the row), so this is latent — but the write side ships now and the destructive cleanup consumer is the sibling epic's next step, which makes the flag a data-loss flag in waiting.
- **Recommendation:** When `cloneSource` is present, require the full metadata tuple, validate the clean GitHub URL + `owner/repo` with the existing parser, require the normalized path under the managed root, and (ideally) verify the directory's `origin`. At minimum, block this before the clone-cleanup epic lands.

Positive on API design otherwise: splitting clone from analysis was the right call; the UI sends the *raw pasted value* to the clone endpoint and lets the server re-parse authoritatively (the client parse is display/disabling only); statuses are correct (400 validation, 201 create); response envelopes are consistent `{ data }` / `{ error, details }`; and `POST /api/projects` now persisting `pathResult.normalizedPath` is a genuine improvement the tests pin down.

## Integration risks (cross-epic, not defects on this branch)

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` does not exist on this branch** (sibling "clone service" epic). The UI is written against the documented `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` contract with mocked-fetch coverage of every branch — verify the contract verbatim at merge, including the 409 mismatch-remote case the UI surfaces.
2. **`/projects` is still absent from `.gitignore`** (spec §4.1). Explicitly deferred to the workspace-layout epic — confirm it lands there, or dogfooding shows every clone as untracked.
3. **Migration `0027` dedupe risk** — if a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the journal entry and the `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.
4. **`remote.ts` re-export** — see Finding 1.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 3 (Findings 3, 4, 8) |
| Minor | 3 (Findings 5, 6, 9) |
| Suggestion | 3 (Findings 1, 2, 7) |

The UI itself — source switch, distinct progress steps, clone-metadata forwarding, per-step failure surfacing, and the `origin/HEAD` worktree fix — is well built and well tested. But the failure-path hardening that US4 promises has two real dead ends still in it (the 2xx envelope-less freeze and the post-Cancel permanently-locked preview), and the worktree fix's newly-reachable merge path still hard-guesses `main`/`master`, breaking the lifecycle for the exact class of repos this feature imports.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:173`

  ```
  $ node -e "import('simple-git').then(m => m.default('/tmp/notarepo').getRemotes(true))"
  THREW: fatal: not a git repository (or any parent up to mount point /)
  ```
  `validatePath` only proves the path exists and is a directory, so a request with the full tuple and a non-repo path throws out of the handler. The user gets `Request failed (HTTP 500)` instead of the carefully worded 400 that lines 175–184 were written to produce. Reachable via a clone whose `.git` is missing or half-written — the partial-clone case spec §5 anticipates. Both existing callers already guard this: `git/detect-remote/route.ts:38` and `github/detect/route.ts:29` use `try`/`catch` + `errorResponse`.

- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:56` (vs `lib/validation/path.ts:22`)

  ```
  parsed:       {"owner":"owner","repo":"repo..v2", ...}
  validatePath: {"valid":false,"error":"Path must not contain traversal components (..)"}
  ```

## 8. API Design

### Finding 1 — Major
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/pr/route.ts:47`; also `lib/git/diff.ts:50`, `hooks/useEpicPr.ts:53`, `lib/git/release.ts:12`

  2. **`lib/git/diff.ts:50`** — worse, because it fails *silently*. `merge-base main HEAD` throws, is swallowed at `:61`, `mergeBase` stays null → `files = []`, `ahead/behind = 0`; the fallback at `:108` requires `mergeBase` truthy so it's skipped. `DiffViewer` then renders *"The branch has not diverged from main"* over an epic with real commits.   3. **`lib/git/release.ts:12`** — degrades via `branches[0]` rather than breaking, but can pick a feature branch.

Add a `develop`-default case for the PR base and for `getWorktreeDiff`.

### Finding 4 — Minor
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:504`
- **Description:** `busy={validating || createdProjectId !== null}` collapses two states. After a partial import `validating` is false but `busy` stays true, so `ImportPreview.tsx:144` renders *"Importing..."* indefinitely while nothing runs. The locking intent is right; the label reads as a hung operation on the exact screen US4 exists to make legible.

### Finding 5 — Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:142`
- **Description:** Provenance is verified but not *anchored*: nothing requires `normalizedRepoPath` to equal `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>`. A user with their own clone of `owner/repo` at `~/code/repo` would pass every check if a crafted or buggy request named that path, marking it `clone_source = 'github'`. Inert today (`DELETE` only removes the row) but the flag's whole purpose is to authorise recursive deletion, and that consumer is the sibling epic's next step. ### Finding 7 — Suggestion
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:39` and `app/api/projects/route.ts:197`
- **Description:** Two smaller consequences of the same gap. (a) `resolveBaseBranch` prefers a local `main`/`master` over `origin/HEAD` — deliberate and well justified for backward compatibility, but it means a gitflow repo whose GitHub default is `develop` while a local `main` also exists will cut and merge into `main` while `default_branch` says `develop`, with the two never reconciling. (b) The tuple check *hard-requires* `defaultBranch` for a field nothing reads — the strictest contract in the route guards the deadest value, and a clone whose default branch couldn't be determined (empty repo) becomes unimportable for want of an unused string.
- **Recommendation:** give `resolveBaseBranch` an optional `preferred` argument filled from `project.defaultBranch` (existence-checked, falling through to today's chain), which makes the DB authoritative and keeps every fallback. Both resolve once the column gains consumers — fix them together rather than relaxing the requirement in isolation.

---

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` still does not exist here.** The UI degrades gracefully (404 → `Request failed (HTTP 404)` → back to the selector), but no acceptance criterion involving a real clone can be verified on this branch.
2. **Migration `0027` dedupe** — if a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the journal entry and the three `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 (Finding 1) |
| Minor | 4 (Findings 2, 3, 4, 5) |
| Suggestion | 2 (Findings 6, 7) |

The UI, the failure surfacing and the test suite are all in good shape, and every finding from the last round is properly closed. What blocks is that the default-branch work was threaded through worktree and merge but not through PR and diff — and the diff case returns a *silently wrong* empty result on the review screen for exactly the repos this epic newly makes importable.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

Genuinely strong, and the reason the previous rounds' fixes could be *verified* rather than trusted: 29 cases in `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` (gated-response sequencing, the 2xx-non-JSON / no-envelope / malformed-preview trio, partial→Cancel→fresh import, Cancel-while-in-flight, busy-vs-locked labels), 22 in `projects-create-clone-metadata.test.ts` (incl. the non-repository-directory 400 and case-insensitive owner/repo), 21 grammar-parity cases, `develop`-default cases across `createWorktree`, `mergeWorktree`, `resolveDefaultBranch`, `pickBaseBranch`, the PR route and the diff route, and a whole-chain test that a `repo..v2` name survives parse → clone destination → `validatePath`.

### Finding 5 — Suggestion
- **Location:** `__tests__/import-page-github-flow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/project-route-github-owner-repo.test.ts`
- **Description:** The findings above sit in the two seams the suite does not reach: a malformed *story* entry (F1/F2 — the epic-level equivalents are both covered at `:590` and `:624`), and a PATCH that respells the same directory (F6). Both are one test each in harnesses that already exist.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 6 — Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:38-46` and `:57-65`
- **Description:** PATCH validates `gitRepoPath` but discards the result — `updates.gitRepoPath = body.gitRepoPath` stores the **raw** input, while `POST` was deliberately fixed this epic to store `pathResult.normalizedPath` (a US3 acceptance criterion). Two consequences, the second of which is new:
  1. The invariant the new comment relies on — *"the stored path is normalised on insert, so 'no change' is an exact string match"* — is broken by the first PATCH that stores a relative or untidy path.
  2. Re-sending the **same** directory with a different spelling (`/home/u/projects/owner-repo/`, `./projects/owner-repo`) compares unequal, is read as a move, and silently clears `clone_source` / `git_remote_url` / `default_branch` — quietly downgrading this epic's own default-branch behaviour back to the `main`/`master` guess on a repo that never moved.

  The raw-path storage predates this epic; only the provenance-clearing dependency on it is new. Latent for now — no UI PATCHes `gitRepoPath` (verified by grep) — but the clearing logic is the doorway the `TODO(workspace-epic)` is meant to guard.
- **Recommendation:** store `pathResult.normalizedPath` (mirroring `route.ts:127`) and compare normalised-to-normalised.

### Finding 7 — Suggestion
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:221-235`, `lib/db/schema.ts:16-21`
- **Description:** Nothing prevents two project rows on the same `git_repo_path`. The clone layer is deliberately idempotent (`reused` → *"Repository already cloned — updating"*), and the destination is deterministic `<owner>-<repo>` — so re-importing the same URL now reliably lands two Arij projects driving one clone: same `.arij-worktrees` directory, same default branch, merges from either project checking out and merging into it. The spec's "re-running an import is cheap and safe" holds at the clone layer only. Pre-existing in principle (a user could paste the same local path twice), but this epic makes it the natural outcome of an ordinary retry.
- **Recommendation:** look up an existing project by normalised `git_repo_path` (or `github_owner_repo` + `clone_source`) and either return it or 409 with a link — ideally surfaced at clone time, where the UI already has a "reused" branch to hang it on.

**Positive on API design otherwise:** the provenance validation is the right shape (full tuple → URL/ownerRepo consistency → the directory's *actual* `origin`, with a non-repo directory correctly degrading to a 400 rather than escaping as a 500); the default-branch threading now reaches every consumer — worktree, merge, resolve-merge, diff, PR, release, build, review, pipeline — with `useEpicPr` no longer force-sending `"main"`; envelopes stay `{ data }` / `{ error, details }`; and the migration/journal/legacy-baseline triple is correct.

## Integration risks (cross-epic, not defects on this branch)

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` still does not exist here.** The UI degrades honestly (404 → back to the selector with a named message) and every branch is covered by mocked fetch, but no acceptance criterion involving a real clone is verifiable on this branch. Confirm `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` verbatim at merge — `handleGitHubImport:322-333` hard-requires all four, `defaultBranch` included.
2. **Migration `0027` dedupe.** If a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the `idx: 26` journal entry and the three `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.
3. **`lib/projects/workspace.ts` / `projects_root`** are still absent, so `normalizedRepoPath` is not yet anchored to the managed destination. Both `TODO(workspace-epic)` markers say so, and the recursive clone cleanup must not ship before that anchor.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 3 (Findings 1, 2, 6) |
| Suggestion | 4 (Findings 3, 4, 5, 7) |

Every blocking finding from the previous four rounds is closed and pinned by a test, the suite is green at 2557 tests, and the default-branch work is now threaded end to end. What remains is one narrow residual of the preview-guard class (a `null` story entry still blanks the app), the missing `catch` that would have contained it, and a PATCH path that stores an unnormalised value the new provenance logic assumes is normalised. None of these blocks the epic; all three are small, well-localised fixes.

*(`mcp__arij__submit_findings` was not filed — plan mode forbids non-read-only tool calls, including MCP writes. Findings are anchored to `file:line` above.)*

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: Le badge « Session failed » réapparaît après un retry réussi
epics.description:
## Symptôme

Une carte epic ayant subi un échec d'agent garde l'indicateur rouge « Session failed · <erreur> » **même après un retry réussi**, et même si l'epic a depuis changé de colonne.

Le badge est correctement masqué pendant que le retry tourne, puis **réapparaît dès que le retry se termine**.

## Comportement attendu

L'indicateur d'échec doit disparaître **dès qu'un retry est lancé** sur l'epic, et ne pas revenir : seul le résultat de la **dernière** session doit être reflété sur la carte.

## Cause probable

Le badge est dérivé de « la dernière session **en échec** » de l'epic, et non de « la dernière session tout court » (`hooks/useAgentPolling.ts`).

Un retry crée une **nouvelle** ligne dans `agent_sessions` ; l'ancienne ligne reste en base avec `status = "failed"` (les statuts sont terminaux — `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = []` dans `lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts`). D'où la séquence observée :

1. pendant le retry, l'epic est dans la liste des sessions actives → le badge est masqué ;
2. le retry se termine en `completed`, l'epic sort de la liste active → l'ancienne ligne `failed` redevient « la plus récente en échec » → **le badge revient**.

Le filtre « failed session » de la `FilterBar` dérive de la même donnée (`hasFailedSession`) et est donc affecté de la même manière.

## Piste de correction

Passer à une sémantique « la dernière session gagne » : pour chaque epic, ne retenir que la session la plus récente, et n'afficher le badge que si **celle-ci** est en échec. Un retry en `queued` / `running` efface alors le badge immédiatement, ce qui est le comportement demandé.

Point d'attention : `created_at` est un `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` SQLite (précision **seconde**) et le tri serveur départage les ex æquo par `id` (nanoid → ordre arbitraire). Un retry lancé dans la même seconde que l'échec qu'il remplace doit donc être départagé explicitement **en faveur de l'effacement** du badge, sans quoi le bug subsiste de façon intermittente.

## Hors périmètre

La page `sessions/` doit continuer d'afficher l'historique complet, échecs inclus : c'est un journal, pas un état courant.

Conserver la garde sur les sessions actives issues du registry (celles qui n'ont pas encore de ligne en base). Départager explicitement les sessions de même timestamp en faveur de l'effacement du badge, la précision de created_at étant la seconde.

- Après un retry qui échoue à nouveau, le badge réapparaît avec l'erreur de la NOUVELLE session, et « View log » pointe vers celle-ci.
- Le filtre « failed session » de la FilterBar suit exactement la même logique.

# Code Review — « Le badge "Session failed" réapparaît après un retry réussi »

**Commit:** `9c11796` — *fix(kanban): derive session-failed badge from the epic's latest session*
**Files:** `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts` (new), `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts`, `components/kanban/Board.tsx`, `components/kanban/EpicCard.tsx`, `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts` (new)

## Does it fix the bug?

Yes, and I verified it against real data rather than only by reading. Probing the live DB read-only (`/home/orosius/workspace/arij/data/arij.db`): **7 epics currently hold ≥1 failed session; under the new selector only 2 stay badged.** All 5 that clear had a later session *in the same scope* — their own retry. So the change removes exactly the stale badges the ticket describes and no legitimate ones.

Walking the reported sequence:

| Step | Newest session | Badge |
|---|---|---|
| Build fails at T1 | `failed` | shown, T1's error ✔ |
| Retry queued at T2 | `queued` | cleared ✔ |
| Retry completes at T3 | `completed` | **stays cleared** ✔ — the regression, fixed |
| Retry fails at T3 | `failed` | shown, with the *retry's* error and `sessionId` ✔ |

Extracting a pure selector is the right call — it removes the old code's hidden dependency on the API's sort order (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/route.ts:72-78`). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean; 60 tests pass across `latest-failure`, `epic-card*`, `kanban-board-filters`, `kanban-filter-bar`. `FilterBar`'s `hasFailedSession` follows automatically via `Board.tsx:283`.

---

## 1. Readability

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:10` — the docstring's premise is false for this codebase.**

> "created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision)."

Not true for any row the app writes. `createQueuedSession` (`lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts:325`) is the sole insert path and all 14 call sites pass `createdAt: new Date().toISOString()` — millisecond precision. Measured: `created_at` 237/237 ISO, **0 same-`created_at` groups per epic**. So the tie-break block (l.57-66) is unreachable for app data, and two of the nine tests pin an input the app cannot produce.

*Recommendation:* correct the docstring; keep the tie-break as the deliberate companion to finding 2 — once normalization lands, a legacy SQLite-format row genuinely *does* have second precision, which is when that block earns its place.

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:50` — the guard's stated rationale is wrong.**

> `// Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.`

Registry activities are hard-coded to `epicId: null` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:180`), so they can never reach `runningEpicIds`. That set only holds epicIds of **DB** rows in `running`/`queued` (same route, l.137). The guard's real effect is narrower: suppress the badge while a stale `queued`/`running` row coexists with a newer `failed` row. Behavior is unchanged from the old code — only the comment misleads.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:55` (also l.57, l.65) — re-implements a comparison this repo already solved, without the fix.**

`createdAt` and `endedAt` are compared as raw strings. `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:20-28` — a sibling module doing the same job for the same kanban cards — documents this exact hazard and ships the helper:

```ts
// Timestamps mix ISO-8601 (2026-08-16T09:00:00.000Z, written by routes) and
// SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (2026-08-16 09:00:00, both UTC). Normalizing the
// separator makes lexicographic comparison chronologically correct.
function normalizeTimestamp(value: string | null | undefined): string | null
```

`'T'` is `0x54`, `' '` is `0x20`, so **any** same-day ISO row sorts above **any** SQLite-format row regardless of real chronology. An epic with an ISO `failed` row and a *newer* SQLite-format `completed` retry picks the older failure as "newest" — a silent, intermittent recurrence of the very bug this ticket closes.

To be precise about the risk: this is **latent, not live**. I measured every timestamp column that feeds these comparisons and found no mixed formats anywhere (`agent_sessions` 237/237 and `ended_at` 234/234 ISO; `ticket_comments`, `epics`, `agent_session_chunks` likewise 100% ISO). `awaiting-reply.ts`'s helper is itself defensive — this repo *anticipated* the hazard, it hasn't hit it. But `agentSessions.createdAt` still defaults to `sql\`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\`` (`lib/db/schema.ts:188`), so one new call site omitting `createdAt:` reintroduces it, and raw-SQL fixtures already produce that format (`__tests__/permanent-delete.test.ts:57`).

I'm rating this Major on DRY grounds rather than live-defect grounds: a solved, documented helper twenty lines away was not reused, the fix is one import, and the failure mode is a silent return of the reported bug.

*Recommendation:* lift `normalizeTimestamp` into a shared module (e.g. `lib/utils/timestamps.ts`), apply it to both `createdAt` and `endedAt`, and have `awaiting-reply.ts` import it instead of keeping its private copy.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. The `try/catch` in `useAgentPolling.poll` is unchanged, `error || "Unknown error"` and `agentType || "build"` cover null columns, and the selector is total — no throw path.

## 4. Performance

**Suggestion — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:55` — object identity churn re-renders the whole board every 3 s.**

`setFailedSessions(failed)` always stores a freshly-built object, so the `epicViews` and `visibleColumns` memos (`components/kanban/Board.tsx:261,294`) invalidate on every poll and every card re-renders even when nothing failed. Pre-existing (the old inline loop did the same), but the selector is pure now, so a shallow compare against previous state would make the common "nothing changed" poll free.

The algorithm itself is fine: O(n) grouping plus O(m) per epic.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `selectLatestFailures` / `FailureCandidateSession` / `FailedSessionInfo` are descriptive, the file matches the directory's kebab-case convention, and the test sits with its peers.

## 6. Type Safety

**Minor — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:43` — the selector's input is untyped.**

```ts
const sessions = allData.data || [];   // any
```

Passed straight into `selectLatestFailures`, so nothing at that call site is checked — while `activeData` on l.47 gained an explicit `as UnifiedActivity[]` in this very commit. Annotate as `FailureCandidateSession[]` for symmetry. Otherwise clean: no `any` in the new module, and `FailedSessionInfo` now lives next to its selector, which is the right home.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts:13` — every fixture uses a format the app never writes.**

The `session()` helper defaults to `createdAt: "2026-08-21 10:00:00"` (SQLite format). The suite therefore never exercises real ISO input, and — because the format is uniform within each case — structurally cannot catch finding 2. Re-anchor the default to ISO and add an explicit mixed-format case once normalization lands.

**Minor — four coverage gaps.** The four cases that matter most (retry queued/running, retry completed, retry re-failed, registry guard) are present and well-named. Missing: `cancelled` as the latest status (it clears the badge — a real product decision worth pinning); two epics not leaking into each other; independence from input order (the selector no longer depends on the API's sort — lock that in); the `endedAt`-null fallback at l.63 where `newestGroup[0]` makes the choice arbitrary.

**Minor — behavior worth pinning, not changing: any newer session on the epic clears the badge.** `ticket_build`, `review_*`, `merge`, `qa` and `forensic` all set `epicId`, so a later story completing can erase an earlier story's failure with no retry. The obvious narrowing — keying on `(epicId, userStoryId)` — would **break** the Retry button, since `handleRetryBuild` (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:182`) posts an epic-level build with `userStoryId: null`. So the current key is right. I searched the live DB for this collateral and found **zero** instances: every failed session in a now-cleared epic had a later session in its own scope. Add a test documenting the trade-off so the next reader doesn't file it as a bug.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. No routes changed; `/api/projects/:id/sessions` still returns the full journal, so the out-of-scope requirement (the `sessions/` page keeps showing every failure) is respected.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 1 |

The fix is correct for the reported bug and the extraction into a pure selector is a genuine structural improvement, confirmed against production data. What holds it back is the Major: the new comparison re-implements timestamp ordering while ignoring a hazard this repo already documented and solved in the sibling module serving the same cards. It's latent rather than live — I measured that, and it corrects an earlier review pass on this ticket which implied the mixed format was already present in fixtures and data. But the fix is one import and the failure mode is a silent, intermittent return of the exact badge resurrection this ticket exists to kill.

**Filing status:** plan mode is active in this session, which forbids the non-read-only `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and `post_comment` calls. The anchored finding list and the filing steps are written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-glowing-dragonfly.md` and need relaying from a session that can write — verdict `changes_requested`. A previous review pass left compatible notes at `project-arij-misty-comet.md` that were also never filed; mine supersede them. The ticket status is untouched: it sits in `review`, and `review → done` is a human call.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**
