| Retry completes at T3 | `completed` | **stays cleared** ✔ — the regression, fixed |
| Retry fails at T3 | `failed` | shown, with the *retry's* error and `sessionId` ✔ |

Extracting a pure selector is the right call: it drops the old code's hidden dependency on the API's sort order (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/route.ts:68-78`). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean; 31 tests pass across `latest-failure`, `kanban-board-filters`, `kanban-filter-bar`. `FilterBar`'s `hasFailedSession` follows automatically via `Board.tsx:283`.

I also checked the ordering premise holds: `lib/agents/concurrency.ts` blocks a second `queued`/`running` session on the same epic (and story-scope dispatch blocks on the parent epic too), so created-order equals outcome-order. Live data confirms it — 1 create/end inversion in 170 epic-scoped sessions, none harmful, and `orchestration_mode` is `solo` for all 245 rows. Ordering by `createdAt` is therefore sound here.

---

## 1. Readability

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:10` — the docstring's premise is false, twice over.**

> "created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision)."

All 15 production `createQueuedSession` call sites pass `createdAt: now` where `now = new Date().toISOString()` — millisecond precision. Measured: `created_at` is **244/244 ISO**, 0 SQLite-format. And the code compares *full* strings, never second-truncated, so the scenario the paragraph describes — "a retry created in the same second as the failure it replaces" — does **not** produce a tie. Measured: **0 exact `created_at` collisions within an epic**, so lines 57–66 are unreachable for app-written data.

The ticket asserted second precision and the implementation took it at face value. Keep the tie-break — it earns its place once finding 2 lands, because a legacy SQLite-format row genuinely does have second precision — but say that's what it is.

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:50` — the guard's stated rationale is wrong.**

> `// Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.`

Registry activities are hard-coded `epicId: null` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:180`), so they can never reach `runningEpicIds`; that set only holds epicIds of **DB** rows in `running`/`queued`. The guard's real effect is narrower — suppress the badge while a stale `queued`/`running` row coexists with a newer `failed` row. Behaviour is unchanged from the old code; only the comment misleads.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:55` (also 57, 65) — re-implements a comparison this repo has already solved six times, and omits the fix.**

`createdAt` and `endedAt` are compared as raw strings. `normalizeTimestamp` exists in **six** places, including the two modules `Board.tsx` imports right alongside this one:

```
lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:25    lib/kanban/unread-ai.ts:34
lib/auto-mode/select.ts:89         lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:411
app/api/inbox/route.ts:45
```

and `awaiting-reply.ts` documents the exact hazard: `'T'` is `0x54`, `' '` is `0x20`, so **any** same-day ISO row sorts above **any** SQLite-format row regardless of real chronology. An epic holding an ISO `failed` row and a *newer* SQLite-format `completed` retry picks the older failure as "newest" — a silent, intermittent recurrence of the very bug this ticket closes.

To be precise about the risk: this is **latent, not live**. I measured every column feeding these comparisons and found no mixed formats (`created_at` 244/244, `ended_at` 242/242 ISO). But `agentSessions.createdAt` still defaults to `sql\`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\`` (`lib/db/schema.ts:188`), so one new call site omitting `createdAt:` reintroduces it, and raw-SQL fixtures already produce that format.

I'm rating this Major on DRY grounds, not live-defect grounds: a documented helper exists in the sibling files serving the same cards, this is the seventh site and the first to skip it, the fix is one import, and the failure mode is a silent return of the reported bug.

*Recommendation:* lift `normalizeTimestamp` into `lib/utils/timestamps.ts`, apply it to both fields here, and have the six existing copies import it.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. The `try/catch` in `useAgentPolling.poll` is unchanged, `error || "Unknown error"` and `agentType || "build"` cover null columns, the degenerate all-`createdAt`-null case falls through sanely, and the selector is total — no throw path.

## 4. Performance

The algorithm is fine: O(n) grouping plus O(m) per epic.

**Info — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:55` — object identity churn re-renders the whole board every 3 s.** `setFailedSessions` always stores a freshly-built object, invalidating the `epicViews` and `visibleColumns` memos (`Board.tsx:226,273`) on every poll. Pre-existing (the old inline loop did the same), but the selector is pure now, so a shallow compare would make the common no-change poll free.

**Info — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:36` — the selector needs 8 fields; the endpoint ships 30 columns.** `/api/projects/:id/sessions` does `db.select().from(agentSessions)` and spreads every row, so the board re-downloads every session `prompt`. Measured for the busiest project: **6.6 MB, 93 % of it prompt text**, re-fetched every 3 s (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:74`). Pre-existing and outside this ticket, but worth recording: `FailureCandidateSession` now documents exactly which columns the board actually needs.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `selectLatestFailures` / `FailureCandidateSession` / `FailedSessionInfo` are descriptive, the file matches the directory's kebab-case convention, and the test sits with its peers.

## 6. Type Safety

**Minor — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:43` — the selector's input is untyped.**

```ts
const sessions = allData.data || [];   // any
```

Flows straight into `selectLatestFailures`, so nothing at that call site is checked — while `activeData` on line 47 gained an explicit `as UnifiedActivity[]` in this very commit. Annotate as `FailureCandidateSession[]` for symmetry. Otherwise clean: no `any` in the new module, and `FailedSessionInfo` now lives next to its selector, which is the right home.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts:13` — every fixture uses a format the app never writes.** The `session()` helper defaults to `createdAt: "2026-08-21 10:00:00"`. The suite never exercises real ISO input and — because the format is uniform within each case — structurally cannot catch finding 2. Re-anchor the default to ISO, add an explicit mixed-format case once normalization lands.

**Minor — four coverage gaps.** The cases that matter most (retry queued/running, retry completed, retry re-failed, registry guard) are present and well-named. Missing: `cancelled` as the latest status; two epics not leaking into each other; independence from input order (the selector no longer depends on the API sort — lock that in); and the `endedAt`-null fallback at line 63 where `newestGroup[0]` is arbitrary.

**Minor — collateral worth pinning, not changing.** `ticket_build`, `review_*`, `merge`, `qa` and `forensic` all set `epicId`, so a later story completing can erase an earlier story's failure with no retry. The obvious narrowing — keying on `(epicId, userStoryId)` — would **break** the Retry button, since `handleRetryBuild` posts an epic-level build with `userStoryId: null`. So the current key is right. I searched the live DB and found **zero** instances of this collateral: all 5 cleared epics had a later success in the failure's own scope. Add a test documenting the trade-off.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. No routes changed; `/api/projects/:id/sessions` still returns the full journal, so the out-of-scope requirement (the `sessions/` page keeps showing every failure) is respected.

---

## Behaviour changes worth a decision, not just a test

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:60` — a `cancelled` latest session clears the badge.** Fail → retry → user cancels the retry now leaves a clean card, even though nothing succeeded. Under the old logic the failure kept badging. The sharp edge is `components/kanban/Board.tsx:246`: `onRetryBuild` is only passed when `failedSession` is set, so clearing the badge also removes the Retry button *and* the session-log link. Either treat `cancelled` as non-clearing, or decouple the retry affordance from the badge — clearing is much more frequent now.

**Open question for the ticket owner.** The *Symptôme* section says the badge persists « même si l'epic a depuis changé de colonne ». After the fix, **both** remaining badged epics are in `done` (`DRAGGABLE_COLUMNS` excludes only `released`, so `done` cards render the badge) — e.g. `noiu4l-H`, whose last session was a `review_feature` that died on `spawn E2BIG`. The stated *Comportement attendu* — "seul le résultat de la dernière session" — **is** satisfied, so this is a judgment call rather than a defect: confirm it's intended, or suppress the badge for `done`/`released`.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 7 |
| Info | 2 |

The fix is correct for the reported bug — verified against production data, not just by reading — and the extraction into a pure selector is a genuine structural improvement. What holds it back is the Major: the new comparison re-implements timestamp ordering while skipping a normalization this repo has written six times, twice in the modules serving these same cards. It's latent rather than live (I measured that), but the fix is one import and the failure mode is a silent, intermittent return of the exact badge resurrection this ticket exists to kill. The `cancelled`-clears-the-retry-button interaction is the one behaviour change that needs an explicit decision before this ships.

**Filing status:** plan mode is active in this session and blocks every non-read-only call — `mcp__arij__submit_findings`, `post_comment`, and even `get_ticket` return *"Cannot call … while in plan mode."* The anchored finding list (10 entries with file, line and severity, ready to paste into `submit_findings`) plus the verification data is written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-rosy-piglet.md` and needs relaying from a writable session — verdict `changes_requested`. Two earlier passes left compatible notes at `project-arij-misty-comet.md` and `project-arij-glowing-dragonfly.md` that were also never filed; mine supersede both. The ticket status is untouched: it sits in `review`, and `review → done` is a human call.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Review : le verdict structuré de submit_findings pilote les transitions
epics.description:
## Contexte
Le verdict de review est aujourd'hui du substring matching de prose (« changes requested », « not complete », « partially complete ») dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts`, alors que l'outil MCP `submit_findings` transmet déjà un verdict structuré — explicitement marqué « v1 » dans `app/api/mcp/submit-findings/route.ts` et `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts`. Enseignement de Code with Claude 2026 (« The expanding toolkit ») : le code qui compense l'infiabilité du modèle (parsing de prose) a une demi-vie courte ; le canal structuré doit devenir autoritaire.

## À construire
1. **Persister le verdict** : à la réception de `submit_findings`, écrire le verdict transmis (reprendre l'enum réelle de l'outil) avec l'id de session. Recommandation : colonne `reviewVerdict` sur `agent_sessions` (migration SQL manuscrite + `meta/_journal.json`, jamais `drizzle-kit generate`) — le verdict est un attribut de LA session de review, pas d'un finding.
2. **Priorité des canaux** dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts` et `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts` : (a) verdict structuré de la session de review du stage s'il existe — autoritaire, la prose est alors ignorée ; (b) sinon fallback prose actuel inchangé. Le fallback reste NÉCESSAIRE : les providers sans MCP (gemini-cli et les 8 autres) ne peuvent pas appeler submit_findings, et `review_provider_segregation` peut router vers eux.
3. **Prompt** : `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts` — présenter `submit_findings` comme LE canal attendu, le verdict prose n'étant qu'un fallback pour les sessions sans MCP.
4. **Cohérence findings bloquants** : la définition actuelle (agent + open + fenêtre du stage + préfixe `[critical]`/`[major]`) reste inchangée. Un verdict `approve` avec findings bloquants ouverts reste bloquant (les findings priment) — documenter ce cas dans le module et le tester.
5. **Traçabilité** : `ticket_activity_log` mentionne la source du verdict (`structured` vs `prose`) dans `reason`.

## Contraintes
- Aucun changement de la machine à états elle-même : on ne touche qu'à la DÉCISION, pas aux arêtes (`review → done` reste humain, cf. `docs/architecture/ticket-state-machine.md`).
- Rétro-compat totale : zéro submit_findings dans la fenêtre du stage → comportement bit-à-bit identique à aujourd'hui.
- Matrice de tests vitest : (verdict structuré négatif + prose positive → retour in_progress) ; (structuré positif + prose négative → pas de retour) ; (approve + finding [critical] ouvert → bloquant) ; (aucun verdict structuré → fallback prose).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Epic terminé — le verdict structuré de `submit_findings` pilote les transitions

Trois commits, un par user story.

### 1. Persistance du verdict — `5f99cdc`
- Migration manuscrite `0032_agent_session_review_verdict.sql` (`ALTER TABLE agent_sessions ADD COLUMN review_verdict text`) + entrée `_journal.json` (idx 31, `when` croissant). Pas de `drizzle-kit generate`.
- Écriture à la réception de `submit_findings`, scopée à `auth.sessionId` : une review ne peut parler que pour elle-même.
- Colonne listée dans `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` (`lib/db/init.ts`) comme 0023/0024/0026/0028/0030/0031 — l'ALTER n'est pas idempotent.
- **Contrat MCP inchangé** : aucun breaking change côté agent.

### 2. Canal structuré prioritaire — `5182683`
Trois canaux, ordre strict, centralisés dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts` :
1. **Verdict structuré** — autoritaire, la prose est ignorée.
2. **Findings bloquants** — un veto, jamais une approbation. `approved` + finding `[critical]`/`[major]` ouvert = **bloquant** : le reviewer s'est contredit, et le finding bloque de toute façon `review → done` dans le workflow engine. Définition du bloquant (agent + open + fenêtre du stage + préfixe) **inchangée**.
3. **Fallback prose** — inchangé. Nécessaire : gemini-cli et les autres providers sans MCP ne peuvent pas appeler l'outil, et `review_provider_segregation` peut router vers eux.

`transitionReviewRejected` accepte `verdictSource` et l'appose au `reason` → `ticket_activity_log` trace `[verdict source: structured|prose]`. Typé structurellement plutôt qu'importé du pipeline : la couche workflow est en dessous.

**Rétro-compat bit-à-bit** : zéro `submit_findings` dans la fenêtre → comportement identique à avant.

### 3. Prompt reviewer — `1f32523`
`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts` et la description de l'outil dans `bin/arij-mcp.mjs` présentent `submit_findings` comme LE canal lu. La consigne `**Overall Verdict: …**` reste présente et documentée comme fallback pour les sessions sans MCP.

### Vérification
- **Suite complète verte** : 374 fichiers, 4265 tests. `tsc --noEmit` propre, eslint propre.
- Matrice des 4 cas testée sur **les deux** points d'entrée (`assessReviewOutcome` et `resolveReviewVerdict`) : structuré négatif + prose propre → retour ; structuré positif + prose négative → pas de retour ; `approved` + `[critical]` ouvert → bloquant ; aucun verdict structuré → fallback prose. Plus un test d'isolation inter-sessions.
- Tests e2e pipeline et dispatch couvrant le cycle de fix piloté par le verdict structuré.

### Points vérifiés au-delà des critères
- **Pas de verdict périmé entre cycles** : chaque dispatch de review crée une nouvelle ligne `agent_sessions` (`createId()`), y compris sur resume — le resume ne réutilise que l'id de session côté CLI. Un verdict du cycle 1 ne peut pas décider du cycle 2.

# Code Review — Epic `sZItU3OorqBy`

**Review : le verdict structuré de `submit_findings` pilote les transitions**

Scope: `fb70006..HEAD`, 3 commits, 23 files (+1312/−82). Full report also written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-playful-creek.md`.

Verification re-run in this worktree: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0, eslint clean on all changed source files, 7 relevant test files green (174 tests).

The implementation is solid and unusually well-documented. All 9 acceptance criteria are met. Findings below are refinements, plus one gap where the epic's own premise isn't carried through to the *other* place a review verdict decides a transition.

---

## Findings

### 1. `lastCleanReviewAt` ignores `review_verdict` — Full Auto can merge a `changes_requested` review — **Major**

`lib/auto-mode/select.ts:311-316`

The merge gate's freshness half counts any review session with `status='completed' AND outcome='answered'` as clean. Its own doc (`select.ts:569-577`) calls it *"a review that COMPLETED WITH A VERDICT"* and *"stricter than the workflow engine on both axes"* — accurate before this epic, since no verdict was persisted anywhere. It now is, and this predicate doesn't read it. A reviewer submitting `changes_requested` with **zero findings** leaves `hasFreshCleanReview() === true` and `hasOpenReviewComments === false`, satisfying the merge gate.

The common path is protected — all three revert sites send the epic back to `in_progress`. But each is guarded by `currentEpic.status === "done" || "review"` (`stages.ts:895-897`, epic route `:365-366`, story route `:358-359`). When the epic isn't in one of those states at finalize time, the negative verdict is dropped with **no transition and no activity-log entry**, while the durable column records it.

**Failure scenario:** epic in `review`, Full Auto dispatches a review. The user drags it to `in_progress` mid-run — a legal drag, since the `in_progress` lock guard (`engine.ts:57-65`) only fires on `fromStatus === "in_progress"`. The reviewer finishes `changes_requested` with zero findings; the status guard skips the revert. The user drags back to `review`. `lastCleanReviewAt > lastTerminalCodeAt`, zero open comments → Full Auto merges to Done against an explicit `changes_requested`.

**Recommendation:** add `AND (review_verdict IS NULL OR review_verdict <> 'changes_requested')` to the CASE. `NULL` must stay clean — that's the MCP-less provider path the epic is built around.

### 2. `verdictSource: "prose"` returned when blocking findings decided — **Minor**

`lib/pipeline/findings.ts:335` — the no-structured-verdict branch always returns `"prose"`, including when `agentCommentCount > 0` and `blockingFindings.length > 0` decided. The type doc (`:274-275`) declares the field as *"which channel decided `blocking`, for the activity-log trail."* The justification at `:285-288` conflates *which code branch ran* with *which channel decided*. Harmless only because nothing consumes it (finding 6); it becomes a wrong log entry the moment someone wires it up. `resolveReviewVerdict` doesn't have this problem — its fallback genuinely is a pure prose scan.

### 3. A delivered structured verdict is discarded when the reviewer also asks a question — **Minor**

`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:862-873`, epic route `:337-347`, story route `:338-348`. The comment *"A reviewer that asked a question delivered no verdict at all"* was true for prose; it isn't now. An agent can call `submit_findings(changes_requested)` — persisted, durable — then ask a question. `askedQuestion` short-circuits before the verdict is read. The ticket is held, so nothing unsafe happens, but the verdict never reaches the log and the resumed cycle starts from a fresh row with `review_verdict = NULL`. At minimum the comment now asserts something the schema disproves.

### 4. `review_verdict` writable by any non-chat session, contradicting the schema comment — **Minor**

`app/api/mcp/submit-findings/route.ts:65-73`, `:107-110`. The route rejects only `agentType === "chat"`; `build` and `fix` are in the `"agent"` toolset (`bin/arij-mcp.mjs:359`) and can stamp their own row. No exploit — the write is correctly scoped to `auth.sessionId` and `readStructuredReviewVerdict` is only called with review session ids. But `schema.ts:175` and `0032_*.sql:12-15` both state *"NULL for non-review sessions"*, which isn't enforced.

### 5. Epic-wide findings veto with a per-session window cross-contaminates concurrent reviewers — **Minor**

`lib/pipeline/findings.ts:388-398`. The epic review route dispatches up to four concurrent sessions; the veto is scoped by epic and time only, with `sinceIso` defaulting to *the calling session's* `startedAt`. A security reviewer submitting `approved` reverts the epic because the code-quality reviewer filed a `[critical]` after it started. The revert is defensible; the attribution isn't — the log reads `Review verdict: changes requested (Security Review) [verdict source: structured]` when that session's structured verdict was `approved`. New behaviour for the routes, which never consulted findings rows before. `ReviewVerdictDecision` already carries `structuredVerdict` and `blockingFindings` separately; the callers just collapse them.

### 6–9. Suggestions

- **`runner.ts:88-94`** — `verdictSource`/`structuredVerdict` populated by `stages.ts:208-209`, consumed by nothing outside tests. `structuredVerdict?: string | null` needlessly widens the enum. (The union duplication is defensible — `runner.ts` deliberately imports only from `./constants`.)
- **`constants.ts:176-177`** — `blocking` can now be true with `blockingFindings.length === 0`, so the pipeline fails citing *"blocking findings remain"* when none exist, and `runner.ts:528` explicitly relies on the findings being the diagnostic.
- **`findings.ts:222-235`** — the `createdAt` fallback would misparse SQLite's `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"`, UTC, no zone) as local time, opening the window early. Unreachable today — the function is only called after a structured verdict exists, which implies `running`, which sets ISO `startedAt` (`lifecycle.ts:293`) — but it's exported, so worth a note.
- **`submit-findings/route.ts:86-122`** — three independent `.run()` calls; the verdict is a new third write between two pre-existing ones. Consequences are benign, but `db.transaction()` makes it atomic for free.

---

## Checklist

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| Readability | Strong — headers state channel priority, the retro-compat contract, and *why* the prose fallback isn't legacy baggage. |
| DRY | Good. Prose parsing existed at three sites; `NEGATIVE_VERDICT_SUBSTRINGS` (`findings.ts:245-249`) is now the only place that knows the vocabulary (verified by grep across `lib/`, `app/`, `bin/`). |
| Error handling | Adequate. An unrecognised stored value is treated as absent rather than trusted (`:194-201`) — right default for a free-text column. See findings 3, 9. |
| Performance | No concern — PK lookup on an already query-heavy path. |
| Naming | Consistent. One misleading *value*, not a name (finding 2). |
| Type safety | No `any`; `StructuredReviewVerdict` derived from the const tuple with a real type guard. One avoidable widening (finding 6). |
| Testing | Strong — all four matrix cases on **both** entry points, plus `approved_with_minor_issues`, resolved-finding, omitted-session-id, cross-session isolation, window boundaries. Migration bookkeeping tested on three paths (baseline stamp, bookkeeping-less recovery, journal-reorder re-run). |
| API design | Input schema byte-identical (AC 1.3); verdict write scoped to `auth.sessionId`; no state-machine edge touched — `review → done` stays human. |

**Acceptance criteria: 9/9 met.** Migration hand-written, monotonic `_journal.json` entry, `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` recovery entry; snapshots still stop at `0013`, so no `drizzle-kit generate`.

**Summary:** 0 Critical · 1 Major · 4 Minor · 4 Suggestion

Two process notes: plan mode is active, so I could not call `submit_findings` to file these through the MCP channel — the findings above are the report only, not persisted rows. And I did not move the ticket; a session cannot promote its own.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: Outil MCP report_friction : les agents signalent ce qui les gêne (WCF)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement Cursor (skill « WCF », Code with Claude 2026) : « quand quelque chose est agaçant, cassé ou confus, signale-le au lieu de forcer ». Les agents d'Arij rencontrent des frictions (scripts cassés, docs mensongères, conventions ambiguës) et les contournent silencieusement — l'information est perdue. Un canal structuré transforme ces frictions en backlog de DevX.

## À construire
1. **Outil MCP `report_friction`** (toolset agent) : payload `{ category: broken_tooling|misleading_docs|flaky_test|unclear_convention|other, description, filePath? }`. Table `frictions` (id, projectId, epicId nullable, agentSessionId, category, description, filePath, occurrences, status: new|triaged|converted|dismissed, createdAt — migration SQL manuscrite + `_journal.json`). Dédoublonnage doux : une friction ouverte avec même (category, filePath) → incrémenter `occurrences` au lieu de créer une ligne.
2. **Prompt** : une phrase dans la section « Arij tools » (voir `lib/claude/process-manager.ts` / prompt-sections) : signaler les frictions SANS s'arrêter de travailler — l'outil est fire-and-forget, jamais une excuse pour ne pas finir la tâche.
3. **UI** : vue « Frictions » par projet (section des réglages ou onglet dédié) : liste triée par occurrences, filtres par catégorie/statut, actions : « créer un ticket » (pré-remplit un epic via la création existante, lie la friction → status converted) et « ignorer » (dismissed).
4. **Intégration Dreaming** : si le ticket Dreaming est livré, les frictions ouvertes entrent dans le digest (signal de pièges récurrents).

## Contraintes
- L'outil ne modifie JAMAIS le board (pas de transition, pas de commentaire ticket) — il écrit uniquement dans frictions.
- Auth par token MCP, scope projet/session comme les autres outils.
- Tests vitest : validation payload, dédoublonnage par (category, filePath), scope token, conversion en ticket (statuts cohérents).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

Here is the review report.

# Code Review — Epic « Outil MCP `report_friction` »

Scope: `4957611..HEAD` (3 commits, 30 files, +1871/−21). Reviewed statically; the test suite was **not** executed (plan mode is active), and no findings were filed via `submit_findings` — see the note at the end.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong. Every new module carries a header explaining *why*, not just what: the `frictions` table documents why `agentSessionId` is deliberately not a foreign key (`lib/db/schema.ts:231-238`), the MCP route states up front that the token is the sole scope authority, and `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts` comments were updated in lockstep with the allowlist. Naming is clear throughout.

One nit — **Suggestion**: `components/kanban/EpicCreateDialog.tsx:76-89`, the new seed effect duplicates `resetForm()` (`:110-117`) minus `pendingFocusKey` and `storyTitleRefs`. Two reset paths that quietly differ. A single `seedForm(draft?)` used by both would remove the divergence.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/frictions/route.ts:24`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:270`, `app/projects/[projectId]/frictions/page.tsx:36`**
The same predicate appears verbatim three times:

```ts
OPEN_FRICTION_STATUSES.includes(row.status as (typeof OPEN_FRICTION_STATUSES)[number])
```

Export `isOpenFrictionStatus(status: string): boolean` from `lib/frictions/constants.ts` and drop all three casts.

Otherwise good reuse: conversion goes through the existing `POST /epics` transaction rather than a parallel path, and the friction inbox reuses `EpicCreateDialog` instead of forking a form.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. The MCP route distinguishes malformed JSON from schema failures, emits field-level `INVALID_PAYLOAD` detail an agent can act on, and its 500 message explicitly tells the agent the board was untouched and to keep working — correct for a fire-and-forget tool. Conversion conflicts surface as `409 FRICTION_CLOSED` rather than a generic 500. `ProjectFrictionLink` swallows its fetch error on purpose, with a comment saying why.

## 4. Performance

**Major — `app/api/mcp/report-friction/route.ts:85-113`** *(this is the blocking one; details under Correctness below)*

**Minor — `components/frictions/ProjectFrictionLink.tsx:20` + `app/api/projects/[projectId]/frictions/route.ts:16-30`**
`GET /frictions` is unbounded — every row, each `description` up to 4000 chars — and `openCount` is computed in JS over the full result set. `ProjectFrictionLink` fetches that entire payload to render one number, on every mount of `AgentConfigPanel`. Add a `?summary=1` count mode and a limit on the list.

Indexes themselves are well chosen; `frictions_open_dedupe_idx` covers the write-path lookup exactly.

## 5. Naming Conventions

**Suggestion** — `filePath` is camelCase while the rest of the agent MCP surface is snake_case: `submit_findings` takes `file_path`, and `get_ticket` / `post_comment` / `ask_question` / `update_ticket_status` all take `ticket_id`. Precedent is already mixed (`submit_grading` uses `storyId`), so this is consistency-of-the-schema-the-model-sees, not a defect.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `FrictionCategory` / `FrictionStatus` are threaded through `$type<>()` so the Drizzle row is narrowed, and `Friction` / `NewFriction` are exported and asserted in `db-schema.test.ts:950`. The only rough edges are the `as (typeof OPEN_FRICTION_STATUSES)[number]` casts from finding 4 and `targetType as "feature" | "bug"` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:396`), both fixable by typing the constant lookup rather than casting at the call site.

**Suggestion** — `lib/db/schema.ts` names three CHECK constraints (`frictions_category_check`, `_status_check`, `_occurrences_check`) that `lib/db/migrations/0034_frictions.sql:9-12` emits unnamed. Cosmetic since `drizzle-kit generate` is forbidden, but the two sources of truth disagree.

## 7. Testing

Genuinely thorough — ~430 lines on the MCP route alone: every category, trimming, token-derived scope, cross-project isolation, missing/unknown/revoked/chat tokens, ticketless sessions, dedup across sessions, the omitted-path key, non-dedup cases, and an explicit assertion that no transition, comment or activity row is produced. Plus API, page, dialog, schema, prompt and shim coverage.

Gaps worth noting (not findings): the `FRICTION_WRITE_FAILED` 500 path is untested, and `frictions-page.test.tsx` mocks `EpicCreateDialog` — pre-fill is covered instead by `epic-create-dialog.test.tsx`, which is a reasonable split.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. `{ data }` / `{ error, code }` shapes are consistent, status codes are right (400 payload, 401 token, 403 chat token, 404 unknown, 409 closed), and the chat-token rejection mirrors `ask_question` / `submit_findings` / `submit_grading` exactly. `GET` returning `{ frictions, openCount }` instead of a bare array is a justified departure.

---

## Correctness — the blocking finding

**Major — Path-less deduplication merges unrelated frictions and discards their text**
`app/api/mcp/report-friction/route.ts:85-113`

```ts
const sameFile = body.filePath === undefined
  ? isNull(frictions.filePath)
  : eq(frictions.filePath, body.filePath);
```

When `filePath` is omitted, the dedupe key degenerates to `(projectId, category)`. Every path-less report in a category collapses onto the oldest open row; only `occurrences` is bumped, and the new `description`, `agentSessionId` and `epicId` are dropped with no trace.

Path-less reports are the *expected* common case: `filePath` is optional in the shim schema (`bin/arij-mcp.mjs:145-150`), the prompt sentence never asks for one (`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:199-202`), and `other` is definitionally heterogeneous. So the inbox will show `×7 — "The check script exits without diagnostics"` when six of those seven reports were about something else entirely. That is misleading during triage, not merely lossy — and the occurrence count is what the whole UI sorts by.

This *does* match the written acceptance criterion (« Dédoublonnage (category, filePath) ouvert → occurrences++ »). The AC simply didn't anticipate the absent-path case, which is why I'm flagging it rather than treating it as delivered-as-specified.

**Fix (smallest correct change):** skip the dedup lookup entirely when `body.filePath === undefined`. Better: add an indexed `dedupe_key` column computed at write time from `category + filePath + normalized(description)` — the convention this repo already uses for grouping keys. At minimum, append the new description to the existing row instead of discarding it.

## Other correctness notes

**Minor — a deduplicated report never refreshes recency.** There is no `last_seen_at`; `created_at` is the only timestamp, the page renders it as *the* report date (`app/projects/[projectId]/frictions/page.tsx:236`), and the list tiebreak is `createdAt DESC`. A friction hit 30 times over two months reads as two months stale.

**Minor — `triaged` is unreachable.** It exists in `lib/frictions/constants.ts:11-17`, the CHECK constraint, the labels and the status `<select>`, but nothing writes it: PATCH accepts only `z.literal("dismissed")` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/frictions/[frictionId]/route.ts:10`), and conversion writes `converted`. Selecting "Triaged" always returns an empty list.

**Minor — epic item 4 (Dreaming integration) is not implemented.** Neither `collectDreamDigest` (`lib/workflow/dreaming.ts:594`) nor `assembleDreamDigest` (`lib/workflow/dreaming-digest.ts:420`) reads `frictions`. The epic gated this on « si le ticket Dreaming est livré » and Dreaming *is* on main, so the condition holds — but it appears in none of the three user stories' acceptance criteria. Worth confirming as scope rather than assuming a defect.

**Suggestion — conversion hard-codes `type: "feature"`** (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:296-297`). A `broken_tooling` or `flaky_test` friction is usually a bug ticket, and the coercion is silent.

**Suggestion — "Source session" can 404** (`app/projects/[projectId]/frictions/page.tsx:229`), since the schema comment states friction deliberately outlives session cleanup.

---

## What is solid

- **Scope safety.** Project/session/epic come only from the bearer token; the payload is `.strict()` with no scope fields, and a test proves cross-project reports stay isolated.
- **Board isolation** — the constraint the epic cared most about — is enforced by construction and asserted by a dedicated test.
- **Conversion atomicity.** The epic insert and the `converted` update share one transaction; the in-transaction `changes !== 1` guard makes the pre-check TOCTOU-safe, and `FrictionConversionConflict` rolls back the `ticket_counter` bump so no readable-ID gap is burned.
- **Migration hygiene.** Hand-written SQL, monotone journal entry (`idx 33`, `when 1786713100000`), FKs and indexes mirrored in `schema.ts` and asserted in tests. No `drizzle-kit generate`.
- **Shim routing** falls out of the existing generic `name.replace(/_/g, "-")` mapping — no special case added.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 5 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

This is careful, well-tested work that gets the security-relevant parts right. The one Major is a small, well-localized change in the write path, and everything else is polish.

Two process notes: plan mode was active, so I did not run the suite and did not file these through `submit_findings` — the report and a remediation plan are written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-golden-yao.md`. Approving the plan lets me file the findings and apply the fixes.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

Path-less is the expected common case — the prompt never asks for a path (`prompt-sections.ts:199`), `filePath` is optional in the shim schema, and `other` is definitionally path-less. Neither `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts` nor `lib/workflow/dreaming-digest.ts` references `frictions` (verified by grep over `lib/workflow/`). |---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

The blocking finding from the first pass is genuinely fixed and covered by a regression test. `frictions_open_dedupe_idx` is still exactly right for the write path.

## 5. Naming Conventions

**Suggestion** — `bin/arij-mcp.mjs:147`: `filePath` is camelCase while `submit_findings` takes `file_path` and the ticket tools take `ticket_id`. Precedent is already mixed (`submit_grading` uses `storyId`), so this is consistency of the schema the model sees, not a defect.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `FrictionCategory` / `FrictionStatus` are threaded through `$type<>()` so the Drizzle row is narrowed, and `Friction` / `NewFriction` are exported and asserted in `__tests__/db-schema.test.ts`. The rough edges are the casts from finding 2 and `targetType as "feature" | "bug"` (`epics/route.ts:396`), both fixable by typing the constant lookup rather than casting at the call site.

**Suggestion** — `lib/db/schema.ts:265-277` names three CHECK constraints that `0034_frictions.sql:9-13` emits unnamed. Cosmetic since `drizzle-kit generate` is forbidden, but the two sources of truth disagree.

## 7. Testing

Thorough — 12 cases and ~440 lines on the MCP route alone: every category, trimming, token-derived scope, cross-project isolation, missing/unknown/revoked/chat tokens, ticketless sessions, dedup across sessions, non-dedup cases, and an explicit assertion that no transition, comment, or activity row is produced (`report-friction-mcp.test.ts:422`). Plus API (4), page (3), settings-link, dialog, schema, prompt, and shim coverage.

Gaps (not blocking): the `FRICTION_WRITE_FAILED` 500 path is untested; nothing covers two *identical* path-less reports (finding below); nothing covers the same file under two path spellings (finding below); and `frictions-page.test.tsx` mocks `EpicCreateDialog`, with pre-fill covered separately in `epic-create-dialog.test.tsx` — a reasonable split.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. `{ data }` / `{ error, code }` shapes are consistent, status codes are right (400 payload, 401 token, 403 chat token, 404 unknown, 409 closed), and the chat-token rejection mirrors `ask_question` / `submit_findings` / `submit_grading` exactly. `GET` returning `{ frictions, openCount }` instead of a bare array is a justified departure.

---

## Correctness

All four below were raised in earlier passes and are unchanged at HEAD.

**Minor — `filePath` is never normalized, so the only surviving dedup key is exact-string.** `report-friction/route.ts:26` (schema), `:99` (comparison). `z.string().trim()` trims whitespace and nothing else. Build sessions run in per-epic worktrees under `.arij-worktrees/<epic-branch-slug>/`, and this project's own memory instructs agents to *"cite files by their worktree path"* — while the shim description asks for a "repository-relative path" and nothing enforces it. Two epics hitting the same broken script report different absolute strings, producing two `×1` rows and no bump; same for `lib/x.ts` vs `./lib/x.ts`. `occurrences` is what the entire inbox sorts by. `lib/documents/scan.ts:88` already does `path.relative(root, abs).split(path.sep).join("/")` and `lib/projects/workspace.ts:71` already resolves containment.

**Minor — the fix trades a false merge for a false split.** `report-friction/route.ts:88`: identical repeat reports with no `filePath` each create their own `×1` row. Path-less is the common case — the prompt never asks for a path (`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:199-202`), `filePath` is optional, and `other` is definitionally path-less. Nothing is lost or misleading, which is why this is Minor and not a re-raise — but it runs against the convention the project already records (derive a stable dedup key from the source signature and check it before inserting). Both directions close with one indexed `dedupe_key` computed from `category + normalizedPath + normalize(description)`.

**Minor — `frictions.epicId` is overloaded and conversion destroys provenance.** `lib/db/schema.ts:246`, `epics/route.ts:424`. On insert it is the epic the reporting session was building; conversion overwrites it with the new ticket's id. With `ON DELETE set null`, deleting the converted ticket leaves a `converted` row with no link and no route back — the "View ticket" button (`page.tsx:265`) is gated on `friction.epicId`. A separate `converted_epic_id` keeps both facts.

**Minor — `triaged` is unreachable.** It exists in `lib/frictions/constants.ts:13`, the CHECK constraint, the labels, `OPEN_FRICTION_STATUSES`, and the status `<select>` (`page.tsx:171`), but nothing writes it: PATCH accepts only `z.literal("dismissed")` (`frictions/[frictionId]/route.ts:10`), conversion writes `converted`, MCP writes `new`. Selecting "Triaged" always returns an empty list.

**Minor — a deduplicated report never refreshes recency.** No `last_seen_at`; `created_at` is the only timestamp and `page.tsx:235-237` renders it as *the* report date. A path-anchored friction hit 30 times over two months reads as two months stale.

A `broken_tooling` or `flaky_test` friction is usually a bug, and the dialog offers no choice. `__tests__/frictions-api.test.ts:131` shows this is deliberate hardening against a smuggled payload field, which is fair — but every converted friction lands as a feature.

**Suggestion — "Source session" can 404** (`page.tsx:229`). The route exists (`app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx`), but the schema comment states friction deliberately outlives session cleanup, so the link is knowingly dangling for old rows.

**Suggestion — the inbox has no live refresh.** New frictions from running agents only appear on reload, even though the project has a scoped SSE bus. Not in any acceptance criterion; worth noting since the whole point is unattended agents filing reports.

---

## Scope note — epic item 4 is not implemented

`grep -rn friction lib/workflow/` returns nothing: neither `dreaming.ts` nor `dreaming-digest.ts` reads `frictions`. The epic gated this on « si le ticket Dreaming est livré » and Dreaming *is* on main, so the condition holds — but it appears in none of the three stories' acceptance criteria. Worth confirming as scope rather than assuming a defect.

## What is solid

- **Scope safety.** Project, session, and epic come only from the bearer token (`McpTokenRecord`, `lib/mcp/token-store.ts:28-41`); the payload is `.strict()` with no scope fields; a test proves cross-project reports stay isolated.
- **Board isolation** — the constraint the epic cared most about — holds through three independent gates: absent from `lib/chat/board-tools.ts`, absent from `ARIJ_MCP_CHAT_ALLOWED_TOOL_NAMES`, and rejected at the route for `agentType === "chat"`. Asserted by a dedicated test.
- **Conversion atomicity.** Epic insert and the `converted` update share one transaction; the in-transaction `changes !== 1` guard makes the pre-check TOCTOU-safe; `FrictionConversionConflict` rolls back the `ticket_counter` bump so no readable-ID gap is burned. - **Prompt and injection wiring.** The fire-and-forget sentence rides the shared `base` string in `arijToolsSection` (`prompt-sections.ts:190-202`), so it reaches every non-exempt agent type without touching the build/review/grading extras, and it is gated behind `providerSupportsMcp(provider) && isMcpToolsEnabled()` (`process-manager.ts:117`) — no agent is told to call a tool it does not have.
- **Shim routing** falls out of the existing generic `name.replace(/_/g, "-")` mapping (`bin/arij-mcp.mjs:469`) — no special case added, and `TOOL_NAMES` keeps the tool uncallable under the chat toolset.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 7 |
| Suggestion | 7 |

The pass-1 blocking finding remains genuinely fixed and covered by a regression test. Everything here is polish or follow-up; nothing blocks the merge. The highest-value change is still a single `0035` migration adding `dedupe_key` + `last_seen_at` + `converted_epic_id` and normalizing `filePath` at the write boundary — that closes four findings at once. The second is bounding the inbox read and swapping the dead index, which closes the two performance items.

**Process notes:** plan mode is active, so I did not run the suite and did not file these through `submit_findings`. The report and a sequenced remediation plan are at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-iterative-sloth.md`; approving it lets me file the findings and apply the fixes. Live MCP validation of `report_friction` remains pending the merge — the orchestrator runs `main`, not this branch.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

## Epic livrée — 3 commits sur `feature/epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise`

Un refus n'est pas une erreur : le projet est supprimé et la réponse dit quel garde-fou a refusé (`not_managed` / `outside_projects_root` / `missing`).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Epic delivered — 3 commits, full suite green (2496 tests / 257 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on every file I touched.

## What I built

**Story 1 — deletion cleanup.** `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]?removeDirectory=true`, honoured only when two independent gates both pass: `clone_source = "github"` **and** the path is a strict descendant of the current projects root. A refusal isn't an error — the project is deleted either way and the response reports which gate refused. Removal runs `git worktree prune`, then detaches and deletes the worktrees **git has registered** for that clone (worktrees are named after the branch, not the repo, so guessing directory names would hit the wrong clone), then the clone. The shared `.arij-worktrees` is never removed. Sessions and ephemeral activities are cancelled on every delete, and per-project settings rows are swept — `settings` has no FK to `projects`, so they'd otherwise be inherited by a later project reusing the id.

**Story 2 — resume.** Destination classification decides between three outcomes: healthy clone of the same repo → fetch only, `reused: true`; clone of a *different* repo → 409, never overwritten; debris from an interrupted run (`.git` present, HEAD unborn) → replaced, not reported as a conflict. A valid `arji.json` still short-circuits the LLM.

**Story 3 — provenance.** Header strip with the absolute path, one-click copy, and an "Arij-managed clone" badge plus source link. The badge keys off `clone_source`, not the presence of a remote, so a user's own checkout of a GitHub repo isn't mislabelled.

The guard tests run against real git repositories in temp dirs — the story is about which directories vanish from disk, and a mocked `simple-git` can't show that. They cover symlink-escape, root-itself, and shared-prefix cases. One real defect surfaced and was fixed along the way: `simpleGit()` throws *synchronously* from its factory on a missing directory, which sat outside the guarded blocks in `detectDefaultBranch`.

## One thing you need to decide

This epic depends on a clone foundation that **isn't on `main`** — it's being built right now on four sibling branches. I implemented it so this branch compiles and tests standalone, which means `0027_project_clone_source.sql`, `lib/projects/workspace*.ts`, `lib/git/clone.ts` and `parseGitHubRepoInput` exist here *and* on those branches.

Worth knowing before you plan the merge: **the sibling branches already conflict with each other** independently of me. `epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC` adds `0027_git_sync_log_nullable_project.sql` claiming the same journal `idx: 26` as `epic-UY7xsxcNN41T`'s `0027_project_clone_source.sql`. One of them needs renumbering regardless of what happens to my branch.

Recommended order: foundation → parsing → clone service → this one, keeping the sibling implementations for foundation files and taking only `lib/projects/{clone-cleanup,cancel-sessions,project-settings-keys}.ts`, the `DELETE` handler, `ProjectSourceBadge.tsx` and the seven `__tests__/clone-lifecycle-*` files from here. Their nullable `git_sync_log.project_id` is a better fix than my workaround (console-log the clone when no project row exists yet) — prefer theirs.

Ticket moved to review; the merge guidance is in a comment on it.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Critical — Pre-existing directories can be recursively deleted

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:156](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:156)

**Description:** Any non-empty destination without a readable origin is classified as `partial_clone`, including arbitrary directories, files, and valid local repositories without remotes. It is then recursively deleted before cloning. The tests currently codify this unsafe behavior.

**Recommendation:** Treat every existing destination as a conflict unless it is positively identified as the expected clone or carries a trusted Arij-created marker. Only clean up directories created by the current clone attempt.

### 2. Major — Concurrent clone requests can delete each other’s result

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:273](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:273)

**Description:** Classification, cloning, and cleanup are not serialized. Two requests can both observe an absent destination; when one clone subsequently fails because the other created it, its error handler deletes the shared destination.

**Recommendation:** Add a per-destination lock covering classification through completion. Cleanup must only remove a directory proven to have been created by that invocation.

### 3. Major — Clone ownership is client-writable

**Location:** [app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60)

**Description:** The generic PATCH route can set `cloneSource` to `"github"`, while deletion trusts that value as proof of ownership. A user-supplied project inside the projects root can therefore be reclassified and recursively removed. The generic creation route similarly trusts client-supplied provenance.

**Recommendation:** Make provenance immutable through PATCH and establish it through a trusted server-side clone handoff or durable pending-clone record.

### 4. Major — Cleanup can delete non-Arij worktrees

**Location:** [lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158)

**Description:** Registered worktrees are deleted whenever they are anywhere beneath `projectsRoot`. The acceptance criterion limits removal to the clone’s `.arij-worktrees` entries. A manually created worktree elsewhere under the root, including uncommitted work, would be force-removed.

**Recommendation:** Require strict containment under the shared `.arij-worktrees` directory before either `git worktree remove` or `fs.rm`.

### 5. Major — First-time clones are not written to `git_sync_log`

**Location:** [app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144)

**Description:** A normal import has no project ID yet, so the function returns without creating an audit row. Consequently, almost every first-time clone and clone failure violates the requirement that each clone be recorded.

**Recommendation:** Make `git_sync_log.project_id` nullable and log pre-project operations with `NULL`, as already anticipated in the merge guidance.

### 6. Major — Persisted default branch is never consumed

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:331](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:331)

**Description:** `defaultBranch` is detected and stored, but no production code reads it. `lib/git/manager.ts` still guesses only `main` or `master`, so repositories using branches such as `develop` will clone successfully but fail during worktree creation or merging.

**Recommendation:** Thread the persisted branch through worktree, merge, and release operations, retaining the old guess only for legacy rows.

## Checklist Assessment

1. **Readability:** No additional issues found.
2. **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
3. **Error Handling:** Findings 1, 2, and 5.
4. **Performance:** No issues found.
5. **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
6. **Type Safety:** No issues found.
7. **Testing:** Tests are extensive, but currently assert the unsafe behavior in Finding 1 and omit concurrent cloning, manually placed worktrees, and non-`main` default-branch integration.
8. **API Design:** Findings 3 and 5.

## Verification

- TypeScript: passed.
- Targeted ESLint: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Targeted Vitest execution was blocked before collection because the read-only environment prevented Vitest from creating its temporary directory.
- Arij’s structured findings endpoint was invoked, but the connector required approval while this session’s approval policy was `never`; the findings could not be persisted to the ticket.

## Summary

- Critical: 1
- Major: 5
- Minor: 0
- Suggestions: 0

The findings apply to the current checkout. Some overlapping clone-service code may be replaced during the documented sibling-branch merge, but the resolved tree requires another review before approval.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
The epic itself was already implemented; the actual work was the **Changes Requested** review — 1 critical and 5 major findings. All six are fixed in `cae1682`, suite green at 2525 tests / 259 files, typecheck clean.

**The critical finding and the ownership finding were one bug.** Nothing on disk distinguished a clone Arij made from a directory that merely sat where Arij would have put one — classification guessed from `origin`, and `clone_source` (the flag authorising deletion) was a column any PATCH could set. Both now rest on a fact: `.git/arij-clone.json`, written by the clone service into repositories it creates. Inside `.git` deliberately — git never shows it, it can't be committed, and it dies with the repo it vouches for.

For the critical one I didn't just fix the classification. Downloads now run into a staging sibling and land with a single `rename`, so the destination is never observably half-cloned and the whole detect-and-delete-the-debris path is gone. A failed clone can only delete its own staging directory. That also satisfies the story's "interrupted clone is reused, not a conflict" criterion by construction rather than by heuristic.

The rest: a per-destination lock (in-process by design — one local server, and a lock file would add stale-lock recovery to solve a case that can't occur here); provenance derived server-side and absent from both request schemas, with a managed clone's path frozen; worktree cleanup confined to `.arij-worktrees`; `git_sync_log.project_id` nullable via hand-written `0028`; and `resolveBaseBranch` replacing the `main`/`master` guess across all 14 call sites.

Two things worth your attention:

- **The default-branch fix reaches further than the finding did.** `resolveBaseBranch` consults `origin/HEAD`, so `develop`-based repositories now work for *user-supplied* projects too — those never had a recorded branch to read, and were equally broken.
- **Three tests asserted the unsafe behaviour** and now assert the refusal instead. I kept a separate `arij_debris` case so the safe replace path stays pinned. Updating a test to match new behaviour is worth a second look from you, since it's exactly the move that can hide a regression.

The merge caveat from the earlier session is unchanged and still the main risk: this branch carries a clone foundation that isn't on `main`, and two sibling branches still both claim journal `idx: 26` independently of anything I did. Ticket is back in review.

epics.title: Docs : scan du projet pour importer automatiquement les documents (pdf/md/doc/docx…)
epics.description:
## Contexte

La partie **Docs** d'Arij permet d'attacher des documents au projet (utilisés par ex. dans le contexte des sessions agents, cf. E-arij-008). Aujourd'hui, il faut les ajouter un à un manuellement.

Il faut ajouter la possibilité de **scanner le projet** pour récupérer automatiquement tous les fichiers documents (`.pdf`, `.md`, `.doc`, `.docx`, et autres formats lisibles au besoin) et de **demander à l'utilisateur** lesquels il veut rendre accessibles via Arij.

## Comportement souhaité

1. Bouton **« Scanner le projet »** dans la vue Docs.
2. Le scan parcours le répertoire du projet et liste tous les fichiers documents détectés (nom, chemin, taille).
3. L'utilisateur coche les documents qu'il veut importer → confirmation → ils deviennent des documents accessibles via Arij, au même titre que les docs ajoutés manuellement.
4. Les docs déjà importés sont détectés et ne sont **pas dupliqués** au rescan.

## Questions ouvertes

- Formats pris en charge : au minimum pdf/md/doc/docx — on inclut aussi txt/rtf/html ?
- En cas de rescan sur un fichier modifié depuis son import : on met à jour la version Arij, on propose, ou on ignore ?
- Plafond de taille fichier ou de nombre de fichiers à importer (les docs partent dans les prompts agents, cf. E-arij-008) ?
- Ignorer certains répertoires (node_modules, .git, builds) — oui, évidemment, à documenter.

# Code Review — Epic « Docs : scan du projet pour importer automatiquement les documents »

**Scope:** `56e0779`, `1279bde`, `986a906` — 9 files, +1366 lines vs `main`.
**Verification run:** `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean. `npx vitest run __tests__/documents-import-route.test.ts __tests__/scan-project-dialog.test.tsx` → **13/13 pass**.

## Acceptance criteria

All four stories meet their criteria. Worth noting explicitly for Story 3: scanned docs are inserted with `kind: "text"` + `markdownContent`, which is exactly what `listProjectTextDocuments` (`lib/documents/query.ts:16`) selects on — so they reach agent session context identically to manual uploads. No extra wiring was needed and none is missing.

## 1. Readability — No blocking issues

The code is unusually well-commented, and the comments explain *why* rather than *what* (the iterative-walk rationale at `lib/documents/scan.ts:42`, the symlink policy at `:27`, the `« conserver et signaler »` decision at `ScanProjectDialog.tsx:149`). Open questions from the epic are answered in code with their reasoning attached.

## 2. DRY

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/documents/import/route.ts:60`**
Lines 60-74 duplicate `scan/route.ts:20-34` verbatim: stat the repo path, 400 on missing, 400 on not-a-directory.
*Recommendation:* extract `getProjectDirectoryOr400` alongside `getProjectOr404` in `lib/api/route-helpers.ts`.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:90`**
`MIME_BY_EXTENSION` and `DOCUMENT_SCAN_EXTENSIONS` are independent literals that can drift — and the epic explicitly floats adding `.rtf`/`.html`. Adding one to the scanner alone leaves `mimeType` `undefined` at runtime (typed `string`, so the `?? null` is dead code today), surfacing as `Unsupported file type "null"` to the user. Derive one map from the other.

## 3. Error Handling

**Minor — `lib/documents/import.ts:163`**
The bare `catch` around the insert labels *every* failure `"Déjà importé."`. SQLITE_BUSY, disk-full or a future constraint violation all reach the user as a confidently wrong statement.
*Recommendation:* match the error on `UNIQUE`/`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT` and fall through to a generic reason otherwise.

**Minor — `lib/documents/import.ts:94`**
`statSync`/`readFileSync` follow symlinks that `scanProjectDocuments` deliberately refuses (`lib/documents/scan.ts:66`, reason spelled out in its doc comment). The lexical `..`/prefix guard on lines 68-77 does not catch `docs/link-to-outside/passwd`. To be fair on threat model: not reachable from the dialog (the scan never lists a symlink), and cross-origin POST is preflight-blocked — this is defense-in-depth and honoring the module's own documented invariant, not a live hole.
*Recommendation:* `fs.realpathSync` the resolved path and re-check the root prefix, or `lstatSync` and skip.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:62`** — empty/blank paths `continue` with no `skipped` entry, so `imported.length + skipped.length` silently fails to reconcile with the request.

Otherwise the error posture is consistent and good: per-entry failures never abort either the walk or the batch, and every skip carries an actionable reason.

## 4. Performance

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:59`** — up to 100 files of up to 20 MB are read and converted **sequentially and synchronously** inside one request; PDF conversion is the slow path. This blocks the Node event loop for the whole orchestrator, and the dialog shows only a spinner. Defensible for a local-first app and the cap is documented, but worth an explicit note.

**Info — `lib/documents/scan.ts:47`** — `truncated` is a false positive when the repo holds exactly 500 documents: after the 500th push, any still-unvisited directory makes the next `while` iteration set the flag even though nothing was dropped.

The per-file duplicate `SELECT` is not an N+1 concern — bounded at 100 and served by the `LOWER(original_filename)` expression index from migration 0014.

## 5. Naming Conventions — No issues found

## 6. Type Safety — No issues found

No `any`. `getProjectOr404`'s `requireGitRepo: true` overload is used correctly to narrow `gitRepoPath` to `string`. The one cast (`relativePaths as string[]`, import route line 80) follows a real runtime validation.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:124` vs `ScanProjectDialog.tsx:135`** — the two dedup layers claim to mirror each other but diverge for non-ASCII: SQLite's `LOWER()` is ASCII-only, JS `toLowerCase()` is Unicode-aware. `RÉSUMÉ.pdf` on disk against `résumé.pdf` in the DB is marked « déjà importé » client-side while the server and the unique index would accept it.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `lib/documents/scan.ts:37`**
`scanProjectDocuments` has **no test**, and neither does the scan route. Story 1's acceptance criteria are entirely about this walker — ignores `.git`/`node_modules`/`dist`, reports errors clearly — and none of it is asserted anywhere; the ignore list, symlink policy, `truncated` flag and `errors` array are all unverified. It is the only new module without coverage.
*Recommendation:* add `__tests__/documents-scan.test.ts` against a real temp tree, mirroring `documents-import-route.test.ts`.

The two tests that do exist are strong — real filesystem, real components, minimal mocking, and they cover the genuinely tricky cases (path escape, same-basename collision within a batch, imports landing between two scans).

## 8. API Design

Envelope contract (`{ data }` / `{ error }`) and status codes follow `lib/api/route-helpers.ts` correctly. `POST` for a read-only scan is defensible and has precedent in `POST /api/projects/import`.

**Minor — `documents/import/route.ts:49`** — error strings mix French ("Aucun fichier sélectionné.", "Trop de fichiers") with English ("Invalid JSON body.", "relativePaths must be an array of strings."). The sibling upload route is English throughout, and `scan.ts` emits English while `import.ts` emits French — both land in the same dialog. Pick one language for the API layer.

## 9. UX correctness

**Minor — `components/documents/ScanProjectDialog.tsx:307`**
`.doc` rows are listed, selectable, and swept in by « Tout sélectionner » — but `lib/documents/import.ts:84` refuses every one of them. The default happy path (select-all → import) therefore always produces skip noise on any repo holding a legacy `.doc`, and the dialog description at line 257 advertises `doc` as supported.
*Recommendation:* mark `.doc` rows unsupported and non-selectable up front, or drop it from `DOCUMENT_SCAN_EXTENSIONS`.

**Minor — `components/documents/ScanProjectDialog.tsx:155`**
`missingSources` matches on basename only, so every manually-uploaded document with no repo counterpart is permanently reported as "ne correspond à aucun fichier du dépôt". The comment acknowledges this, but it makes the orphan signal noise for any project mixing upload and scan. There is no provenance on `documents` to tell the two apart; a `source`/`source_path` column would make the signal mean what Story 4 asks.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion / Info | 6 |

Solid work: the walk is iterative and bounded, path traversal is guarded and tested, dedup matches the existing unique index, one bad file never aborts a batch, and the epic's four open questions are each answered in code with the reasoning recorded. The two things I'd actually fix before merge are the untested scan walker (Story 1's entire AC surface) and the `.doc` extensions being offered but never importable. Nothing here blocks.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

Grader : évaluation structurée des critères d'acceptation (Outcomes)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Les `acceptanceCriteria` des user stories sont injectés dans les prompts de build et de review, mais personne ne les évalue jamais un par un. Motif « Outcomes » des Claude Managed Agents (Code with Claude 2026) : un agent évaluateur note le travail contre une rubrique, et le producteur itère jusqu'à satisfaire les critères. Ici la rubrique existe déjà : ce sont les critères d'acceptation.

## À construire
1. **Outil MCP `submit_grading`** (nouveau, toolset agent) : payload `{ gradings: [{ storyId, criterion, status: met|partial|missed, evidence }], summary }`. Route `app/api/mcp/submit-grading/route.ts` sur le modèle de `submit_findings` (auth par token, scope epic, erreurs lisibles par l'agent). Persistance : table `grading_reports` (migration SQL manuscrite + `_journal.json`).
2. **Agent grader** : agentType `grading`, session en mode plan sur le worktree, prompt `buildGradingPrompt` — reçoit les user stories et leurs critères, examine le diff/le worktree, et DOIT appeler submit_grading. Distinct du reviewer : le grader ne juge pas la qualité du code, uniquement « chaque critère est-il satisfait, avec quelle preuve ». Ségrégation de provider souhaitable (réutiliser la logique de `lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts`).
3. **Déclenchement** : bouton manuel sur le ticket (comme les reviews) + option pipeline `pipeline_grader_enabled` (tri-state, défaut OFF) : s'exécute après verify (si présent) et avant review ; un critère `missed` → fix cycle avec les critères manqués et leurs evidence injectés dans le prompt de fix.
4. **UI** : dans le détail du ticket, badge par critère sur chaque user story (met/partial/missed, evidence au survol) et état agrégé sur la carte kanban.

## Contraintes
- Le grading n'introduit AUCUNE nouvelle transition : il alimente les fix cycles existants et l'affichage ; `review → done` reste humain (cf. `docs/architecture/ticket-state-machine.md`).
- Epic sans user stories ou sans critères → grader sauté (no-op journalisé), jamais un échec.
- Intégrer l'agentType `grading` aux constantes/enums (watchdog, classification) comme pour les autres types.
- Tests vitest : route MCP (validation payload, scope token, storyId hors epic rejeté), câblage pipeline (missed → fix, all met → continue, sans stories → skip), section Arij tools des prompts à jour.
