comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Grader: évaluation structurée des critères d'acceptation (Outcomes)

**Scope reviewed:** `269e399..7e75278` (3 commits, 62 files, +2972/−99) — MCP tool + persistence, plan-mode grader agent, pipeline wiring and UI badges.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong. Every new module opens with a doc comment that states the *invariant*, not just the mechanism — `submit-grading/route.ts:1-8` explains why story validation precedes the atomic insert, `runner.ts:678-679` explains why grading success is keyed to the exact report id, and `report.ts:1-7` states the "malformed row must never green-light a pipeline" contract. `RUNNING_STATE_BY_STAGE` and `PIPELINE_REASONS` keep the new stage symmetrical with the existing ones.

One readability nit: `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:228-238` now carries two consecutive `/** ... */` blocks for the single `parkRejectedTicket` field (the first, describing the regression-gate use, was left orphaned when the second was added). Harmless, but a reader hits a doc comment that documents nothing.

## 2. DRY Principle

Good reuse throughout: `dispatchGradingSession` is a single implementation shared by the manual route and the pipeline stage (per the project's "manual and automatic paths share one effectful function" convention); provider segregation reuses `pickAlternativeReviewProvider` / `resolveAgentForDispatch` rather than cloning it; `parseAcceptanceCriteria` is shared by prompt display and badge matching.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/constants.ts:115`** — `resolvePipelineGraderEnabledDefault` is dead code. Its sibling `resolvePipelineEnabledDefault` exists because `AgentActionsBar.tsx:204` needs a client-side effective value for the pipeline checkbox; the grader has no client-side consumer, and the only references to this function in the repository are in `__tests__/pipeline-settings-section.test.tsx`. **Recommendation:** delete the function (and its test), or wire it into the dispatch dialog if the grader is meant to be visible there.

## 3. Error Handling

Well covered. The `settled` promises never reject; the scheduler safety net is correctly relied on for the throw path in `dispatch.ts:384-395`; `assessGrading` throwing is routed into the retry ladder rather than green-lighting; `parkRejectedTicket` calls are individually try/caught so they cannot change how the run terminates. `GradingDispatchError` carrying `status`/`code`/`payload` keeps the route thin without losing the 409 conflict contract.

**Major — `lib/grading/dispatch.ts:333`** — a grading session that ends with `asked_question` is silently swallowed. The terminal block classifies the outcome, computes `success = false` (no report was filed), and calls `emitSessionFailed`. But `createNotificationFromSession` (`lib/notifications/create.ts:299`) *deliberately returns early* for `outcome === "asked_question"`, because that notification is owned by `createAskedQuestionNotificationFromSession`, invoked only through `handleAskedQuestionOutcome`. The grading dispatcher never calls it. The terminal hook (`terminal-notification.ts:32`) hits the same early return.

Net effect: the grader asks the user something → **no notification at all** (neither the question flavour nor the generic failure one) and no held-status activity entry. In the pipeline this is worse than cosmetic: `runner.ts:544-548` returns `paused_question` on the strength of an explicit comment — *"the stage closure already held the ticket, notified, and logged via handleAskedQuestionOutcome"* — which is true for `finalizeReviewSession` (`stages.ts:954`) and `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome`, and false for grading. The run stops and the only trace is the pipeline activity line. `mcp__arij__ask_question` is in the agent allowlist, so the grader can reach it.

**Recommendation:** in the terminal block, mirror the review stage:
```ts
if (outcome === "asked_question") {
  handleAskedQuestionOutcome({
    projectId: input.projectId,
    epicIds: [input.epicId],
    sessionId,
    ticketStatus: gradingTarget.status ?? "review",
  });
}
```
and add a dispatch test for it — `__tests__/grading-agent-dispatch.test.ts` currently has no `asked_question` case.

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/grading/route.ts:36`** — a malformed stored report returns HTTP 500. `report.ts:1-7` states the opposite contract ("must render as ungraded"). The client happens to degrade correctly (`useEpicDetail.ts:64` gates on `gradingRes.ok`), so the symptom is only a spurious server error in the network log — but the status code asserts a server fault for what is a data condition. **Recommendation:** return `{ data: null }` (200) and log, matching how `epics/route.ts` handles the same row via `parseGradingEntries` → `null`.

## 4. Performance

The board query is handled well — one `ROW_NUMBER()` subquery joined once, backed by the new `(epic_id, created_at)` index, rather than a per-epic lookup.

**Minor — `lib/grading/report.ts:97` / `EpicUserStoriesSection.tsx:144`** — `findCriterionGrading` re-normalizes every report entry for every criterion, on every render. `normalizeCriterion` is a split + three regex replaces + a lowercase, and the lookup is `O(criteria × entries)`. A 6-story epic with 5 criteria each and a 30-entry report is ~900 normalizations per render, and the detail panel re-renders on a 5 s poll *and* on every project SSE event. **Recommendation:** build the normalized index once per report — `useMemo(() => new Map(gradings.map(g => [`${g.storyId}|${normalizeCriterion(g.criterion)}`, g])), [gradingReport])` — and look up by key.

**Minor — `components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:229`** — `if (refreshTrigger > 0) void refresh()` fires three fetches (full epics list + user stories + grading report) on *every* project-scoped SSE event, including `ticket:updated` / `session:started` for unrelated tickets, on top of the existing 5 s poll. The stated goal ("grader completion arrives as `session:completed`") is narrower than the trigger. **Recommendation:** either accept it explicitly in the comment, or have the board pass an epic-scoped trigger so unrelated events don't refetch an open panel.

**Suggestion — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:202`** — `gradingSummary` (up to 4000 chars) is now returned for every epic on every board load, solely to fill the card tooltip. On a large board that is a meaningful payload increase for a hover affordance; consider truncating server-side.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `grading` as an agent type, `GRADING_AGENT_TYPE`, `PIPELINE_GRADER_ENABLED_SETTING_KEY`, `gradingReports`/`grading_reports`, `buildGradingPrompt`, `GradingStatusBadge` — all consistent with their neighbours. The `grader`(setting)/`grading`(agent type) split reads as intentional and matches the epic's wording.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `GradingStatus` is derived from the `GRADING_STATUSES` tuple and shared by the Zod enum, the DB parse path, and the UI; `DispatchGradingResult` is a discriminated union on `skipped`, so the route cannot read `sessionId` off a skip. `PromptGradingStory extends PromptUserStory` with a required `id` correctly encodes what `submit_grading` needs. `parseGradingEntries` narrows `unknown` through a real type guard rather than a cast.

## 7. Testing

Genuinely good coverage of the contracts the epic named: strict status enum, unknown-key rejection at both levels, mixed-scope `STORY_NOT_IN_EPIC` with a no-partial-write assertion, `ticket_id` rejection, OFF-by-default pipeline flow, `verify → grading → review` ordering, missed → fix with criterion+evidence threading, rubric-free skip, watchdog classification, and the Arij-tools prompt section.

Gaps worth closing:

- **`asked_question` on a grading session** (see §3) — untested, and the missing behaviour is precisely what a test would have caught.
- **Grading-stage failure paths** — `__tests__/pipeline-grading.test.ts` only exercises successful graders. There is no test for the retry ladder on a grader that fails, for `assessGrading` throwing (malformed report → `handleStageFailure`), or for `missed` with `fixCycles >= maxFixCycles` → `parkRejectedTicket` + `failed`. That last one is a user-visible terminal state with a board side effect.
- **Story-scoped grading in the pipeline** — `dispatchPipelineGradingStage` passes `userStoryId` for story runs, but only epic-scoped dispatch is covered.

## 8. API Design

`{ data }` / `{ error }` shape is respected, `STORY_NOT_IN_EPIC` is agent-readable and names the offending id, and the 409 conflict reuses `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload` so the client's existing `isAgentAlreadyRunningError` handling works unchanged. Validation order (auth → chat rejection → body → ticket scope) mirrors `submit-findings` exactly, as the epic required.

**Minor — `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:51-58`** — `submit_grading` is added to `ARIJ_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOL_NAMES`, i.e. every agent session gets it, and the route only rejects `agentType === "chat"`. A `build` or `ticket_build` session can therefore file a grading report on its own epic, and that report becomes the epic's latest — it drives the Kanban aggregate badge and the per-criterion badges. The pipeline is safe (`assessGrading` matches on `agentSessionId`), so this is a display-integrity issue, not a gate bypass. It also directly undercuts the Outcomes premise that the evaluator is independent of the producer. The epic text does say "toolset agent", so this may be deliberate — but the tool description already says "(Grading sessions)". **Recommendation:** if independence is intended, gate the route on `auth.agentType === "grading"` (one line, mirrors the existing chat guard); if not, drop "(Grading sessions)" from the description.

**Suggestion — `app/api/mcp/submit-grading/route.ts:97`** — unlike `submit_findings`, no ticket comment mirrors the summary into the activity feed. After a manual "Grade Criteria" run the only durable user-visible output is a badge tooltip; the feed shows nothing. A one-line summary comment would make manual grading auditable the way reviews are.

**Suggestion — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:262`** — `dispatchPipelineGradingStage` ignores `request.attempt` and `previousAttemptSessionId`, so the grading stage has no resume-on-attempt-2 and no escalate-on-attempt-3, and always reports `escalatedToProvider: null`. Consequence: a grader on a weaker CLI that never calls `submit_grading` burns the full ladder on the *same* provider, triggers a forensic, and **fails the whole run before review ever executes** — for a stage the module header calls "intentionally observational". Either route grading through `resolveStageAgent`'s ladder, or degrade a grader-infrastructure failure to "skip grading, continue to review" and keep hard failure for `missed` criteria only.

**Suggestion — `components/kanban/EpicCard.tsx:381`** — the aggregate badge has no relation to the code state it graded. A report survives subsequent builds and merges, so a card can show "Criteria met" over code that changed afterwards. `gradingCreatedAt` is already selected, joined, and typed in `KanbanEpic` — but never rendered. Comparing it against the epic's latest code session (or just showing the age in the tooltip) would make the signal honest.

**Suggestion — session budget** — enabling the grader adds one session per cycle against the fixed `PIPELINE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN = 12`, and missed criteria consume the *same* `maxFixCycles` budget as review findings. With the defaults a grading-driven fix can leave zero budget for blocking review findings, turning a previously-fixable review into an immediate terminal failure. Worth stating in the settings copy (which currently mentions the shared budget but not that it can starve the review stage).

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

This is careful, well-tested work that honours the epic's hard constraints: no new transitions, `review → done` untouched, rubric-free epics are journalled no-ops rather than failures, the setting is genuinely OFF by default and the OFF path is proven byte-identical to the previous flow, the migration is hand-written with a monotonic journal entry, and `grading` is threaded through the constants, watchdog, classification, monitor and session views. The one Major finding — silent `asked_question` handling — is a narrow, well-localized gap with an obvious three-line fix and an existing pattern to copy; the rest are polish.

*Note: findings are reported here as prose rather than filed through `submit_findings`, because this session is running under plan mode, which forbids state-changing tool calls.*

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

Epic complete. All four stories delivered; ticket moved to review.

## What I found first

The branch was sitting at `main` with **none** of the code this epic exists to test — the clone service, the parser, and the workspace module were on three sibling epic branches, and they conflicted with each other. I merged them rather than reimplementing, resolving:

- **Two `lib/projects/workspace.ts`** — kept the socle epic's version; the clone route now calls `cloneDestinationFor()`.
- **Two `0027` migrations at journal idx 26** — drizzle only applies a migration whose `when` exceeds the last recorded one, so the `git_sync_log` rebuild became `0028` at idx 27.
- **Two `parseGitHubRepoInput()`** — kept the stricter one (refuses a leading `-`).

## The four stories

**Parsing & workspace** — renamed the parsing suite to the AC filename and added traversal payloads (encoded, double-encoded, Windows, UNC, control chars), idempotence over the emitted `cloneUrl`, and refusal of credential-bearing URLs. Rebuilt the workspace suite on `createTestDb()`: the chain mock returns the queued row regardless of the query, so it structurally cannot catch a resolver reading the wrong settings key. Consolidated the two `assertInsideRoot()` implementations — the pure one had no production consumer at all.

**Clone & routes** — `POST /api/projects` had zero coverage and didn't carry the clone metadata, so I implemented that (`cloneSource` restricted to the one value Arij issues) plus normalised-path storage; a trailing slash would have pushed `<path>/../.arij-worktrees` a directory too deep. Added partial-destination cleanup tests on both failure and timeout, with the counterpart that a pre-existing directory is never deleted.

**E2E** — the import UI epic has no commits, so the GitHub source had to be built here. Gated stubs hold each endpoint open until the test observes that step, rather than racing a sleep. This surfaced two real defects: the typed URL was lost after a failed clone (fixed), and `role="alert"` collided with Next's route announcer.

**Docs** — README, CLAUDE.md, and a new `docs/architecture/github-import.md`, with a test pinning the actionable facts. While there I corrected CLAUDE.md advertising `npx drizzle-kit generate`, which must never be run on this repo.

Two things worth your attention: this PR carries the three sibling epics' commits, so if they merge to `main` first the `0027`→`0028` resolution is already here; and `playwright.config.ts` now honours `E2E_BROWSER_CHANNEL` because Playwright's bundled chromium doesn't support this machine's Ubuntu — CI still uses the bundled build.

**Revue traitée** — 5 constats sur 5 corrigés (commit `7f6f448`). Suite verte : `npm test` 2730 tests / 263 fichiers, `npm run test:e2e` 12 tests, `tsc --noEmit` propre.

| # | Constat | Traitement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fetch de réutilisation non authentifié | corrigé |
| 2 | Fuite des métadonnées de clone vers un import local | corrigé |
| 3 | Propriété du clone décidée par le client | corrigé |
| 4 | Branche par défaut non utilisée | corrigé (voir réserve) |
| 5 | Points consécutifs refusés à tort | corrigé |

**1 — fetch authentifié et borné.** Le PAT est volontairement absent de `.git/config`, donc `fetchGitRemote()` sur le chemin de réutilisation partait sans identifiant : pour un dépôt privé, git demandait des identifiants sans terminal attaché — un blocage, pas une erreur. Le constructeur `-c http.extraHeader` est désormais partagé avec le clone, et le fetch porte le même timeout et `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

**2 — provenance liée à l'analyse.** `clone` survivait à une prévisualisation annulée, à une analyse en échec et au retour vers « Local folder ». La provenance voyage maintenant avec le résultat d'analyse et n'est posée que pour la prévisualisation à laquelle elle appartient. Trois tests de non-régression couvrent les trois chemins, plus la contre-épreuve que le cas GitHub légitime enregistre toujours sa provenance.

**3 — propriété vérifiée côté serveur.** `POST /api/projects` recalcule `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` et refuse le drapeau pour tout autre chemin ; `gitRemoteUrl` est ré-analysée (une URL porteuse d'identifiants ne parse pas), stockée normalisée, et la cohérence owner/repo est vérifiée. `defaultBranch` est validée au niveau du schéma contre les formes que git refuse dans une réf.

**4 — branche par défaut.** `resolveRemoteDefaultBranch()` (`origin/HEAD`) est partagée par le service de clone, `manager.ts` et `release.ts` ; la convention `main`/`master` ne sert plus que de repli quand il n'y a pas de distant à interroger. La réponse du distant n'est retenue que si la branche existe localement — `main` seul ne résout pas `refs/remotes/origin/main`, on échangerait un échec contre un autre. Le clone rapporte cette branche plutôt que celle qui se trouve extraite dans un clone réutilisé.

⚠️ **Réserve assumée** : je n'ai pas étendu le transport authentifié à `pushGitBranch()` / `pullGitBranchWithConflictSupport()` / au tag de release, comme le suggérait la recommandation du constat 1. Ces fonctions préexistent à l'import et le débordement touchait l'orchestration git de toute l'application, hors périmètre d'un epic tests+doc. Le manque est documenté explicitement dans `docs/architecture/github-import.md` sous « Known gap » : un dépôt privé importé ainsi aura besoin d'un credential helper pour pousser. À arbitrer comme ticket dédié si vous le voulez couvert.

**5 — points consécutifs.** `repo..archive` est un nom GitHub légal et la classe de caractères exclut déjà tout séparateur ; seuls les composants exacts `.` et `..` sont de la traversée. En corrigeant le parseur j'ai trouvé la même sévérité excessive un cran plus bas : `validatePath()` refusait toute sous-chaîne `..`, ce qui aurait fait échouer l'import du clone que le parseur venait d'accepter. Les deux couches tracent maintenant la ligne au même endroit, et les charges utiles de traversée réelles restent refusées (103 tests sur le parseur).

Doc mise à jour en conséquence : le tableau des propriétés de sûreté, la section « Default branch », et la réserve ci-dessus.

comments.content:
All five review findings are fixed and the ticket is back in review (commit `7f6f448`).

## What the findings actually were

**Three were real defects in code this epic authored:**

- **Reuse fetch had no credentials, timeout, or prompt suppression.** Because the PAT is deliberately kept out of `.git/config`, the fetch on the reuse path was unauthenticated — a private-repo re-import blocked on a credential prompt with no terminal attached, which is a hang rather than an error. The `-c http.extraHeader` builder is now shared with the clone path.
- **Clone provenance leaked between imports.** `clone` state survived a cancelled preview, a failed analysis, and a switch back to "Local folder", so the next local import was created carrying the previous repo's `cloneSource`/owner/remote/branch. Provenance now travels with the analysis result.
- **`cloneSource` was client-authoritative.** It's the flag that later authorises Arij to delete a directory. The route now recomputes `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` and refuses the claim for any other path, and re-parses `gitRemoteUrl` so a credential-bearing URL can't be persisted.

**One was a pre-existing bug the import surfaced:** `createWorktree`/`mergeWorktree` guessed `main`-else-`master`, so a `trunk` or `develop` repo imported cleanly and then failed at `worktree add`. All call sites now resolve `origin/HEAD` through a shared helper.

## Two things worth flagging

**I found a second instance of finding 5.** Fixing the parser to accept `repo..archive` (legal on GitHub; the character class already excludes separators) exposed that `validatePath()` rejected *any* `..` substring — so a clone the parser had just accepted would have failed at import. Both layers now draw the line at exact `.`/`..` components. Real traversal payloads stay rejected.

**I deliberately did not do part of finding 1.** The reviewer recommended a credential-aware transport for push, pull, and tag as well. Those functions predate the import flow and rewiring them touches the whole app's git orchestration — well outside a tests-and-docs epic, with real regression risk. I fixed the reuse fetch, which is the path this epic owns, and documented the remainder as a "Known gap" in `docs/architecture/github-import.md`: a private repo imported this way needs a credential helper to push. That's a judgement call on scope, so it's yours to overrule — say the word and I'll do it as a follow-up.

Verification: `npm test` 2730 passed / 263 files, `npm run test:e2e` 12 passed, `tsc --noEmit` clean. The one ESLint warning in `manager.ts:133` is pre-existing and untouched by this diff.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

## What the findings actually were

**Three were real defects in code this epic authored:**

- **Reuse fetch had no credentials, timeout, or prompt suppression.** Because the PAT is deliberately kept out of `.git/config`, the fetch on the reuse path was unauthenticated — a private-repo re-import blocked on a credential prompt with no terminal attached, which is a hang rather than an error. The `-c http.extraHeader` builder is now shared with the clone path.
- **Clone provenance leaked between imports.** `clone` state survived a cancelled preview, a failed analysis, and a switch back to "Local folder", so the next local import was created carrying the previous repo's `cloneSource`/owner/remote/branch. Provenance now travels with the analysis result.
- **`cloneSource` was client-authoritative.** It's the flag that later authorises Arij to delete a directory. The route now recomputes `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` and refuses the claim for any other path, and re-parses `gitRemoteUrl` so a credential-bearing URL can't be persisted.

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

/**
 * Pure parsing of GitHub repository references.
 *
 * Split out of lib/git/remote.ts — which imports `simple-git` and therefore
 * cannot be bundled for the browser — so the import page can validate what the
 * user pastes with the exact same rules the clone route applies server-side.
 * Same pattern as lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts: no db, no node builtins,
 * no I/O of any kind.
 *
 * lib/git/remote.ts re-exports everything here, so server code keeps importing
 * from a single place.
 */

export interface ParsedGitHubRemote {
  owner: string;
  repo: string;
  ownerRepo: string;
}

export interface ParsedGitHubRepoInput extends ParsedGitHubRemote {
  /** Always normalised to https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git */
  cloneUrl: string;
}

export function normalizeRemoteUrl(raw: string): string {
  return raw.trim();
}

export function parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(
  remoteUrl: string
): ParsedGitHubRemote | null {
  const value = normalizeRemoteUrl(remoteUrl);
  if (!value) return null;

  const patterns = [
    /^git@github\.com:(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^ssh:\/\/git@github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^git:\/\/github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
  ];

  for (const pattern of patterns) {
    const match = value.match(pattern);
    if (!match?.groups?.owner || !match.groups.repo) {
      continue;
    }

    const owner = match.groups.owner;
    const repo = match.groups.repo;
    if (!owner || !repo) continue;

    return {
      owner,
      repo,
      ownerRepo: `${owner}/${repo}`,
    };
  }

  return null;
}

/**
 * GitHub allows letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` in owner and repo names.
 * Anything else — separators, NUL bytes, whitespace — is rejected here so a
 * crafted URL can never reach the filesystem layer. A leading `-` is refused
 * as well: it would otherwise be read as an option by `git clone`.
 */
const REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

function isSafeRepoSegment(segment: string): boolean {
  if (!segment) return false;
  if (segment.startsWith("-")) return false;
  // Only the exact `.` and `..` components traverse. Dots *inside* a name are
  // ordinary GitHub characters (`repo..archive` is a legal repository), and the
  // character class below already excludes every separator, so an embedded `..`
  // cannot climb out of the clone root. Matches assertSegment() in
  // lib/projects/workspace.ts, which draws the line in the same place.
  if (segment === "." || segment === "..") return false;
  return REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN.test(segment);
}

function buildRepoInput(
  owner: string,
  repo: string
): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  const cleanRepo = repo.replace(/\.git$/i, "");
  if (!isSafeRepoSegment(owner) || !isSafeRepoSegment(cleanRepo)) {
    return null;
  }

  return {
    owner,
    repo: cleanRepo,
    ownerRepo: `${owner}/${cleanRepo}`,
    cloneUrl: `https://github.com/${owner}/${cleanRepo}.git`,
  };
}

/**
 * Browser URLs carry a suffix the remote-url parser does not know about:
 * `/tree/main`, `/blob/main/README.md`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme-ov-file`,
 * `#anchor`. Keep the first two path segments and drop the rest.
 */
function stripBrowserSuffix(value: string): string | null {
  const match = value.match(
    /^(?<base>https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?github\.com\/[^/?#]+\/[^/?#]+)[/?#]/i
  );
  return match?.groups?.base ?? null;
}

/** `owner/repo` shorthand — exactly two segments, no scheme, no host. */
function parseShorthand(value: string): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  const match = value.match(/^(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)\/?$/);
  if (!match?.groups?.owner || !match.groups.repo) return null;
  return buildRepoInput(match.groups.owner, match.groups.repo);
}

/**
 * Parses every GitHub repo reference a user is likely to paste — remote URLs
 * (https, ssh, git), browser URLs with trailing segments, and the `owner/repo`
 * shorthand — into a normalised clone target. Returns null for anything that
 * is not a GitHub repository or whose owner/repo fails strict validation.
 */
export function parseGitHubRepoInput(
  input: string
): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  if (typeof input !== "string") return null;

  const value = input.trim();
  if (!value || value.includes("\0")) return null;

  // `github.com/owner/repo` pasted without a scheme.
  const withScheme = /^(?:www\.)?github\.com\//i.test(value)
    ? `https://${value}`
    : value;

  for (const candidate of [withScheme, stripBrowserSuffix(withScheme)]) {
    if (!candidate) continue;
    const parsed = parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(candidate);
    if (!parsed) continue;
    // A `?query` or `#anchor` is swallowed by the remote parser's `[^/]+?`
    // repo group, so a rejected candidate falls through to the stripped one
    // rather than failing the whole parse.
    const result = buildRepoInput(parsed.owner, parsed.repo);
    if (result) return result;
  }

  // A github.com URL that did not parse is not a repo reference; do not fall
  // through to the shorthand rule and mis-read the host as an owner.
  if (withScheme !== value) return null;

  return parseShorthand(value);
}


import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { settings } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import {
  DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME,
  PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY,
  parseProjectsRoot,
} from "./workspace-constants";
import { assertInsideRoot as assertPathInsideRoot } from "./workspace-path";

/**
 * Server-side resolution of the app-managed clone root.
 *
 * Every repository Arij clones lands in `<root>/<owner>-<repo>`, which becomes
 * the project's `git_repo_path`. Worktrees are then created at
 * `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")` (lib/git/manager.ts), i.e.
 * `<root>/.arij-worktrees` — so a single `/projects` .gitignore rule covers
 * both clones and their worktrees when dogfooding Arij on itself.
 */

/** Built-in root used when no `projects_root` override is configured. */
export function defaultProjectsRoot(): string {
  return path.join(process.cwd(), DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME);
}

/**
 * The effective clone root: the `projects_root` setting when set, otherwise
 * `<cwd>/projects`. Always absolute — a relative override is anchored to the
 * working directory so clone destinations never depend on the caller's cwd.
 */
export function resolveProjectsRoot(): string {
  const row = db
    .select({ value: settings.value })
    .from(settings)
    .where(eq(settings.key, PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY))
    .get();

  const override = row ? parseProjectsRoot(row.value) : null;
  if (!override) return defaultProjectsRoot();

  return path.resolve(process.cwd(), override);
}

/**
 * Creates the clone root if it does not exist and returns it. A no-op when the
 * directory is already there (`mkdirSync` with `recursive: true`).
 */
export function ensureProjectsRoot(): string {
  const root = resolveProjectsRoot();
  fs.mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
  return root;
}

/**
 * Guards a clone destination against escaping the root.
 *
 * The URL parsing layer already validates owner/repo, but this is the last
 * line of defence before any filesystem write: a crafted `owner` such as
 * `../../etc` must never resolve outside the root. The root itself is rejected
 * too — cloning into it would nest every later clone inside the first one.
 *
 * The containment check itself lives in the db-free ./workspace-path module so
 * it can be reasoned about (and tested) without a settings lookup; this wrapper
 * only supplies the configured root and the caller-facing message.
 *
 * Returns the resolved absolute destination.
 */
export function assertInsideRoot(
  destination: string,
  root: string = resolveProjectsRoot()
): string {
  try {
    return assertPathInsideRoot(root, destination);
  } catch (cause) {
    throw new Error(
      `Refusing to use a path outside the projects root: ${destination}`,
      { cause }
    );
  }
}

/** Owner and repository segments Arij accepts in a clone destination. */
const SEGMENT_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

function assertSegment(value: string, label: string): string {
  const trimmed = typeof value === "string" ? value.trim() : "";

  // `.` and `..` match the character class but are traversal components.
  if (!SEGMENT_PATTERN.test(trimmed) || trimmed === "." || trimmed === "..") {
    throw new Error(`Invalid GitHub ${label}: ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
  }

  return trimmed;
}

/**
 * Destination directory for a clone of `owner/repo`: `<root>/<owner>-<repo>`.
 *
 * Deterministic and collision-free across owners, which makes re-importing the
 * same repository idempotent — the clone service can detect the existing
 * directory and fetch instead of re-cloning.
 */
export function cloneDestinationFor(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  root: string = resolveProjectsRoot()
): string {
  const dirName = `${assertSegment(owner, "owner")}-${assertSegment(repo, "repository")}`;
  return assertInsideRoot(path.join(root, dirName), root);
}


/**
 * Client-safe constants for the app-managed clone root — the directory Arij
 * clones GitHub repositories into.
 *
 * Kept separate from lib/projects/workspace.ts (which imports the database and
 * node:fs) so client components — the Settings page — can import the setting
 * key and the parser without pulling server modules into the bundle. Same
 * pattern as lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts and lib/night/constants.ts.
 */

/**
 * Global settings key holding the user's clone-root override. Stored in the
 * key/value settings table (JSON-encoded by the settings PATCH route).
 */
export const PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY = "projects_root";

/**
 * Directory name appended to `process.cwd()` when no override is configured.
 * Mirrored by the `/projects` rule in the repo's .gitignore so dogfooding
 * never commits a clone.
 */
export const DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME = "projects";

/**
 * Normalizes a raw settings value into a clone-root override.
 *
 * Accepts both shapes the value takes in practice: the JSON-encoded text read
 * straight from the settings row (server side) and the already-decoded value
 * the GET route hands to the client.
 *
 * Returns null for anything that is not a non-empty string, so callers fall
 * back to `<cwd>/projects`. A blank string is how the Settings page clears the
 * override, and must therefore read as "no override" rather than "root is ''"
 * — an empty root would resolve to the working directory and scatter clones
 * across the app checkout.
 */
export function parseProjectsRoot(value: unknown): string | null {
  let candidate: unknown = value;

  if (typeof candidate === "string") {
    try {
      const decoded: unknown = JSON.parse(candidate);
      // Only a decoded string replaces the raw text: a path that happens to be
      // valid JSON (e.g. "123") must stay the literal directory name.
      if (typeof decoded === "string") candidate = decoded;
    } catch {
      // raw (non-JSON) string — use as-is
    }
  }

  if (typeof candidate !== "string") return null;

  const trimmed = candidate.trim();
  return trimmed.length > 0 ? trimmed : null;
}


import { isAbsolute, relative, resolve } from "node:path";

/**
 * Pure path helpers for the app-managed clone root. Deliberately free of any
 * `db` or settings import so it stays safe to use from anywhere, including the
 * parsing layer that runs before a root has been resolved.
 */

export class WorkspacePathError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "WorkspacePathError";
  }
}

/**
 * Resolves `candidate` against `root` and guarantees the result is a strict
 * descendant of it. Defence in depth behind `parseGitHubRepoInput()`: even if a
 * traversal component reached this far, it cannot produce a path outside the
 * clone root.
 *
 * @returns the resolved absolute path
 * @throws WorkspacePathError when the candidate escapes, or equals, the root
 */
export function assertInsideRoot(root: string, candidate: string): string {
  if (!root || !root.trim()) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Clone root is required.");
  }
  if (!candidate || !candidate.trim()) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Clone destination is required.");
  }
  if (root.includes("\0") || candidate.includes("\0")) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Path contains invalid characters.");
  }

  const resolvedRoot = resolve(root);
  const resolvedCandidate = resolve(resolvedRoot, candidate);
  const rel = relative(resolvedRoot, resolvedCandidate);

  if (rel === "" || /^\.\.($|[\\/])/.test(rel) || isAbsolute(rel)) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError(
      `Resolved path escapes the clone root: ${resolvedCandidate}`
    );
  }

  return resolvedCandidate;
}

 * `/tree/main`, `/blob/main/README.md`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme-ov-file`,
 * `#anchor`. Keep the first two path segments and drop the rest.
 */
function stripBrowserSuffix(value: string): string | null {
  const match = value.match(
    /^(?<base>https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?github\.com\/[^/?#]+\/[^/?#]+)[/?#]/i
  );
  return match?.groups?.base ?? null;
}

/** `owner/repo` shorthand — exactly two segments, no scheme, no host. */
function parseShorthand(value: string): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  const match = value.match(/^(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)\/?$/);
  if (!match?.groups?.owner || !match.groups.repo) return null;
  return buildRepoInput(match.groups.owner, match.groups.repo);
}

/**
 * Parses every GitHub repo reference a user is likely to paste — remote URLs
 * (https, ssh, git), browser URLs with trailing segments, and the `owner/repo`
 * shorthand — into a normalised clone target. Returns null for anything that
 * is not a GitHub repository or whose owner/repo fails strict validation.
 */
export function parseGitHubRepoInput(
  input: string
): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  if (typeof input !== "string") return null;

  const value = input.trim();
  if (!value || value.includes("\0")) return null;

  // `github.com/owner/repo` pasted without a scheme.
  const withScheme = /^(?:www\.)?github\.com\//i.test(value)
    ? `https://${value}`
    : value;

  for (const candidate of [withScheme, stripBrowserSuffix(withScheme)]) {
    if (!candidate) continue;
    const parsed = parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(candidate);
    if (!parsed) continue;
    // A `?query` or `#anchor` is swallowed by the remote parser's `[^/]+?`
    // repo group, so a rejected candidate falls through to the stripped one
    // rather than failing the whole parse.
    const result = buildRepoInput(parsed.owner, parsed.repo);
    if (result) return result;
  }

  // A github.com URL that did not parse is not a repo reference; do not fall
  // through to the shorthand rule and mis-read the host as an owner.
  if (withScheme !== value) return null;

  return parseShorthand(value);
}

 * Pure parsing of GitHub repository references.

 * Split out of lib/git/remote.ts — which imports `simple-git` and therefore
 * cannot be bundled for the browser — so the import page can validate what the
 * user pastes with the exact same rules the clone route applies server-side.

 * no I/O of any kind.

 * from a single place.
 */

export interface ParsedGitHubRemote {
  owner: string;
  repo: string;
  ownerRepo: string;
}

export interface ParsedGitHubRepoInput extends ParsedGitHubRemote {
  /** Always normalised to https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git */

}

export function normalizeRemoteUrl(raw: string): string {
  return raw.trim();
}

export function parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(
  remoteUrl: string
): ParsedGitHubRemote | null {
  const value = normalizeRemoteUrl(remoteUrl);
  if (!value) return null;

  const patterns = [
    /^git@github\.com:(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^ssh:\/\/git@github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^git:\/\/github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
  ];

  for (const pattern of patterns) {
    const match = value.match(pattern);
    if (!match?.groups?.owner || !match.groups.repo) {
      continue;
    }

    const owner = match.groups.owner;
    const repo = match.groups.repo;
    if (!owner || !repo) continue;

    return {
      owner,
      repo,
      ownerRepo: `${owner}/${repo}`,
    };
  }

  return null;

/**
 * GitHub allows letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` in owner and repo names.
 * Anything else — separators, NUL bytes, whitespace — is rejected here so a
 * crafted URL can never reach the filesystem layer. A leading `-` is refused
 * as well: it would otherwise be read as an option by `git clone`.
 */
const REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

function isSafeRepoSegment(segment: string): boolean {
  if (!segment) return false;
  if (segment.startsWith("-")) return false;
  // Only the exact `.` and `..` components traverse. Dots *inside* a name are
  // ordinary GitHub characters (`repo..archive` is a legal repository), and the
  // character class below already excludes every separator, so an embedded `..`
  // cannot climb out of the clone root. Matches assertSegment() in
  // lib/projects/workspace.ts, which draws the line in the same place.
  if (segment === "." || segment === "..") return false;
  return REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN.test(segment);

  owner: string,
  repo: string
): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  const cleanRepo = repo.replace(/\.git$/i, "");
  if (!isSafeRepoSegment(owner) || !isSafeRepoSegment(cleanRepo)) {
    return null;

  return {
    owner,
    repo: cleanRepo,
    ownerRepo: `${owner}/${cleanRepo}`,
    cloneUrl: `https://github.com/${owner}/${cleanRepo}.git`,

}

import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { settings } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import {
  DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME,
  PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY,
  parseProjectsRoot,
} from "./workspace-constants";
import { assertInsideRoot as assertPathInsideRoot } from "./workspace-path";

/**
 * Server-side resolution of the app-managed clone root.
 *
 * Every repository Arij clones lands in `<root>/<owner>-<repo>`, which becomes
 * the project's `git_repo_path`. Worktrees are then created at
 * `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")` (lib/git/manager.ts), i.e.
 * `<root>/.arij-worktrees` — so a single `/projects` .gitignore rule covers
 * both clones and their worktrees when dogfooding Arij on itself.
 */

/** Built-in root used when no `projects_root` override is configured. */
export function defaultProjectsRoot(): string {
  return path.join(process.cwd(), DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME);
}

/**
 * The effective clone root: the `projects_root` setting when set, otherwise
 * `<cwd>/projects`. Always absolute — a relative override is anchored to the
 * working directory so clone destinations never depend on the caller's cwd.
 */
export function resolveProjectsRoot(): string {
  const row = db
    .select({ value: settings.value })
    .from(settings)
    .where(eq(settings.key, PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY))
    .get();

  const override = row ? parseProjectsRoot(row.value) : null;
  if (!override) return defaultProjectsRoot();

  return path.resolve(process.cwd(), override);
}

/**
 * Creates the clone root if it does not exist and returns it. A no-op when the
 * directory is already there (`mkdirSync` with `recursive: true`).
 */
export function ensureProjectsRoot(): string {
  const root = resolveProjectsRoot();
  fs.mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
  return root;
}

/**
 * Guards a clone destination against escaping the root.
 *
 * The URL parsing layer already validates owner/repo, but this is the last
 * line of defence before any filesystem write: a crafted `owner` such as
 * `../../etc` must never resolve outside the root. The root itself is rejected
 * too — cloning into it would nest every later clone inside the first one.
 *
 * The containment check itself lives in the db-free ./workspace-path module so
 * it can be reasoned about (and tested) without a settings lookup; this wrapper
 * only supplies the configured root and the caller-facing message.
 *
 * Returns the resolved absolute destination.
 */
export function assertInsideRoot(
  destination: string,
  root: string = resolveProjectsRoot()
): string {
  try {
    return assertPathInsideRoot(root, destination);
  } catch (cause) {
    throw new Error(
      `Refusing to use a path outside the projects root: ${destination}`,
      { cause }
    );
  }
}

/** Owner and repository segments Arij accepts in a clone destination. */
const SEGMENT_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

function assertSegment(value: string, label: string): string {
  const trimmed = typeof value === "string" ? value.trim() : "";

  // `.` and `..` match the character class but are traversal components.
  if (!SEGMENT_PATTERN.test(trimmed) || trimmed === "." || trimmed === "..") {
    throw new Error(`Invalid GitHub ${label}: ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
  }

  return trimmed;
}

/**
 * Destination directory for a clone of `owner/repo`: `<root>/<owner>-<repo>`.
 *
 * Deterministic and collision-free across owners, which makes re-importing the
 * same repository idempotent — the clone service can detect the existing
 * directory and fetch instead of re-cloning.
 */
export function cloneDestinationFor(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  root: string = resolveProjectsRoot()
): string {
  const dirName = `${assertSegment(owner, "owner")}-${assertSegment(repo, "repository")}`;
  return assertInsideRoot(path.join(root, dirName), root);
}

import { isAbsolute, relative, resolve } from "node:path";

/**
 * Pure path helpers for the app-managed clone root. Deliberately free of any
 * `db` or settings import so it stays safe to use from anywhere, including the
 * parsing layer that runs before a root has been resolved.
 */

export class WorkspacePathError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "WorkspacePathError";
  }
}

/**
 * Resolves `candidate` against `root` and guarantees the result is a strict
 * descendant of it. Defence in depth behind `parseGitHubRepoInput()`: even if a
 * traversal component reached this far, it cannot produce a path outside the
 * clone root.
 *
 * @returns the resolved absolute path
 * @throws WorkspacePathError when the candidate escapes, or equals, the root
 */
export function assertInsideRoot(root: string, candidate: string): string {
  if (!root || !root.trim()) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Clone root is required.");
  }
  if (!candidate || !candidate.trim()) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Clone destination is required.");
  }
  if (root.includes("\0") || candidate.includes("\0")) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError("Path contains invalid characters.");
  }

  const resolvedRoot = resolve(root);
  const resolvedCandidate = resolve(resolvedRoot, candidate);
  const rel = relative(resolvedRoot, resolvedCandidate);

  if (rel === "" || /^\.\.($|[\\/])/.test(rel) || isAbsolute(rel)) {
    throw new WorkspacePathError(
      `Resolved path escapes the clone root: ${resolvedCandidate}`
    );
  }

  return resolvedCandidate;
}

/**
 * Client-safe constants for the app-managed clone root — the directory Arij
 * clones GitHub repositories into.
 *
 * Kept separate from lib/projects/workspace.ts (which imports the database and
 * node:fs) so client components — the Settings page — can import the setting
 * key and the parser without pulling server modules into the bundle. Same
 * pattern as lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts and lib/night/constants.ts.
 */

/**
 * Global settings key holding the user's clone-root override. Stored in the
 * key/value settings table (JSON-encoded by the settings PATCH route).
 */
export const PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY = "projects_root";

/**
 * Directory name appended to `process.cwd()` when no override is configured.
 * Mirrored by the `/projects` rule in the repo's .gitignore so dogfooding
 * never commits a clone.
 */
export const DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME = "projects";

/**
 * Normalizes a raw settings value into a clone-root override.
 *
 * Accepts both shapes the value takes in practice: the JSON-encoded text read
 * straight from the settings row (server side) and the already-decoded value
 * the GET route hands to the client.
 *
 * Returns null for anything that is not a non-empty string, so callers fall
 * back to `<cwd>/projects`. A blank string is how the Settings page clears the
 * override, and must therefore read as "no override" rather than "root is ''"
 * — an empty root would resolve to the working directory and scatter clones
 * across the app checkout.
 */
export function parseProjectsRoot(value: unknown): string | null {
  let candidate: unknown = value;

  if (typeof candidate === "string") {
    try {
      const decoded: unknown = JSON.parse(candidate);
      // Only a decoded string replaces the raw text: a path that happens to be
      // valid JSON (e.g. "123") must stay the literal directory name.
      if (typeof decoded === "string") candidate = decoded;
    } catch {
      // raw (non-JSON) string — use as-is
    }
  }

  if (typeof candidate !== "string") return null;

  const trimmed = candidate.trim();
  return trimmed.length > 0 ? trimmed : null;
}

import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import simpleGit, { CheckRepoActions, type SimpleGit } from "simple-git";
import {
  detectGitHubRemote,
  getCurrentGitBranch,
  resolveRemoteDefaultBranch,
} from "./remote";
import { DEFAULT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS } from "./clone-constants";

/**
 * Git clone service.
 *
 * Clones a repository into an app-managed directory, authenticating with the
 * PAT stored in settings when one is available. Three invariants drive the
 * implementation:
 *
 *  1. **Full clones only.** No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`: Arij creates
 *     worktrees off `main`, merges epic branches and tags releases, all of
 *     which need complete history.
 *  2. **The token never touches disk.** It is passed as an `http.extraHeader`
 *     via `-c`, so it stays out of `.git/config` and `origin` keeps the clean
 *     URL — `fetch`/`pull`/`push` afterwards behave like a hand-made clone.
 *  3. **Nothing existing is ever destroyed.** A destination that already holds
 *     the same repository is reused (fetch only); anything else is a conflict.
 *     Only a directory this service created is removed, and only when its own
 *     clone failed.
 */

export type CloneErrorCode =
  | "invalid_input"
  | "conflict"
  | "not_found"
  | "auth_failed"
  | "network"
  | "branch_not_found"
  | "timeout"
  | "clone_failed";

export class CloneError extends Error {
  readonly code: CloneErrorCode;
  readonly details: Record<string, unknown>;

  constructor(
    code: CloneErrorCode,
    message: string,
    details: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "CloneError";
    this.code = code;
    this.details = details;
  }
}

export interface CloneRepositoryOptions {
  /** Clean HTTPS (or, in tests, `file://`) URL. Never carries credentials. */
  cloneUrl: string;
  /** Absolute destination directory — `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>`. */
  dest: string;
  /** Optional branch to check out instead of the remote's default. */
  branch?: string | null;
  /** GitHub PAT, injected as an Authorization header for this command only. */
  token?: string | null;
  /**
   * `owner/repo` an existing destination must already point at to be reused.
   * When omitted, reuse falls back to comparing `origin` with `cloneUrl`.
   */
  expectedOwnerRepo?: string | null;
  /** Wall-clock budget; the clone is aborted past it. */
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

export interface CloneRepositoryResult {
  /** Absolute path of the clone — becomes `projects.git_repo_path`. */
  path: string;
  /** Branch checked out in the clone. */
  defaultBranch: string;
  /** True when an existing clone of the same repo was fetched instead. */
  reused: boolean;
  durationMs: number;
}

const REDACTED = "[REDACTED]";

/**
 * Strips credentials from a git error before it reaches the UI, a log line or
 * `git_sync_log`. Covers the header this service injects (`Basic <base64>`),
 * URL userinfo (`https://user:pass@host`), and raw GitHub token shapes, plus
 * any exact secret the caller passes in.
 */
export function redactGitError(value: unknown, secrets: string[] = []): string {
  let text =
    value instanceof Error
      ? value.message
      : typeof value === "string"
        ? value
        : value == null
          ? ""
          : String(value);

  for (const secret of secrets) {
    const clean = secret?.trim();
    if (!clean) continue;
    text = text.split(clean).join(REDACTED);
  }

  return text
    // `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ...` — everything after the
    // key is ours and secret, so drop the rest of the line wholesale.
    .replace(/(http\.extraheader=)[^\n]*/gi, `$1${REDACTED}`)
    .replace(/(\bbasic\s+)[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]+/gi, `$1${REDACTED}`)
    .replace(/(\bbearer\s+)[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/gi, `$1${REDACTED}`)
    // `https://user:token@github.com/...`
    .replace(/:\/\/[^/\s@]+@/g, `://${REDACTED}@`)
    // Raw PAT shapes, in case git echoes one we never injected.
    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b/g, REDACTED)
    .replace(/\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{16,}\b/g, REDACTED);

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Destination serialization                                           */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/**
 * One clone at a time per destination. Two concurrent imports of the same
 * repository would otherwise race: both see an empty destination, both clone
 * into it, and the loser corrupts the winner's work tree. The second caller
 * waits and then takes the reuse path.
 */
const destinationLocks = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();

async function withDestinationLock<T>(
  key: string,
  fn: () => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  const previous = destinationLocks.get(key) ?? Promise.resolve();

  let release!: () => void;
  const gate = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    release = resolve;
  });
  const chained = previous.then(() => gate);
  destinationLocks.set(key, chained);

  await previous;
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    release();
    if (destinationLocks.get(key) === chained) {
      destinationLocks.delete(key);
    }
  }
}
