describe("clone cleanup", () => {
  /** Mimics git: the destination appears, then the command fails. */
  function failingClone(message: string) {
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) => {
      const target = args[args.length - 1];
      fs.mkdirSync(path.join(target, ".git"), { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(target, ".git", "HEAD"), "ref: refs/heads/main");
      throw new Error(message);
    });
  }

  it("removes the partial destination when the clone fails", async () => {
    failingClone("fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly");

    await expect(
      cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: dest() })
    ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CloneError);

    // A half-written tree left behind would be picked up as a "matching"
    // clone on the next attempt and reused instead of re-cloned.
    expect(fs.existsSync(dest())).toBe(false);
  });

  it("removes the partial destination when the clone times out", async () => {
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) => {
      fs.mkdirSync(args[args.length - 1], { recursive: true });
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
      throw new Error("aborted");
    });

    await expect(
      cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: dest(), timeoutMs: 10 })
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "timeout" });

    expect(fs.existsSync(dest())).toBe(false);
  });

  it("leaves the parent root in place after a failure", async () => {
    failingClone("fatal: repository not found");

    await expect(
      cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: dest() })
    ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CloneError);

    // Only the clone's own directory is ours to delete.
    expect(fs.existsSync(root)).toBe(true);
  });

  it("never deletes a directory it did not create", async () => {
    // A pre-existing destination goes down the reuse path, which either
    // fetches or conflicts — it must never be cleaned up as "partial".
    const occupied = dest("occupied");
    fs.mkdirSync(occupied, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(occupied, "IMPORTANT.txt"), "user data");
    gitMock.checkIsRepo = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(false);

    await expect(
      cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: occupied })
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "conflict" });

    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(occupied, "IMPORTANT.txt"), "utf-8")).toBe(
      "user data"
    );
    // And git was never asked to clone into it.
    expect(gitMock.raw).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

/**
 * The reuse path talks to the remote just like the clone path does. It is the
 * easy one to get wrong: the token is deliberately absent from `.git/config`,
 * so a fetch that does not re-supply it is unauthenticated — which for a
 * private repository means a credential prompt, and with no terminal attached
 * that is a hang rather than an error.
 */
describe("reuse transport", () => {
  /** An existing destination holding the same repository. */
  function reusableDestination(name = "octocat-hello-world"): string {
    const target = dest(name);
    fs.mkdirSync(target, { recursive: true });
    gitMock.checkIsRepo = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
    gitMock.getRemotes = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([
      { name: "origin", refs: { fetch: CLONE_URL, push: CLONE_URL } },
    ]);
    return target;
  }

  function fetchArgs(): string[] {
    const call = gitMock.raw.mock.calls.find((args) =>
      (args[0] as string[]).includes("fetch")
    );
    if (!call) throw new Error("git never fetched");
    return call[0] as string[];
  }

  it("re-supplies the PAT on the fetch", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();

    const result = await cloneRepository({
      cloneUrl: CLONE_URL,
      dest: target,
      token: PAT,
      expectedOwnerRepo: "octocat/hello-world",
    });

    expect(result.reused).toBe(true);

    const args = fetchArgs();
    expect(args[0]).toBe("-c");
    expect(args[1]).toMatch(/^http\.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic /);
    expect(args.slice(2)).toEqual(["fetch", "origin"]);

    const basic = args[1].replace("http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ", "");
    expect(Buffer.from(basic, "base64").toString("utf-8")).toBe(
      `x-access-token:${PAT}`
    );
  });

  it("fetches unauthenticated when there is no PAT", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();

    await cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: target });

    expect(fetchArgs()).toEqual(["fetch", "origin"]);
  });

  it("disables interactive credential prompts on the fetch", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();

    await cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: target, token: PAT });

    expect(gitMock.env).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0" })
    );
  });

  it("bounds the fetch with the clone timeout instead of hanging", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) => {
      if (!args.includes("fetch")) return "";
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
      throw new Error("aborted");
    });

    await expect(
      cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: target, timeoutMs: 10 })
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "timeout" });

    // The destination was the user's before this call and stays untouched: a
    // failed *fetch* is not a partial clone.
    expect(fs.existsSync(target)).toBe(true);
  });

  it("keeps the PAT out of a failed fetch's error", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) => {
      if (!args.includes("fetch")) return "";
      throw new Error(
        `fatal: could not read from 'https://x-access-token:${PAT}@github.com/octocat/hello-world.git'`
      );
    });

    const error = await cloneRepository({
      cloneUrl: CLONE_URL,
      dest: target,
      token: PAT,
    }).catch((e) => e);

    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(CloneError);
    expect(`${error.message} ${JSON.stringify(error.details)}`).not.toContain(PAT);
  });

  it("reports the remote's default branch, not whatever is checked out", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();
    // The user left this clone on a feature branch. Persisting that as the
    // project's default branch would send every later worktree to the wrong
    // base, so `origin/HEAD` wins.
    gitMock.branchLocal.mockResolvedValue({
      current: "feature/wip",
      all: ["feature/wip", "trunk"],
    });
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) =>
      args.includes("symbolic-ref") ? "origin/trunk\n" : ""
    );

    const result = await cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: target });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ reused: true, defaultBranch: "trunk" });
  });

  it("falls back to the checked-out branch when the remote advertises no HEAD", async () => {
    const target = reusableDestination();
    gitMock.branchLocal.mockResolvedValue({ current: "main", all: ["main"] });
    gitMock.raw.mockImplementation(async (args: string[]) => {
      if (args.includes("symbolic-ref")) throw new Error("fatal: ref not a symbolic ref");
      return "";
    });

    const result = await cloneRepository({ cloneUrl: CLONE_URL, dest: target });

    expect(result.defaultBranch).toBe("main");
  });
});


import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { redactGitError } from "@/lib/git/clone";

const PAT = "ghp_A1b2C3d4E5f6G7h8I9j0K1l2M3n4O5p6Q7r8";

describe("redactGitError", () => {
  it("strips the Basic header this service injects", () => {
    const basic = Buffer.from(`x-access-token:${PAT}`).toString("base64");
    const stderr = [
      `fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/acme/private.git/':`,
      `while running: git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ${basic} clone -- https://github.com/acme/private.git /w/acme-private`,
    ].join("\n");

    const redacted = redactGitError(stderr);

    expect(redacted).not.toContain(basic);
    expect(redacted).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(redacted).toContain("[REDACTED]");
  });

  it("strips credentials embedded in a remote URL", () => {
    const redacted = redactGitError(
      `fatal: could not read from 'https://x-access-token:${PAT}@github.com/acme/private.git'`
    );

    expect(redacted).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(redacted).toContain("https://[REDACTED]@github.com/acme/private.git");
  });

  it("strips a raw PAT the caller passes in, wherever it appears", () => {
    const redacted = redactGitError(
      new Error(`remote: token ${PAT} was rejected`),
      [PAT]
    );

    expect(redacted).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(redacted).toContain("remote: token [REDACTED] was rejected");
  });

  it("strips bare GitHub token shapes even when nothing was passed in", () => {
    expect(redactGitError(`fatal: bad token ${PAT}`)).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(
      redactGitError("fatal: bad token github_pat_11ABCDEFG0abcdefghij1234")
    ).not.toContain("github_pat_11ABCDEFG0abcdefghij1234");
    expect(redactGitError("Authorization: Bearer abcdef.ghijkl-123")).toBe(
      "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]"
    );
  });

  it("keeps the actionable part of the message intact", () => {
    const redacted = redactGitError(
      new Error("fatal: repository 'https://github.com/acme/nope.git/' not found")
    );

    expect(redacted).toBe(
      "fatal: repository 'https://github.com/acme/nope.git/' not found"
    );
  });

  it("fully redacts a real clone failure carrying the token in every form", () => {
    // One sample, every way git manages to echo a credential back: the header
    // we injected, the base64 payload on its own, a URL with userinfo, and the
    // raw PAT in a remote's message. A single leak here reaches the UI and
    // git_sync_log at once.
    const basic = Buffer.from(`x-access-token:${PAT}`).toString("base64");
    const stderr = [
      `Cloning into '/home/user/arij/projects/acme-private'...`,
      `fatal: unable to access 'https://x-access-token:${PAT}@github.com/acme/private.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403`,
      `remote: Invalid username or password for token ${PAT}`,
      `error: RPC failed; HTTP 403 curl 22`,
      `while running: git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ${basic} clone -- https://github.com/acme/private.git /home/user/arij/projects/acme-private`,
    ].join("\n");

    const redacted = redactGitError(new Error(stderr), [PAT]);

    expect(redacted).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(redacted).not.toContain(basic);
    expect(redacted).not.toMatch(/x-access-token:/);
    // Still diagnosable: the repository and the HTTP status survive.
    expect(redacted).toContain("github.com/acme/private.git");
    expect(redacted).toContain("403");
  });

  it("handles non-string inputs without throwing", () => {
    expect(redactGitError(null)).toBe("");
    expect(redactGitError(undefined)).toBe("");
    expect(redactGitError({ toString: () => `boom ${PAT}` }, [PAT])).toBe(
      "boom [REDACTED]"
    );
  });
});

  const cases: Array<[string, ConstructorParameters<typeof CloneError>[0], number]> = [
    ["missing repository", "not_found", 404],
    ["bad credentials", "auth_failed", 401],
    ["unreachable host", "network", 502],
    ["unknown branch", "branch_not_found", 400],
    ["occupied destination", "conflict", 409],
    ["slow clone", "timeout", 504],
    ["anything else", "clone_failed", 500],
  ];

  it.each(cases)("maps %s to HTTP %s", async (_label, code, status) => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(new CloneError(code, `boom: ${code}`));

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(status);
    expect(body).toEqual({ error: `boom: ${code}`, code });
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });

  it("returns 409 when the destination holds a different repository", async () => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(
      new CloneError(
        "conflict",
        "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world already holds a different repository (https://github.com/someone-else/other.git). Move or remove it, then retry.",
        { path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world" }
      )
    );

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    // the directory that is in the way. Never silently overwritten.

  });

import { POST } from "@/app/api/projects/clone/route";

import { DEFAULT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS } from "@/lib/git/clone-constants";

const PAT = "ghp_A1b2C3d4E5f6G7h8I9j0K1l2M3n4O5p6Q7r8";

function cloneRequest(body: Record<string, unknown>) {
  return mockJsonRequest(body, { url: "http://localhost:3000/api/projects/clone" });
}

function syncLogRows() {
  return dbMockState.insertCalls as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  resetDbMockState();
  mockGetToken.mockReturnValue(null);
  mockEnsureProjectsRoot.mockReturnValue("/workspace/projects");
  mockCloneDest.mockImplementation(
    (owner: string, repo: string, root: string) => `${root}/${owner}-${repo}`
  );
  mockCloneRepository.mockResolvedValue({

describe("POST /api/projects/clone — success", () => {
  it("returns 201 with the clone metadata", async () => {
    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(body.data).toEqual({
      path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world",
      ownerRepo: "octocat/hello-world",
      remoteUrl: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world.git",
      defaultBranch: "main",
      reused: false,
    });
  });

  it("clones into <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo> from the clean URL", async () => {
    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(mockCloneDest).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      "octocat",
      "hello-world",
      "/workspace/projects"
    );
    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({
        cloneUrl: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world.git",
        dest: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world",
        expectedOwnerRepo: "octocat/hello-world",
        branch: null,
        timeoutMs: DEFAULT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS,
      })
    );
  });

  it.each([
    ["git@github.com:octocat/hello-world.git"],
    ["octocat/hello-world"],
    ["https://github.com/octocat/hello-world/tree/main"],
    ["https://github.com/octocat/hello-world.git"],
    ["https://www.github.com/octocat/hello-world?tab=readme-ov-file"],
  ])("accepts %s", async (url) => {
    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url }));

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({
        cloneUrl: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world.git",
      })
    );
  });

  it("passes an explicit branch through to the clone", async () => {
    mockCloneRepository.mockResolvedValue({
      path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world",
      defaultBranch: "develop",
      reused: false,
      durationMs: 10,
    });

    const response = await POST(
      cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world", branch: "develop" })
    );
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ branch: "develop" })
    );
    expect(body.data.defaultBranch).toBe("develop");
  });

  it("returns 200 when an existing clone was reused", async () => {
    mockCloneRepository.mockResolvedValue({
      path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world",
      defaultBranch: "main",
      reused: true,
      durationMs: 42,
    });

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(body.data.reused).toBe(true);
  });

  it("uses the configured clone timeout when one is set", async () => {
    dbMockState.getQueue.push({ key: "clone_timeout_ms", value: "60000" });

    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: 60000 })
    );
  });

  it("records a git_sync_log row with operation 'clone'", async () => {
    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(syncLogRows()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(syncLogRows()[0]).toMatchObject({
      operation: "clone",
      status: "success",
      projectId: null,
      branch: "main",
    });
    // The clone runs before any project row exists, so the audit row cannot
    // reference one (migration 0028_git_sync_log_nullable_project).
    const detail = JSON.parse(syncLogRows()[0].detail as string);
    expect(detail).toMatchObject({
      ownerRepo: "octocat/hello-world",
      path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world",
      reused: false,
      durationMs: 1234,
    });
  });
});

describe("POST /api/projects/clone — credentials", () => {
  it("passes the stored PAT to the clone", async () => {
    mockGetToken.mockReturnValue(PAT);

    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ token: PAT })
    );
  });

  it("clones public repos with no token at all", async () => {
    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(mockCloneRepository).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ token: null })
    );
  });

  it("never leaks the PAT into the response, the log row or the console", async () => {
    mockGetToken.mockReturnValue(PAT);
    const basic = Buffer.from(`x-access-token:${PAT}`).toString("base64");
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(
      new Error(
        `fatal: unable to access 'https://x-access-token:${PAT}@github.com/acme/private.git/'\n` +
          `while running: git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ${basic} clone`
      )
    );

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "acme/private" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(500);
    expect(JSON.stringify(body)).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(JSON.stringify(body)).not.toContain(basic);
    expect(JSON.stringify(syncLogRows())).not.toContain(PAT);
    expect(JSON.stringify(syncLogRows())).not.toContain(basic);
    expect(JSON.stringify(consoleError.mock.calls)).not.toContain(PAT);
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });
});

/**
 * Body validation happens before the route reads anything, so the schema is
 * asserted directly: an over-long branch or a non-string url must never reach
 * the parser, let alone the git layer.
 */
describe("cloneProjectSchema", () => {
  it("accepts a url alone", () => {
    expect(
      cloneProjectSchema.safeParse({
        url: "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world",
      }).success
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  it("accepts an optional branch", () => {
    const result = cloneProjectSchema.safeParse({
      url: "octocat/hello-world",
      branch: "develop",
    });

    expect(result.success).toBe(true);
    if (result.success) expect(result.data.branch).toBe("develop");
  });

  it.each([
    ["a missing url", {}],
    ["an empty url", { url: "" }],
    ["a non-string url", { url: 42 }],
    ["a url over 500 chars", { url: `https://github.com/o/${"a".repeat(500)}` }],
    [
      "a branch over 255 chars",
      { url: "octocat/hello-world", branch: "b".repeat(256) },
    ],
  ])("rejects %s", (_label, body) => {
    expect(cloneProjectSchema.safeParse(body).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("POST /api/projects/clone — failures", () => {
  const cases: Array<[string, ConstructorParameters<typeof CloneError>[0], number]> = [
    ["missing repository", "not_found", 404],
    ["bad credentials", "auth_failed", 401],
    ["unreachable host", "network", 502],
    ["unknown branch", "branch_not_found", 400],
    ["occupied destination", "conflict", 409],
    ["slow clone", "timeout", 504],
    ["anything else", "clone_failed", 500],
  ];

  it.each(cases)("maps %s to HTTP %s", async (_label, code, status) => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(new CloneError(code, `boom: ${code}`));

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(status);
    expect(body).toEqual({ error: `boom: ${code}`, code });
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });

  it("returns 409 when the destination holds a different repository", async () => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(
      new CloneError(
        "conflict",
        "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world already holds a different repository (https://github.com/someone-else/other.git). Move or remove it, then retry.",
        { path: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world" }
      )
    );

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    // 409, not 500: nothing is broken — the user has to decide what happens to
    // the directory that is in the way. Never silently overwritten.
    expect(response.status).toBe(409);
    expect(body.code).toBe("conflict");
    expect(body.error).toMatch(/different repository/);
    expect(body.error).toMatch(/Move or remove it/);
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });

  it("returns 409 when the destination exists but is not a git repository", async () => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(
      new CloneError(
        "conflict",
        "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world already exists and is not a git repository. Move or remove it, then retry."
      )
    );

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(409);
    expect(body.code).toBe("conflict");
    expect(body.error).toMatch(/not a git repository/);
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });

  it("logs the failure to git_sync_log with the reason", async () => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockCloneRepository.mockRejectedValue(
      new CloneError("conflict", "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world is in the way.")
    );

    await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));

    expect(syncLogRows()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(syncLogRows()[0]).toMatchObject({
      operation: "clone",
      status: "failure",
      projectId: null,
    });
    const detail = JSON.parse(syncLogRows()[0].detail as string);
    expect(detail).toMatchObject({
      ownerRepo: "octocat/hello-world",
      code: "conflict",
      error: "/workspace/projects/octocat-hello-world is in the way.",
    });
    expect(detail.durationMs).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });

  it("returns 500 when the workspace root cannot be prepared", async () => {
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockEnsureProjectsRoot.mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspace/projects'");
    });

    const response = await POST(cloneRequest({ url: "octocat/hello-world" }));
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(500);
    expect(body.error).toContain("EACCES");
    expect(mockCloneRepository).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });
});


/**
 * `POST /api/projects` — the last step of every import, and until now the only
 * project route with no coverage at all.
 *
 * Runs against `createTestDb()` (real migration chain, real columns) rather
 * than a query-chain mock: the point of most of these assertions is that a
 * value survives into the column migration 0027 added, which a mock that
 * records `.values()` calls cannot show. Paths are real temp directories —
 * `validatePath()` stats them — and nothing here touches the network.
 */

import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { projects, settings } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import { PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY } from "@/lib/projects/workspace-constants";
import { mockJsonRequest, mockNextRequest } from "@/__tests__/helpers/db-mock";

vi.mock("@/lib/db", async () => {
  const { createTestDb } = await import("@/lib/db/test-utils");
  return { db: createTestDb().db };
});

import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { POST } from "@/app/api/projects/route";

const tempDirs: string[] = [];

function repoDir(): string {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-project-post-"));
  tempDirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

function post(body: unknown) {
  return POST(
    mockJsonRequest(body, { url: "http://localhost:3000/api/projects" })
  );
}

/** The row as SQLite actually holds it, not as the route echoed it back. */
function storedProject(id: string) {
  return db.select().from(projects).where(eq(projects.id, id)).get();
}

/**
 * Reproduces what the clone service leaves on disk: a managed clone root, with
 * `<owner>-<repo>` inside it. `cloneSource: "github"` is only accepted for
 * exactly this path, so tests that claim it have to earn it.
 */
function managedClone(owner: string, repo: string): { root: string; dir: string } {
  const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-projects-root-"));
  tempDirs.push(root);

  db.insert(settings)
    .values({ key: PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY, value: JSON.stringify(root) })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({
      target: settings.key,
      set: { value: JSON.stringify(root) },
    })
    .run();

  const dir = path.join(root, `${owner}-${repo}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  return { root, dir };
}

beforeEach(() => {
  db.delete(projects).run();
  db.delete(settings).run();
});

afterEach(() => {
  while (tempDirs.length > 0) {
    fs.rmSync(tempDirs.pop() as string, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

      gitRepoPath: null,
      githubOwnerRepo: null,
      cloneSource: null,

    });
  });

  it("rejects a missing name with 400 and writes nothing", async () => {
    const response = await post({ description: "no name" });

    expect((await response.json()).error).toBe("Validation failed");
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);

      mockNextRequest({

      })
    );

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toBe("Invalid JSON body");
  });
});

describe("POST /api/projects — clone metadata", () => {
  it("persists githubOwnerRepo so push/PR/release work with no Connect step", async () => {
    const body = await (
      await post({ name: "Arij", githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij" })
    ).json();

    expect(body.data.githubOwnerRepo).toBe("Orolol/arij");
    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.githubOwnerRepo).toBe("Orolol/arij");
  });

  it("persists the full clone provenance an import writes", async () => {
    const { dir } = managedClone("Orolol", "arij");

    const body = await (
      await post({
        name: "arij",
        gitRepoPath: dir,
        githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
        cloneSource: "github",
        gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
        defaultBranch: "main",
      })
    ).json();

    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)).toMatchObject({
      gitRepoPath: dir,
      githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
      cloneSource: "github",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
      defaultBranch: "main",
    });
  });

  it("leaves cloneSource NULL for a user-supplied path", async () => {
    // The ownership flag: a directory Arij did not create must never be
    // offered for deletion when the project is deleted.
    const body = await (
      await post({ name: "Local repo", gitRepoPath: repoDir() })
    ).json();

    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.cloneSource).toBeNull();
  });

  it("rejects a cloneSource Arij does not issue", async () => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Spoofed", cloneSource: "gitlab" });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("accepts an explicit null for each optional clone field", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Nulls",
      cloneSource: null,
      gitRemoteUrl: null,
      defaultBranch: null,
      githubOwnerRepo: null,
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
  });

  it("rejects an over-length remote url", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Long",
      gitRemoteUrl: `https://github.com/o/${"a".repeat(500)}.git`,
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
  });
});

describe("POST /api/projects — path normalisation", () => {
  it("stores the resolved path, not the string the caller typed", async () => {
    const dir = repoDir();

    for (const input of [`${dir}/`, `${dir}//`, `${dir}/.`, ` ${dir} `]) {
      db.delete(projects).run();
      const body = await (await post({ name: "Normalised", gitRepoPath: input })).json();

      expect(body.data.gitRepoPath).toBe(dir);
      expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.gitRepoPath).toBe(dir);
    }
  });

  it("stores a path that worktrees can be hung off unchanged", async () => {
    // createWorktree() joins `<gitRepoPath>/../.arij-worktrees`; a stored
    // trailing slash would push that one directory too deep.
    const dir = repoDir();
    const body = await (
      await post({ name: "Worktree host", gitRepoPath: `${dir}/` })
    ).json();

    const stored = storedProject(body.data.id)!.gitRepoPath!;
    expect(path.join(stored, "..", ".arij-worktrees")).toBe(
      path.join(path.dirname(dir), ".arij-worktrees")
    );
  });

  it("rejects a path that does not exist", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Ghost",
      gitRepoPath: path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-does-not-exist-4c1f"),
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/does not exist/i);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("rejects a path pointing at a file rather than a directory", async () => {
    const file = path.join(repoDir(), "README.md");
    fs.writeFileSync(file, "# not a repo");

    const response = await post({ name: "File", gitRepoPath: file });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/not a directory/i);
  });

  it.each([
    ["traversal", "/tmp/../etc"],
    ["embedded traversal", "/tmp/foo/../../etc"],
    ["NUL byte", "/tmp/evil\0/repo"],
  ])("rejects a %s path with 400", async (_label, gitRepoPath) => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Escape", gitRepoPath });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("treats an empty path as no path at all", async () => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Blank", gitRepoPath: "" });
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.gitRepoPath).toBeNull();
  });
});

/**
 * `cloneSource` is an ownership claim: it is what later authorises Arij to
 * delete the directory, so it cannot be something a request simply asserts.
 * `gitRemoteUrl` is bound by the no-secret-on-disk contract in the same way.
 */
describe("POST /api/projects — clone provenance is server-verified", () => {
  it("refuses to mark a directory Arij never cloned as a github clone", async () => {
    managedClone("Orolol", "arij");
    // A real directory, but not the managed destination for this repository.
    const outsider = repoDir();

    const response = await post({
      name: "Spoofed",
      gitRepoPath: outsider,
      githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
      cloneSource: "github",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/cloned itself/i);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("refuses a managed path claimed for the wrong repository", async () => {

 * than a query-chain mock: the point of most of these assertions is that a
 * value survives into the column migration 0027 added, which a mock that
 * records `.values()` calls cannot show. Paths are real temp directories —
 * `validatePath()` stats them — and nothing here touches the network.

import fs from "node:fs";

import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { projects, settings } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import { PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY } from "@/lib/projects/workspace-constants";
import { mockJsonRequest, mockNextRequest } from "@/__tests__/helpers/db-mock";

vi.mock("@/lib/db", async () => {
  const { createTestDb } = await import("@/lib/db/test-utils");
  return { db: createTestDb().db };
});

import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { POST } from "@/app/api/projects/route";

const tempDirs: string[] = [];

function repoDir(): string {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-project-post-"));
  tempDirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

function post(body: unknown) {
  return POST(
    mockJsonRequest(body, { url: "http://localhost:3000/api/projects" })
  );
}

/** The row as SQLite actually holds it, not as the route echoed it back. */
function storedProject(id: string) {
  return db.select().from(projects).where(eq(projects.id, id)).get();
}

/**
 * Reproduces what the clone service leaves on disk: a managed clone root, with
 * `<owner>-<repo>` inside it. `cloneSource: "github"` is only accepted for
 * exactly this path, so tests that claim it have to earn it.
 */
function managedClone(owner: string, repo: string): { root: string; dir: string } {
  const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-projects-root-"));
  tempDirs.push(root);

  db.insert(settings)
    .values({ key: PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY, value: JSON.stringify(root) })
    .onConflictDoUpdate({
      target: settings.key,
      set: { value: JSON.stringify(root) },
    })
    .run();

  const dir = path.join(root, `${owner}-${repo}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  return { root, dir };
}

describe("POST /api/projects — path normalisation", () => {
  it("stores the resolved path, not the string the caller typed", async () => {
    const dir = repoDir();

    for (const input of [`${dir}/`, `${dir}//`, `${dir}/.`, ` ${dir} `]) {
      db.delete(projects).run();
      const body = await (await post({ name: "Normalised", gitRepoPath: input })).json();

      expect(body.data.gitRepoPath).toBe(dir);
      expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.gitRepoPath).toBe(dir);
    }
  });

  it("stores a path that worktrees can be hung off unchanged", async () => {
    // createWorktree() joins `<gitRepoPath>/../.arij-worktrees`; a stored
    // trailing slash would push that one directory too deep.

    const body = await (
      await post({ name: "Worktree host", gitRepoPath: `${dir}/` })
    ).json();

    const stored = storedProject(body.data.id)!.gitRepoPath!;
    expect(path.join(stored, "..", ".arij-worktrees")).toBe(
      path.join(path.dirname(dir), ".arij-worktrees")
    );
  });

  it("rejects a path that does not exist", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Ghost",
      gitRepoPath: path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-does-not-exist-4c1f"),
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/does not exist/i);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("rejects a path pointing at a file rather than a directory", async () => {
    const file = path.join(repoDir(), "README.md");
    fs.writeFileSync(file, "# not a repo");

    const response = await post({ name: "File", gitRepoPath: file });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/not a directory/i);
  });

    ["embedded traversal", "/tmp/foo/../../etc"],

    const body = await response.json();

  });
});

      gitRepoPath: path.join(os.tmpdir(), "arij-does-not-exist-4c1f"),
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/does not exist/i);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("rejects a path pointing at a file rather than a directory", async () => {
    const file = path.join(repoDir(), "README.md");
    fs.writeFileSync(file, "# not a repo");

    const response = await post({ name: "File", gitRepoPath: file });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/not a directory/i);
  });

  it.each([
    ["traversal", "/tmp/../etc"],
    ["embedded traversal", "/tmp/foo/../../etc"],
    ["NUL byte", "/tmp/evil\0/repo"],
  ])("rejects a %s path with 400", async (_label, gitRepoPath) => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Escape", gitRepoPath });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("treats an empty path as no path at all", async () => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Blank", gitRepoPath: "" });
    const body = await response.json();

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.gitRepoPath).toBeNull();
  });
});

/**
 * `cloneSource` is an ownership claim: it is what later authorises Arij to
 * delete the directory, so it cannot be something a request simply asserts.
 * `gitRemoteUrl` is bound by the no-secret-on-disk contract in the same way.
 */
describe("POST /api/projects — clone provenance is server-verified", () => {
  it("refuses to mark a directory Arij never cloned as a github clone", async () => {
    managedClone("Orolol", "arij");
    // A real directory, but not the managed destination for this repository.
    const outsider = repoDir();

    const response = await post({
      name: "Spoofed",
      gitRepoPath: outsider,
      githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
      cloneSource: "github",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/cloned itself/i);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("refuses a managed path claimed for the wrong repository", async () => {
    const { dir } = managedClone("Orolol", "arij");

    const response = await post({
      name: "Mismatched",
      gitRepoPath: dir,
      githubOwnerRepo: "attacker/evil",
      cloneSource: "github",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/attacker/evil.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("refuses github provenance with no path at all", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Pathless",
      cloneSource: "github",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it.each([
    ["https://x-access-token:ghp_secret@github.com/Orolol/arij.git"],
    ["https://user:password@github.com/Orolol/arij.git"],
  ])("refuses to store a credential-bearing remote url (%s)", async (url) => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Tokenised", gitRemoteUrl: url });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    // The point is not just the rejection: nothing carrying the secret is
    // written, so it cannot leak later through a diff or a log surface.
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
    expect((await response.json()).error).not.toContain("ghp_secret");
  });

  it("refuses a remote url that is not a GitHub repository", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Elsewhere",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://gitlab.com/Orolol/arij.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
  });

  it("refuses a remote url that contradicts githubOwnerRepo", async () => {
    const response = await post({
      name: "Contradictory",
      githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/someone/else.git",
    });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await response.json()).error).toMatch(/does not match/i);
  });

  it("normalises the stored remote url instead of echoing the input", async () => {
    const body = await (
      await post({
        name: "Browser URL",
        // What a user actually pastes out of the address bar.
        gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij/tree/main",
      })
    ).json();

    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)).toMatchObject({
      gitRemoteUrl: "https://github.com/Orolol/arij.git",
      // Derived rather than demanded: the remote already names the repo.
      githubOwnerRepo: "Orolol/arij",
    });
  });

  it("still accepts a plain local import with no provenance", async () => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Local", gitRepoPath: repoDir() });

    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(storedProject((await response.json()).data.id)).toMatchObject({
      cloneSource: null,
      gitRemoteUrl: null,
    });
  });

  it.each([
    ["leading dash", "--upload-pack=touch/pwned"],
    ["whitespace", "main branch"],
    ["ref metacharacter", "main^{}"],
  ])("refuses a branch name git would reject (%s)", async (_label, branch) => {
    const response = await post({ name: "Bad branch", defaultBranch: branch });

    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(db.select().from(projects).all()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("accepts an ordinary slashed branch name", async () => {
    const body = await (
      await post({ name: "Slashed", defaultBranch: "release/v2" })
    ).json();

    expect(storedProject(body.data.id)?.defaultBranch).toBe("release/v2");
  });
});

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**

**Probable root cause** — The `build` stage never started: `spawn E2BIG` is the kernel's `execve()` "argument list too long" error, surfaced by Node before the child process exists. Arij's Codex provider passes the entire prompt as a single `argv` element (`lib/providers/codex.ts:181`, `args.push(prompt)`), plus a `-c developer_instructions=<JSON>` argument. Linux caps *one* argv string at 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) and the whole argv+env block at ~2 MB. The build prompt for this ticket is assembled by concatenation with no size guard — ticket body, all comments, review context, fix instructions, mention enrichment and the Arij tools section (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:476-552`, `lib/claude/process-manager.ts:135`) — and grows further on each retry. For a docs-and-tests ticket on the GitHub import (which typically carries long pasted diffs/logs in comments), that pushed a single argument past the limit. This is deterministic, not transient, which is exactly why both attempts failed identically.

**Evidence**

- `spawn E2BIG` — Node emits this string only when `execve` fails with `E2BIG`; the failure is at process creation, not inside the build.
- "Raw stream (tail): (none)", "Output stream (tail): (none)", "Last text produced: (none)" — no stdout/stderr at all, confirming the Codex CLI never ran. A build failure or model error would have produced output.
- `lib/providers/codex.ts:181` `args.push(prompt)` combined with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` (`lib/providers/base-provider.ts:~397`) — stdin is closed, so the prompt can only travel via argv; there is no length check anywhere (`grep -rn "E2BIG\|prompt.length" lib/` returns only logging).

**Recommended next action**

- Re-dispatch this ticket on the `claude` provider (which overrides `spawn()` and does not pass the prompt as a Codex-style argv element), and in parallel have a human trim the ticket's accumulated comments/review context — the oversized inputs are the trigger. The durable fix, once someone picks it up: pass the Codex prompt over stdin or a temp file instead of `argv`, and add a hard prompt-size guard in `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` so this fails with a readable message instead of `E2BIG`.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Reprise après l'échec `spawn E2BIG` — rien à reconstruire, tout est vert.**

Cette session a été relancée sur le provider `claude` après les deux échecs `spawn E2BIG` du 19/08. Ces échecs n'ont **rien à voir avec le code de l'epic** : `execve()` échouait avant même le démarrage du build, parce que le provider Codex passe le prompt entier comme un seul élément d'`argv` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:181`) et que le fil de commentaires de ce ticket — dont une revue de 579 000 caractères — dépassait la limite `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` de 128 Kio. Le diagnostic forensique précédent était correct.

Le travail des 4 stories était déjà livré (`5379f3c` → `7f6f448`), avec les 5 constats de revue corrigés. Je l'ai revérifié intégralement plutôt que de le prendre pour acquis.

## Vérification

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **2730 tests / 263 fichiers, tous verts** |
| `npx playwright test` | **12 tests verts** (dont les 9 de `project-import.spec.ts`) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` | propre |
| `git status` | arbre propre, rien de non commité |

E2E lancé avec `E2E_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome` : le chromium livré par Playwright n'est pas installé sur cette machine et sa build ne supporte pas cet Ubuntu. C'est précisément le repli que `playwright.config.ts` a ajouté pour cette raison ; la CI continue d'utiliser la build livrée.

## Critères d'acceptation

**Story 1 — parsing et workspace.** `github-url-parse.test.ts` couvre https, ssh, git, shorthand, URLs suffixées et entrées invalides, avec un bloc dédié « traversal payloads reach no filesystem path ». `projects-workspace.test.ts` couvre le défaut, l'override `projects_root` et les racines relatives sur `createTestDb()`, et teste `assertInsideRoot()` dans son propre `describe`, indépendamment du parseur.

**Story 2 — clone et routes, git mocké.** `simple-git` est mocké. L'argv est asserté sans `--depth` et sans `extraHeader` en l'absence de PAT, avec `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic …` uniquement quand un token existe. `redactGitError()` est asserté sur un stderr réel contenant le header Basic, une URL porteuse d'identifiants et un PAT brut. Réutilisation, remote divergent (409) et destination non-dépôt (409) ont chacun leur test, et la suppression de la destination partielle est couverte à l'échec **et** au timeout — avec la contre-épreuve qu'un répertoire préexistant n'est jamais supprimé.

**Story 3 — e2e.** Les 9 tests couvrent les deux sources et leur bascule, l'URL invalide (feedback inline, bouton désactivé), le parcours `cloning` → `analyzing` → `preview` avec les deux endpoints stubés, et le retour à `select` sur échec de clone avec le message visible. Aucun accès réseau.

**Story 4 — documentation.** README (parcours d'import, `projects_root`, PAT en Settings, correction explicite du `GITHUB_TOKEN` obsolète), CLAUDE.md (`projects/` en clones gitignorés gérés par l'app), et `docs/architecture/github-import.md` (flux, clone complet et ce qu'un clone superficiel casserait, gestion des identifiants). `github-import-docs.test.ts` épingle chacun de ces faits, y compris l'existence des fichiers de test qu'il référence.

## À signaler séparément

La cause de l'`E2BIG` est un défaut du pipeline Arij, hors périmètre de cet epic : le prompt Codex devrait passer par stdin ou un fichier temporaire, et `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` devrait garder une limite de taille pour échouer avec un message lisible. Je ne l'ai pas corrigé ici — ça mérite son propre ticket.

comments.content:
Epic done — ticket moved to **review**. Nothing needed rebuilding: the work was already delivered across `5379f3c` → `7f6f448`, so I verified it end to end rather than taking it on faith.

**The earlier failure wasn't the code.** The two `spawn E2BIG` errors came from `execve()` failing before the child process existed — the Codex provider passes the whole prompt as one `argv` element, and this ticket's comment thread (including a 579k-character review comment) blew past Linux's 128 KiB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`. Deterministic, not transient, which is why both attempts failed identically. Running on the `claude` provider sidesteps it.

**Verification:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 2730 passed / 263 files |
| `npx playwright test` | 12 passed (9 in `project-import.spec.ts`) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` | clean |
| `git status` | clean, nothing uncommitted |

E2E needed `E2E_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome` — Playwright's bundled chromium isn't installed here and its build doesn't support this Ubuntu. That's exactly the fallback `playwright.config.ts` added; CI still uses the bundled browser.

All four stories' criteria hold up under inspection: the parser suite has a dedicated traversal block and `assertInsideRoot()` is tested independently of the parser; the clone suite asserts argv carries no `--depth` and only injects `-c http.extraHeader` when a PAT exists, covers reuse / 409-mismatch / 409-not-a-repo, and checks partial-destination cleanup on both failure *and* timeout with the counter-test that a pre-existing directory is never deleted; the e2e spec drives `cloning` → `analyzing` → `preview` on stubs and the failure path back to `select`; and `github-import-docs.test.ts` pins each documented fact, including that the referenced test files exist.

One thing I deliberately left alone: the `E2BIG` root cause is an Arij pipeline defect (prompt should go over stdin or a temp file, with a size guard so it fails readably). That's outside this epic's scope — I flagged it on the ticket as deserving its own.

epics.title: Multi-Provider CLI Integration with Base Class Refactor
epics.description:
Add 6 new CLI providers (Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Kimi/Moonshot, Zai) and refactor the provider layer with a BaseCliProvider abstract class to reduce duplication. Updates the provider registry, named agents UI, and availability checks to support all 9 providers.

New providers:
- Mistral Vibe (`vibe`): --prompt, --agent, --output json, --resume, --max-turns, --max-price
- Qwen Code (`qwen`): -p, --yolo, --model, /resume
- OpenCode (`opencode`): run "...", --format json, --session, --file
- DeepSeek (`deepseek`): -q, --model, --no-stream, SQLite history
- Kimi/Moonshot (`kimi`): --print, --continue, stream-json
- Zai/Zhipu AI (`zai`): API-based via subprocess wrapper, GLM models

Architecture: BaseCliProvider abstract class handles 70% of shared spawn/kill/log/parse logic. Each provider is ~80-120 lines. Existing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini refactored onto base class first.

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want a BaseCliProvider abstract class so that adding new CLI providers requires minimal boilerplate
user_stories.description:
Create lib/providers/base-provider.ts with an abstract class that encapsulates the shared provider lifecycle: child_process.spawn with stdio piping, stdout/stderr buffer collection, SIGTERM then SIGKILL kill logic, session ID extraction via extractCliSessionIdFromOutput, NDJSON session logging, endedWithQuestion detection, duration tracking, display command building, and exit code to success/error mapping.

Abstract methods for subclasses:
- get binaryName(): string
- buildArgs(options: ProviderSpawnOptions): string[]
- extractResult(stdout: string, stderr: string): string
- Optional overrides: parseSessionId(), isAvailable(), buildEnv()

Also support chunk callbacks (onRawChunk, onOutputChunk, onResponseChunk) in the base for providers that stream.

epics.title: when asking for a review on a bug ticket, the agent instead do a review of a porevious epic
Preuves visuelles : artefacts de session (screenshots) joints à la review
epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement Cursor (Code with Claude 2026) : les agents enregistrent des démos de leurs changements — une revue « à haute bande passante » où l'humain regarde la preuve avant de lire le diff. Dans Arij, la review humaine n'a que le diff et la prose de l'agent. Note environnement : Playwright fonctionne sur cette machine via le Chrome système (`channel: "chrome"`) — l'install de chromium échoue.

## À construire
1. **Outil MCP `attach_artifact`** (toolset agent) : payload `{ path, caption }` — le fichier (png/jpg/webp, max 5 Mo, max 10 par session) est COPIÉ depuis le worktree vers `data/sessions/<sessionId>/artifacts/` (le worktree peut être détruit ensuite) et enregistré dans une table `session_artifacts` (id, agentSessionId, epicId, filename, caption, createdAt — migration SQL manuscrite + `_journal.json`). Valider que `path` résout DANS le worktree de la session (pas de traversée), type vérifié par extension ET par sniff des magic bytes.

epics.title: Telescope-lite : digest périodique des échecs récurrents
epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement Replit (Telescope, Code with Claude 2026) : les pannes récurrentes à ~1 % sont invisibles dans les logs bruts ; c'est le clustering des traces qui les révèle. Arij accumule déjà la matière : sessions failed/silent, outcomes `transition_refused`, rapports forensic, findings critiques récurrents — mais personne ne les regarde transversalement.

## À construire
1. **Collecteur** `lib/telescope/collect.ts` : sur une fenêtre glissante (14 jours, configurable), agréger par projet : sessions failed/silent (avec dernier chunk et message d'erreur), transition_refused (avec raison), rapports forensic, findings `[critical]`/`[major]` récurrents (même filePath ou même préfixe de message). Pré-groupage MÉCANIQUE par signature normalisée (provider + agentType + motif d'erreur) AVANT tout LLM, pour borner le volume.
2. **Session d'analyse** : agent en mode plan (agentType `failure_digest`), prompt `buildFailureDigestPrompt` : reçoit les groupes pré-agrégés et produit un rapport markdown — clusters nommés, fréquence, tickets touchés, hypothèse de cause racine, remédiation proposée. Persisté via `qa_reports` avec un nouveau `checkType: 'failure_digest'` (réutiliser l'UI des rapports QA existante).
3. **Action** : la route existante `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics` doit fonctionner sur ce checkType — un cluster devient un ticket en un clic, le ticket référence le rapport source.
4. **Déclencheurs** : bouton manuel dans l'onglet QA ; kind de routine si le ticket Routines est livré — sinon manuel uniquement (ne PAS créer de timer dédié).

## Contraintes
- Fenêtre vide → aucune session lancée (no-op journalisé).
- Comme le forensic (`lib/pipeline/forensic.ts`) : pas d'epicId sur la ligne de session (ne bloque aucun ticket), mode plan.
- agentType `failure_digest` intégré aux constantes/enums (watchdog, classification).
- Tests vitest : collecteur (fenêtre, signatures, pré-groupage, volume borné), no-op à vide, checkType accepté par create-epics.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

`submit_findings` is blocked in this session (plan mode), so the review is delivered as prose below — the fallback Arij parses. Findings are file+line anchored so they can be re-filed verbatim.

# Code Review — Telescope-lite: digest périodique des échecs récurrents

**Scope:** `9dce322..488b3bc` (3 commits, 26 files, +1977/−50) — `lib/telescope/collect.ts`, `buildFailureDigestPrompt`, `qa/check`, `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics`, `sessions/active`, QA UI, agent-type constants.

## Summary of the implementation

The mechanical-before-LLM boundary is the right architecture and it is respected end to end: the collector is a pure, injectable (`options.database`) function with no provider call in it, every dimension of the payload is capped, and the prompt hands the agent only the pre-grouped structure. `failure_digest` is threaded correctly through `AGENT_TYPES`, `AGENT_TYPE_LABELS`, `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`, `DISPATCH_ROLE_AGENT_TYPES.qa`, notification routing, the activity monitor (`type: "qa"` in both the route and the hook copy of `UnifiedActivity`), and `MCP_EXEMPT_AGENT_TYPES` — the last with a correct rationale: the digest's entire response *is* the report body, so appending ticket-tool guidance would land after its output contract. It is automatically excluded from `AUTO_DISTILL_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` (allowlist) and correctly *not* exempted from the watchdog. No migration was added, and none was needed — `qa_reports.check_type` is free-form text — which matches the project's hand-written-migration rule.

All three stories' acceptance criteria are met: configurable 14-day window, four sources, normalized signatures, bounded pre-LLM volume, plan mode with no `epicId`, `qa_reports` persistence reusing the existing QA UI, a journaled no-op, and `create-epics` producing one bug ticket per cluster with mechanically-appended provenance.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The module header states the stop-before-LLM contract, the non-obvious decisions carry their reasoning (the "conservative and deterministic: this is pre-grouping, not semantic diagnosis" note on `normalizeFailureMotif`, the tie-break comment at `collect.ts:620`, the shedding priority at `collect.ts:733`), and the no-op comment in `qa/check/route.ts:125` explains *why* a report row rather than silence.

## 2. DRY

No significant duplication introduced. `create-epics` extends the existing prompt-assembly rather than forking a digest-specific route, and the digest reuses `ReportDetail` unchanged.

- **Suggestion** — `UnifiedActivity` is declared twice (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:16` and `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:10`) and this change had to edit both copies in lockstep. Pre-existing, but the new `"qa"` member is the second time it has had to be mirrored; worth extracting to a shared type.
- The `isE2e ? … : isFailureDigest ? … : …` ladder now appears five times in `create-epics/route.ts:156-211`. A single `CHECK_TYPE_COPY: Record<string, {title, task, typeRule, groupingRule, agentType, epicType}>` lookup would collapse all five and make a fourth check type a one-line addition.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. `resolveOptions` rejects an invalid clock explicitly; every option falls back rather than throwing; `parseTimestamp` returns `null` for unparseable values instead of producing `NaN` comparisons; the no-op path returns a well-formed `{ data }` envelope. The scheduler closure's existing try/catch around `markSessionTerminal` is untouched.

## 4. Performance — **two blocking issues**

### 🔴 Major — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:344` — the last-chunk lookup reads every chunk's full content

```ts
.from(agentSessionChunks)
.where(inArray(agentSessionChunks.sessionId, ids))
.all()
```

`agent_session_chunks` stores the raw CLI stream (`streamType: raw | output | response`). A single long build session is easily thousands of rows and several MB, so 50 eligible sessions in the window can materialise hundreds of MB of JS strings — all to keep one row per session. `better-sqlite3` is synchronous and Arij is single-process, so this runs inside the `POST /qa/check` handler and blocks SSE, polling, and every other route for its duration. It degrades on exactly the projects with enough failure history to want a digest.

The comment says the shape avoids an N+1, but the cure costs more than the disease.

**Recommendation:** two indexed queries — `select({ sessionId, seq: max(sequence) }).from(agentSessionChunks).where(inArray(...)).groupBy(agentSessionChunks.sessionId)`, then fetch `content` only for the winning `(sessionId, sequence)` pairs. Both are served by the existing `agent_session_chunks_session_sequence_unique` index; volume read becomes O(sessions) instead of O(all chunks).

### 🟡 Minor — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:390`, `:488`, `:554` — whole-table scans filtered in JS

All three collectors read a full project-scoped table before rejecting most of it: sessions (including the unbounded `error` and `lastNonEmptyText` columns) before the failed/silent/refused test; every agent ticket comment with full `content` before a `startsWith`; every agent review comment with full `body` before a regex.

All three predicates are pushable: `or(eq(status,"failed"), inArray(outcome, ["silent","transition_refused"]))`; `like(ticketComments.content, FORENSIC_COMMENT_HEADING + "%")`; and since timestamps are ISO-8601 strings, the window is a lexicographic `gte(createdAt, sinceIso)` for the two comment tables. (Sessions need the `endedAt ?? completedAt ?? startedAt ?? createdAt` chain, so a conservative `gte` on `createdAt` plus the existing JS check preserves semantics.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:731` — O(n²) payload sizing

`payloadSize()` re-serialises the whole array on every shed iteration, and one item is shed per iteration — up to ~300 full `JSON.stringify` passes over a 60 KB structure. Correct and bounded, but linear is easy: size each group once, subtract as items are shed, confirm with one final stringify.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `TELESCOPE_*` constants, camelCase functions, `PascalCase` interfaces, `collect.ts` under `lib/telescope/` — all consistent with the codebase. `collectFailureEvidence` as an alias of `collectFailureDigestEvidence` (`collect.ts:805`) is currently unused; if nothing adopts it, drop it rather than carry two public names for one function.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `TelescopeEvidenceSource` is a closed union and `emptySourceCounts()` is `Record<TelescopeEvidenceSource, number>`, so a new source is a compile error rather than an `undefined++`. `isWithinWindow` is a proper type predicate, which is what makes the `occurredAt: sessionTerminalAt(row)!` assertion at `collect.ts:433` sound. `findLastIndex` is fine under `lib: ["esnext"]` and Node ≥20.

Two non-null assertions (`collect.ts:433`, `qa/check/route.ts:170`) are both guarded by control flow immediately above them.

## 7. Testing

Strong coverage: 490 lines of collector tests over window/scope, all four sources, signature normalisation, provider/agentType separation, recurrence filtering, the empty window, and every volume bound including the payload-char budget; plus route tests for plan mode, the no-op, and the full create-epics path through to the epic/story inserts.

Gaps worth closing:

- No test for `create-epics` invoked on a **no-op** digest report (see the Correctness finding below) — the failing path is currently unowned.
- The recurrence tests seed all findings from one review session, so the cross-provider grouping mismatch below is invisible to the suite.
- `__tests__/telescope-collector.test.ts:387` seeds a `status: "resolved"` finding and asserts it *is* collected. That is defensible for a historical digest, but it is an undocumented product decision made by an assertion — worth a comment saying resolved findings still count as evidence that the failure occurred.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. `{ data }` / `{ error }` shapes are consistent, `noOp`/`evidenceCount`/`windowDays` are additive so existing clients keep working, and 200-with-`noOp` is the right code for "handled successfully, nothing to do". The `checkType` parser defaults rather than 400s, matching the pre-existing behaviour.

- **Suggestion** — `qa/check/route.ts:74`: `parseWindowDays` accepts any positive finite number (`0.5` and `1e9` both pass), and `positiveNumber` in the collector has no ceiling either, unlike every other option, which `boundedNonNegativeInteger` clamps. The dialog has `min={1}` but no `max` and no integer coercion. Clamp to e.g. `[1, 365]` and floor, so the `windowDays` echoed in the report header is always what the collector applied.

## Correctness / logic

### 🔴 Major — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:497` — forensic evidence is signed with the diagnostician's dimensions

The `leftJoin` on `ticketComments.agentSessionId` resolves to the session that *wrote* the diagnostic — the forensic agent — so `provider: row.provider` and `agentType: row.agentType ?? "forensic"` describe the diagnostician, not the failure. Two consequences:

1. `agentType` is constant (`forensic`) across the entire source, so one of the three signature dimensions carries zero information for forensic rows.
2. The prompt asks the agent to report "the provider and agent type dimensions" per cluster, so a cluster of claude-code `ticket_build` failures diagnosed by a cheap codex forensic agent is reported to the user as `provider: codex`.

`__tests__/telescope-collector.test.ts:405-411` locks this in: the dead session is claude-code/`ticket_build`, the assertion expects `provider: "codex", agentType: "forensic"`.

The correct dimensions are already in reach — `parseForensicDeadSessionId` is called two lines below to populate `relatedSessionId`. Resolve provider/agentType from the dead session, falling back to the forensic session only when the marker is absent (pre-marker rows), and update the expectation.

*(By contrast, attributing a finding to the review session that filed it — `collect.ts:626` — is defensible: the builder that introduced the code isn't knowable from the finding row.)*

### 🟡 Minor — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:622` — recurrence is decided project-wide, grouping is per provider

`pathCounts`/`prefixCounts` are accumulated across all candidates regardless of who filed them (`:592-607`), but the signature built here adds `provider` and `agentType`. Two `[major]` findings on `lib/auth.ts` filed by different review agents both pass `pathCount >= findingMinOccurrences`, then land in two groups of `count: 1`. The digest shows singleton "recurring" clusters while the agent is explicitly told the frequencies are evidence. Either scope the counters by the grouping key, or drop provider/agentType from the finding signature.

### 🟡 Minor — `create-epics/route.ts:147` — no-op reports reach the epic-generation agent

The empty-window report is written `status: "completed"` with non-empty `reportContent`, so it passes this guard, and `ReportDetail.tsx:361` gates the button on exactly `status === "completed" && Boolean(reportContent)` — Create Epics is offered. Clicking it spawns a full agent run whose only correct answer is `[]`, which then trips `generatedEpics.length === 0` and returns **500 "Failed to parse epics JSON from agent response"**. The user pays for a run and is told parsing failed when nothing was wrong.

Short-circuit on `checkType === "failure_digest" && agentSessionId === null` (the durable marker of the no-op path) with a 200 and zero epics, or hide the button for that case.

### 🟡 Minor — `app/projects/[projectId]/qa/page.tsx:42` — `?reportId=` applies only at mount

Read once in the `useState` initialiser and never cleared. App Router navigations don't remount the page, so back/forward between two `?reportId` values, or a second source link clicked while already on the QA tab, silently keeps the previous selection; the stale param also survives later manual selections, so a refresh snaps back. The primary flow does work — `MarkdownContent` renders links with `target="_blank"`, so the ticket's Source link opens a fresh document — but `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:225-234` already solves this generally: apply in an effect keyed on `searchParams`, then strip via `router.replace`.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:283` — the hash rule over-matches

`\b[0-9a-f]{7,64}\b` with `/i` rewrites any 7+ character word of a–f/0–9 — "defaced", "effaced", "acceded" all become `<hash>` — and swallows 7+ digit decimals (an epoch-ms value becomes `<hash>`, not `<n>`, since it precedes `\b\d+\b`). Neither breaks grouping; both blur motifs that would otherwise stay distinct. Require at least one digit *and* one letter, or raise the minimum for the pure-alpha case.

### ⚪ Suggestion — silent truncation

`trimHead`/`trimTail` (`collect.ts:249-259`) cut without a marker, so the agent cannot distinguish a truncated error from a complete short one — while the collection header does report `truncated` at the payload level. An ellipsis on per-field cuts would make the distinction visible where it matters.

---

## Findings by severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

**Blocking:** the chunk read (`collect.ts:344`) and the forensic signature attribution (`collect.ts:497`). The first can stall or exhaust the single-process orchestrator synchronously inside a request handler, on exactly the projects this feature exists for; the second makes one of the four required evidence sources report the wrong provider and a constant agent type, undermining the signature contract in story 1's acceptance criteria. Both fixes are local and the second has its input (`relatedSessionId`) already parsed.

Everything else is non-blocking. Live validation of the new flow remains pending until merge, as the running orchestrator executes `main` — the test coverage in the worktree is the right substitute and it is thorough.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Telescope-lite : digest périodique des échecs récurrents

**Scope:** `9dce322..c08796d` (5 commits, 27 files, +2385/−51) — `lib/telescope/collect.ts`, `buildFailureDigestPrompt`, `qa/check`, `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics`, `sessions/active`, QA UI, agent-type constants.

This is a re-review. The previous pass returned *Changes Requested* on two blocking issues; commits `85b8798` and `c08796d` address those plus four of the six non-blocking items. `submit_findings` is unavailable in this plan-mode session, so findings are delivered as prose with file+line anchors — the fallback Arij parses.

**Verification run in the worktree:** the 7 epic suites (47/47 pass), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` on all 7 touched source files clean. I also probed `better-sqlite3` directly to confirm the new SQL pushdown's timestamp handling, and measured the prompt's pretty-printed JSON inflation (1.13× — not material, so no finding).

---

## Both blocking issues are fixed

**`collect.ts:337` — the chunk read.** `loadLatestChunks` now runs `MAX(sequence) … GROUP BY session_id`, then fetches `content` only for the winning `(sessionId, sequence)` pairs. Both queries are served by the existing `agent_session_chunks_session_sequence_unique` index, and the 400-session batching keeps the second query's two-parameters-per-session under any SQLite variable ceiling. Raw stream bodies no longer land in memory.

**`collect.ts:580` — forensic attribution.** Forensic evidence now resolves provider/agentType from the dead session named by the durable `arij:dead-session` marker, falling back to the forensic session only for pre-marker rows. `telescope-collector.test.ts:416` inverts the old expectation and asserts `claude-code` / `ticket_build`. `postForensicDiagnostic` always sets `epicId`, so the `innerJoin(epics)` is safe.

Also addressed since the last pass: finding recurrence is now counted in the same `provider + agentType` dimensions as its signature (`collect.ts:699`, plus a dedicated test); the three source filters are pushed into SQLite; truncation is marked with an ellipsis; the hash rule now requires both a digit and a letter (`collect.ts:286`, tested with `"defaced"`); `create-epics` short-circuits empty digests and `ReportDetail` hides the button; `?reportId=` is applied in an effect and consumed via `router.replace`, with tests for both fresh-mount and already-mounted navigation.

I confirmed the pushdown is behaviourally sound rather than assuming it: SQLite's `datetime()` parses both formats present in these columns — `new Date().toISOString()` (what every current writer uses) and the `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` column default — so no legacy rows are silently excluded.

## 1. Readability / 2. DRY / 3. Error Handling / 5. Naming / 6. Type Safety

No blocking issues. Two carry-over suggestions below.

## 4. Performance

The two whole-table reads are gone. Remaining items are suggestions, not defects.

## 7. Testing / 8. API Design

Coverage is strong: 564 lines of collector tests, route tests for plan mode, the no-op, and create-epics through to the epic/story inserts, plus component tests for the digest report and the hidden create button.

---

## Findings

### 🟡 Minor — `qa/check/route.ts:67` and `collect.ts:175` — unbounded `windowDays` produces a silent empty digest

`parseWindowDays` accepts any positive finite number, and `positiveNumber()` is the one collector option that skips `boundedNonNegativeInteger`'s clamp. At `windowDays ≳ 740000` the derived `sinceIso` becomes an expanded-year string (`-271765-12-13T16:41:32.415Z`); I verified against `better-sqlite3` that `datetime()` returns NULL for that form, so every window predicate evaluates to NULL, all three sources return zero rows, and the route writes a *"No eligible recurring failure evidence was found"* report with `noOp: true`. A silent false negative is the worst failure mode for a diagnostics feature. Above `1e9`, `new Date(sinceMs).toISOString()` at `collect.ts:401` throws an unhandled `RangeError` → 500.

This needs an absurd input to hit — the dialog has `min={1}` and no user types 740,000 — which is why it's Minor and not Major. **Recommendation:** clamp to `[1, 365]` and floor in `parseWindowDays`, and add `max` to the dialog input, so the `windowDays` echoed in the report header is always what the collector applied.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:403`, `:490`, `:632` — the read is unbounded even though the payload is bounded

Every cap (`maxGroups`, examples, ticket ids, payload chars) applies *after* the rows are in memory. None of the three source queries carries a `LIMIT`, and the session query still selects the unbounded `error` and `lastNonEmptyText` columns for every eligible row. Story 1's "volume borné avant LLM" is satisfied for what reaches the prompt; a `ORDER BY … LIMIT N` per source would extend that guarantee to the read itself.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:652` — `ltrim()` strips only spaces

The SQL prefilter is `like(lower(ltrim(body)), '[critical]%')`, but the JS side uses `row.body.trim()`. SQLite's one-argument `ltrim` removes U+0020 only, so a finding body starting with a tab or newline now passes the regex but never reaches it. Reachable only via `POST …/review-comments` with `author: "agent"` (that route stores `body.body` verbatim; `submit_findings` always emits a `[severity] ` prefix), so this is narrow — but it's a silent narrowing introduced by the pushdown. `trim(body, char(32)||char(9)||char(10)||char(13))` or a looser `%[critical]%` prefilter would restore parity.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:854` — O(n²) payload sizing

`payloadSize()` re-serialises the whole array on every shed iteration and one item is shed per iteration. Bounded and correct, but linear is easy: size each group once and subtract as items are shed.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:928` — unused alias

`collectFailureEvidence` is still exported and, confirmed by grep, has no callers. Drop it rather than carry two public names for one function. (`loadLatestChunks`'s `wanted` set at `:342` is likewise now vestigial — only `.size === 0` is read.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `qa/page.tsx:61` — `router.replace` scrolls to top

Consuming `?reportId=` triggers a navigation with default scroll behaviour, so selecting the linked report also jumps the page to top. `{ scroll: false }` fixes it.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `create-epics/route.ts:164-219` — the check-type ladder now appears five times

`isE2e ? … : isFailureDigest ? … : …` is repeated for title, task, type rule, grouping rule, and agent type. A single `CHECK_TYPE_COPY: Record<string, {...}>` lookup would collapse all five and make a fourth check type a one-line addition. (Carried over — still worth doing now that a third type exists.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `sessions/active/route.ts:16` + `useAgentPolling.ts:10` — `UnifiedActivity` declared twice

The new `"qa"` member had to be mirrored across both copies. Carried over; worth extracting to a shared type.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `telescope-collector.test.ts:398` — undocumented product decision

The suite seeds a `status: "resolved"` finding and asserts it *is* collected. Defensible for a historical digest, but the decision lives only in an assertion — a comment saying resolved findings still count as evidence that the failure occurred would make it durable.

---

## Integration audit

`failure_digest` is threaded correctly through `AGENT_TYPES`, `AGENT_TYPE_LABELS`, `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`, both session-page label maps, notification routing, the activity monitor (`"qa"` added to both `UnifiedActivity` copies and to `typeIcons`, which already falls back to `Loader2`), and `MCP_EXEMPT_AGENT_TYPES`. Three exclusions I checked explicitly and found correct by construction rather than by omission: `DISPATCH_ROLE_AGENT_TYPES` has a module-load completeness assertion, so the `qa` mapping was mandatory; `AUTO_DISTILL_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` and `DREAM_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` are closed allowlists, so digest sessions cannot feed the memory writers back into themselves; and the watchdog's thresholds are settings-driven with a uniform default, so nothing was needed there. No migration was added and none is required — `qa_reports.check_type` is free-form text.

All three stories' acceptance criteria are met: configurable 14-day window, four sources, normalized signatures, bounded pre-LLM volume, plan mode with no `epicId`, `qa_reports` persistence reusing the existing QA UI, a journaled no-op, and `create-epics` producing one bug ticket per cluster with mechanically-appended provenance.

## Findings by severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 1 |
| Suggestion | 7 |

Nothing here blocks. The one Minor is an input-validation gap with an unpleasant failure mode but an unreachable trigger in practice; the rest are cleanups. Live validation of the new flow remains pending until merge, since the running orchestrator executes `main` — the worktree test coverage is the right substitute and it is thorough.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**
