### Step 1 — Server-side routing in /api/chat/stream
- Modify the chat stream endpoint to check the conversation's `type` field
- When type is `epic_creation`, use the epic refinement prompt builder (existing `buildSpecPrompt` or a new `buildEpicCreationPrompt`) instead of the default brainstorm prompt
- Ensure the prompt includes project context (spec, documents) and instructs Claude to help the user define an epic with user stories

### Step 2 — New useEpicCreate hook
- Create a small React hook (`useEpicCreate`) that takes the conversation context and calls the API to create an epic with generated user stories
- The hook calls `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/epics` with the epic data extracted from the conversation
- Returns loading/error/success states

### Step 3 — UnifiedChatPanel UI updates
- Add a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button that appears in `epic_creation` conversations once enough context has been discussed
- Differentiate tab icons: sparkles icon for `epic_creation` tabs vs message icon for regular chat tabs
- Add an empty-state hint in new `epic_creation` tabs explaining what the user can do
- Wire `onEpicCreated` callback to refresh the kanban board and optionally close the tab

### Step 4 — MessageInput placeholder
- Add a `placeholder` prop to the MessageInput component
- Set context-aware placeholder text: 'Describe your epic idea...' for epic_creation tabs, 'Ask a question...' for brainstorm tabs

### Step 5 — Rewire page.tsx
- Point the 'New Epic' button in the project page to `panelRef.current?.openNewEpic()` which creates a new `epic_creation` tab
- Remove the old modal/sheet import and rendering

### Step 6 — Delete dead code
- Remove `CreateEpicSheet.tsx` component
- Remove `useEpicCreation.ts` hook
- Clean up any unused imports

epics.title: Agent Configuration Side Panel & Custom Review Agents
epics.description:
Dedicated side panel for configuring agent prompts (global + per-project override), creating custom review agents, and setting the default AI provider per agent type.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer

**Agent Prompts Table:**
- Add `agentPrompts` table: id, agentType (text: 'build', 'review_security', 'review_code', 'review_compliance', 'chat', 'spec_generation', 'team_build', 'ticket_build'), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Global prompts have scope='global', project overrides store the projectId
- When resolving a prompt, project-scoped prompt takes precedence over global, which takes precedence over built-in defaults

**Custom Review Agents Table:**
- Add `customReviewAgents` table: id, name (text), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), position (integer), isEnabled (integer, default 1), createdAt, updatedAt
- Custom review agents are user-defined and appear alongside the 3 built-in review types

**Agent Provider Defaults Table:**
- Add `agentProviderDefaults` table: id, agentType (text), provider ('claude-code' | 'codex'), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Allows setting CC or Codex as default per agent type, with project override

### Phase 2 — API Routes

**Agent Prompts:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/prompts` — list all global agent prompts
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts` — list project-scoped prompts (merged with global defaults)
- `PUT /api/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert global prompt for an agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert project override
- `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — remove project override (fall back to global)

**Custom Review Agents:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/review-agents` — list global custom review agents
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — list project-scoped + global review agents
- `POST /api/agent-config/review-agents` — create a custom review agent (global)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — create project-scoped review agent
- `PATCH /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — update name, prompt, enabled status
- `DELETE /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — delete a custom review agent

**Agent Provider Defaults:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/providers` — list global provider defaults per agent type
- `PUT /api/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set global default provider for agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set project override

### Phase 3 — Prompt Builder Integration
- Refactor all prompt builder functions to load custom prompts from DB before composing
- Resolution order: project override → global custom → built-in default
- Update `buildReviewPrompt` to accept custom review agent prompts in addition to built-in types
- Update `buildBuildPrompt`, `buildChatPrompt`, `buildSpecPrompt`, `buildTeamBuildPrompt`, `buildTicketBuildPrompt` to use configurable prompts

### Phase 4 — Side Panel UI
- New `AgentConfigPanel` component accessible from the main sidebar
- Three tabs: **Agent Prompts**, **Review Agents**, **Provider Defaults**
- Agent Prompts tab: list of agent types with expandable prompt editors, toggle between global/project scope
- Review Agents tab: list of built-in (read-only name) + custom review agents, each with name/prompt fields, add/delete actions
- Provider Defaults tab: per-agent-type dropdown to select CC or Codex as default
- Panel slides in from the left sidebar, can be toggled open/closed

### Phase 5 — Review Dialog Integration
- Update the Agent Review dialog on the story detail page to include custom review agents alongside the 3 built-in types
- Custom agents displayed as additional checkboxes with their name
- Each selected custom agent dispatches a plan-mode agent with the custom prompt
- Agent output posted as a comment with the custom agent's name as label

### Step 5 — Rewire page.tsx

epics.title: Agent Teams & Codex Provider Integration
epics.description:
Two-part feature: (1) Agent Teams mode that leverages Claude Code's native Task tool to delegate multiple tickets to sub-agents in a single session, and (2) OpenAI Codex integration as an alternative AI provider alongside Claude Code.

## Implementation Plan

### Part A — Agent Teams (Claude Code Only)

**Schema & Data Layer:**
- Add `orchestrationMode` column to `agentSessions` table (`'solo' | 'team'`, default `'solo'`)
- Team mode is exclusive to Claude Code (Codex has no equivalent sub-agent delegation)

**Prompt Builder:**
- New `buildTeamBuildPrompt()` function that describes all selected epics with their worktree paths
- Instructs Claude Code to act as a team lead and use the `Task` tool to spawn sub-agents per ticket
- Lets CC decide team composition and size

**Build Route Changes:**
- When `team=true` in the batch build request, pre-create all git worktrees for selected epics
- Spawn a single CC session from the main repo root (not inside a worktree)
- Add `Task` to the `--allowedTools` list for team mode
- Track as a single `agentSession` with `orchestrationMode: 'team'`
- On completion, update all associated epics' statuses

**UI — Build Toolbar:**
- Add 'Team mode' checkbox in the build toolbar, visible when 2+ epics are selected
- Checkbox disabled when fewer than 2 epics selected or when provider is Codex
- Tooltip explains team mode behavior

### Part B — Codex Provider Integration

**Provider Abstraction Layer:**
- New `lib/providers/` directory with provider interface (`AgentProvider`)
- `lib/providers/claude-code.ts` — wraps existing CC spawn logic
- `lib/providers/codex.ts` — wraps `@openai/codex-sdk` using `Codex` class, `startThread()`, `runStreamed()` for streaming events
- `lib/providers/index.ts` — factory function `getProvider(type: 'claude-code' | 'codex')`
- Codex provider uses `workingDirectory` option on `startThread()` for worktree paths

**Schema Changes:**
- Add `provider` column to `agentSessions` (`'claude-code' | 'codex'`, default `'claude-code'`)
- Add `provider` column to `chatConversations` (if table exists) or chat messages

**Process Manager Generalization:**
- Refactor `lib/claude/process-manager.ts` to accept provider-agnostic session handles
- Codex sessions tracked via thread ID, CC sessions tracked via PID
- Unified start/cancel/status interface

**Build & Review Routes:**
- Build route accepts `provider` parameter, dispatches via provider factory
- Review route accepts `provider` parameter
- Send-to-dev route accepts `provider` parameter

**UI — Provider Selector:**
- Dropdown in build toolbar to choose between Claude Code and Codex
- Provider selector in Send to Dev dialog
- Provider selector in Agent Review dialog
- Provider toggle in chat header (locked/disabled after first message in conversation)
- Codex option disabled with tooltip if no API key configured

**Settings:**
- Add Codex API key field to Settings page
- Stored in `settings` table with key `codex_api_key`
- Validated on save (non-empty string check)

**Codex SDK Integration Details:**
- Install `@openai/codex-sdk` dependency
- Use `new Codex({ env: { CODEX_API_KEY: ... } })` with API key from settings
- `startThread({ workingDirectory })` for worktree-scoped execution
- `runStreamed()` for streaming events, map to unified event format
- Thread IDs stored in session metadata for resumption support

epics.title: Ticket Comments, Send-to-Dev & Agent Review
epics.description:
Add a comment system to user stories (tickets), a dedicated story detail page replacing the sheet, and review workflows powered by Claude Code agents.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer
- Add `ticketComments` table (id, userStoryId, author: 'user'|'agent', content, agentSessionId?, createdAt)
- Add `userStoryId` column to `agentSessions` to link agent work back to a specific ticket
- Add `"review"` as a valid status for user stories (todo → in_progress → review → done)

### Phase 2 — API Routes
- `GET/PATCH /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]` — fetch & update story detail
- `GET/POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/comments` — list & add comments
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/build` — dispatch a code-mode agent for the ticket (send-to-dev)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/review` — dispatch review agents (security, code-review, compliance/accessibility)

### Phase 3 — Hooks
- `useStoryDetail` — fetch story with epic context
- `useComments` — fetch comments with 5s polling
- `useTicketAgent` — dispatch agent + poll session status, auto-post final output as agent comment

### Phase 4 — Story Detail Page
- New route: `/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]`
- Two-column layout: left = story details (title, description, acceptance criteria, status, priority), right = comment thread
- Navigate to this page by clicking story titles in the epic detail view

### Phase 5 — Send to Dev
- Available on tickets in `todo` or `in_progress` status
- "Send to Dev" button opens a dialog with an optional comment field
- On confirm: post comment (if provided), dispatch code-mode agent with ticket context + full comment history, move ticket to `in_progress`
- Agent reuses the epic's existing git worktree/branch with concurrency guard

### Phase 6 — Agent Review (Review status)
- Available on tickets in `review` status
- "Send to Dev" button (requires mandatory comment explaining what to fix) → dispatches code agent, moves ticket back to `in_progress`
- "Agent Review" button opens dialog with 3 checkboxes: Security, Code Review, Compliance/Accessibility
- Each selected review type dispatches a separate agent in plan mode with a specialized review checklist
- Agent outputs are posted as comments on the ticket

### Phase 7 — Approve & Merge
- "Approve" action on review-status tickets marks the ticket as `done`
- Triggers merge of the epic's worktree branch into the target branch

### Prompt Builder
- `buildTicketBuildPrompt` — code mode, includes project spec, epic context, ticket details, and full comment history
- `buildReviewPrompt` — plan mode, 3 specialized checklists (security audit, code review best practices, compliance/accessibility standards)

epics.title: Chat Image Upload & Clipboard Paste
epics.description:
Add image support to chat panels — users can upload images via a file picker or paste them from the clipboard. Images are saved locally, displayed as thumbnails before sending, and rendered inline in chat messages.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Storage & Schema
- Create `data/uploads/` directory for storing chat image files (gitignored)
- Add `chatAttachments` table to Drizzle schema (id, chatMessageId FK, fileName, filePath, mimeType, sizeBytes, createdAt)
- Add cascade delete from chatMessages to chatAttachments
- Generate and push migration

### Phase 2 — Upload API
- Create `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/upload` route
- Accept multipart form data with image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp)
- Validate file type and size (max 10MB per file)
- Save files to `data/uploads/{projectId}/{nanoid}-{originalName}`
- Return attachment metadata (id, fileName, filePath, mimeType)
- Create `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]` to serve images

### Phase 3 — Enhanced MessageInput Component
- Add paste event handler on the textarea to intercept `clipboardData.items` with `type.startsWith('image/')`
- Convert pasted image blobs to File objects and upload immediately
- Add image upload button (paperclip/image icon) next to the send button
- Hidden file input accepting image MIME types, triggered by the button
- Display pending image thumbnails in a preview strip above the textarea
- Allow removing individual thumbnails before sending
- On send, include attachment IDs alongside the message content

### Phase 4 — Message Rendering
- Update MessageList / MarkdownContent to detect and render images associated with messages
- Fetch attachments for each message and display them as inline images below the text
- Support lightbox/modal view on image click for full-size viewing
- Lazy-load images with placeholder skeleton

### Phase 5 — Chat API Integration
- Update `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to accept an optional `attachmentIds` array
- Link uploaded attachments to the created message
- Update `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to include attachment metadata in response
- Ensure attachments are cleaned up when messages are deleted (cascade)

epics.title: Pipeline : étage `verify` déterministe (tests/lint/build exécutés par Arij)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Arij ne vérifie jamais programmatiquement le travail des agents : « run the tests and commit » n'existe que comme consigne de prose dans les prompts (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts`). Le pipeline autonome (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts` + `lib/pipeline/stages.ts`) enchaîne build → review → fix sans aucune étape déterministe : un ticket passe en `review` sur la seule foi de l'agent. Enseignement central de Code with Claude 2026 : la vérification est le goulot, pas l'écriture du code.

## À construire
1. **Settings** : `verify_commands` (JSON, tableau de `{ name, command }`, ex. `[{"name":"test","command":"npm test"},{"name":"lint","command":"npm run lint"}]`) et `verify_timeout_ms` (défaut 600000), résolus en tri-state projet → global → défaut comme les autres clés (voir `lib/settings/`). Constantes dans un fichier `verify-constants.ts` client-safe (convention du repo). Clé absente = verify désactivé, aucun changement de comportement.
2. **Runner** `lib/verify/runner.ts` : exécute chaque commande séquentiellement dans le worktree de l'epic (`cwd = worktreePath`), capture stdout/stderr borné (~64 Ko par commande, garder la FIN de la sortie), exit code, durée. Timeout dur par commande avec kill du process group (SIGTERM puis SIGKILL, même échelle que `lib/providers/base-provider.ts`). Zéro LLM dans ce module. Arrêt à la première commande en échec.
3. **Persistance** : nouvelle table `verify_reports` (id, projectId, epicId, agentSessionId nullable, status pass|fail, startedAt, finishedAt, `commands` JSON `[{name, command, exitCode, durationMs, tail}]`). Migration SQL écrite à la main : fichier numéroté dans `lib/db/migrations/` + entrée ajoutée dans `meta/_journal.json` (ne JAMAIS lancer `drizzle-kit generate`, cf. CLAUDE.md — les snapshots sont figés à 0013).
4. **Câblage pipeline** (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`) : après un stage build réussi (outcome `answered`) et avant le stage review, exécuter verify si configuré. Échec → consommer un fix cycle existant (`pipeline_max_fix_cycles`) avec un prompt de fix enrichi du tail de la sortie d'erreur (nouvelle section dans `prompt-builder.ts`) ; succès → injecter un résumé une-ligne-par-commande dans le prompt du reviewer. Le run verify n'est PAS une session agent : il ne compte ni dans le plafond de 12 sessions/run ni dans les budgets ; il est journalisé dans `ticket_activity_log` (actor `system`).
5. **Déclenchement manuel** : `POST /api/projects/:projectId/epics/:epicId/verify` (réponse d'erreur lisible si aucun worktree), et affichage du dernier rapport dans le détail du ticket (statut par commande + tail dépliable).

## Contraintes
- N'exécuter que dans le worktree de l'epic, jamais dans le repo principal ni sur main.
- Les commandes viennent exclusivement des settings (saisies par l'humain) — un agent ne doit jamais pouvoir écrire `verify_commands`.
- Full Auto et night run héritent du comportement via le pipeline : aucune logique spécifique chez eux.
- Tests vitest : runner (child_process mocké : succès, échec, timeout, troncature) et câblage stages (échec → fix cycle, succès → review, non configuré → passthrough bit-à-bit identique).

## Hors scope
La règle « test de régression obligatoire pour les bugs » — ticket séparé qui dépend de celui-ci.

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe

**Scope:** `269e399..96acc8c` (4 commits, 24 files, +2674/−8), covering all four user stories.

## Summary of what was built

The epic is implemented end to end and the architecture is sound: a client-safe constants module, a tri-state resolver over SQLite, an LLM-free sequential runner with byte-bounded output capture and process-group kill escalation, a hand-written migration (`0033`, journal `idx: 32`, `when` strictly increasing — no `drizzle-kit generate`), pipeline wiring that consumes the *existing* fix-cycle budget without touching the 12-session ceiling, `actor: "system"` activity traces, a manual `GET`/`POST` route with worktree containment, and an `EpicDetail` panel. The passthrough path is proven bit-identical by comparing two harness runs' `requests`/`traces`/`summary` — a genuinely strong test.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. Comments explain *why* (the `detached`/negative-pid rationale at `lib/verify/runner.ts:66-71`, the "empty array is deliberately valid" note at `verify-constants.ts:112-118`, the "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" contract at `runner.ts:27`) rather than restating the code. Naming is precise and consistent with the surrounding pipeline vocabulary.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:177`** — `resolveVerifyConfig` is a complete second implementation of the precedence logic in `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` (`lib/verify/config.ts:24`), and it has **no production caller** — `grep` finds it only in `__tests__/verify-settings.test.ts`. The "client-safe resolver" rationale in its doc comment never pays off because no client consumes it (see finding 8.1).
*Recommendation:* either wire it into the settings UI or delete it and keep one resolver.

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:35`** — `parseCommandResults` re-implements, field for field, the per-command validation already in `isVerificationReport` (`verify-constants.ts:63-73`).
*Recommendation:* export an `isVerifyCommandResult` predicate from `verify-constants.ts` and call it from both.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:161` and `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:266`** — nothing serialises verification against concurrent work in the same worktree. The POST route runs regardless of whether a build, fix, review or Full Auto merge-fix session is live on that epic, and neither call site takes a per-worktree lock.
*Failure scenario:* a night run's pipeline is executing `npm run build` in epic E's worktree when the user opens the ticket and clicks **Run verification**. Two `next build` processes write `.next/` in the same directory; both reports are garbage, and the pipeline consumes a fix cycle — dispatching a real agent — against a phantom failure. Same class of corruption when the manual run races an agent that is mid-edit.
*Recommendation:* the ingredients already exist — `getRunningSessionForTarget` is imported at `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:15`; use it to refuse the POST with a 409 while a session owns the epic, and add an in-process per-worktree mutex around `runVerification` so pipeline and manual runs cannot interleave.

**Minor — `lib/verify/runner.ts:148`** — `runCommand` resolves only on `close`, which requires both process exit *and* every inherited stdio pipe closing. A descendant that escapes the group kill (`setsid`) while holding stdout leaves the promise pending forever: after SIGKILL there is no absolute deadline. `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:556` awaits this inline, and the stalled-session watchdog cannot help because a verify run is deliberately not an agent session — so the pipeline run stalls with no terminal state and no notification.
*Recommendation:* after the SIGKILL escalation, arm one final timer that calls `finish(null)` unconditionally (or settle on `exit` with a bounded grace for `close`).

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:196`** — with an empty `commands` array, `commandResults.length === input.commands.length` holds and `[].every(...)` is `true`, so the function persists a `status: "pass"` report having executed nothing. Both current callers pre-check `config.enabled`, so it is unreachable today, but `runVerification` is exported and the whole point of the table is that a `pass` row means something was mechanically proven.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:52`** — the verify `GET` was added to `fetchData`, which is also the 5-second poll callback (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:98`). Each tick re-downloads the full report, whose `commands` blob carries up to 64 KiB of `tail` **per command** (`VERIFY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES`). A two-command config means ~128 KiB every 5 s for a payload that changes only when a run finishes.
*Recommendation:* serve tails lazily (`?tails=1`, or a per-command endpoint), or refetch the report on the `ticket:updated` event and after a manual run instead of on every tick.

Otherwise fine: the `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` index matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, and `OutputTail` is correctly O(limit) rather than accumulating unbounded output.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify_reports` / `verifyReports`, `verify-constants.ts` (mirrors the existing `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention), `VerificationReportSection.tsx` under `components/kanban/epic-detail/` — all consistent.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommandResult`/`VerificationReport` are shared across server, route and client from one client-safe module; the `PromptVerificationCommand` structural projection in `prompt-builder.ts` correctly avoids dragging a server type into the prompt layer.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:132`** — the two highest-consequence new branches have no coverage:
- exhaustion (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:589-611`) — emits `failedDeterministicVerification`, calls `parkRejectedTicket` to pull the ticket back out of Review, and terminates the run;
- crash (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`) — same park + terminate on any throw from the driver, including the two `throw`s in `runPipelineVerification` (`stages.ts:246`, `stages.ts:261`).

`grep` confirms no test references `failedDeterministicVerification` or either park reason. The suite covers pass / fail→fix→pass / disabled, which is the happy topology; the paths that move a ticket backwards are the ones a regression would hurt most. Also untested: the "not configured" 409 in `POST` (`route.ts:150-159`) and the runner's spawn-error branch (`runner.ts:140-143`).

Positives worth noting: the `maxSessions: 2` test is exactly the right way to prove the session-ceiling criterion, and the disabled-path equality assertion is stronger than the acceptance criterion asked for.

## 8. API Design

**Major — `lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:177` / `app/settings/page.tsx`** — there is no way for a user to configure `verify_commands` or `verify_timeout_ms` anywhere in the product. `app/settings/page.tsx` imports `@/lib/verify/regression-constants` (the sibling epic wired `BUG_REGRESSION_COMMAND_SETTING_KEY` and `TEST_FILE_PATTERNS_SETTING_KEY` into it at lines 28-30/329-366), but nothing from `verify-constants.ts`; `grep` for the verify keys across `app/` and `components/` returns only `lib/` and tests.
*Failure scenario:* a user opens a ticket, sees the new **Verification** panel, clicks **Run verification**, and gets `409 "Verification is not configured for this project. Add at least one verify command in Settings."` — pointing at a Settings page with no such field. The only way to enable the epic's entire feature is to hand-craft a `PATCH /api/settings` call or edit SQLite. Meanwhile the pipeline stage sits permanently on the disabled passthrough path, and `resolveVerifyConfig` — the client resolver written for precisely this UI — stays dead.
I acknowledge story 1's literal acceptance criteria are all about resolution semantics and say nothing about a control, so this may have been consciously deferred. But the epic states the commands are "saisies par l'humain", and as shipped no human can enter them, which makes stories 2–4 unreachable in the product.
*Recommendation:* add the two controls to `app/settings/page.tsx` mirroring the regression-command/test-patterns block, reusing `parseVerifyCommands`, `parseVerifyTimeoutMs` and `resolveVerifyConfig`. If the UI is genuinely a follow-up ticket, then hide `VerificationReportSection` when no commands resolve, so the product does not advertise a button that cannot work.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:260`** — the pipeline path trusts `agentSessions.worktreePath` verbatim, while the manual route validates the same value with `containsPathOnDisk(candidate, worktreesRootFor(repoPath))` (`route.ts:90-102`). The epic's hard constraint — never execute in the main checkout or on `main` — is therefore enforced at one of the two call sites. Sessions carrying `worktreePath = project.gitRepoPath` do exist (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/git/pull/route.ts:170`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/releases/route.ts:228`); they happen to have no `epicId`, so the `projectId + epicId + sessionId` lookup cannot reach them today — but the invariant rests on that accident rather than on a check.
*Recommendation:* lift the containment check out of the route into `lib/verify/` and apply it in `runPipelineVerification` too.

Otherwise the REST shape is correct: `{ data }` / `{ error }`, 404 via the shared `getProjectOr404`/`getEpicOr404` helpers, 409 for both "no worktree" and "not configured", `errorResponse` for 500, and `emitTicketUpdated` reused instead of inventing a verify-only SSE event that every consumer would have to learn.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 1 |

**Major:** (1) verification has no configuration surface, so the feature cannot be enabled from the product and its own UI button always 409s; (2) no mutual exclusion — a manual run can race a live agent session or a pipeline verify run in the same worktree and produce corrupt mechanical "evidence" that then spends a real fix cycle.

Both are fixable within the existing code (`app/settings/page.tsx` already has the pattern to copy; `getRunningSessionForTarget` is already imported in `stages.ts`). The core engineering — the runner, the tri-state resolution, the migration, the passthrough-identity proof, and the session-ceiling isolation — is solid and I'd approve it on its own.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I did not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and no finding rows exist to block approval. The two Major items need to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe (re-review)

## Summary of what changed since the last review

`920602e` added the **Deterministic verification** card to global Settings (JSON command list + per-command timeout), wired through the same client-safe parsers, and made `resolveVerifyConfig` a shared resolver instead of dead code — closing prior Major #1. `f81a7e9` added `lib/verify/worktree.ts` (containment enforced at *both* call sites now, not just the route), `lib/verify/execution-lock.ts` (per-worktree serialisation), and an agent-active 409 in the POST route — closing prior Major #2. Prior Minors #2 (duplicate command validation), #3 (`close`-only settle), #4 (poll payload) and the empty-commands suggestion were not addressed.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comments carry the *why*: the negative-pid rationale (`lib/verify/runner.ts:70-71`), "empty array is deliberately valid" (`lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:112-118`), "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" (`lib/verify/runner.ts:27`), and the lock's fail-fast-vs-queue split (`lib/verify/execution-lock.ts:3-10`). `verificationOutputFence` (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:113`) and the "untrusted command output" framing in the fix section are a thoughtful touch — agent-visible output is fenced so a failing test's stdout can't impersonate instructions.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:35`** — `parseCommandResults` still re-implements, field for field, the per-command validation in `isVerificationReport` (`lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:63-73`). Unchanged since the last review. The two copies also disagree semantically: the route silently drops malformed entries and returns a partial report, while the client predicate rejects the whole report — so a half-corrupt row renders as a *shorter* passing report instead of an error.
*Recommendation:* export an `isVerifyCommandResult` predicate from `verify-constants.ts` and call it from both.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `lib/verify/runner.ts:148`** — `runCommand` settles only on `close` (or `error`). The timeout path at `:150-158` *only signals*; it never settles the promise. `close` requires both process exit **and** every inherited stdio pipe closing, so any descendant that outlives the process group while holding stdout leaves the promise pending forever — and the timeout cannot rescue it, because the timeout has no terminal settle of its own.

I reproduced both halves of this against the exact spawn options the runner uses (`shell: true, detached, stdio: ["ignore","pipe","pipe"]`):

```
# escapee + group kill (the timeout path)
exit fired at 1001 ms
SIGKILL err ESRCH
after group SIGKILL -> exited: true  closed: false   <-- never settles

# clean exit, background descendant holding stdout
stdout: "done\n"
exit 0 at 3 ms
still not closed after 4s
CLOSE 0 at 8006 ms                                   <-- settle deferred to the descendant
```

*Failure scenario:* a project configures `{"name":"e2e","command":"npm run test:e2e"}`. A run leaves a stray dev server / watcher / `setsid` descendant holding the inherited pipe. `runCommand` never resolves → `runVerification` never returns → and because `f81a7e9` now wraps both call sites in `withVerificationWorktreeLock`, the `finally` at `execution-lock.ts:49-52` never runs. The lock key is poisoned for the lifetime of the server process: the pipeline (`wait` defaulted to true) queues behind it **forever** on every subsequent run for that epic, and the manual POST (`wait: false`) returns 409 forever. The originating pipeline run has no terminal state, emits no notification, and the stalled-session watchdog cannot see it because a verify run is deliberately not an agent session. On Windows this is not a corner case but the guaranteed timeout behaviour: `detached` is false, so `signalProcessGroup` falls through to `child.kill()`, which reaches only `cmd.exe` while the grandchild keeps the pipes open.

The lock is the right fix for the concurrency Major — it just converted a single hung command into a permanent per-worktree deadlock, which is why I'm raising this from the Minor it was last time.

*Recommendation:* give `finish` an unconditional deadline. Simplest form: settle on `exit` with a short grace window for `close` to flush, and arm one final `setTimeout(() => finish(null), VERIFY_KILL_GRACE_MS)` when escalating to SIGKILL. Secondary benefit: `durationMs` is currently measured to `close` (8 006 ms in the trace above for a command that exited in 3 ms), so the persisted duration is wrong whenever a descendant lingers.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:248, 264, 275, 277`** — `runPipelineVerification` throws on every *applicability* fault (no code session, no recorded worktree, no `gitRepoPath`, non-managed path), and the runner's crash handler (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`) responds by calling `parkRejectedTicket` — pulling the ticket back out of Review — and terminating the run as `failed`. The sibling regression gate deliberately does the opposite and documents why at `lib/pipeline/verify.ts:179-185`: *"the gate is TOTAL: a transient database error must resolve to 'did not apply', never to a thrown gate. The runner's crash path would otherwise fail the run and park a ticket … for a fault that says nothing about the branch."*
*Failure scenario:* the most reachable one is inside `runVerification` itself — all commands pass, then `database.insert(verifyReports).values(...).run()` (`lib/verify/runner.ts:207-213`) throws (FK, disk, lock). The exception propagates into the crash path, so a fully green branch is parked back to `in_progress` and the run is reported failed, with the only diagnostic a `console.warn`.
*Recommendation:* mirror the gate's split — wrap the applicability reads and the persistence in a total path that returns `{ ran: false }`, and reserve the crash/park path for "commands ran and told us something".

**Minor — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:142` vs `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` stage dispatch** — the new exclusion covers verification-vs-verification only. The agent-active check at `:142` is a point-in-time read, and nothing on the dispatch side consults the verification lock. A manual run started while the epic is idle can therefore overlap a fix or review agent that the pipeline dispatches into the same worktree seconds later. The blast radius is now much smaller than before (a misleading manual report, not a spent fix cycle), which is why this is Minor rather than a repeat Major.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:196-200`** — with an empty `commands` array, `[].every(...)` is `true`, so the function persists `status: "pass"` having executed nothing. Both callers pre-check `config.enabled`, so it's unreachable today, but `runVerification` is exported and the point of the table is that a `pass` row means something was mechanically proven.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:133`** — `env: process.env` inherits the Arij server's environment, including `NODE_ENV`. This epic's own comment history records a `npm run build` failing under an inherited non-standard `NODE_ENV` and passing under `env -u NODE_ENV`. A `build` verify command run from the dev server will inherit `NODE_ENV=development`. Worth either scrubbing `NODE_ENV` or documenting it next to the Settings field.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:57`** — the verify `GET` was added to `fetchData`, which is also the 5-second poll callback (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:99`). Each tick re-downloads the full report, whose `commands` blob carries up to `VERIFY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES` (64 KiB) of `tail` **per command**. Polling is gated on `isRunning` (`components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:221`), so this is bounded to "an agent is working on this ticket and the panel is open" — but that is exactly the window a user watches. Unchanged since the last review.
There is also a small ordering race: a poll `GET` issued before a manual run finishes can resolve *after* `onReportChange`, reverting the panel to the stale report for one tick.
*Recommendation:* serve tails lazily (`?tails=1` or a per-command endpoint), or refetch on `ticket:updated` plus after a manual run rather than every tick.

Otherwise sound: `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `OutputTail` is O(limit) rather than accumulating, and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` fetches all four keys in one `inArray` read.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify-constants.ts` mirrors the existing `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention, `verify_reports` / `verifyReports` follow the schema's snake/camel split, and `VerificationReportSection.tsx` sits with its siblings under `components/kanban/epic-detail/`.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommand` / `VerifyCommandResult` / `VerificationReport` are shared from one client-safe module across server, route and client; `PromptVerificationCommand` is a structural projection that keeps a server type out of the prompt layer. `VerifyConfig.enabled` being *derived* from `commands.length` rather than stored is the right call — it makes "configured but empty" unrepresentable.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:132`** — the two branches that move a ticket *backwards* remain the only uncovered ones, unchanged since the last review. `grep` finds no test referencing `failedDeterministicVerification`, `failedDeterministicVerificationCrashed`, or a `parkRejectedTicket` spy in this file (the harness at `:62-127` never passes one):
- exhaustion — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:589-611`: park + terminate;
- crash — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`: park + terminate on any throw from the driver, including the four `throw`s at `stages.ts:248/264/275/277`.

Also untested: the "not configured" 409 in `POST` (`route.ts:170-179`) and the runner's spawn-error branch (`runner.ts:140-143`).

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:460-462`** — `handleStageFailure` now forwards `currentRequest.verifyFailure` to retried stages; before this branch it forwarded nothing (confirmed against the merge-base). That changes the *regression gate's* retried-fix prompt for bug tickets even when `verify_commands` is unset, so "verify non configuré → comportement strictement identique" holds only for projects without the regression gate enabled. The new behaviour is almost certainly the better one — a retried fix should keep its failure context — but it is an undeclared, untested change to a neighbouring feature riding inside a commit that claims strict passthrough.
*Recommendation:* add a retry-carries-`verifyFailure` case to `__tests__/pipeline-regression-gate.test.ts`, or split the line out of this epic.

Positives worth keeping: the disabled-path test comparing two full harness runs' `requests`/`traces`/`summary` (`:133-148`) is a stronger proof than the acceptance criterion asked for; `maxSessions: 2` (`:189`) is exactly the right way to prove the session-ceiling criterion; and `pipeline-stages-dispatch.test.ts` now proves the driver *refuses* a session-recorded main checkout, which is the epic's hard constraint tested rather than assumed.

## 8. API Design

No blocking issues. `{ data }` / `{ error }` throughout, `getProjectOr404` / `getEpicOr404` for 404s, 409 for all three refusal modes (no worktree, agent active, not configured) with the standard `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload` shape reused for the agent case, `errorResponse` for 500, and `emitTicketUpdated` reused instead of a verify-only SSE event.

One design note, not a defect: the Settings card writes the **global** keys only. Per-project overrides are resolvable (`verifyCommandsSettingKey`) and are cleaned up on project delete (`lib/projects/project-settings-keys.ts:40-41`), but a user cannot set them from the UI — so a single global command list applies to every project until someone hand-crafts a PATCH. That matches how `bug_regression_command` behaves today, so it's consistent, and the story's criteria are about resolution semantics; worth a follow-up ticket rather than a change here.

Also correct and worth calling out: `POST` never creates a worktree and never falls back to `gitRepoPath`, `findExistingWorktree` walks older sessions when a recorded worktree has been pruned, and `verify_commands` is reachable only through `/api/settings` — no MCP tool can write it, satisfying the "saisies par l'humain" constraint.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The two Majors from the previous review are properly closed, and the additions in `f81a7e9` are the right shape — containment lifted into `lib/verify/worktree.ts` and applied at both call sites, a process-local lock rather than a lock file. The one blocker is that the lock exposed a pre-existing gap: `runCommand` has no unconditional settle, so a hung command now permanently poisons its worktree's lock and strands the pipeline run with no terminal state. I reproduced it above; the fix is a few lines in `lib/verify/runner.ts`. Everything else here I would approve.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I could not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — no finding rows exist to block approval, and the Major needs to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe (third pass)

**Scope:** `269e399..715a8b8` — 7 commits, 32 files, +3443/−14, covering all four user stories.

Verification I ran myself in this worktree: the 12 touched test files pass (**347 tests**), `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean, ESLint on every changed `.ts`/`.tsx` file is clean, `git diff --check` is clean, and the worktree has no uncommitted changes. The comment history's claims hold.

The two Majors from review #1 (no Settings surface; no worktree exclusion) and the Major from review #2 (`runCommand` had no unconditional settle, poisoning the lock) are all genuinely closed. I re-read `lib/verify/runner.ts:169-199`: `exit` now arms a bounded close-grace, the SIGKILL escalation arms an absolute deadline, and `durationMs` is measured at exit — the deadlock is gone, and both halves are covered by tests at `__tests__/verify-runner.test.ts:219` and `:243`.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comments carry the *why* consistently: the negative-pid rationale (`lib/verify/runner.ts:85-86`), the close-grace rationale (`runner.ts:20-26`), "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" (`runner.ts:42`), "empty array is deliberately valid" (`verify-constants.ts:119-125`), the lock's fail-fast-vs-queue split (`execution-lock.ts:3-10`), and the totality argument in `runPipelineVerification` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:237-244`) that cites its own precedent. `verificationOutputFence` + the "untrusted command output" framing (`prompt-builder.ts:112-118`, `:148`) is the right instinct — a failing test's stdout can't impersonate instructions.

## 2. DRY Principle

No blocking issues. `isVerifyCommandResult` is now exported once from `verify-constants.ts:46` and consumed by both the route parser and the report guard, closing the prior duplicate. `resolveVerifyConfig` is a single resolver shared by the Settings UI and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject`. See the Suggestion in §3 for the one behavioural difference that survived the deduplication.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:117-123`** — the comment claims *"Pipeline and manual runs announce finished reports via `ticket:updated`"*. Only the manual run does. `grep` for `emitTicketUpdated` across `lib/` and `app/` returns exactly two production call sites: the epic `PATCH` route (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/route.ts:76`) and the new verify `POST` (`verify/route.ts:203`). The pipeline path never emits it — `runPipelineVerification` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:245-315`) emits nothing, and the pipeline's own `trace()` (`lib/pipeline/index.ts:165-188`) only calls `logTransition`, which writes a row and returns.

This is a regression introduced by `715a8b8`. Before it, the verify `GET` was part of `fetchData` (confirmed at `git show 96acc8c:hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:50-58`), so it rode the 5-second poll that `EpicDetail.tsx:221` enables whenever `isRunning`. `715a8b8` removed it from the poll — correctly, to kill the ~128 KiB/tick payload I flagged last time — and replaced it with a `ticket:updated` subscription that the pipeline never fires.

*Failure scenario:* a user opens a ticket and starts an autonomous build. Arij runs `npm test` in the worktree, it fails, a fix cycle is spent, a fix agent is dispatched, verification runs again. Throughout the entire run — potentially an hour — the Verification panel shows "No verification report yet". `EpicDetail` never remounts (`epicId` is stable), the effect deps `[loadData, fetchVerification]` are stable `useCallback`s, and **Run verification** returns 409 while an agent is active (`verify/route.ts:136-145`). The only way to see the mechanical evidence is to close and reopen the panel. This is precisely the observability the epic exists to add, silently absent from the primary path.

*Recommendation:* emit from the pipeline too — `emitTicketUpdated(init.projectId, init.epicId, { verifyReportId, verifyStatus })` after `executeVerification` resolves in `runPipelineVerification`. That also gives the board the same refresh signal the manual route already provides, and makes the hook's comment true.

**Minor — `lib/verify/runner.ts:141-149` / `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:571-608`** — `VerifyCommandResult` cannot distinguish *"could not start"* from *"timed out"* from *"ran and failed"*: `finish` collapses the first two into `exitCode: null`, and the spawn-error flag is not carried into the result. The pipeline consequently treats all three as a fixable code defect and spends a fix cycle. The regression gate in the *same function* deliberately does the opposite and documents why at `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:688-691`: *"An agent in a fix cycle cannot fix an environment fault — fail immediately rather than burning the fix budget."*

*Failure scenario:* a project configures `{"name":"test","command":"npm test"}` and that script defaults to watch mode. Every invocation hangs to the 10-minute default timeout. Night run, per epic: verify (10 min) → fix cycle → real agent session → verify (10 min) → exhausted → park + failed run. Roughly 20–30 minutes and one-to-two agent sessions burned per ticket on a fault no agent can repair, repeated across every epic in the wave.

*Recommendation:* add a discriminator to `VerifyCommandResult` (`outcome: "exited" | "timeout" | "spawn_error"`), and fast-fail the `spawn_error` case in the runner the way `gate.result.reason === "command_error"` already does.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:245-315`** — making the stage total was the right call, but every applicability fault now resolves to `{ ran: false }` with only a `console.warn`: no `onTrace`, therefore no `ticket_activity_log` entry, therefore no user-visible signal. That includes `assertManagedEpicWorktreePath` throwing (`:296`) — the epic's hard constraint firing — and a pruned worktree.

*Failure scenario:* a project has verification configured. The epic's worktree is pruned after a merge; the next pipeline run's session row still records the stale path, `spawn` never happens, and the ticket lands in Review with no verification and nothing in the activity feed to say so. The operator reasonably reads "reached Review" as "the configured checks passed". `{ ran: false }` is currently indistinguishable from *"verify_commands is not configured"*, which is the one case where silence is correct.

*Recommendation:* return a reason with `{ ran: false }` and emit a `PIPELINE_REASONS.deterministicVerificationSkipped(reason)` trace for everything except the genuinely-disabled path. `trace()` already writes an `actor: "system"` activity row, so this is a one-line addition per branch.

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:85-87` vs `:198-204`** — the stale-response guard's comment names two writers (*"a manual run or a later fetch"*), but `setVerificationReport` never touches `verifyRequestSeq`. A `fetchVerification` issued before a manual run and resolving after it therefore installs the older report over the manual result. The window is real: `fetchVerification` fires on every `ticket:updated` for the epic, the `POST` holds the request open for the full command duration, and the server is CPU-loaded by the very commands being verified.
*Recommendation:* `++verifyRequestSeq.current` inside `setVerificationReport`.

**Suggestion — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:36-45`** — `parseCommandResults` now shares `isVerifyCommandResult`, but the two guards still disagree on what to do with a malformed entry: the route `.filter()`s it out and returns a *shorter* report, while `isVerificationReport` rejects the whole thing. A row whose failing command entry is corrupt renders as "Checks failed" with only passing commands listed. Rejecting the row (returning `null`, as the "never verified" case already does) is the safer default for evidence.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:166-167`** — after settling via the close-grace or the absolute deadline, the `stdout`/`stderr` listeners stay attached and the pipes are never destroyed or `unref`'d. The escaped descendant the grace exists for keeps writing into a stream nobody drains. Memory is bounded by `OutputTail`, but the handles are not released for the server's lifetime. Consider `child.stdout?.destroy()` / `child.stderr?.destroy()` inside `finish`.

**Suggestion — `app/settings/page.tsx:341-370`** — `handleSaveVerifySettings` passes `() => {}` as the revert callback, unlike every sibling handler. It also normalises the two fields *before* awaiting the PATCH, so a failed save leaves the textarea showing reformatted JSON that was never persisted, next to "Failed to save the pipeline settings."

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:119`** — `useProjectEvents` opens its own `EventSource` to `/api/projects/${projectId}/events`, and `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:80` already holds one for the same project — with `EpicDetail` rendered inside that page (`page.tsx:493`). Opening a ticket therefore holds two SSE connections to the same stream, consuming two of the browser's six per-origin HTTP/1.1 sockets and two server-side `eventBus` subscribers, while the parent's `ticket:updated` handler is already firing on the exact same event.
*Recommendation:* thread a refresh signal down from the page's existing subscription (it already bumps `refreshTrigger` on `ticket:updated`) rather than opening a second stream.

Otherwise sound, and the headline payload fix landed: `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `OutputTail` is O(limit) rather than accumulating, `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` reads all four keys in one `inArray`, and the 64 KiB-per-command tails are off the 5-second poll.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify-constants.ts` mirrors the existing `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention, `verify_reports` / `verifyReports` follow the schema's snake/camel split, and `VerificationReportSection.tsx` sits with its siblings under `components/kanban/epic-detail/`.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommand` / `VerifyCommandResult` / `VerificationReport` are shared from one client-safe module across server, route and client; `PromptVerificationCommand` is a structural projection that keeps a server type out of the prompt layer; `VerifyConfig.enabled` is derived from `commands.length` rather than stored, which makes "configured but empty" unrepresentable.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is now genuinely good — both previously-uncovered park paths are tested (`__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:213`, `:242`), as are the "not configured" 409 (`epic-verify-route.test.ts:298`), the spawn-error branch, the exit-grace settle, the SIGKILL absolute deadline, the `NODE_ENV` scrub, the empty-commands guard, and tolerant persistence (`verify-runner.test.ts:219-320`). `pipeline-stages-dispatch.test.ts:1073` proves the driver refuses a session-recorded main checkout — the epic's hard constraint tested rather than assumed. The disabled-path test comparing two full harness runs' `requests`/`traces`/`summary` and the `maxSessions: 2` ceiling test remain stronger than the acceptance criteria asked for.

**Minor — `__tests__/pipeline-regression-gate.test.ts:169`** — `715a8b8` deleted an existing assertion from the *regression gate's* test:

```
-    // The post-fix code stage is verified again before review.
-    expect(h.seenSessionIds[1]).toBe("s-fix-1");
```

`git log -L` confirms it was introduced with the gate in `d1244a4` and removed by `715a8b8`, whose stated purpose is "address re-review findings" — no review finding asked for it, no commit message mentions it, and the test added immediately below asserts request payloads rather than restoring the `seenSessionIds` coverage. Tracing the runner, the assertion should still hold (`lastCodeSessionId` is assigned at `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:551`, unchanged in position by this branch), so this reads as an unnecessary coverage deletion in a neighbouring feature rather than an accommodation of changed behaviour — but that is exactly why it should not disappear silently.
*Recommendation:* restore the line, or state in the commit why the gate no longer needs to prove it re-verifies the post-fix worktree.

**Minor — no coverage for the skip-reason gap in §3** — `grep` finds no test asserting what `runPipelineVerification` does when `assertManagedEpicWorktreePath` throws *other than* returning `{ran:false}`; `pipeline-stages-dispatch.test.ts:1073` locks in the silent-skip semantics as correct. ---

|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 4 |

## 1. Readability

No issues found. Comments consistently carry the *why*: the negative-pid rationale (`lib/verify/runner.ts:85-86`), the close-grace bound (`runner.ts:20-26`), "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" (`runner.ts:42`), "empty array is deliberately valid" (`verify-constants.ts:119-125`), the lock's fail-fast-vs-queue split (`execution-lock.ts:3-10`), and the totality argument at `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:239-251` that cites its own precedent. `verificationOutputFence` (`prompt-builder.ts:112-118`) picks a fence longer than any backtick run in captured output and frames it as untrusted — a failing test's stdout cannot impersonate instructions.

## 2. DRY Principle

No blocking issues. `isVerifyCommandResult` is exported once (`verify-constants.ts:46`) and shared by the route parser and the report guard. `resolveVerifyConfig` is one resolver used by both the Settings UI and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject`. See §3 for the one behavioural divergence that survived.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `lib/pipeline/index.ts:227` / `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:228`** — deterministic verification never runs in **Full Auto Mode**.

`runDeterministicVerification` is wired in exactly one place: `startPipelineRun` (`lib/pipeline/index.ts:227`). `grep` for `startPipelineRun(` returns three callers — the epic build route (`:411`), the story build route (`:367`), and the night run (`lib/night/run.ts:336`). Full Auto is not among them: it constructs the driver but calls `driver.launchStage(...)` directly (`lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:228`) and lets the board state machine loop, exactly as its own header comment describes (`engine.ts:41-48`). `runPipeline` is never entered, so the verification hook is never called.

*Failure scenario:* a project configures `verify_commands` and enables Full Auto. Full Auto dispatches a build; the agent promotes the epic to Review; Full Auto dispatches a review; the review comes back clean with no blocking findings; `tryAutoMerge` merges the epic into the default branch. Arij's own `npm test` / `npm run lint` / `npm run build` were never executed, no `verify_reports` row was written, and no `deterministicVerificationSkipped` trace reached `ticket_activity_log` — so the operator has no signal at all. The Verification panel shows whatever stale report the epic last had, or "No verification report yet". This is the mode that merges to the default branch unattended, and it is the one mode that ships the epic's headline guarantee as a no-op.

This contradicts the epic's stated constraint ("Full Auto et night run héritent du comportement via le pipeline : aucune logique spécifique chez eux") for one of the two named modes. In fairness: the boundary is **inherited, not introduced** — the already-merged regression gate (`runVerifyGate`, `lib/pipeline/index.ts:229`) has exactly the same wiring and is equally absent from Full Auto, and §5.6 of the project spec never claims Full Auto runs the pipeline. Nothing here got worse than before the branch. But "Arij now mechanically verifies your work" and "the autonomous merger doesn't" cannot both ship silently.

*Recommendation:* the cheapest honest options, in increasing cost — (a) refuse `tryAutoMerge` when verification is configured and the epic has no `pass` report newer than its last code session, and log the skip; (b) call `driver.runDeterministicVerification(...)` from Full Auto's post-build reconcile; (c) if this is genuinely a follow-up, say so in the ticket and hide/annotate the Verification panel for Full Auto epics so the gap is visible. There is no test asserting either behaviour today.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:264-322`** — the `try` is wider than the comment above it claims. It states applicability is "plain DB reads plus a path check … wrapped together so the stage is TOTAL", but the block also wraps `withVerificationWorktreeLock(... executeVerification ...)` (`:299`) and `emitTicketUpdated` (`:313`). Any failure after the checks therefore returns `skip("applicability check failed: …")` — a mislabelled reason — and the pipeline proceeds to review as if nothing was configured.

A direct consequence: the runner's crash handling (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:640-661`) — `failedDeterministicVerificationCrashed`, `parkRejectedTicket`, terminate — is **unreachable in production**. The only production driver never throws; only the synthetic driver in `__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:123` does. The test at `:244` passes but proves nothing about shipped behaviour.
*Recommendation:* narrow the `try` to the four applicability reads (what the comment describes) and let execution faults reach the runner's park path, which then becomes live. If fail-open is the deliberate choice, drop the crash branch and say so.

**Minor — `lib/verify/worktree.ts:13`** — `isManagedEpicWorktreePath` delegates to `containsPathOnDisk`, which is a *deletion-safety* predicate: when the candidate cannot be `realpath`'d it returns **true** (`lib/projects/workspace.ts:97-99`, commented "candidate does not exist — nothing to delete anyway"). Fail-open is right for "is it safe to delete"; it is inverted for "is it safe to execute in". The lexical check still blocks the main checkout, so the hard constraint holds — but the pipeline path has no existence check at all, unlike the manual route, which explicitly stats the directory (`app/api/.../verify/route.ts:88-95`, commented "A session may outlive a pruned or merged worktree").

*Failure scenario:* the epic worktree is pruned while a code session's row still records its path. `assertManagedEpicWorktreePath` passes, `spawn` gets a `cwd` that doesn't exist, Node emits `error` (ENOENT), `finish(null, error)` records `exitCode: null`, and the pipeline reads that as a code defect: it spends a fix cycle and a real agent session on a phantom failure. With `pipeline_max_fix_cycles` already consumed it parks the ticket back to `in_progress` and fails the run.
*Recommendation:* reuse the route's stat check (or lift `findExistingWorktree` into `lib/verify/`) inside `runPipelineVerification`, and return it as a traced `skip`.

**Minor — `lib/verify/runner.ts:141-149` vs `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:701-725`** — `VerifyCommandResult` still cannot distinguish "could not start" from "timed out" from "ran and failed": `finish` collapses the first two into `exitCode: null` and the spawn-error flag is not carried into the result. The regression gate in the *same function* deliberately fast-fails `command_error` for exactly this reason ("An agent in a fix cycle cannot fix an environment fault — fail immediately rather than burning the fix budget"). A `npm test` that defaults to watch mode hangs to the timeout on every invocation: per epic, ~10 min → fix cycle → real agent session → ~10 min → park + failed run. The author listed this as an accepted follow-up in the last comment; re-raising only because it is the one deferred item with a per-ticket cost measured in agent sessions.

**Suggestion — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:36-45`** — `parseCommandResults` shares the guard now but not the policy: it `.filter()`s malformed entries and returns a *shorter* report, while `isVerificationReport` rejects the whole value. A row whose failing entry is corrupt renders as "Checks failed" listing only the passing commands. Returning `null` (the same shape as "never verified") is the safer default for evidence.

**Suggestion — `app/settings/page.tsx:341-370`** — `handleSaveVerifySettings` passes `() => {}` as the revert callback, unlike every sibling handler, and normalises both fields *before* awaiting the PATCH. A failed save leaves reformatted JSON on screen next to "Failed to save the pipeline settings", implying a persisted value that was never written.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:119`** — `useProjectEvents` opens its own `EventSource` to `/api/projects/${projectId}/events`, while `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:80` already holds one for the same project and renders `EpicDetail` inside it (`page.tsx:493`). Opening a ticket holds two SSE connections to the same stream — two of six per-origin HTTP/1.1 sockets and two `eventBus` subscribers — while the parent's `ticket:updated` handler already fires on the identical event. Known follow-up; unchanged.

The headline payload fix from the last round holds: the 64 KiB-per-command tails are off the 5-second poll, `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `OutputTail` is O(limit) rather than accumulating, and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` reads all four keys in one `inArray`.

One unbounded-growth note: `verify_reports` has no retention policy. Every pipeline run persists up to `VERIFY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES` × command-count of tail, and a night run over many epics with fix cycles writes a row per code stage. Nothing prunes them.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify-constants.ts` mirrors the `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention, `verify_reports` / `verifyReports` follow the schema's snake/camel split, and `VerificationReportSection.tsx` sits with its siblings under `components/kanban/epic-detail/`.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommand` / `VerifyCommandResult` / `VerificationReport` are shared from one client-safe module across server, route and client; `PromptVerificationCommand` is a structural projection that keeps a server type out of the prompt layer; `VerifyConfig.enabled` is derived from `commands.length`, making "configured but empty" unrepresentable. `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is strong. Both park paths (`__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:216`, `:244`), the skip trace (`:269`), the disabled-path bit-identity comparison of two full harness runs (`:141`), the `maxSessions: 2` session-ceiling proof (`:191`), the exit-grace and SIGKILL-deadline settlements, the `NODE_ENV` scrub, the empty-commands guard, tolerant persistence, the spawn-error branch (`verify-runner.test.ts:221-335`), all five route refusal/success paths including the concurrent-run 409 (`epic-verify-route.test.ts:314`), the main-checkout skip with its `skipReason` (`pipeline-stages-dispatch.test.ts:1090`), and the `actor: system` activity row end-to-end (`pipeline-start-run.test.ts:193`).

**Minor — no test covers the Full Auto path.** `grep` finds no assertion, in either direction, that `lib/auto-mode/` does or does not run verification. Whichever way §3's Major is resolved, that behaviour should be pinned — right now the epic's most consequential automation mode is unspecified by tests.

**Minor — `__tests__/epic-verify-route.test.ts`** — no case for a `verify_reports` row whose `commands` JSON is malformed, which is the divergence behind the §3 suggestion. A test would force the two guards to agree on a policy.

## 8. API Design

No blocking issues. `{ data }` / `{ error }` throughout, `getProjectOr404` / `getEpicOr404` for 404s, 409 for all four refusal modes (no worktree, unmanaged path, agent active, not configured) reusing `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload` for the agent case, `errorResponse` for 500, and `emitTicketUpdated` rather than a verify-only event. `POST` never creates a worktree and never falls back to `gitRepoPath`; `findExistingWorktree` walks older sessions when a recorded worktree was pruned.

The migration is correct: `0033_verify_reports.sql` is hand-written with `IF NOT EXISTS`, FKs cascade on project/epic and `set null` on session, and `_journal.json` gains `idx: 32` with a strictly increasing `when` (`1786713000000`). No `drizzle-kit generate` was run.

The "saisies par l'humain" constraint holds: `grep` for `insert(settings)` finds five writers — `app/api/settings`, `app/api/settings/webhooks`, `auto-mode/route.ts`, `github/label-mapping.ts` and `workflow/dreaming.ts` — none reachable from an MCP tool, and `middleware.ts` gates `/api/:path*` on local host/origin, so this new shell-execution surface inherits the existing protection.

One design note, not a defect: `verify_reports` records no commit SHA or branch head, so a report cannot be tied to the tree it verified. `EpicDetail` shows the epic's latest report regardless of what has been committed since — "All checks passed" can describe a tree that has moved on. The visible `finishedAt` (`VerificationReportSection.tsx:112`) partly mitigates it. Worth a follow-up if verification is ever to gate merges (see §3's option (a), which needs exactly this).

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The engineering is in good shape and every accepted finding from the three previous rounds is closed. The runner's settlement contract is airtight and well tested, containment is enforced at both call sites, the stage is total, the lock is process-local rather than a lock file, the migration is correct, and the disabled-path bit-identity and session-ceiling proofs are stronger than the acceptance criteria asked for. I ran the full suite, typecheck, lint and `diff --check` myself and all are green.

The blocker is scope rather than craft: `runDeterministicVerification` is wired only into `runPipeline`, and **Full Auto Mode never enters `runPipeline`** — it dispatches stages directly and merges to the default branch on its own. With `verify_commands` configured, the mode that most needs mechanical evidence silently has none, and logs no skip. The boundary is inherited from the already-merged regression gate rather than introduced here, and a follow-up ticket is a legitimate resolution — but it should not ship unrecorded, because the whole point of this epic is that an agent's assertion is not evidence a gate passed.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I could not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and could not open a `create_bug` follow-up either. No finding rows exist to block approval — the Major and the untested Full Auto path need to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

## Summary

Fourth-review fixes committed in `8f63da6` (4 files, +301/−30).

**Major fixed — Full Auto never ran verification:** `runDeterministicVerification` was wired only into `startPipelineRun`; Full Auto dispatches stages directly via `driver.launchStage` and merges on its own, so with `verify_commands` configured the one mode that lands code on `main` unattended had zero mechanical evidence and logged nothing. Resolution follows the review's option (a), the cheapest honest gate:

- `tryAutoMerge` (`lib/auto-mode/merge.ts`) now runs `verificationGateReason()` after its workflow pre-flight. With verification configured it refuses — logged via `AUTO_MODE_REASONS.mergeRefused`, epic left unparked so the next passing report unlocks the merge — when: no verify report exists for the epic, the latest report did not pass, or the passing report's `finishedAt` predates the last build/fix session's end (the report describes a tree that no longer exists). Verification not configured stays silent: off ≠ unsatisfied.
- Five new tests in `__tests__/auto-mode-merge.test.ts` pin the Full Auto path both ways: never-run/fail/stale → skipped + git untouched + activity entry; fresh pass / unconfigured → merge proceeds.

**Minors also closed (both correctness-relevant and small):**
- **Narrowed applicability try** (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`): only the DB reads and path checks sit inside the `try`, as its comment always claimed. Execution faults now reach the runner's live crash path instead of being mislabelled `"applicability check failed"` skips.
- **Pruned-worktree check:** a session row outliving a merged-away worktree now yields a traced skip ("no longer exists on disk") instead of a spawn-ENOENT phantom failure that would burn a real fix cycle. Pinned by a new dispatch test.

**Validation:** full Vitest suite 392 files / 4,605 tests green; `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` clean (including after the final test-only `afterEach` import); ESLint clean on touched files; `git diff --check` clean; worktree clean. The last change between the full-suite run and commit was a single test-file import, whose suite re-passed. Live Full Auto behavior remains pending merge — the orchestrator runs `main`.

Still deferred follow-ups (unchanged from prior triage): `VerifyCommandResult` outcome discriminator with spawn-error fast-fail, stream destruction after settle, per-project verify settings in the UI, shared SSE connection instead of the hook's own `EventSource`, report-to-commit-SHA binding for future merge gating, and `verify_reports` retention.
